items.source: finding R1; external review
acceptanceCriteria: A v2-unit CI job runs the no-services V2 tests on every push
The job states what it does NOT cover, so it cannot imply full V2 coverage
Proven: breaking a v2 unit test turns the job red
evidence: git grep 'npm test' .github/workflows -> ci.yml:76 and deploy.yml:73, both the ROOT suite only
v2 test script requires --env-file=.env; v2/.env is gitignored
ci.yml has no services: block

RUNTIME CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-25 TO EVERY RESULT RECORDED TODAY: all local verification in this run was executed on Node v22.23.2, while package.json requires >=24.0.0, .nvmrc says 24 and CI uses 24. This does not invalidate the passes, but it RECLASSIFIES them - each was obtained on a runtime the project does not support, and any could differ on Node 24. DEMOTED UAT -> BLOCKED 2026-09-25, same shape as CS-7. AC3 is "proven: breaking a v2 unit test turns the job red" and TWO THINGS WERE MISSING. First, NO MUTATION IS RECORDED ON THIS TICKET AT ALL - its evidence is "33/33 passed, exit 0", A PASSING RUN, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT AC3 ASKS FOR. Second, "the job" has never run, and even a local mutation proves the SCRIPT goes red, not the JOB.

THE LOCAL HALF IS ALREADY DISCHARGED - ON THE WRONG TICKET. CS-48 ev[8] records a falsification of this exact script: "breaking one assertion in ai-provider.test.ts produced not ok 19 - requestCompletion: success returns the completion text, 48 pass / 1 fail, exit 1". That genuinely proves the script goes red when a v2 unit test breaks. CITED HERE rather than moved, so CS-48 evidence stays intact, and only the pipeline half of AC3 remains outstanding.

STALE FIGURE REFRESHED, because a count that has silently drifted is the same defect class as the census proxy: this ticket recorded "33/33 passed". A live run of the same script in this session reports 55 tests, 55 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, exit 0. The 33 predated CS-48 (which took it to 49) and CS-35 (which took it to 54). THE FIGURE DESCRIBED A SUITE THAT NO LONGER EXISTED AT THAT SIZE.

RUNTIME CAVEAT ON THAT REFRESH: the 55/55 run was executed on Node v22.23.2, two major versions below the declared floor of >=24. The number is current for this runtime; it has not been confirmed on Node 24.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; re-check if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 17:00 IST on 2026-09-25.

PROVISIONAL MARKING WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25, SAME DAY IT WAS APPLIED, BECAUSE IT WAS TOO BROAD AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENT. The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". THE GATE COULD FAIL; ONLY ITS FIRST LINK COULD NOT. `npm run typecheck` chains four commands and the last, check-test-types.mjs, filters on /^\S+\.ts\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - WHICH MATCHES A PRODUCTION FILE AS READILY AS A TEST FILE - and exits 1. Anyone running the npm script WOULD have been told.

THIS TICKET DOES NOT CITE A BARE `tsc -b`, so its typecheck evidence was never in the unfalsifiable form and stands unqualified. The narrowed set is 4 of the original 29: CS-53, CS-62, CS-76, CS-77 - ALL FOUR WRITTEN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, which is the correct place for the correction to land.

AC3 CLOSED in v2/ARCHITECTURE.md: the V2 search worker depends on the legacy V1 matcher only through the deliberately narrowed MatchableProfile projection, with V2 owning the source shape and projection and V1 owning the deterministic matcher API. The record explicitly forbids casts/any and states that a fourth-field read must fail type-check.

AC4 MUTATION PROOF RETAKEN on Node 24: temporarily adding `void application.currentCtc` at the matcher boundary made npm run typecheck fail with TS2339 because the narrowed application type excludes currentCtc; removing the mutation restored a zero-exit typecheck. The source was restored byte-identically after the falsification.

Hosted mutation proof run 36448394587 for temporary PR #19 commit a092f220c81bd4468047a6b9019b9124e46fe1e2 failed exactly at 'Test V2 (unit only — mocked HTTP, no database, queue or browser coverage)' after the intentional assertion mutation; recovery and integration jobs passed. items.title: Lead table header offset is wrong on Linux WebKit at 768px
items.userProblem: The sticky header is 48px out on Safari at tablet width, so rows sit underneath it.
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduced in the Playwright Linux container, not guessed from Windows
Root cause named; the assertion is not widened
check-ui.mjs green on all three engines in CI
evidence: webkit: sticky offset mismatch at 768px - header 57, expected 105, delta -48.0000
57 = 3.5rem*16+1 and 105 = 6.5rem*16+1: two breakpoints apart, not a settle race
Passes on Windows WebKit (webkit-2359); CI runs Linux WebKit

2026-09-21 genuine Linux reproduction (Docker, mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-noble matching installed Playwright 1.63.0, built app, ran check-ui.mjs): chromium and firefox both report headerHeight 105 == expectedHeight 105 at 768px, headerOverlap false — the specific 768px offset this ticket names did not reproduce on chromium/firefox. webkit itself never reached that comparison: it threw first on a DIFFERENT, earlier assertion — 'webkit: rows must stack at 390px. 11 rows, 10 overlapping' — identical error text and overlap indices to the prior recorded failure in test-results/focused-readiness-20260920-204601-135/root-ui.log.

Root cause found: apps/web/src/components/LeadTable.tsx's own code comment already documented the exact mechanism — crossing the compact/card breakpoint calls virtualizer.measure() then re-measures mounted rows in the same layout effect, but WebKit delivers ResizeObserver entries before React's layout effects, so the manual re-measure read stale (pre-compact) row heights: 261px-tall cards on a 233px pitch, 28px overlap, matching the observed defect exactly

Fix: deferred the manual re-measurement into a double requestAnimationFrame after virtualizer.measure(), so it reads row geometry only after the browser has actually painted the new compact/card layout, removing the race instead of widening the assertion

2026-09-21 verification: 4 consecutive clean check-ui.mjs runs in the real Linux Playwright container (webkit included, errors: [] on all three engines each time), plus 1 clean run of npm run test:ui on Windows (exit 0). No 'rows must stack' failure in any run.
npx prettier --check, npx eslint and npm run typecheck all pass on the changed file

DEMOTED UAT -> QA 2026-09-25 on independent audit. THE DEFECT IN THIS TICKETS TITLE WAS NEVER REPRODUCED. AC1 requires "reproduced in the Playwright Linux container, not guessed from Windows", and the evidence states verbatim that chromium and firefox both reported headerHeight 105 == expectedHeight 105 at 768px with headerOverlap false - "the specific 768px offset this ticket names did not reproduce" - while webkit threw first on a DIFFERENT, EARLIER assertion about rows stacking at 390px.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY FOUND, ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT AT A DIFFERENT VIEWPORT: a ResizeObserver-versus-layout-effect race causing 28px row overlap at 390px. That work looks genuinely good, and THE EVIDENCE IS UNUSUALLY HONEST ABOUT THE SUBSTITUTION, which is why this is a status problem and not an engineering one. But a ticket whose named defect was never confirmed cannot sit in the state meaning "acceptance evidence exists", because there is no acceptance evidence for the thing it names.
TWO ACCEPTABLE RESOLUTIONS, both fine, and the current state is neither: either the 768px offset is real and still unfixed, or this ticket is retitled and re-scoped onto the defect actually fixed.

AC3 IS THE SHARPER HALF AND IT IS THE CONCRETE COST OF NOT COMMITTING. It is THE ONLY ACCEPTANCE CRITERION ACROSS THE AUDITED TICKETS THAT NAMES CI IN ITS OWN TEXT - "check-ui.mjs green on all three engines IN CI". The evidence is four container runs plus one Windows run, and the fix in apps/web/src/components/LeadTable.tsx is UNCOMMITTED, so every CI run that exists predates it. AC3 IS NOT MERELY UNPROVEN, IT IS UNPROVABLE until the change is committed and a pipeline runs. This is the one ticket whose promotion is blocked by the commit gate by its own wording.

items.title: Proxy restart strands every service behind a healthy-looking 502
items.userProblem: The site can be entirely down while every container reports healthy.
items.source: real incident during this project
acceptanceCriteria: A Caddy crash recovers without operator action, or is detected and alerted
Proven by killing Caddy and observing the result
evidence: restart-stack.sh is operator recovery, not self-healing

2026-09-23: implementation, both real reviewers full findings and fixes (including a genuine P1 latent availability bug in the circuit breaker itself, caught by Security and fixed with an explicit systemd TimeoutStartSec), and the QA mutation-test proof - see completedSteps.

STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-24 from UAT to BLOCKED by the Orchestrator, after a forensic audit found status had outrun evidence. Nothing about the implementation is being questioned - it was built carefully and its limitations were disclosed honestly at the time. The issue is purely what UAT means in this project: "acceptance evidence exists". This ticket has an acceptance criterion of the form "proven by doing X on a real host", and NO live-host evidence is recorded anywhere in this repository. Verification level is LOCALLY VERIFIED, not LIVE-HOST VERIFIED. No host verification is possible from this environment - there is no authorized host access, and attempting it is out of scope. BLOCKED is the honest status: the blocker is the missing operator-run acceptance evidence, not a defect. An operator can clear this by performing the host-side proof and recording the real output.

OPERATOR RUNBOOK READY 2026-09-25: .ai/OPERATOR-RUNBOOK-host-evidence.md contains the exact commands, expected output and pass criterion for this ticket, sequenced so ONE operator session clears all seven host-blocked tickets (CS-3, CS-24, CS-25, CS-26, CS-27, CS-30, CS-47) in a single pass. It carries the incident prohibitions explicitly (never nft flush ruleset, never restart the proxy alone, never docker system prune -a, never regenerate POSTGRES_PASSWORD, never delete a PG volume) and instructs the operator to record FAILING output too - a failure captured is worth more than a success assumed. This ticket remains BLOCKED. The runbook is not evidence; it is what makes the evidence obtainable in one pass.

AC1 IS MET LOCALLY 2026-09-25 ON ITS OWN DISJUNCTION: the criterion offers "recovers without operator action, OR is detected and alerted", and the second branch is proven locally at 14/14, shown non-vacuous by QAs own mutation. Only AC2 is strictly host-bound. Recorded because reading this ticket as wholly host-blocked overstates what is outstanding.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; re-check if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 16:10 IST on 2026-09-25.

2026-09-28 controlled host session: provenance and /api/health passed on deployed revision 1401597f84368e87d8f7e637e034a15d83b9b352, but no CareerScope systemd units or timers are installed on the Hostinger VPS. The required restart-and-observe proof was not run because the deployment has no installed recovery unit; CS-3 remains BLOCKED rather than being inferred from local tests.

2026-09-29 protected Deploy #17 deployed 05fe963bfb09b3f55ad99242a261287aa04a604b; careerscope-proxy-recovery.timer was enabled. Controlled proof killed only careerscope-proxy-1; two timer checks recorded consecutive failures, invoked /opt/careerscope/infra/v3/restart-stack.sh, logged auto-restart completed, and https://careerscope.tech/api/health returned status ok. The deployed restart script mode was 775 after fixing its Git executable bit.

items.architectureImpact: compose topology
items.currentStep: BLOCKED on operator-run live-host acceptance evidence. Implementation complete and locally verified; host proof never recorded.
completedSteps: Real CareerScope System Designer invocation (native runSubagent, read-only) produced a full design review before any infra/v3 edit, given this ticket's own reviewAgents require System Designer + Security first and a naive self-healing approach (a Docker-socket-mounted watchdog) would introduce a new root-equivalent privilege class on this single-host system.

Design confirmed: proxy has no healthcheck of its own; no monitoring/cron/systemd timer exists anywhere in infra/v3 today; no Docker socket is mounted into any container currently (clean boundary worth preserving). restart-stack.sh's own header comment accurately documents the split-brain mechanism - this is a named, known gap, not a doc/code drift.

Five options produced and traded off. Recommended path: Option 1 (host-native systemd timer probing the published origin, same symptom restart-stack.sh already checks; alert via journald + optional webhook) - needs no Docker socket, no new container, no new listening port, fully testable locally against compose.acceptance.yml by killing the proxy, and satisfies the acceptance criterion's 'detected and alerted' branch. Option 2 (same detector auto-invoking restart-stack.sh's dependents logic, with a circuit breaker and symptom-based not restart-event-based trigger to avoid thrashing Postgres/Redis or false-firing during normal deploys) is the natural next step for the stronger 'recovers without operator action' branch, and stays in the same privilege class as Option 1 (host operator's existing docker access, never inside a container).

Option 3 (add a healthcheck to the proxy service) flagged as trivial and worth doing regardless, but explicitly does NOT alone satisfy either acceptance criterion (Docker does not auto-restart on failed healthcheck; nothing watches for it).

Option 4 (replace network_mode: service:proxy with per-service netns + internal bridge network) flagged as out of scope for this ticket: it changes a documented security invariant and needs its own ticket/ADR with explicit owner sign-off, not a drive-by inclusion here.

Option 5 (Docker-socket-mounted watchdog) explicitly rejected: hands any container root-equivalent host control, a new privilege class on a box with zero containers holding that power today; needs explicit owner approval and is not recommended as this ticket's implementation.

No infra/v3 files were changed. This is design input only, per the ticket's own review-before-implementation requirement; Infrastructure can proceed directly to implementing Option 1 (and, once proven, Option 2) without further owner approval per the designer's judgment, since neither touches the existing security boundary.

Implemented Option 1 + Option 2 per the System Designer's own recommendation (already recorded above): infra/v3/recover-proxy.sh - a host-native detector reusing CS-24 monitor.sh's exact symptom check (does the public origin actually answer), requiring PROXY_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD (default 2) consecutive bad checks before acting so a single blip cannot trigger a restart, then automatically invoking the existing, already-tested restart-stack.sh - satisfying AC1's 'recovers without operator action' branch, not only 'is detected'. A circuit breaker (PROXY_COOLDOWN_SECONDS, default 1 hour) prevents more than one auto-restart per confirmed-outage window, escalating to an alert instead of thrashing the stack if restart-stack.sh itself cannot fix the underlying cause.

Added careerscope-proxy-recovery.service/.timer (every 2 minutes - 2-3 confirm-then-restart cycles inside a 4-6 minute recovery window) and setup-proxy-recovery.sh (idempotent installer, shares /etc/careerscope-monitor.env with CS-24's monitor - one webhook, configured once). Added infra/v3/check-proxy-recovery.sh: a fully offline test suite (stub curl/restart-stack.sh, no real host needed) proving the confirm-then-act-then-cooldown state machine, one-shot recovery announcement, and that a failing restart-stack.sh invocation is still alerted - 14/14 passing. Wired into CI (ci.yml verify job, alongside CS-24/25's own self-contained infra checks).

Added docs/OPERATIONS/PROXY-RECOVERY.md (design, install, the literal 'kill Caddy and observe the automatic recovery' proof this ticket's own AC2 requires) and a one-time manual-install step in docs/OPERATIONS/DEPLOYMENT.md.

Real Security review (native runSubagent): verdict REVISE, now fixed. Found one real P1: careerscope-proxy-recovery.service had no explicit TimeoutStartSec, so systemd's default 90-second Type=oneshot timeout could kill the unit mid-restart-stack.sh-run (which itself does 8 sequential docker compose restart calls plus up to a 60s health-poll plus verification probes, plausibly exceeding 90s on the happy path alone) - critically, recover-proxy.sh's own LAST_RESTART state write only happens after restart-stack.sh returns, so a systemd-induced kill would silently disable the circuit breaker the very next tick, letting a second restart fire within the same hour the breaker exists to prevent. This was a latent availability bug in the safety mechanism itself, reachable with no adversary at all - fixed with an explicit, generous TimeoutStartSec=600. Confirmed clean: the only path to invoking restart-stack.sh requires both the confirm-threshold and the cooldown gates in sequence (no bypass), the state file only ever contains self-generated integer values (same safe pattern as monitor.sh), the webhook alerting is byte-for-byte the same proven pattern as monitor.sh/backup.sh, and the systemd hardening doesn't interfere with restart-stack.sh's actual docker calls. Noted (not fixed, out of scope, disclosed in KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md) that CS-24/CS-25's own services have the identical missing TimeoutStartSec, worth a follow-up since they don't have a circuit-breaker whose correctness depends on completing.

Real QA invocation (native runSubagent) independently verified: check-proxy-recovery.sh 14/14, independently traced the confirm-threshold and cooldown gates as the sole, unconditional, no-bypass control paths into the restart logic, proved the test suite non-vacuous via a live mutation (removed the confirm-threshold gate on a scratch copy, watched the specific 'no restart on first bad check' assertion fail with the exact expected/got mismatch, restored, reconfirmed 14/14), confirmed systemd unit/timer/installer path consistency including the explicit absolute PROXY_RESTART_SCRIPT path matching the real deployed checkout location, confirmed CI wiring, root typecheck/lint/format/test all clean (1055/1055 root tests), and confirmed CS-24/CS-25 unaffected. Verdict: PASS.

Final re-verification after the TimeoutStartSec fix: check-proxy-recovery.sh 14/14, check-monitoring.sh clean, check-backup.sh 17/19 (same 2 confirmed-environmental Windows-only failures), root format:check clean for every CS-3 file, ci.yml validated as parseable YAML.
QA
items.summary: If the web server in front of everything crashes, the whole site goes down while every internal health check still reports fine. Nobody is told. Fixing this means it either recovers by itself or you find out immediately.
items.blockedReason: AC2 requires live-host evidence: proxy recovery observed on the real deployment. Clearable in the operator SSH session (runbook §CS-3). AC1 is already met locally on its own disjunction - "detected and alerted", 14/14, shown non-vacuous by mutation.

DEMOTED UAT -> BLOCKED 2026-09-25, AND THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL DEMOTION OF THE AUDIT. Verified in this session: CS-7 IS THE ONLY P0 IN THE BACKLOG. AC3 is "proven by pushing a commit with a deliberately failing check and observing deploy refuse" - and that has never been done. No commit has been pushed; the SHA has not moved.

WHY IT IS NOT AN ORDINARY CI-PENDING ITEM, AND THIS IS THE ARGUMENT: this project has already adjudicated this exact criterion shape FIVE TIMES IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION. CS-3, CS-24, CS-25, CS-26 and CS-27 were each demoted UAT -> BLOCKED on the stated principle that the ticket has a criterion of the form "proven by doing X on a real host" with no live evidence recorded. ALL FIVE VERIFIED STILL BLOCKED IN THIS SESSION. CS-7 AC3 IS THAT SAME SENTENCE WITH "PIPELINE" IN PLACE OF "HOST", and it was not demoted with them.

AND IT IS THE TICKET A RELEASE DECISION RESTS ON. It is the control that stops a deployment shipping code CI rejected, and its own evidence records that "deploy succeeded at least four times while CI was red". ACCEPTING CS-7 AT UAT MEANS ACCEPTING, ON LOCAL EVIDENCE ALONE, THAT THE GUARD AGAINST SHIPPING REJECTED CODE WORKS. If a release proceeds on the strength of the UAT tier, this is the one ticket where an unproven criterion carries the highest possible cost.

BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT IS PROVEN, BECAUSE THE WORK IS GOOD: AC1 require-ci querying the Actions API for the exact head SHA, and AC2 override requiring explicit intent, are both recorded with mutation-tested gate logic (22 checks, 5 mutations detected; deploy-gate 9/9). THE DECISION LOGIC IS WELL PROVEN. WHAT IS UNPROVEN IS THAT THE WORKFLOW WIRING AROUND IT DOES WHAT THE LOGIC SAYS. That distinction is the whole finding, and it is why local mutation testing - however good - cannot discharge AC3.

items.title: Twenty-four agents exist with no activation policy
items.userProblem: A roster nobody can route confidently becomes ceremony, and ceremony hides real review gaps.
items.source: external review (ChatGPT)
acceptanceCriteria: Each agent is retained only if it produces a unique artefact, holds a distinct permission boundary, makes a materially different decision, or supplies independent evidence
A written activation policy states which agents a given change class requires
Agents failing the retention test are merged or removed, not left dormant
evidence: The roster grew 11 to 24 in one session
AGENT-SETUP.md described 11 agents for two cycles while the validator stayed green

AC1 SATISFIED 2026-09-24: a real CareerScope Agent Operations dispatch (read-only, no edit tool) applied the four-part retention test to each of the 24 agents individually and returned a per-agent verdict with unique artefact, permission boundary, distinct decision, independent evidence and observed-usage citation. Result: 24 KEEP, 0 MERGE, 0 REMOVE. Transcribed verbatim into .ai/agent-operations.json "agents" (previously an empty object {}), which now holds all 24 records keyed identically to .ai/LOOP-STATE.json - verified set-equal, 24/24, no orphans either direction.

Count reconciliation VERIFIED, not assumed: 24 files in .github/agents/, 24 rows in AGENT-SETUP.md, 24 in docs/ai/agent-matrix.md, 24 keys in LOOP-STATE.json, 23+self in the orchestrator allowlist. No missing or unreadable file, no orphan entry. node scripts/check-agents.mjs passes all checks including "PASS 24 agent files (got 24)".

AC2 WAS ALREADY SATISFIED IN THE NARROW SENSE ONLY, and is now genuinely satisfied: the activation table existed but covered only 11 of 24 agents. 13 appeared in no row at all - most sharply the Independent Reviewer, which the invocation record shows is the single most-invoked and most-productive specialist. Seven change classes had no row whatsoever. FIXED 2026-09-24 in .ai/AGENT-SETUP.md: the table now covers all 24 agents and adds rows for documentation-only, design-system/token, release cut, git/tag/commit, new skill/extension/MCP, agent failure/loop bound, and backlog intake. Added a disambiguation table for the six overlapping pairs (O-1..O-6). The default-of-four and never-run-all-agents rules are preserved and restated; the table explicitly says it is not an attendance list.

AC3 SATISFIED BY JUSTIFICATION, NOT BY ACTION - recorded deliberately rather than smoothed over, at Agent Operations explicit instruction. Zero agents were merged or removed because none failed the test: criterion 1 is disjunctive and the merge bar (duplicate artefact AND boundary AND decision) is met by no agent. Six agents fail exactly one leg and every one is flagged in the record. The residual risk has moved from "unexamined roster" to "six flagged overlaps needing activation-policy disambiguation", which the new table now provides.

FOUR DEFECTS REMAIN OPEN AND ARE OPERATOR-ACTION-REQUIRED, all in .github/agents/careerscope-orchestrator.agent.md. D-1 (CRITICAL): the activation table is duplicated there and CONTRADICTS the canonical copy - its "System redesign => all" row directly violates this repository own "never run all agents" rule, and because the Orchestrator reads its own file, the contradicting copy is the one that will actually be obeyed. D-2: says "all ten agents" against a roster of 24. D-7: makes Product Architect and System Designer mutual fallbacks while AGENT-SETUP defends them as not duplicates - both cannot be true. D-8: makes the Final Auditor the Independent Reviewer fallback, which spends the only independent check mid-loop when it is given no fallback precisely because it is last. ORCHESTRATOR DECISION, recorded: I did not edit any file under .github/agents/, because every permission guarantee in this system rests on agent tool-grants being operator-owned - an agent that can edit agent definitions can grant itself the edit tool. These four are therefore DISCLOSED in .ai/AGENT-SETUP.md and .ai/agent-operations.json rather than silently fixed.

D-9 DISCLOSED: LOOP-STATE records 18 of 24 agents as WAITING while review.txt 2026-09-20 records contributions returned from all 24. Both are true under different senses of "ran". Every agent record now carries an invocationEvidence field distinguishing task-dispatch (7 agents) from discussion-contribution (17 agents) from none, so a discussion contribution can never again read as a successful task dispatch. Constraints honoured verbatim: no failureCount above 0 was written (Agent Operations found no agent failure; 18 never-dispatched agents is a state, not a failure), and lastError is null - never "" or "none" - wherever no failure occurred, so an absent value can never collapse into "no failures".

OPERATOR-ACTION DIFF PROPOSAL WRITTEN 2026-09-24: .ai/OPERATOR-ACTION-orchestrator-agent-file.md now contains a precise, reviewable diff for D-1, D-2, D-7 and D-8 - exact line numbers against current bytes (D-1 table at lines 63-72, D-2 at line 60, D-7 at lines 189-190, D-8 at line 191), exact replacement text, the reasoning for each, the alternative where one exists, and the verification commands to run after applying. This satisfies "fix the underlying mismatch, do not merely edit prose" WITHOUT the Orchestrator silently granting itself authority over the permission model that constrains it. For D-1 the proposal deliberately deletes the duplicate table rather than correcting its wrong row, because two copies of a routing policy will drift again - the fix is that there is one copy. For D-7 it offers both defensible resolutions (keep the roles distinct and remove the mutual fallback, OR merge them and stop claiming they are distinct) and states plainly that the current state - claiming distinct while treating them as substitutes - is the one option that is not defensible. SEVERITY CORRECTED, per the forensic audit: D-1 is P1, not CRITICAL. There is no data or security impact. D-8 carries the real risk - using the Final Auditor as the Independent Reviewer fallback spends the only independent check mid-loop, after which a result can still be presented as having passed final audit. That is an integrity risk to every verdict this system produces. The audit explicitly UPHELD the Orchestrator refusal to self-edit .github/agents/. Applying the diff is a one-commit operator task.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2026-09-25 (read-only, no shell - it marked everything requiring execution UNCONFIRMED rather than implying agreement). VERDICT: REJECTED for UAT. ITS DECISIVE FINDING, INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED: .ai/agent-operations.json carries retentionPolicy.criterion3Satisfied = false with the explicit note "Do not record as satisfied", while this backlog entry claimed "AC3 SATISFIED BY JUSTIFICATION, NOT BY ACTION". TWO CANONICAL RECORDS CONTRADICTED EACH OTHER ABOUT THE SAME CRITERION, and the backlog is the one automation reads. RECONCILED 2026-09-25 IN FAVOUR OF agent-operations.json, which is the ticket own machine state and explicitly instructed otherwise: AC3 IS NOT SATISFIED. My earlier "satisfied by justification" phrasing is RETRACTED. Zero agents were merged or removed, which was correct on the evidence, but the criterion asks for action and no action was taken - that is an open criterion, not a satisfied one, and dressing it as satisfied was precisely the reinterpretation this project forbids. ITS SECOND FINDING, ALSO ACCEPTED: a ticket cannot be UAT-ready while a P1 defect defeats its own AC2 at the point of use. AC2 requires a written activation policy stating which agents a change class needs; D-1 means the copy the Orchestrator actually obeys still says "System redesign -> all". DISCLOSURE IS NOT REMEDIATION. All four defects confirmed still present at the exact lines the proposal names (D-2 ~60, D-1 63-72 ending "| System redesign | all |", D-7 189-190, D-8 191). It explicitly upholds the refusal to self-edit .github/agents/. UNLOCK: operator applies .ai/OPERATOR-ACTION-orchestrator-agent-file.md.

REVIEWER D VERDICT 2026-09-25: REJECTED. All four defects confirmed PRESENT IN CURRENT BYTES at the lines .ai/OPERATOR-ACTION-orchestrator-agent-file.md names. D-1: "| System redesign | all |" in the duplicated table. D-2: "Invoking all ten agents" against a roster of 24. D-7: System Designer and Product Architect set as MUTUAL fallbacks for two roles AGENT-SETUP.md explicitly defends as non-duplicates. D-8: Independent Reviewer falling back to Final Auditor, which spends the only independent check mid-loop - immediately above the paragraph explaining why the Final Auditor gets no fallback. Status held at QA, NOT promoted.

REVIEWER D - AC2 IS NOT SATISFIED AT THE POINT OF USE. A written activation policy that the routing agent contradicts in its own file is not one policy but TWO, and the wrong one wins - because the file the agent actually reads while routing is the one that governs behaviour, not the document describing it.

REVIEWER D - AC3 IS NOT SATISFIED BY THE TICKETS OWN CANONICAL RECORD: agent-operations.json carries criterion3Satisfied: false together with the instruction "Do not record as satisfied". The reviewer reached the previous reviewers conclusion INDEPENDENTLY, FROM THE BYTES RATHER THAN FROM ITS VERDICT, which makes it a second observation rather than an echo: DISCLOSURE IS NOT REMEDIATION. Writing down that a file is wrong does not make the file right.

REVIEWER D EXPLICITLY ENDORSES THE REFUSAL TO SELF-EDIT .github/agents/, and it is recorded here as UPHELD rather than as an open question: an agent that can edit agent definitions can grant itself the edit tool, and every read-only guarantee in this workflow rests on that boundary holding. The remediation must be applied by the operator in a reviewed commit, not by an agent editing its own definition.

STATUS MOVED QA -> BLOCKED 2026-09-25 on the reviewers recommendation, which the coordinator agreed and this session applied. The reasoning is that BLOCKED-WITH-A-NAMED-REASON describes this state more honestly than QA: it is neither CI-blocked nor host-blocked, it is blocked on an OPERATOR COMMIT applying the D-1 to D-8 proposal in .ai/OPERATOR-ACTION-orchestrator-agent-file.md. That matches how CS-46 records an owner-decision block. QA implies something is awaiting testing; nothing here is.

THE REFUSAL TO SELF-EDIT .github/agents/ IS NOW SETTLED, NOT OPEN. The reviewer endorsed it independently: an agent that can edit agent definitions can grant itself the edit tool, and every read-only guarantee in this roster - including the one constraining the reviewer itself - rests on that boundary holding. The remediation is the operators, in a reviewed commit.

REVIEWER D - CONSUMER CHAIN: AGENT-SETUP.md -> the Orchestrator -> its own agent file, WHERE IT IS CONTRADICTED. The chain terminates in a disagreement rather than in something that executes, which is why a written policy the routing agent contradicts is two policies and the wrong one wins.

REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT, carried on this verdict deliberately: the reviewer states it cannot detect whether its reads fell inside another session write window. Three sessions were writing concurrently. If any file cited in this verdict was edited between roughly 15:05 and 15:25 IST on 2026-09-25, THIS VERDICT SHOULD BE RE-TAKEN RATHER THAN TRUSTED. Recorded so a later reader can judge it rather than inherit it.

items.title: Signed-in screens have no shared loading, empty or error treatment
items.summary: Each screen invents its own behaviour while data is loading, when there is nothing to show, or when something fails. The result is that the product feels different from page to page, and some failures show nothing at all. One shared set of states fixes both.
items.userProblem: A screen that silently shows nothing is indistinguishable from a screen that is still loading.
items.source: operator request — frontend workstream
acceptanceCriteria: One shared set of loading, empty and error components used by every signed-in route
Every error state says what failed and offers the next action, never a bare message
Empty states distinguish "nothing yet" from "nothing matches your filters"
Verified in all three browser engines at 320, 768 and 1440 widths
evidence: Each route currently implements its own handling; several have no error state

STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-24 from UAT to IN PROGRESS. AC1 is "One shared set of loading, empty and error components used by EVERY signed-in route". Verified by the Orchestrator against current bytes: v2/apps/web/src/components/ui-states.tsx is imported by exactly TWO modules - authenticated-shell.tsx and job-search-view.tsx - while the (app) route group contains EIGHT routes: applications, career-resources, dashboard, jobs, preparation, resume, saved, settings. So the shared treatment reaches the shell and one view, and the remaining routes still implement their own handling or none. This ticket also carried only ONE evidence entry, and that entry ("Each route currently implements its own handling; several have no error state") is the PROBLEM STATEMENT, not completion evidence - there was nothing recorded that could have supported UAT. Remaining work is the rollout to the other routes plus AC4 (three engines at 320, 768 and 1440), which the repaired browser suite can now actually enforce.

RECOVERY CONTEXT, recorded because it changes how this evidence should be read. A Frontend sub-agent was dispatched for this ticket and wrote eight files between 08:33 and 08:39 on 2026-09-25. The session then died on a DNS failure reaching the model API - infrastructure, not the repository - BEFORE the agent returned its report. So there is NO per-criterion table from the implementer, NO record of where it chose not to consolidate and why, and NO falsification proof for any assertion it added. The edits landed with no typecheck, lint or test run behind them. THE ORCHESTRATOR ESTABLISHED THE FACTS RATHER THAN ASSUMING EITHER WAY: typecheck exit 0 and lint exit 0, which ruled out the loud failure mode (a half-applied API where some call sites use the new shape and others the old) and left only the quiet one (a rollout that compiles but is incomplete). ui-states consumers went from 2 modules to 11, and the shapes agree, so the rollout is CONSISTENT rather than partial.

TWO STALE ASSERTIONS FOUND AND FIXED - direct evidence the agent never ran the suite. Both expected the OLD bare error text after its own change had improved it. (1) check-ui.ts export error expected exact "Request failed. Please try again." while job-search-view now renders "Could not export this search. Request failed. Please try again."; (2) the SaveJob error expected the same bare text while saved-leads now renders "Could not save this job. ...". Both corrected to assert the FULL message, which is stronger than the original: it pins criterion 2 "what failed" prefix, so a regression to a bare {error.message} now fails. MY OWN FIRST READ WAS WRONG AND I CORRECTED IT: I initially recorded that job-search-view still rendered three bare {error.message} states violating AC2. It does not. Those use the ErrorState BLOCK variant, which carries title ("Could not load these results", "Could not cancel that search", "Could not load your search history") plus onRetry. The rollout has two coherent shapes - inline concatenates the prefix into message, block supplies title plus action - and both satisfy AC2. I had judged the inline pattern as the only valid one.

PER-CRITERION STATE, verified by the Orchestrator against current bytes. AC1 MET: ui-states is imported by 11 modules covering every signed-in surface (dashboard, preparation, resume, settings route files plus authenticated-shell, career-links-view, job-search-view, preparation-panel, profile-editor, resume-panel, saved-leads). AC2 MET via two shapes, above. AC3 MET and genuinely distinguishes the two cases - saved-leads.tsx:731-732 renders "No leads with status X. That is this status filter only - Y has leads; choose it above to see them." when a sibling status is populated, versus "No leads with status X yet. Save a job from Search to add one here." when nothing exists at all. Surfaces with no filter (search history, resume list) correctly use the nothing-yet form only. AC4 MET: check-ui.ts carries a real for-loop over [320, 768, 1440] exercising the consolidated states, running in all three engines.

ORCHESTRATOR-SUPPLIED FALSIFICATION for the single most criterion-specific new assertion, because none existed. Collapsed AC3 two branches by replacing the filtered-empty wording, mutation VERIFIED PRESENT before running (printed the mutated source line), and the suite failed waiting for the exact filtered-empty text, exit 1. Restored, verified, green on chromium/firefox/webkit exit 0. So the AC3 distinction is proven to be load-bearing rather than decorative. THE REMAINING NEW ASSERTIONS ARE UNFALSIFIED - stated plainly rather than implied. I proved one; the agent proved none. An independent reviewer should treat the others as unproven and is right to ask for them. FULL VERIFICATION BY THE ORCHESTRATOR: v2 typecheck 0, lint 0, web build 0 (compiled successfully), test:ui exit 0 on all three engines, test:integration 43/43 exit 0 on a quiet re-run (one earlier run showed the known CS-58 intermittent), test:registration PASS 17/17, format:check 0, eol:check 0. No styling change was made by me; I did not audit the agent diff for styling changes and cannot certify the UI freeze held across its edits - that is an open question for review.

UI-FREEZE COMPLIANCE: PARTIALLY ESTABLISHED, PARTIALLY UNVERIFIABLE - and the unverifiable half has a specific mechanical cause, not a general caveat. ESTABLISHED: NO stylesheet was touched. Every .css under v2/apps/web/src was checked for a write inside the 08:33-08:39 rollout window and none was modified - ui-states.module.css last changed 09-23 22:31, globals.css 09-24 18:23, dashboard-shell.module.css 09-24 11:53, application-details.module.css 09-24 00:26. The sub-agent introduced no CSS change of any kind. NOT VERIFIABLE: whether the .tsx edits altered inline className usage. Four of the touched files are tracked, but their diff is against HEAD 5239b0a and therefore carries six days of accumulated work, so this ticket contribution cannot be isolated from it. The other three - ui-states.tsx, career-links-view.tsx, job-search-view.tsx - are UNTRACKED and have NO BASELINE AT ALL. THIS IS NOW A PATTERN, NOT AN EXCUSE, AND THE OWNER SHOULD SEE IT AS ONE: this is the SECOND ticket whose UI-freeze compliance is unverifiable for the identical mechanical reason. CS-51 carries the same finding. 98 of 196 dirty entries are untracked, meaning no before/after claim about any of them is checkable by any tool. Both tickets trace to the same commit blocker. Two occurrences of one cause is a structural consequence of the uncommitted tree, and it will recur on every subsequent ticket touching an untracked file until that changes.

F-1 CLOSED 2026-09-25 - the ninth check-that-cannot-fail and the subtlest of the run. check-ui.ts:1055 used filter({ hasText: "Request failed." }), and hasText is a SUBSTRING match, so the old bare text is a substring of the new prefixed text. It passed before the rollout, passed after it, and would have kept passing through a regression to a bare {error.message}. The reviewer observation is the part worth keeping: "It was never stale in the sense of failing - which is exactly why it was not caught alongside the other two." The two I found announced themselves by going red. This one was invisible precisely because it never broke. Now asserts the full string exact: true, so both the what-failed prefix and the recovery instruction are load-bearing.

F-2 CLOSED, AND IT RETIRES THE DEFECT CLASS RATHER THAN THE INSTANCE. ui-states.tsx inline ErrorState took a single unconstrained message: string with an optional action, so <ErrorState variant="inline" message={err.message} /> - a bare transport message naming nothing, exactly what AC2 forbids - compiled cleanly. The discriminated union enforced SHAPE, not CONTENT. The whole point of consolidating into one module was to make the rule structural; it was still discipline, held up by three assertions. The inline variant is now { what: string; detail: string; className?; action? }, concatenated internally. BOTH halves are required, so omitting the what-failed half is UNREPRESENTABLE. All 15 inline call sites migrated, each split by hand rather than by pattern because the split point is a judgement about which half names the operation and which carries the error or the recovery instruction. PROVEN THE RIGHT WAY FOR A TYPE CONTRACT - the proof is a compile error, not a test failure. Reintroducing a bare message at saved-leads.tsx:190 produces "error TS2322: Type { variant: inline; message: string; detail: string; } is not assignable to type IntrinsicAttributes & ErrorStateProps", tc exit 2. Mutation verified present first; restored and verified after. NOTE WHAT THIS IMPLIES: F-2 would have made F-1 IMPOSSIBLE. A screen cannot regress to a bare message without deleting a required prop and failing the build, so no assertion - substring or otherwise - is needed to catch it. That is the fifth convergence on the same principle in this run.

PROCESS NOTE: my first F-2 falsification attempt failed to apply - Python quoting mangled inside PowerShell for the third time tonight - and the mutation-present check caught it before I drew any conclusion. The typecheck reported exit 0, which would have read as "the bare message compiles, so the contract does not work" - the exact OPPOSITE of the truth. A no-op mutation does not merely fail to prove something; it can actively produce the wrong conclusion. Redone with a script file asserting its own precondition.

F-4 CENSUS DONE 2026-09-25 - enumerated, not counted, because as the review put it typecheck rules out the loud failure (a mismatched API) and not the quiet one (a surface that simply never migrated). F-2 has since made the loud failure IMPOSSIBLE, which left the quiet one as the only remaining risk on this ticket. METHOD: every .tsx under apps/web/src carrying useQuery, useMutation or useInfiniteQuery - i.e. everything that CAN be in a loading, empty or error state - checked for whether it imports the shared module. Nine such components exist. RESULT: EIGHT of nine use the shared states - dashboard/page.tsx (4 loading, 6 empty, 1 error), settings/page.tsx, authenticated-shell.tsx, job-search-view.tsx (2/3/5), preparation-panel.tsx, profile-editor.tsx, resume-panel.tsx (2/1/4) and saved-leads.tsx (4/4/6). THE NINTH IS app/page.tsx, AND IT IS OUT OF SCOPE BY THE CRITERION OWN WORDING: AC1 says "every SIGNED-IN route". app/page.tsx is the sign-in screen at /, outside the (app) route group, and is what an UNAUTHENTICATED visitor sees. Its two ad-hoc renders belong to the pre-authentication flow. This is a deliberate scope judgement, recorded rather than silently excluded - if the owner reads AC1 as covering the sign-in screen too, it is one further migration.

THE THREE SURFACES THE REVIEW NAMED AS UNPROVEN ARE NOW RESOLVED INDIVIDUALLY. resume-panel.tsx: MIGRATED, 2 LoadingState, 1 EmptyState, 4 ErrorState. settings route: MIGRATED (1 LoadingState). account-security.tsx: NOT async-bearing at all - it has no useQuery or useMutation, so the census correctly excluded it - and its three role= renders are INLINE FORM AND ACTION FEEDBACK rather than page-level states: a sessionError and a notice beside the Sign out other sessions button (L92-93), and a password-field error bound to the form via id="security-error" for aria-describedby (L135). DELIBERATELY NOT CONSOLIDATED, and this is the line drawn consistently through the whole rollout: a field-level validation message, an inline confirmation, or a spinner inside a button is not a page-level loading/empty/error state. Consolidating those would be churn and would risk restyling under the UI freeze for no gain. career-links-view.tsx is the same judgement from the other direction - it is entirely static, has no async, and its only failable dependency (the session) is handled one level up by AuthenticatedShell. AC1 IS THEREFORE MET FOR ITS ACTUAL SCOPE, and the claim is now backed by an enumeration anyone can re-run rather than by a count.

F-2 SECOND HALF CLOSED 2026-09-25 (re-review finding, P2, same severity as the original because it is the same finding): `variant` was optional on the BLOCK half, so <ErrorState message={err.message} /> resolved to block - the SHORTER of the two spellings - compiled cleanly, and rendered the default title "Something went wrong" over a bare transport message with no action. F-2 had closed the hole for inline and left it open on the DEFAULT path. Fix: `title` is now required and the default string is deleted, so naming what failed is unrepresentable to omit on BOTH halves. `onRetry` stays optional and the comment says why - a terminal error legitimately has nothing to retry and forcing a no-op handler would be worse.

F-2 SECOND HALF PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL, not assumed: a scripted mutation deleted the `title` prop from a real block call site (apps/web/src/components/authenticated-shell.tsx), ASSERTED THE MUTATION ACTUALLY APPLIED (5117 -> 5087 bytes, refusing to proceed on a no-op - the case-3 lesson), and typecheck then failed with apps/web/src/components/authenticated-shell.tsx(93,8): error TS2322: Type { message: string; onRetry: ... } is not assignable to type IntrinsicAttributes & ErrorStateProps. File restored byte-identical afterwards, verified by comparison not by assumption. Unmutated typecheck is clean, so no existing block call site omitted title.

EMPTY-STRING QUESTION RECORDED AS KNOWN AND ACCEPTED (P3, no action): what="" compiles and collapses to the bare detail. TypeScript cannot express non-empty without branded types, and deliberately typing an empty string is a different act from accidentally omitting a prop. Now written into the ui-states.tsx comment so it is a recorded decision rather than an unnoticed hole.

F-4 CENSUS PROXY FAILED AND WAS CORRECTED (P2): the census defined async-bearing as "imports useQuery/useMutation/useInfiniteQuery". account-security.tsx imports only useState but makes TWO real network calls via api() - revoke-others and password change - each with its own pending flag and a catch that renders an error. It is async-bearing in substance and manages async by hand. Corrected proxy is "makes a network call" (react-query hook OR api() helper OR fetch()).

THIRD MEASUREMENT ARTEFACT FOUND WHILE RE-RUNNING THE CENSUS: the proxy regex matched COMMENT TEXT as though it were code. account-security.tsx began matching the OLD proxy the moment a comment in it mentioned "useQuery/useMutation/useInfiniteQuery" - my own explanatory comment poisoned the measurement. The corrected census strips comments first and SELF-TESTS the stripper (it must remove a commented-out hook and must not destroy a real api() call) before trusting any count.

CORRECTED CENSUS RESULT, and the original 9/8/1 DOES NOT REPRODUCE. With comments stripped: old proxy = 7 real members (dashboard, authenticated-shell, job-search-view, preparation-panel, profile-editor, resume-panel, saved-leads), corrected proxy = 9. Two members of the original 9 show NO async evidence by any of four tests (useQuery-family, api(), fetch(), await/async): app/(app)/settings/page.tsx and app/page.tsx. The figure both parties reproduced "independently" was wrong in COMPOSITION, and both reproduced it because both used the same comment-blind method and the same definition. A reproduction that shares the originals definition tests arithmetic, not truth.

REVIEWER-FLAGGED settings/page.tsx RESOLVED: it was NOT READ by the reviewer and flagged as possibly importing ui-states while the component owning its error states does not. Checked with the corrected proxy - app/(app)/settings/page.tsx is NOT async-bearing by either proxy (no react-query hook, no api(), no fetch()). No gap there.

NEW GAP FOUND BY THE CORRECTED PROXY, previously identified by nobody: apps/web/src/components/account-form.tsx calls api(registering ? "/register" : "/login", ...) and does NOT import ui-states. JUDGEMENT: it is imported by exactly one file, app/page.tsx, which is the sign-in screen shown to an UNAUTHENTICATED visitor and sits outside the (app) group. AC1 says "every SIGNED-IN route", so account-form.tsx is out of scope by the same judgement the owner already endorsed for app/page.tsx. Consequence stated so it is a decision rather than an omission: if AC1 is read as covering the sign-in screen, it is now TWO further migrations, not one.

account-security.tsx TWO CATCH BRANCHES MIGRATED, validation branches deliberately untouched. The single `error` state carried both client validation ("Passwords do not match.", "Choose a different password.") and the API catch, rendering into the one element aria-describedby points at, so it became { what?: string; detail: string } - validation sets detail alone, the catch sets both. sessionError routes through what="Could not sign out other sessions." and the password catch through what="Could not change your password.". Fallback strings changed from "Session revocation failed."/"Password change failed." to "Please try again." because `what` now carries the operation name and the old text would have been redundant.

ui-states.tsx GAINED AN `id` PASSTHROUGH on the inline variant, required rather than cosmetic: check-ui.ts:1246 asserts every password input has aria-describedby="security-error", so without `id` the call site would have had to choose between the contract and the accessible association - which would push exactly the form errors this contract exists for back out to a bare

.

BOTH check-ui ASSERTIONS STRENGTHENED, and they were F-1s defect a second time: :1144 and :1235 BOTH filtered on the substring "Request failed. Please try again.", so both passed identically before and after the operation name was added - invisible substring assertions that could not observe the change they existed to protect. Each now waits on the filter and then asserts the WHOLE innerText: "Could not sign out other sessions. Request failed. Please try again." and "Could not change your password. Request failed. Please try again.".

VERIFICATION 2026-09-25: typecheck clean on both apps/web and the scripts project; npm run lint green (note: invoking eslint directly on these files errors with a pre-existing eslint-plugin-react/ESLint 10 incompatibility - the workspace script is the one that works). npm run test:ui: CHROMIUM PASSED ITS ENTIRE PHASE, and the pass message is emitted at check-ui.ts:2411 which is AFTER both strengthened assertions (:1144, :1235) and after the CS-13 block (:2301) - so chromium executed and passed the new exact-match assertions. The run then FAILED ON FIREFOX at :2301 with "cs-13 error state 768 never stopped issuing requests", a quiet() network-idle timeout in a different block. NOT CLAIMED AS PRE-EXISTING WITHOUT EVIDENCE - re-run performed to test determinism; result recorded separately.

RE-RUN RESULT 2026-09-25: the second npm run test:ui passed ALL THREE ENGINES with exit code 0 - chromium, firefox and webkit each reporting "search/export/cancellation, saved leads/notes/archive/conflicts, profile, logout, 320/390/1440px passed", zero Error/AssertionError lines in the log. The firefox failure in run 1 ("cs-13 error state 768 never stopped issuing requests", a quiet() network-idle timeout at check-ui.ts:2301) was therefore INTERMITTENT and not caused by this change, which adds no network requests. Recorded as evidence rather than asserted: run 1 log cs13-rereview-ui.log, run 2 log cs13-rereview-ui2.log.

HONEST WEIGHT OF THAT EVIDENCE: a pass obtained on the second attempt is weaker than a deterministic pass. Both strengthened exact-match assertions (:1144 and :1235) executed and passed on all three engines, which is what this change needed to prove. But the suite as a whole is now demonstrated to be flaky on firefox at 768px, so a single green run of check-ui.ts must not be treated as a stable gate. Belongs to CS-58s intermittent class, recorded there too.

SCOPE BOUNDARY RESTATED AS THE SIGN-IN SURFACE AS A UNIT, not as one file. The AC1 exclusion is NOT "we excluded app/page.tsx" - stated that way, a later reader finding account-form.tsx would reasonably think it had been missed. It is: the sign-in surface is out of scope as a unit - the route (app/page.tsx) AND the form it renders (account-form.tsx, imported by that route and nothing else). Two files, one coherent reason: AC1 says "every SIGNED-IN route" and both render for an unauthenticated visitor outside the (app) group.

WIDEST-PROXY CONFIRMATION: re-ran with the proxy widened again to include "imports from lib/api" alongside the react-query hooks, api() and fetch(). Result is still 9 under .tsx with comments stripped, with ZERO import-only files - no component imports the api helper without calling it. The single gap is account-form.tsx, which is out of scope per the boundary above. AC1 therefore holds under the STRICTEST proxy tried, not merely under the loose one.

COUNT RECONCILED 9 vs 11, and it was a GLOB DIFFERENCE not a substantive one: scanning .tsx alone gives 9; scanning .tsx plus .ts gives 12, the three extras being lib/api.ts, lib/api.test.ts and lib/session.ts - the fetch wrapper, its test and a helper. None render UI states, so all three are correctly outside a COMPONENT census. Also verified that app/(app)/settings/page.tsx and app/page.tsx match NOTHING under any of the four patterns even with comments left in, so neither can account for a higher count.

REFINEMENT OF MY OWN EARLIER CLAIM, corrected rather than left standing: I reported that the comment artefact changed the corrected-census total. It did not. Under .tsx the corrected proxy gives 9 BOTH raw and stripped, because account-security.tsx matches via its real api() call regardless. The artefact changed the OLD-proxy count (8 raw vs 7 stripped) and the attribution of account-security, not the corrected total. The conclusion was right; that part of my reasoning for it was not.

RUNTIME CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-25 TO EVERY RESULT RECORDED TODAY: all local verification in this run was executed on Node v22.23.2, while package.json requires >=24.0.0, .nvmrc says 24 and CI uses 24. This does not invalidate the passes, but it RECLASSIFIES them - each was obtained on a runtime the project does not support, and any could differ on Node 24. Applies to typecheck, lint, test:unit, deploy:gate:test, eol:check and the three-engine test:ui runs alike.

PROVISIONAL MARKING WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25, SAME DAY IT WAS APPLIED, BECAUSE IT WAS TOO BROAD AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENT. The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". THE GATE COULD FAIL; ONLY ITS FIRST LINK COULD NOT. `npm run typecheck` chains four commands and the last, check-test-types.mjs, filters on /^\S+\.ts\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - WHICH MATCHES A PRODUCTION FILE AS READILY AS A TEST FILE - and exits 1. Anyone running the npm script WOULD have been told.

THIS TICKET DOES NOT CITE A BARE `tsc -b`, so its typecheck evidence was never in the unfalsifiable form and stands unqualified. The narrowed set is 4 of the original 29: CS-53, CS-62, CS-76, CS-77 - ALL FOUR WRITTEN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, which is the correct place for the correction to land.

BLOCKER FROM THIS TICKET OWN EVIDENCE NOW CLOSED (2026-09-24). The previously disclosed defect - "the full check-ui.ts suite currently fails end-to-end on an assertion expecting keyboard-focusable items inside nav[aria-label=Career workspace]" - was independently reproduced first, not assumed: npm run test:ui failed deterministically at check-ui.ts:327 with actual [] vs expected [Dashboard, Discovery, Leads, Preparation, Career Links]. Root cause confirmed by repository-wide grep: that aria-label exists nowhere in v2/apps/web/src, having been removed by the CS-6 routing migration. Because the suite aborted there, roughly 700 lines of downstream assertions had not executed since CS-6 and had silently rotted. This materially weakened AC4 - a baseline-enforcing check that cannot run enforces nothing.

FIXED IN THE TEST, NOT THE APPLICATION, per the engineering contract. No obsolete DOM was recreated and no assertion was deleted, skipped or weakened. The stale block was replaced with a navigation check asserting the real current shell: the nav[aria-label=CareerScope] landmark exists; all 8 enabled nav items labels AND hrefs match navItems in DOM order; the 3 href:null items (Skills, Insights, AI Assistant) render as inert spans and are never keyboard focusable; Tab reachability in DOM order; aria-current=page correctness on two different routes so a hardcoded dashboard fallback cannot pass; and mobile behaviour at the real 768/769px breakpoint read from dashboard-shell.module.css including desktop/mobile destination parity. A further 15 stale downstream steps were found and RETARGETED to real routes, never removed.

PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL, which is the whole point of AC4. Valid input passes. Invalid input fails: a wrong href fails with a deepEqual diff; a Soon item made focusable fails with the extra labels listed. MALFORMED input fails LOUDLY: removing aria-label=CareerScope produces "authenticated shell has no accessible CareerScope navigation landmark, 0 !== 1" at the first gate rather than silently collecting an empty array and passing - the exact rot mode that caused this defect is now structurally impossible. All falsification mutations were reverted and the application source verified clean by SHA-256 and by an independent read.

INDEPENDENTLY REVIEWED (real CareerScope Independent Reviewer dispatch, read-only, no edit tool). Verdict APPROVED WITH FINDINGS. It independently confirmed by direct read: no leftover falsification mutation; every new deepEqual compares a DOM-derived array against a hardcoded literal so an empty/renamed/reordered nav fails loudly; the 768px assertions match the real CSS; the test-only DELETE FROM sessions is provably confined to the per-run test_<uuid> database and cannot reach real data; and the assert.deepEqual(errors, []) page-error gate was NOT loosened. It could not verify the strict-superset claim (no shell/diff access) and said so plainly rather than implying agreement.

ORCHESTRATOR RAN THE REVIEWER REQUIRED EXPERIMENT 1 (the highest-downside unverified claim): git diff -U0 shows exactly ONE complete assertion deleted across 411 insertions / 61 deletions - the old lead-details Remote OK href check - and its replacement is STRICTLY STRONGER, adding assert.ok(postingHrefs.length > 0) so an empty collection now fails where before a missing link would have been invisible. NO COVERAGE REGRESSION. Reviewer findings F-1 and F-2 were then fixed in a second implementation round (2 of 3).

REVIEWER FINDING F-1 FIXED, and it was a real weakening: the WebKit Tab walk had been skipped entirely, justified by a comment claiming the DOM-focus assertions covered it. That claim is false for anchors - an <a tabindex="-1"> passes element.focus() but is NOT in the Tab sequence. Required Experiment 5 was executed rather than guessed: the walk was temporarily un-gated on WebKit and printed reachable=[] , confirming the platform premise holds. The walk now runs on ALL THREE engines and WebKit emptiness is ASSERTED, so a future Playwright/WebKit change that starts tabbing to links fails the build instead of silently expanding a permanent carve-out. Proven able to fail both ways with real output. F-2 (an assertion that passed against a missing Search history nav - the same rot shape) now asserts the nav exists before asserting it is empty. F-3 and F-4 also fixed.

REMAINING HONEST GAP, unchanged and NOT closed by this work: axe-core covers a large but not exhaustive subset of WCAG 2.2 AA, and no manual screen-reader validation (NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver) was performed. docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md "Screen reader not validated" stays OPEN - HUMAN VALIDATION. Do not read a green check-ui run as a full WCAG 2.2 AA audit.

CORRECTION OF A FALSE CLAIM IN THIS TICKET OWN EVIDENCE (forensic audit F-4, 2026-09-24). An earlier evidence line described v2/scripts/check-ui.ts as "the CI-run, axe-core-backed accessibility test, wired into .github/workflows/ci.yml". THAT WAS FALSE against current bytes and is retracted here rather than left standing. Verified by the Orchestrator: grep over .github/workflows/*.yml for check-ui|test:ui returns exactly ONE hit, ci.yml line 132 "node --import tsx scripts/check-ui.mjs", which is the V1 ROOT file - a different, older suite that still exists. NOW WIRED (2026-09-24): ci.yml v2-integration job gained three steps - install the lockfile-pinned Playwright 1.63.0 browsers with system deps (verified the CLI and the library resolve to the same root install, so they cannot drift, and the version is printed so a future mismatch is visible); build V2 for the browser suite; then start the production web server on 5280 and run npm --prefix v2 run test:ui across all three engines. The readiness wait POLLS the server (60 x 2s), breaks early if the server pid dies, and on timeout emits ::error:: and exits 1 - it never proceeds against a dead server. Job timeout raised 20 -> 40 minutes. No engine was dropped to save time.

VERIFICATION LEVEL, stated precisely per the project own standard: this is WIRED and LOCALLY VERIFIED, NOT CI-EXECUTED. The workflow YAML was validated by two real parsers (python yaml.safe_load, and actionlint 1.7.7 exit 0 with no findings on ci.yml and deploy.yml). npm run test:ui was run locally by the Orchestrator and exits 0 on chromium, firefox and webkit. It verified the CI wiring hard and it HOLDS: the readiness poll emitting ::error:: and exit 1 rather than proceeding against a dead server; test:ui resolving to check-ui.ts; the nav[aria-label="CareerScope"] gate failing on a removed landmark rather than silently collecting []; the WebKit deepEqual(reachable, []) carve-out; and accessible() injecting real axe-core such that a FAILED INJECTION THROWS rather than returning an empty violation list. F-1 FIXED 2026-09-25, and it was a real mismatch I had not caught: AC1 says WCAG 2.2 AA, but check-ui.ts ran runOnly tags [wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa] - WCAG 2.1. The check enforcing the accessibility baseline was ONE WCAG VERSION BEHIND the criterion it exists to enforce, and axe-core 4.12.1 (confirmed in v2/package.json) ships the 2.2 rules; they were simply never requested. Added wcag22a and wcag22aa. RESULT, and it is a genuinely good one: ZERO new violations across all audited routes on all three engines. The application already satisfies WCAG 2.2 AA under axe, including the new target-size (2.5.8) and focus-not-obscured (2.4.11) rules. No re-baselining was needed and no rule was suppressed to achieve it. AC1 is now enforced at the version it actually names. HONEST NOTE ON THE RUN: the first run with 2.2 enabled went red on WebKit - but NOT on an accessibility violation. It was a click-stability timeout at check-ui.ts:951 waiting for "Back to Search", the locator having resolved but the element not settling. The immediately following run was green on all three engines. That is the suite known WebKit interaction flake, not a 2.2 finding, and one green run after one red is not proof of stability - recorded rather than smoothed.

REVIEWER D - CONSUMER CHAIN: shell -> check-ui.ts -> test:ui -> ci.yml, plus five per-route axe passes. WIRED. But the PAGES HALF OF THIS TICKET TERMINATES AT NOTHING - the static Pages surface has no executing consumer, the same gap that rejected CS-32.

AUDITED 2026-09-25 as a nearest-neighbour of the three demoted tickets, AND IT HOLDS AT UAT. IT LOOKED LIKE A FAILURE AND WAS NOT - recorded because nearly demoting it is the useful part. VERIFIED AT SOURCE INSTEAD OF DEMOTING ON A STALE FIELD, and all four criteria are in fact DELIVERED by v2/apps/web/src/components/match-evidence.tsx - which cites CS-18 in its own comment. AC1: Object.entries(match.dimensions) renders EVERY dimension with its score and reason, including the poor ones, so "including the ones that scored badly" is structural rather than promised. AC2: match.excludedReason is rendered with role="alert" - the exclusion names its rule. AC3: confidence === "low" renders "Limited description - score capped, treat as low-confidence". AC4: the component maps over the matching output and DUPLICATES NO WEIGHTS - it renders dimension.score and dimension.reason straight from the payload.

SO THIS IS A RECORD DEFECT, NOT A DELIVERY FAILURE, and the opposite conclusion to the three demotions. The gap is that the evidence field was never written after the work landed. A mechanical "does any AC have a recorded UNMET status" check would NOT have flagged this - nothing is recorded as unmet. A "does every AC have recorded evidence" check WOULD have flagged it, and would have been right about the bookkeeping and wrong about the code. Both checks are worth having, and they must be reported differently: one blocks promotion, the other demands a write-up.

A NOTE ON METHOD, against myself: demoting CS-18 on the strength of its evidence field would have looked rigorous, produced a defensible-sounding write-up, and been WRONG. The difference was reading the component rather than the record. Evidence about evidence is still not evidence about the code.

completedSteps: Added infra/v3/monitor.sh: a host-native monitor (not a container), run standalone so it keeps working even if the whole stack - API, workers, Postgres - is down. Classifies, worst first: unreachable (public /api/health cannot be reached at all) > unhealthy (responds, but not 200 + status ok, or the backlog signal below cannot itself be read) > stopped (healthy, but a search/files/publisher worker container is not running, per `docker inspect`) > stale (workers running, but durable work is not draining - the same expiredLeases/oldestUnpublishedSeconds/oldestRunningSeconds signal the publisher already computes for its own log, read directly via `docker exec ... psql` against the exact same query as Database.backlog(), so nothing new is exposed over the network) > ok.

Alerting is edge-triggered (fires on a status transition, including a one-time 'recovered' notice) plus a bounded re-notify window while a failure continues, so an outage is never silent for good but a flapping check does not spam the channel every 5 minutes either. Sends to an operator-configured webhook (MONITOR_WEBHOOK_URL) with one payload carrying both `text` (Slack) and `content` (Discord) keys so either works without asking which is configured; a non-https webhook URL is refused rather than sent over in cleartext.

Added careerscope-monitor.service/.timer (systemd, 5-minute interval - 3 chances inside the 15-minute AC1 window even if one run is skipped) and setup-monitoring.sh (idempotent installer: unit files, /usr/local/bin/careerscope-monitor.sh, root-only 0600 /etc/careerscope-monitor.env, 0700 state dir). Wired into CI (ci.yml verify job) since, unlike the other infra/v3 check-*.sh scripts, this one needs no live host to run.

Added docs/OPERATIONS/MONITORING.md (design, install, alerting behavior, verification) and a one-time manual-install step in docs/OPERATIONS/DEPLOYMENT.md (installing a systemd timer is host state, not something apply-migrations.sh should do). completedSteps: Added infra/v3/backup.sh: a daily host-native backup (same pattern as CS-24's monitor.sh - runs on the host, not in a container). Every run: (1) pg_dump via docker exec, custom format, captured to a staging file on the host; (2) restores that exact dump into a disposable scratch database inside the same container and runs a real sanity query (table count), then drops the scratch DB - this is what makes the restore exercised, not documented (AC2), since every scheduled run proves its own dump is actually restorable, not just that pg_dump exited zero; (3) only if both succeed, atomically renames the verified dump into place (root-only 0600) and applies retention (default 14 days).
