items.title: V2 skip-link accessibility regression
items.userProblem: The saved V2 browser run failed the hidden skip-link contract; keyboard access needs a focused investigation.
items.source: ChatGPT TICKET-PLAN-20260920 proposal; owner approved backlog addition; current reproduction pending
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce the saved v2/scripts/check-ui.ts hiddenSkip failure on current bytes and identify the implementation or harness cause without weakening the intended contract
Verify the unfocused hidden state, visible keyboard-focus state and activation moving focus to main content
Run the focused check in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit at the affected viewport and a narrow mobile viewport; report unavailable engines rather than implying a pass
evidence: Root cause confirmed by direct source inspection, not the (currently broken, pre-CS-6-routing) v2/scripts/check-ui.ts harness: only one skip-link exists in the whole app, in v2/apps/web/src/app/page.tsx (the unauthenticated sign-in screen). AuthenticatedShell - the single component every one of the 9 real authenticated routes renders through - had zero skip-link, so a keyboard user on /dashboard, /jobs, /saved, /applications, /resume, /settings, /career-resources or /preparation had no way to reach page content without first tabbing through the entire sidebar nav. This is the real regression CS-31 describes; it predates and is independent of the broken test harness.

Fixed: added a skip-link as the first element inside AuthenticatedShell (v2/apps/web/src/components/authenticated-shell.tsx), targeting a new id="main-content" tabIndex={-1} on the shared <main>, styled via a new .skipLink class in dashboard-shell.module.css using this session's --dash-* tokens (visually hidden 1x1px until focused, matching the existing pattern in globals.css's .skip-link used by the sign-in page) rather than a competing visual language.

Verified live in real Chromium (Chrome DevTools MCP against the actual running dev server, not a mock): unfocused boundingBox is 1x1px (hidden); .focus() makes it 133.7x40.8px with a visible focus outline; pressing Enter moves document.activeElement to the real <main id="main-content">. Lighthouse accessibility/best-practices/SEO/agentic-browsing all 100/100 on /saved after the change, no regression. Confirmed both light and dark theme token pairs (#ffffff/#101323 and #141a2e/#e7eaf5) are each high-contrast for the skip-link text.

Firefox/WebKit NOT verified this pass. Genuine attempt made using this repository's own established pattern (a real mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-noble Linux container, matching CI, per the CS-2/CS-9 precedent in review.txt) across chromium/firefox/webkit at 1280px and 320px. All three engines failed identically at the same step: the sign-in form's session check (GET /api/session, proxied through next.config.ts's rewrite to http://127.0.0.1:5390) never resolves when the request originates from a browser running inside the container (reaching the dev server via host.docker.internal), leaving the page stuck on "Loading workspace" past a 30s timeout. Confirmed this reproduces even in chromium inside the container (so it is a container-networking/dev-proxy interaction, not a per-engine defect) by explicitly listening for the /api/session response and seeing it never fire. This is an honest, reported limitation per this ticket's own acceptance-criteria instruction ("report unavailable engines rather than implying a pass"), not a silently-skipped criterion.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2026-09-25 (real CareerScope Independent Reviewer dispatch, read-only by capability - no edit tool, and it disclosed up front that it had no shell and therefore no git, marking everything requiring execution as UNCONFIRMED rather than implying agreement). Verdict transcribed verbatim by the Orchestrator. VERDICT: REVISE - NOT ready for UAT. Reviewer summary: "The skip link is real and correct, but the cross-engine assertions cited as satisfying criterion 3 test the sign-in page pre-existing #workspace-content link; removing tabIndex={-1} from the shell #main-content would leave the whole suite green." BLOCKING, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THE ENTIRE BATCH - CS31-1 IS A CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL. The implementation is correct. But the cross-engine assertions relied upon to satisfy criterion 3 exercise the SIGN-IN page pre-existing #workspace-content skip link, NOT the AuthenticatedShell #main-content link this ticket added. The reviewer states the consequence precisely: removing tabIndex={-1} from the shell #main-content would leave the whole suite GREEN. So the repaired browser suite does NOT satisfy criterion 3, and the assumption that it did - which I held when dispatching the review - was wrong. This is the same defect class as R3 (--allow-net), CS28-1 (invisible test file) and the Career workspace selector rot: a check pointed at the wrong thing, reporting success. Add an assertion against the authenticated shell own skip link, prove it fails when tabIndex={-1} is removed, then re-review.

CS31-1 FIXED AND PROVEN, 2026-09-25 (Orchestrator). The reviewer was exactly right and I had been wrong to assume the repaired suite satisfied criterion 3. Confirmed against current bytes: the skip-link contract block at check-ui.ts:345-362 runs after page.goto(origin) - the SIGN-IN page, whose link targets #workspace-content - and the only reference to the shell link was a bare .focus() used as a Tab-walk anchor, which asserts nothing. FIX: added the identical three-part contract against AuthenticatedShell own a[href="#main-content"] on an authenticated route - visually hidden (1x1) when unfocused, visible and substantial (>40x40, on-screen) when focused, and Enter moving real focus to #main-content. PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL using the reviewer own demonstration, which is the point: removing tabIndex={-1} from <main id="main-content"> in authenticated-shell.tsx - the exact mutation it said "would leave the whole suite green" - now produces "chromium authenticated shell skip link did not move focus to #main-content (a missing tabindex='-1' would do exactly this)", exit 1. Mutation reverted; full suite then green on chromium, firefox and webkit, exit 0. AC3 STATUS: the cross-engine requirement is now genuinely exercised on all three engines for the link this ticket actually added. The previously recorded Firefox/WebKit gap is closed by execution rather than by argument. Re-review required before UAT - I do not promote on my own authority.

RE-REVIEW 2026-09-25, SPLIT VERDICT: the fix PASSES, the ticket did NOT. The reviewer attacked the CS31-1 fix four ways and could not make it vacuous - no collection to be empty (every assertion is on a single scalar); a missing element fails in BOTH directions (boundingBox() auto-waits and times out loudly if nothing matches; returns null if present-but-display:none, failing assert.ok); removing tabIndex={-1} still fails, and it derived that from source rather than trusting my run - an in-page anchor moves focus only if the target is focusable, a <main> without tabIndex is not, so activeElement stays on the link. Its words: the reported output is a STRUCTURALLY NECESSARY CONSEQUENCE of the source, not merely consistent with it. It also checked strict mode unprompted (a second matching anchor throws rather than silently taking the first) and verified POSITIVELY that nothing was weakened - the original sign-in contract at 345-362 is intact. DEFECT CLASS: CLOSED, not relocated.

F-1 FIXED AND PROVEN 2026-09-25, and it is the finding that actually mattered. AC3 requires the check run "at the affected viewport AND A NARROW MOBILE VIEWPORT". My shell contract ran only after setViewportSize(1440x900) and was never re-run narrow; the nearby [320, 390, 1440] loops assert overflow and axe, NOT the skip link. Not pedantry: .skipLink is hidden-until-focused by positioning and the focused-state assertion is a SIZE assertion (>40x40) - exactly the property a narrow media query is most likely to change. The contract was unverified at the one width where it is most likely to break, and the AC anticipated that. FIXED: the contract now runs in a for-loop over [1440, 320] with the viewport set at the top and 1440 restored after. PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL AT THE NARROW WIDTH SPECIFICALLY, which is the whole point - a generic falsification would not have demonstrated the new coverage. Temporarily added a @media (max-width: 400px) rule shrinking .skipLink:focus to 20x20. Result: PASSED at 1440 and FAILED at 320 with "chromium authenticated shell skip link does not become visible on focus at 320px", exit 1. A defect that exists only at the narrow viewport is now caught, and the message names the width. Mutation reverted (TEMP-FALSIFY markers confirmed absent), suite green on chromium, firefox and webkit, exit 0. F-2 ALSO FIXED in the same edit: the contract now selects by accessible name via getByRole(link, {name: Skip to content, exact: true}) rather than by href attribute alone. An empty would have satisfied every part of the old contract while being a real WCAG 2.4.4 / 4.1.2 defect.

F-4 RECORDED AS A DELIBERATE DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT: the 1x1 hidden-state assertion is over-strict - a future switch to display:none or clip-path-only hiding would fail it even though that is also correct hiding. It is over-strict in the SAFE direction and is being LEFT AS IS ON PURPOSE. The reviewer recorded it specifically so that nobody later "fixes" it by loosening the assertion, which would reopen CS31-1 by the back door. If the hiding technique genuinely changes, update the assertion to match the new technique - do not relax it to accept both. F-3 REASSIGNED TO CS-15, where it belongs: check-ui.ts comments that "the skip link is the first focusable node in the shell, so focusing it makes the walk deterministic", and the Tab walk RELIES on that premise while never asserting it, because it focuses the link directly instead of tabbing to it from document start. If the skip link stopped being the first Tab stop it would fail its entire WCAG 2.4.1 purpose and the suite would stay green. Rated P3 because ordering is not in CS-31 AC2 and it is hard to assert cross-engine (WebKit omits links from the Tab sequence), but recorded because "a premise stated in a comment and relied on without assertion" is this project house failure mode.

CONSUMER-CHAIN DISCLOSURE, per the amended standing rule this ticket caused: the deliverable is authenticated-shell.tsx; its consumer is v2/scripts/check-ui.ts (cited above by line); the consumer own consumer is the test:ui script, consumed by .github/workflows/ci.yml. THAT SECOND HOP IS NOT YET PROVEN: test:ui ran in NO workflow until CS-15 wired it on 2026-09-24, and it is still WIRED, NOT CI-EXECUTED - no pipeline run has executed it. CS-31 therefore inherits CS-15 unproven enforcement status, and this ticket must not be read as CI-enforced until that changes.

REVIEWER D VERDICT 2026-09-25: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS. Recorded by the orchestrator and attributed to the independent review. Status held at QA pending CI execution - NOT promoted, because nothing has been CI-executed today and the SHA has not moved.

REVIEWER D - AC2 SATISFIED AND VERIFIED AT SOURCE: the shell renders the skip link as the FIRST CHILD of .shell with <main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1}>; .skipLink is 1px/1px/clip-path:inset(50%) while unfocused and width:auto/height:auto/clip-path:none/outline on focus; and the contract asserts ALL THREE of those, so it cannot pass against a link that is present but unreachable or visible but unstyled.
REVIEWER D - AC3 SATISFIED: the `for (const width of [1440, 320])` loop sits INSIDE the three-engine loop, giving 3 x 2 real coverage rather than a single width asserted once and assumed elsewhere.

REVIEWER D - AC1 PARTIALLY SATISFIED, and the evidence already says so honestly: the cause was found by SOURCE INSPECTION and the literal reproduction never happened. Recorded as partial rather than argued up to met.

REVIEWER D - THE PRE-EXISTING SIGN-IN CONTRACT WAS VERIFIED UNWEAKENED. That check matters more than it looks: the commonest way an accessibility fix passes is by relaxing the contract that guarded the surface it touched.

RUNTIME CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-25 TO EVERY RESULT RECORDED TODAY: all local verification in this run was executed on Node v22.23.2, while package.json requires >=24.0.0, .nvmrc says 24 and CI uses 24. This does not invalidate the passes, but it RECLASSIFIES them - each was obtained on a runtime the project does not support, and any could differ on Node 24. Applies to typecheck, lint, test:unit, deploy:gate:test, eol:check and the three-engine test:ui runs alike.

DISCLOSURE HOISTED 2026-09-25, FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE SAME RECORD DEFECT. The AC1 partial was recorded honestly in evidence - "the cause was found by SOURCE INSPECTION and the literal reproduction never happened" - while currentStep named AC3, F-1, F-2 and CS31-1 AND NEVER MENTIONED AC1 AT ALL. So the field a promoting reader consults read as "the only issue was AC3, now fixed, awaiting CI" while a criterion sat partial one field away.

THIS IS THE CLEANEST EXAMPLE OF THE FOUR - CS-50 summary, CS-54 evidence, CS-62 evidence, now CS-31 - PRECISELY BECAUSE NOBODY HID ANYTHING. The disclosure is honest, specific and self-critical; it is simply in the wrong field. THE DEFECT IS THE SHAPE OF THE RECORD, NOT THE HONESTY OF THE WRITER, which is why it keeps recurring among careful people and why a hoist rule beats an exhortation to be candid.

PRIOR currentStep PRESERVED VERBATIM RATHER THAN OVERWRITTEN, per the CS-38 pattern: "QA - re-review returned a SPLIT verdict: the CS31-1 fix PASSES, the ticket did not, because AC3 narrow-viewport coverage was literally unmet. F-1 and F-2 are now fixed and falsification-proven at 320px specifically. Awaiting promotion on the next green CI run; the re-reviewer stated it will not re-litigate CS31-1." An overwrite would destroy the re-reviewer split verdict, which is the record of a real disagreement and is not mine to delete.

PROVISIONAL MARKING WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25, SAME DAY IT WAS APPLIED, BECAUSE IT WAS TOO BROAD AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENT. The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". THE GATE COULD FAIL; ONLY ITS FIRST LINK COULD NOT. `npm run typecheck` chains four commands and the last, check-test-types.mjs, filters on /^\S+\.ts\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - WHICH MATCHES A PRODUCTION FILE AS READILY AS A TEST FILE - and exits 1. Anyone running the npm script WOULD have been told.

THIS TICKET DOES NOT CITE A BARE `tsc -b`, so its typecheck evidence was never in the unfalsifiable form and stands unqualified. The narrowed set is 4 of the original 29: CS-53, CS-62, CS-76, CS-77 - ALL FOUR WRITTEN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, which is the correct place for the correction to land.

SECOND INDEPENDENT VERDICT 2026-09-26: APPROVED, NO NEW FINDINGS - and the structural claim was re-verified here rather than taken from either record. AC3 depends on the [1440, 320] width loop being INSIDE the three-engine loop, so 3 x 2 = 6 real runs rather than one width asserted and the rest assumed.

PROVED BY BRACE BALANCE, NOT BY INDENTATION OR ORDERING: the engine loop at check-ui.ts:316 spans to :2446, and the width loop at :596 opens inside that span. Indentation and line order are suggestive and can both be wrong in a file being edited; containment is the property the claim actually needs. A control line past the loop end was checked to report OUTSIDE, so the containment test can distinguish the two cases.

AC2 VERIFIED IN THE ASSERTIONS THEMSELVES at :594-612: hidden state pinned TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS (boundingBox 1x1 AND clipPath inset(50%)), focused state asserted as genuinely substantial (width > 40 && height > 40, y >= 0) rather than merely present, and activation asserted as REAL FOCUS MOVEMENT (main === document.activeElement) rather than a hash change. Each assertion names engine and viewport in its failure message.

THE ORIGINAL GAP WAS FOUND BY MUTATION AND THE DEMONSTRATION IS EXACT: the skip-link contract ran on / - the SIGN-IN page, targeting #workspace-content - and NEVER TOUCHED THE LINK CS-31 ACTUALLY ADDED, AuthenticatedShell #main-content. REMOVING tabIndex={-1} FROM THE SHELL WOULD HAVE LEFT THE ENTIRE SUITE GREEN. Its comment names the class correctly: "A check pointed at the wrong element is the same defect class as this suite own Career workspace rot."

F-4 DESERVES SPECIFIC CREDIT AND IS THE FIRST OF ITS KIND TONIGHT: the 1x1 hidden assertion is deliberately OVER-STRICT - a future switch to display:none would fail it although that is also correct hiding - AND IT WAS LEFT AS-IS WITH THE REASON RECORDED SO NOBODY LATER "FIXES" IT BY LOOSENING IT, WHICH WOULD REOPEN CS31-1 BY THE BACK DOOR. THAT IS SOMEBODY PROTECTING A CHECK FROM A FUTURE WELL-INTENTIONED REPAIR, which is a different and rarer act than writing a correct check.

QA CLOSED 2026-09-28: hosted run 36398473010 attempt 2 completed green on the exact revision containing the CS-31 fixes. The run covered Chromium, Firefox and WebKit at the configured 1440px and 320px viewports; the skip-link hidden-state, visible-focus and main-content activation assertions all passed. The prior CI gate was therefore discharged without weakening the contract, and this ticket is ready for UAT.

items.title: Pages 320px visual regression triage
items.userProblem: The saved chromium-search-light-320 visual comparison failed without an accepted explanation.
items.source: ChatGPT TICKET-PLAN-20260920 proposal; owner approved backlog addition; current reproduction pending
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce and inspect expected, actual and difference images for chromium-search-light-320 using the documented rendering environment
Name the cause and correct implementation or explicitly review an intentional baseline change; never approve a snapshot merely to turn the check green
Rerun Pages visual checks and focused three-engine mobile workspace checks without changing snapshot allowlists or publication boundaries
evidence: Reproduced the check (scripts/check-pages-ui.mjs, a local-only dev check - confirmed not referenced anywhere in .github/workflows/ci.yml) directly, twice, before any fix. Each run failed on a DIFFERENT randomly-chosen snapshot across different engines (firefox-applications-light-320, then chromium-admin-empty-mobile) - never chromium-search-light-320 itself, but the same failure class. Quantified both with a real pixelmatch diff at threshold 0.1: both showed 0 mismatched pixels out of 270080/329160 - the images were perceptually identical despite failing Buffer.equals(). Root cause: the check used raw byte-for-byte PNG comparison (image.equals()), and Playwright screenshot PNG encoding is not byte-stable across runs even for pixel-identical renders. This is the real, generalizable explanation for the original chromium-search-light-320 report too - a random snapshot fails on any given run.

Fixed: capture() in check-pages-ui.mjs now does a fast-path exact-byte check (free, for the common case) and, only on a byte mismatch, falls back to a real perceptual comparison via pixelmatch/pngjs (same libraries already used correctly by v2/scripts/visual-regression.ts) with mismatchedPixels required to be exactly 0 - not loosened to "close enough", so a genuine regression of even a handful of pixels still fails loudly, and a diff PNG is written for inspection on any real failure. Verified: 3 consecutive full clean runs across chromium+firefox+webkit with zero spurious failures (previously: 2 different runs, 2 different spurious failures).

Added playwright, pixelmatch and pngjs as real, declared root devDependencies (package.json + package-lock.json) - they were already present in node_modules/package-lock.json (pre-installed ad hoc, presumably for this exact script) but never declared, so a genuinely fresh `npm install` on a clean checkout would have silently been unable to run this check at all. Fixed as a directly-related reproducibility gap, not scope creep.

Separately discovered, while making the fix reproducible, a second real and distinct issue: WebKit does not include the skip-link <a> in its Tab order by default (a well-documented, external, upstream WebKit/Playwright constraint - github.com/microsoft/playwright#2114 and #5609 - Safari only tabs to links when the OS/browser "Full Keyboard Access: All controls" setting is on; the existing code's Alt+Tab workaround is the documented mitigation but is not 100% reliable in this pinned WebKit build). This is not a CareerScope markup defect - the skip-link is a plain, correctly-focusable <a href>, and Chromium/Firefox both reach it via a single Tab every time. Handled with the exact same pattern the script already uses for a different WebKit-only quirk two lines below (recorded as a `limitations` entry, not silently ignored and not weakened for Chromium/Firefox, which still require it strictly).

This WebKit keyboard quirk explains a third finding: ALL 88 WebKit local baseline snapshots were dated 2026-09-17, while Chromium's and Firefox's were a mix of 2026-09-17 (64 files, genuinely unaffected by the change below) and 2026-09-19 (24 files, correctly refreshed). Traced to a real, already-committed, intentional design change: commit a751049 ('fix(v1): Windows portability, provider fixes and the new logo', 2026-09-18) replaced mobile-site/favicon.svg with a new logo mark. Chromium/Firefox baselines were refreshed after that commit; WebKit's were not - almost certainly because the historical baseline-refresh run crashed on WebKit's own keyboard-order assertion (the same bug just fixed above) before it could capture WebKit's snapshots, per engines running in chromium/firefox/webkit order.

Verified this explanation exhaustively before updating anything, per this ticket's explicit instruction never to approve a snapshot merely to turn the check green: surveyed all 64 of WebKit's real (non-zero) mismatches in one pass (a temporary, since-reverted diagnostic mode that logs instead of throwing) and visually inspected multiple representative diff images across different pages/themes/widths (webkit-public-light-320, webkit-applications-dark-1440) - every one showed the identical signature (the new logo mark plus a uniform few-pixel vertical cascade through the rest of the page, consistent with one header-row height change propagating down a single-column layout), not a mix of unrelated defects. The other 24 WebKit snapshots (matching the 24 unaffected Chromium/Firefox ones) already matched with 0 pixel difference and were left untouched.

test-results/ (including pages-baseline/) is git-ignored (confirmed via `git check-ignore`), so refreshing WebKit's 88 local baseline files is a local, disposable artifact - not a tracked change requiring review as source, and not something that alters CI (this check does not run in CI at all). Any other checkout regenerates it locally the same way.

Final verification: 3 consecutive clean runs of `node scripts/check-pages-ui.mjs` across chromium/firefox/webkit with zero failures of any kind. `npx eslint` and `npx prettier --check` clean on scripts/check-pages-ui.mjs, package.json and package-lock.json. `node scripts/check-agents.mjs` still passes after the devDependency additions.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2026-09-25 (real CareerScope Independent Reviewer dispatch, read-only by capability - no edit tool, and it disclosed up front that it had no shell and therefore no git, marking everything requiring execution as UNCONFIRMED rather than implying agreement). Verdict transcribed verbatim by the Orchestrator. VERDICT: REVISE - NOT ready for UAT. Reviewer summary: "The fix is real and the devDependencies are genuinely declared, but the check is described as strict while running at threshold: 0.1 with anti-aliased pixels discarded, the 88-baseline approval evidence is gitignored and unreproducible, and the check runs in no pipeline at all." BLOCKING: (CS32-2) the check description and its real tolerance disagree - it runs at pixelmatch threshold 0.1 with anti-aliased pixels discarded while being described as strict; the description must match the actual tolerance. (CS32-3) the evidence approving all 88 WebKit baselines lives in gitignored test-results/ and is therefore unreproducible, which does not satisfy this ticket own criterion "never approve a snapshot merely to turn the check green" - a durable artifact is required. (CS32-4, not this ticket fault but recorded on it): scripts/check-pages-ui.mjs runs in NO pipeline, so green here is a developer-machine fact, not a release control. Tracked systemically as CS-52.
REVIEWER D VERDICT 2026-09-25: REJECTED. Recorded by the orchestrator (sole backlog writer) and attributed to the independent review. Status held at QA, NOT promoted.

REVIEWER D - THE CONSUMER CHAIN HAS NO SECOND HOP: check-pages-ui.mjs -> pages:visual -> NOTHING. Applying the standing rule that evidence must cite the consumer, and the consumers consumer, until something that executes, the chain simply terminates. A check nothing runs is indistinguishable from a check that does not exist.
REVIEWER D - DESCRIBED AS STRICT WHILE RUNNING AT threshold: 0.1 WITH ANTI-ALIASED PIXELS DISCARDED. The description and the configuration disagree, and the description is the one people rely on.

REVIEWER D - THE 88-BASELINE APPROVAL EVIDENCE IS GITIGNORED AND UNREPRODUCIBLE, which does not satisfy this tickets OWN criterion that a snapshot must never be approved merely to turn the check green. The ticket set the standard and the evidence does not meet it.

ORCHESTRATOR VERIFIED THE GITIGNORE CLAIM INDEPENDENTLY AT SOURCE, and it is worse than stated: .gitignore:21 is "test-results/", check-pages-ui.mjs:16 sets the baseline directory to test-results/pages-baseline - INSIDE the ignored tree - and ZERO visual baselines are tracked anywhere (the 20 files matching baseline/snapshot/png patterns are drizzle migration snapshots, design concept images and unrelated crypto helpers). test-results/ currently holds 1864 files including 534 PNGs, none of them in the repository.

ORCHESTRATOR CONSEQUENCE, derived rather than relayed: on a FRESH CLONE there is no baseline, so the first run must create one from whatever the code renders at that moment. A visual check whose baseline is generated by its own first run CANNOT FAIL on a fresh clone. That is a check-that-cannot-fail at the repository level rather than inside a single assertion, and it is why CS-69 was filed as the structural ticket.

REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT, carried on this verdict deliberately: the reviewer states it cannot detect whether its reads fell inside another session write window. Three sessions were writing concurrently. If any file cited in this verdict was edited between roughly 15:05 and 15:25 IST on 2026-09-25, THIS VERDICT SHOULD BE RE-TAKEN RATHER THAN TRUSTED. Recorded so a later reader can judge it rather than inherit it.

RUNTIME CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-25 TO EVERY RESULT RECORDED TODAY: all local verification in this run was executed on Node v22.23.2, while package.json requires >=24.0.0, .nvmrc says 24 and CI uses 24. This does not invalidate the passes, but it RECLASSIFIES them - each was obtained on a runtime the project does not support, and any could differ on Node 24. Applies to typecheck, lint, test:unit, deploy:gate:test, eol:check and the three-engine test:ui runs alike.

CS32-2 STAYS OPEN, AND IT WAS NEARLY REPORTED AS FIXED ON A NON-MATCH. A grep of scripts/check-pages-ui.mjs for "near-zero" returns NOTHING - because THE PHRASE IS SPLIT ACROSS A LINE BREAK inside a wrapped comment ("near-" / "zero"). Verified in this session by unwrapping comment continuations before searching: the phrase is present, it sits beside threshold: 0.1, and the file mtime is 2026-09-23T20:34:55Z - UNTOUCHED BY THIS ENTIRE RUN. The comment still describes pixelmatch default tolerance as "near-zero".

THE COMMENT AND THE CONFIGURATION STILL DISAGREE, which is the whole of CS32-2: "perceptual comparison at a near-zero tolerance catches real regressions" sits directly above { threshold: 0.1 }. The description is what people rely on.
RUNTIME CAVEAT: verified on Node v22.23.2, below the declared minimum of 24.

PROVISIONAL MARKING WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25, SAME DAY IT WAS APPLIED, BECAUSE IT WAS TOO BROAD AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENT. The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". THE GATE COULD FAIL; ONLY ITS FIRST LINK COULD NOT. `npm run typecheck` chains four commands and the last, check-test-types.mjs, filters on /^\S+\.ts\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - WHICH MATCHES A PRODUCTION FILE AS READILY AS A TEST FILE - and exits 1. Anyone running the npm script WOULD have been told.

THIS TICKET DOES NOT CITE A BARE `tsc -b`, so its typecheck evidence was never in the unfalsifiable form and stands unqualified. The narrowed set is 4 of the original 29: CS-53, CS-62, CS-76, CS-77 - ALL FOUR WRITTEN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, which is the correct place for the correction to land.

items.title: Owner-scoped job detail and match evidence read contract
items.userProblem: Detail, export and evidence views need a consistent validated projection of retained job facts without invented fields or duplicate scoring.
items.source: ChatGPT TICKET-PLAN-20260920 proposal and supplied CQ-05 observation; source validation pending
acceptanceCriteria: Inventory existing owner/run/job identity and stored evidence; define a bounded validated read contract for facts, source links, freshness and frozen-profile match evidence with explicit unknown fields
Keep existing API/export compatibility and allowlists, ordering and row limits; reuse a projection only where the detail/export semantics actually agree
Prove valid stored data renders, malformed data fails safely, foreign-owner identifiers reveal no data, and evidence uses deterministic stored results rather than recalculating frontend scores
evidence: Real inventory of the current read paths (v2/packages/core/src/leads.ts, v2/packages/core/src/jobs.ts, v2/apps/api/src/app.ts) found a single, already-shared, Zod-validated schema (CollectedJob/collectedJobSchema) used across search results (search_jobs table), saved leads (saved_leads table) and exports - satisfying AC1/AC2 in spirit - and every lead/job read query is parameterized and owner-scoped (WHERE owner_id = $1). Empirically verified against the live local API (authenticated session): a well-formed but nonexistent lead id -> 404 "Lead not found"; a malformed (non-UUID) id -> 400 "Invalid request"; a real owned id -> 200 with correct data. No internals leaked in any case.

A real CareerScope Security review found a genuine S2 gap (not a cross-owner leak or injection - the isolation itself was independently re-verified and confirmed correct): GET /api/searches/:id (detail) and every LeadRepository read (get/list/save/update) returned stored `data` straight from Postgres, trusting write-time discipline (Database.settle() and LeadRepository.save() both validate before insert) rather than independently re-validating on read - unlike GET /api/searches/:id/export, which already parsed through collectedJobSchema.strip(). A future direct DB write, migration or backfill touching search_jobs.data or saved_leads.data would silently reach the client unfiltered/unbounded through the two unvalidated surfaces while export alone would catch it.

Fixed: GET /api/searches/:id now maps jobs.rows through the identical collectedJobSchema.strip().parse(row.data) the export route already used. Added a hydrate() helper in leads.ts that re-validates data the same way, applied at every LeadRepository read/write return site (get, list, save - both the INSERT...RETURNING and the ON CONFLICT fallback SELECT - and update - both the no-op and the real-change paths). All three read surfaces (search detail, search export, lead detail/list/save/update) now share one enforced projection instead of two relying on unverifiable write-time trust.

Added a real, executable negative-path integration test (v2/packages/core/src/database.test.ts, inside the existing real-Postgres "partial search outcomes..." test) that directly SQL-updates search_jobs.data and saved_leads.data to bypass both settle() and save() entirely, then asserts the exact two properties this fix is supposed to guarantee, across all three routes: (a) an unrecognized extra field is silently stripped before the client ever sees it (verified the response body genuinely does not contain the injected field, not just that the status was 200); (b) removing a required field (title) causes every one of the three routes to fail with a generic 400 {error, requestId} and nothing else - not just export. Confirmed the test fails without the fix (reproduced the exact failure first: detail route returned 200 with the corrupted data before the fix existed) and passes after it, both for the extra-field and the missing-field case.

Full v2 npm run test:integration (real Postgres/Redis/LocalStack service containers, 41 tests across database/market/queue/resumes/runtime/bull-queue plus scheduled-discovery/lead-liveness/search-retention scripts): 41/41 passing on a clean re-run. An unrelated, pre-existing flake (a Postgres statement-timeout in run-scheduled-discovery.test.ts under back-to-back load) was observed once and did not reproduce on immediate re-run - not touched by or related to this change, disclosed rather than hidden.
typecheck/lint clean across the whole v2 workspace; Prettier clean on every touched file (v2/apps/api/src/app.ts, v2/packages/core/src/leads.ts, v2/packages/core/src/database.test.ts).

FORENSIC AUDIT CONFIRMATION 2026-09-24: an independent read of current source confirmed this ticket is genuinely IMPLEMENTED - collectedJobSchema.strip().parse present on the detail route, and the hydrate() helper applied at every LeadRepository return site. Status remains QA pending an independent QA/reviewer pass; recorded so the implementation is not re-litigated.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2026-09-25 (real CareerScope Independent Reviewer dispatch, read-only by capability - no edit tool, and it disclosed up front that it had no shell and therefore no git, marking everything requiring execution as UNCONFIRMED rather than implying agreement). Verdict transcribed verbatim by the Orchestrator. VERDICT: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS - findings do NOT block UAT. Reviewer summary: "Real fix, real test that can genuinely fail, CI-executed; one stored field (search_runs.request) was left outside the projection the evidence claims is now universal." NON-BLOCKING FINDING TO CARRY: the evidence describes the validated projection as applying universally, but search_runs.request is not covered by it. That is a scope overstatement in the evidence rather than a defect in the fix, and it should be corrected or the field brought into the projection in a follow-up.

HOLDS AT UAT on independent audit - no demotion. ONE FALSE CLAIM CORRECTED: evidence[7] quotes a reviewer summary containing "Real fix, real test that can genuinely fail, CI-EXECUTED". NOTHING IN THIS TREE HAS BEEN CI-EXECUTED. The committed ci.yml and gates:test differ from the working tree, and the SHA has not moved. The correct level is WIRED, PENDING CI EXECUTION.

THE QUOTATION IS DELIBERATELY LEFT INTACT rather than edited: it is a record of what a reviewer said, and rewriting someone elses quoted words to make them correct would be a worse defect than the claim it fixes. The correction is recorded here instead, adjacent to it.

WHY IT MATTERS DISPROPORTIONATELY: verified by the orchestrator, this is THE ONLY POSITIVE "CI-executed" CLAIM ACROSS THE BACKLOG - every other occurrence (CS-15 ev[14] and ev[18], CS-54 ev[4] and ev[15]) is an explicit NEGATION. And it sits in the state closest to release. If a release decision weighs which UAT tickets are CI-backed, this one would be miscounted.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 15:55 IST on 2026-09-25 this verdict should be re-taken rather than trusted.

RUNTIME CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-25 TO EVERY RESULT RECORDED TODAY: all local verification in this run was executed on Node v22.23.2, while package.json requires >=24.0.0, .nvmrc says 24 and CI uses 24. This does not invalidate the passes, but it RECLASSIFIES them - each was obtained on a runtime the project does not support, and any could differ on Node 24. Applies to typecheck, lint, test:unit, deploy:gate:test, eol:check and the three-engine test:ui runs alike.

HARDENING FINDING 2026-09-25, NOT A DEFECT - THE NEGATIVE-PATH TEST IS SOUND, BUT NOT FOR THE REASON ITS STRUCTURE SUGGESTS. It SQL-writes corrupt data past both validators, then asserts the read routes cope. NONE OF THE SIX UPDATEs CHECKS rowCount - verified in v2/packages/core/src/database.test.ts around :2071-2108. If an UPDATE silently matched zero rows the data would stay clean, the routes would behave normally, and the test would pass while proving nothing.

THE STRIP HALF ALONE WOULD BE VACUOUS: `data || {"unexpectedField"...}` then assert 200 and assert NOT includes("unexpectedField"). A ZERO-ROW UPDATE PRODUCES EXACTLY THAT RESULT - clean data, 200, no unexpectedField. That is the absence-assertion-with-no-positive shape in its purest form, and it is the shape this run has been removing all day.

BUT THE MALFORMED HALF IS A LOAD-BEARING POSITIVE CONTROL: `data - title` then assert 400. A 400 IS ONLY REACHABLE IF THE ROW WAS ACTUALLY MODIFIED - strip the required field and validation fails; had the UPDATE matched nothing the route returns 200 and the assertion goes red. Both UPDATEs use the same WHERE id = $1 with the same jobId, SO THE 400 RETROACTIVELY PROVES THE FIRST UPDATE TARGETED A REAL ROW. The same coupling holds for the saved_leads pair.

SO: THE TEST IS SAFE BECAUSE A LATER ASSERTION IN THE SAME TEST PROVES AN EARLIER ASSERTION PRECONDITION - NOT BECAUSE EITHER ASSERTION IS SELF-VALIDATING. The guarantee is emergent from ordering rather than stated locally.

THE FRAGILITY, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL FINDING: SPLIT THE TWO HALVES INTO SEPARATE TESTS AND THE STRIP HALF BECOMES VACUOUS IMMEDIATELY, WITH NOTHING TO SIGNAL IT. That is a plausible future refactor - "one test per behaviour" is ordinary advice, and the strip case and the malformed case genuinely are different behaviours. The refactor would be locally correct and would silently destroy the only thing making half this test real.

A THIRD SITE CLASS FOUND HERE THAT THE ORIGINAL ANALYSIS DID NOT REACH: THE TWO RESTORE UPDATEs AT THE END (:2104 and :2108) ARE ALSO UNCHECKED, AND NOTHING ASSERTS AFTER THEM AT ALL - so they have no later positive to lean on, not even an emergent one. Their own comment states their purpose: "Restore both rows to their real, valid shape so nothing downstream of this point... inherits a deliberately-corrupted fixture." A SILENTLY-FAILED RESTORE LEAVES EXACTLY THE CORRUPTED FIXTURE THE COMMENT PROMISES TO PREVENT, and it would surface later as an unrelated failure in whatever assertion was added next.

RECOMMENDATION, DELIBERATELY MINIMAL: add assert.equal(result.rowCount, 1) after each of the six UPDATEs. One line per site; makes each half independently sound; removes a coupling that currently exists only by accident of ordering. DO NOT REWRITE THE TEST - it works, and the paired structure is good. This is about making the guarantee LOCAL rather than EMERGENT.

AND THE COMPOUNDING FACTOR FROM CS-76: THIS FILE IS ONE OF THE ELEVEN EXCLUDED FROM TYPE CHECKING. So a refactor that split these halves would be reviewed by neither a type checker nor a failing assertion. The two findings are independent but they stack on the same file.
CS-33 STAYS IN UAT. This changes nothing about its status - it is a hardening recommendation on a test that currently does its job.

A REPORTED EIGHTEENTH CANNOT-FAIL CHECK AT database.test.ts:2184-2193 WAS INVESTIGATED AND ITS CENTRAL CLAIM DOES NOT HOLD. The claim was that :2184 is the only thing standing between the session-expired loop at :2192 and vacuity, so a stream set containing no 200s would let the SSE revocation property go unverified while the test reported green. FOUR LINES ABOVE THE QUOTED RANGE, AT :2178-2181, THERE IS THIS: assert.deepEqual(concurrentStreams.map(r => r.status).sort(), [200, 200, 429]). THE MULTISET IS PINNED EXACTLY, SO liveStreams.length IS FIXED AT 2 AND THE LOOP CANNOT ITERATE ZERO TIMES.

WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION IS REAL BUT MINOR: :2184 IS GENUINELY A TAUTOLOGY - liveStreams is filtered on status === 200 and then asserted to have every status === 200, which cannot fail by construction, and every() on an empty array returns true besides. IT IS REDUNDANT, NOT LOAD-BEARING. Deleting it would change nothing; replacing it with an assertion on the expected count would be a small improvement. It is not a security gap and not an eighteenth instance.

THE SSE SESSION-REVOCATION PROPERTY IS THEREFORE VERIFIED, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERED: a session revoked while a stream is open does provably receive event: session-expired, on both live streams, and the count is asserted rather than assumed.

THE METHOD LESSON IS THE SAME ONE THIS FILE TAUGHT AN HOUR EARLIER, AND IT WAS MISSED IN THE SAME FILE BY THE SAME SWEEP: AN EARLIER ASSERTION ESTABLISHING A LATER ASSERTION PRECONDITION. On CS-33 that pattern was correctly identified with the order reversed - a LATER assertion proving an EARLIER precondition. HERE THE GUARD SITS FOUR LINES ABOVE THE QUOTED WINDOW AND WAS OUTSIDE IT. A quoted range that starts below its own precondition will always read as vacuous.

RECORD THE RULE IN ITS SHARPENED FORM: WHEN JUDGING WHETHER A COLLECTION CAN BE EMPTY, THE GUARD IS OFTEN NOT ADJACENT TO THE LOOP - IT IS WHEREVER THE COLLECTION WAS BUILT. Read from the construction site forward, not from the assertion backward, and never from a quoted excerpt.

THE THREE-LOOP SURVEY THAT PRODUCED IT IS STILL VALUABLE AND IS RETAINED: of 136 in-loop assertions in this file, nearly all iterate LITERAL arrays that cannot be empty, and only three iterate a DERIVED collection. The two nested OpenAPI operation loops at :226-227 are properly guarded by assert.ok(routes.size >= 30) plus a deepEqual tying spec.paths to it. WITH THIS CORRECTION THE FILE IS 3 FOR 3 ON DERIVED-COLLECTION GUARDS, NOT 2 FOR 3.

AND THE NARROWING WAS THE RIGHT MOVE EVEN THOUGH THE CONCLUSION WAS WRONG: a first pass returned 136 candidates and was unactionable; filtering to "can this collection be empty" rather than "is there a loop" returned three. THE FIRST NUMBER WAS NOT WRONG, IT WAS UNUSABLE. A finding buried in noise is a finding nobody acts on.

AND THE PROPOSED FIX FOR :2184 WOULD HAVE BEEN A DOWNGRADE, which is the most useful thing to come out of the correction. The suggestion was assert.ok(liveStreams.length > 0, "the fixture must open at least one live stream"). BUT :2180 ALREADY PINS THE MULTISET TO EXACTLY [200, 200, 429], WHICH IS STRICTLY STRONGER THAN "> 0". Applying it would have replaced a harmless tautology with a WEAKER guard while reading as hardening in the diff.

RECORD THE RULE: A HARDENING FIX PROPOSED FROM AN EXCERPT CAN WEAKEN THE FILE. Before adding a guard, establish what the surrounding code already guarantees - otherwise THE NEW ASSERTION BECOMES THE CEILING RATHER THAN THE FLOOR. Correct minimal action on :2184: delete it, or assert the expected count. Redundant either way, and not urgent.

The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". items.title: Web runtime environment least privilege
items.userProblem: The supplied Compose review suggests the web service inherits database configuration it may not need.
items.source: ChatGPT TICKET-PLAN-20260920 proposal and supplied CQ-01 observation; source validation pending
acceptanceCriteria: Inspect web build/runtime configuration consumers and define the smallest required environment without printing secret values
Verify with synthetic configuration that DATABASE_URL and other API-only credentials are absent from the web runtime while API database access remains configured
Prove web startup and API proxy behavior still work, and missing required web configuration fails clearly rather than falling back to unsafe defaults
evidence: Confirmed by direct source inspection: v2/apps/web reads zero custom environment variables anywhere in its own code - grep across v2/apps/web/src found only process.env.NODE_ENV (Node's own automatic variable, in next.config.ts, used only to toggle a CSP dev-websocket allowance) and nothing else. The /api/* proxy destination (127.0.0.1:5390) is a hardcoded literal in next.config.ts's rewrites(), not env-configured. This means the web service has zero *required* configuration at all - the acceptance criterion's 'missing required web configuration fails clearly' clause is vacuously satisfied because nothing is required; recorded explicitly rather than silently skipped.

infra/v3/compose.production.yml and compose.acceptance.yml both previously gave the web service the full shared *environment anchor (DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, LOCAL_AWS_ENDPOINT, APP_ORIGIN, REGISTRATION_ENABLED, RESUME_STORAGE_DIRECTORY, RESUME_STORAGE_KEY_FILE, NODE_OPTIONS) purely because it shared the *app anchor with api/publisher/search/files, which do need all of those - confirming the CQ-01 observation. Fixed in both files with a new, minimal x-web-environment anchor (NODE_OPTIONS only) applied to the web service only; api/publisher/search/files retain the full environment unchanged.

Verified with `docker compose config` using synthetic values (never real secrets) in both compose files: resolved web service environment is exactly {NODE_OPTIONS}; resolved api/publisher/search/files environment is unchanged (all 7 original keys present).

Strongest verification: built the real production Docker image (infra/v3/Dockerfile, runtime target) and ran the actual web container standalone with only NODE_OPTIONS set - `docker exec ... cat /proc/1/environ` on the live running process confirmed DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, RESUME_STORAGE_KEY_FILE and LOCAL_AWS_ENDPOINT are genuinely absent from the container's real environment (not just the compose file), and a real HTTP GET to the container's / returned 200 OK, proving the Next.js server starts and serves successfully without them. Test container and image removed afterward; no production system touched, no restart of any live service, per the ticket's explicit constraint.
v2 typecheck/lint/prettier clean; full next build 13/13 routes clean (no code changes required beyond the two compose files - this ticket needed no application code change).

INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2026-09-25 (real CareerScope Independent Reviewer dispatch, read-only by capability - no edit tool, and it disclosed up front that it had no shell and therefore no git, marking everything requiring execution as UNCONFIRMED rather than implying agreement). Verdict transcribed verbatim by the Orchestrator. VERDICT: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS - findings do NOT block UAT. Reviewer summary: "Compose change verified correct by reading; AC3 vacuous and honestly disclosed; but the whole control rests on a one-off manual command with no regression guard, and the container run is unreproducible here." NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS TO CARRY: (1) AC3 is vacuous - the reviewer agreed this was disclosed honestly rather than hidden, which is why it does not block. (2) THE REAL RESIDUAL RISK: the least-privilege property is proven by a one-off manual docker compose config run and has NO REGRESSION GUARD. Nothing stops a future edit from re-adding DATABASE_URL to the web service, and nothing would detect it. A cheap automated assertion over the resolved compose environment would convert this from a point-in-time observation into an enforced control, and is recommended as a follow-up.

items.title: Typed conflict contracts and actionable client errors
items.userProblem: Different conflicts may be shown as the same unsaved-edit error, preventing an appropriate recovery action.
items.source: ChatGPT TICKET-PLAN-20260920 proposal and supplied CQ-03 observation; source validation pending
acceptanceCriteria: Trace revision conflict, idempotency-key reuse and missing-target-role paths and assign distinct stable safe machine codes while preserving existing HTTP and redaction contracts
Offer the appropriate client action for each known code without discarding unsaved profile or lead edits
Test every supported code plus unknown codes and malformed responses; fall back to a safe generic error without treating malformed input as success or exposing server details
evidence: Current Node 24 CI verification: runs 36385161068 and 36385785464 completed green, including the service-backed V2 integration path that exercises this contract.

Traced every Conflict-throwing call site across packages/core (30 sites). Confirmed most are internal worker/command-pipeline invariants never reachable from a route response (left with the generic default code, not rewritten - bounded scope, not a blanket rewrite). Identified the real, route-reachable conflicts the acceptance criteria names: revision conflicts (profile, lead - already distinct), idempotency-key reuse (search creation, resume upload), and the missing-target-role path (POST /api/searches with useProfileTitles and no saved title) - this last one was previously mislabeled with the exact same "Idempotency conflict" string as an unrelated case, which is precisely the bug this ticket exists to fix.

Added a stable `code` property to the Conflict base class (packages/core/src/errors.ts) and assigned distinct codes to every route-reachable subclass/throw site: PROFILE_REVISION_CONFLICT, LEAD_REVISION_CONFLICT, PROFILE_NOT_SAVED, MISSING_TARGET_ROLES, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (shared by both the search and resume-upload idempotency cases, since the correct client action is identical for both), UPLOAD_CANCELLED, UPLOAD_NOT_CANCELLABLE, UPLOAD_VERSION_CONFLICT. Anything not explicitly assigned falls back to the generic 'CONFLICT' code and its existing safe message - never the raw internal Error.message.

Rewrote the API's global error handler (v2/apps/api/src/app.ts) to emit `{error, code, requestId}` (code only present for 409s) with a distinct, actionable message per code, replacing the old instanceof-based special-casing that only distinguished 2 of 8 real cases.

Found and fixed a live instance of the exact anti-pattern this ticket targets: v2/scripts/run-scheduled-discovery.ts's isMissingTitlesConflict() matched on the raw message string ('Save target roles before starting profile discovery') rather than a stable code - a wording change would have silently broken this worker's own retry/alerting logic. Now matches error.code === 'MISSING_TARGET_ROLES'. Also found its existing test never actually exercised the true/positive case (only ever asserted false), a real 'test that cannot fail' - added the missing positive case using the real Conflict class.

Added a new, real, executable integration test (v2/packages/core/src/database.test.ts) proving the contract end-to-end: at the domain layer, both MISSING_TARGET_ROLES and IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED reject with the correct distinct code; at the real HTTP layer (via createApp + app.inject, not mocked), both produce a 409 with exactly {error, code, requestId} - no extra fields, no leaked internals - with two DIFFERENT, correct messages (explicitly asserted not equal to each other, closing the original bug where they were identical).
Verified: v2 typecheck/lint clean; Prettier clean on every touched file; full `npm run test:integration` (real Postgres/Redis/LocalStack, 42 tests including the new one) passing.

FORENSIC AUDIT CONFIRMATION 2026-09-24: an independent read of current source confirmed this ticket is genuinely IMPLEMENTED - all eight Conflict code values plus the handler mapping table are present. Status remains QA pending an independent QA/reviewer pass; recorded so the implementation is not re-litigated.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2026-09-25 (real CareerScope Independent Reviewer dispatch, read-only by capability - no edit tool, and it disclosed up front that it had no shell and therefore no git, marking everything requiring execution as UNCONFIRMED rather than implying agreement). Verdict transcribed verbatim by the Orchestrator. VERDICT: REVISE - NOT ready for UAT. Reviewer summary: "Server-side codes and the worker anti-pattern fix are excellent; AC2 is simply not implemented (no client can read code - ApiError has no such field), and the unknown-code assertion tests the constructor rather than the handler it names." BLOCKING: AC2 ("Offer the appropriate client action for each known code without discarding unsaved profile or lead edits") is NOT IMPLEMENTED. The server emits the codes correctly, but the client type ApiError carries no code field, so no client can read one - the contract terminates at the network boundary. Additionally the unknown-code test asserts against the Conflict constructor rather than the HTTP handler it claims to cover, so it does not test the fallback path it names. Fix both, then re-review.

AC2 FIXED 2026-09-25. The reviewer was right that the contract terminated at the network boundary: ApiError carried no code field, so no client could act on the typed codes the server was correctly emitting. v2/apps/web/src/lib/api.ts now carries readonly code?: string, parses the code off the 409 body, and maps it through a client-owned allowlist to a per-code message. THE ALLOWLIST IS A Map, NOT AN OBJECT LITERAL, and the builder explained why in a way worth preserving: {}["__proto__"] returns Object.prototype and would have been handed back as a "message". That hole is covered by a test rather than only by care. The real behavioural win is the second half of AC2 ("without discarding unsaved profile or lead edits"): profile-editor.tsx and saved-leads.tsx previously offered "Discard Edits and Reload" on ANY 409. They now gate it on offersDiscardAndReload(), so PROFILE_NOT_SAVED and MISSING_TARGET_ROLES no longer invite the owner to destroy unsaved work. An unknown or absent code keeps the previous offer, because a stale record must stay recoverable. UI FREEZE RESPECTED: condition and import only - no class, spacing, typography, colour, layout or DOM-shape change.

AC3 FIXED: the unknown-code assertion tested the Conflict CONSTRUCTOR rather than the HTTP handler it named. It now drives two real app.inject requests whose repository call throws a default-code and an unmapped-code Conflict, asserting 409, exactly [error, code, requestId], a generic message and no raw internals. A new v2/apps/web/src/lib/api.test.ts drives the REAL api() against a stubbed fetch for all eight codes, an unknown code and TWELVE malformed bodies, asserting every case REJECTS (never resolves) and never echoes server text. test:unit ALSO GAINED A RUNNER IT NEVER HAD: no script reached v2/apps/web at all before (root vitest apps/web glob targets the V1 app, not V2). Orchestrator-verified: test:unit 49 -> 54, exit 0. FOUR FALSIFICATIONS, EACH SPECIFIC TO THE NEW COVERAGE: dropping code from the ApiError construction fails with "PROFILE_REVISION_CONFLICT must survive the network boundary, actual undefined"; removing the malformed-body guard fails the safe-fallback test; reverting the action gating fails with "PROFILE_NOT_SAVED must not invite the owner to discard unsaved edits"; and making the handler echo the raw Conflict message fails with actual "Search command missing: relation search_commands is locked" vs expected "Idempotency conflict" - which is precisely the falsification the OLD constructor assertion could not produce. All reverted, green after.

RE-REVIEW 2026-09-25: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS. The blocking finding is GENUINELY CLOSED, verified at source on four points: (1) code reaches the client off the parsed response BODY, never inferred from status or message, with no path where the client synthesises one; (2) the Map allowlist is pollution-proof BY CONSTRUCTION and BY TEST - Map.prototype.get("__proto__") is undefined, and api.test.ts explicitly includes {"code":"__proto__"} and {"code":"toString"} among its malformed bodies; (3) the unknown-code path drives the REAL api() against a real Response via a fetch stub, so body parsing genuinely executes rather than the constructor; (4) the discard-gating was verified AT THE CALL SITE (profile-editor.tsx:346-352), not merely at the function. It flagged honestly that it did NOT read saved-leads.tsx call site - inferred only. It also noted the fourth falsification (actual "Search command missing: relation search_commands is locked" vs expected "Idempotency conflict") is exactly what the old constructor assertion was structurally incapable of producing, which is strong evidence the server half was genuinely re-pointed at the handler.

F-1 FIXED 2026-09-25 - a CI comment that my own change had made knowingly false, which is precisely the failure class I had written a standing rule about one ticket earlier. .github/workflows/ci.yml said "These six need nothing at all" and "ai-provider.test.ts is the sixth"; adding apps/web/src/lib/api.test.ts to test:unit made that seven. VERIFIED by parsing v2/package.json: test:unit names exactly 7 files. Corrected to seven, with api.test.ts described and with the note that it is the FIRST thing in any workflow reaching v2/apps/web at all (the root vitest apps/web glob targets the V1 app, not this one). I also added an explicit instruction that the count is load-bearing rather than decoration - it was wrong for exactly one commit, and anyone adding a file to test:unit must change the number in the same edit. ci.yml re-validated with a real YAML parser (jobs: verify, v2-integration, pages, image). VERIFICATION LEVEL: WIRED and LOCALLY VERIFIED, NOT CI-EXECUTED. This ticket is not promotable until a pipeline runs; commit authorisation is the unlock.

RUNTIME CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-25 TO EVERY RESULT RECORDED TODAY: all local verification in this run was executed on Node v22.23.2, while package.json requires >=24.0.0, .nvmrc says 24 and CI uses 24. This does not invalidate the passes, but it RECLASSIFIES them - each was obtained on a runtime the project does not support, and any could differ on Node 24. Applies to typecheck, lint, test:unit, deploy:gate:test, eol:check and the three-engine test:ui runs alike.

STANDARD WORDING ADOPTED 2026-09-25 from CS-39, which stated the claim, its ceiling and its unlock in one line: "All three criteria met and asserted. Promotable on a green CI run; not promoted here." Every ticket in this cohort now carries the same sentence, plus the second bar discovered later - local execution on Node v22.23.2 against a declared floor of 24. NO QA TICKET IS PROMOTABLE TONIGHT ON EXECUTION EVIDENCE, and that is ONE GATE rather than nineteen separate problems.

HISTORICAL CHECKPOINT REVIEWED 2026-09-28: the earlier contradiction-shape sweep was a pre-CI checkpoint and its wording is superseded by the hosted verification below. The implementation and all three acceptance criteria are now closed by source review plus the exact green CI run recorded next.

QA CLOSED 2026-09-28: hosted run 36398473010 attempt 2 completed green on Node 24, including typecheck, lint, unit/API coverage, recovery, service-backed integration, browser acceptance and accessibility suites. Independent re-review at evidence[11] confirmed the client code contract, server handler fallback and unsaved-edit protections. Status is promotable to UAT.

AND THE REVIEWERS THIRD REFUSAL TO GUESS IS RECORDED AS CORRECT BEHAVIOUR: it probed three times, could not locate the ticket because the file had reordered, and declined to answer from a ~15:05 read - "answering from that would be exactly the stale-verdict-dressed-as-current error". THIRD TIME IT HAS DECLINED RATHER THAN GUESSED, AND IT HAS BEEN RIGHT EVERY TIME.

WORDING CORRECTED 2026-09-25 FROM "All applicable criteria met" TO THE COUNTED FORM. The distinction is not cosmetic: "ALL THREE CRITERIA MET" IS FALSIFIABLE BY COUNTING; "ALL APPLICABLE CRITERIA MET" CANNOT FAIL, because an unmet criterion can be reclassified as not-applicable without anyone editing a number. It is the same shape as \bsurfaced\b, DEFERRED and eol=crlf - a word anyone can write that silently changes how a claim is graded - except that this one sat in the STATUS FIELD OF TEN TICKETS, which is the field a promotion decision reads. That makes it the most consequential of the four, not the least.

COUNT NOT YET RE-TAKEN 2026-09-25, recorded as owed work rather than left as an unverified claim. When "All applicable criteria met" was replaced with the counted form across ten tickets, THE WORDING WAS CORRECTED AND THE COUNT WAS NOT. Two of the ten were then found wrong within minutes - CS-74 (AC3 half-met) and CS-52 (AC4 unmet) - so the remaining eight cannot be assumed right. A COUNTED CLAIM OVER AN UNCOUNTED CRITERION IS NO BETTER THAN THE HEDGE IT REPLACED; it is only more falsifiable, and falsifying it is the outstanding work.

AC1 RE-TAKEN BY READING, NOT BY TOKEN MATCH, 2026-09-25 - flagged as the one genuine candidate because the evidence never writes the literal string "AC1". AC1 NAMES THREE PATHS and that is exactly the shape that hides an unmet third, so each was checked in source individually rather than accepted from the evidence account of itself.

ALL THREE PATHS TRACED, WITH DISTINCT CODES, AND ALL MAPPED IN THE HANDLER TABLE AT v2/apps/api/src/app.ts:171-175. REVISION CONFLICT: profile.ts:101 PROFILE_REVISION_CONFLICT and leads.ts:61 LEAD_REVISION_CONFLICT - two distinct codes, not one shared one, which is stronger than the criterion requires. IDEMPOTENCY-KEY REUSE: database.ts:83 and resumes.ts:192 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. MISSING TARGET ROLE: database.ts:95 MISSING_TARGET_ROLES, plus profile.ts:130 PROFILE_NOT_SAVED for the adjacent precondition.

ALL FIVE CODES ARE DISTINCT, STABLE AND SAFE - no identifier, no user content, no server internals in any code value, which is the "safe machine codes" half of AC1. The HTTP contract is preserved: the handler emits {error, code, requestId} with code present only on 409s, and the re-review at ev[10] verified at source that the client reads code off the PARSED BODY and never infers it from status or message.

SO AC1 IS MET. COUNT RE-TAKEN: CS-35 IS 3 OF 3 - AC1 by this source read, AC2 and AC3 by the explicit fixes at ev[8] and ev[9] confirmed by the source-level re-review at ev[10]. The COUNT NOT YET RE-TAKEN label is discharged for this ticket, by reading rather than by a scan.

AC1 INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-25 BY A SECOND READER AGAINST THE SAME TABLE, reaching 3 of 3 separately. ONE DETAIL RECORDED AS CORRECT RATHER THAN ACCIDENTAL: PROFILE_REVISION_CONFLICT and LEAD_REVISION_CONFLICT SHARE A MESSAGE BUT ARE DISTINCT CODES. That is right, because THE CLIENT ALLOWLIST DECIDES PER CODE, NOT PER MESSAGE - two surfaces can offer different recovery actions while reading identically to the user today. COLLAPSING THEM WOULD LOOK LIKE TIDYING AND WOULD REMOVE A REAL DEGREE OF FREEDOM.

AND THE SECOND READER FIRST PASS COUNTED MENTIONS - revision 7, idempotency 9, target role 3 - WHICH TOLD IT NOTHING ABOUT WHETHER DISTINCT CODES EXIST. Same token-versus-property mistake as the AC2 scan, twice in one evening, by a different session. READING THE TABLE SETTLED IT IN ONE COMMAND. The cheap proxy is not the error; believing its output is.

items.title: Login and account-security journeys with consistent session reset
items.userProblem: Authentication and expiry handling are spread across existing views; protected deep links and stale cached state need one explicit policy.
items.source: ChatGPT TICKET-PLAN-20260920 session-reset proposal and supplied CQ-04 observation; source validation pending
acceptanceCriteria: Verify login, private deep-link entry, logout, expiry and reauthentication without transient protected rendering; keep registration disabled unless separately authorized
Define and test a shared reset policy across search SSE, preparation, leads, profile and resumes so old requests or caches cannot restore prior-session data; explicitly define unsaved-edit handling

Exercise existing authenticated password-change and session-revocation journeys with failure/retry states, preserved CSRF/origin/rate limits and server owner-isolation tests; do not add self-service recovery
evidence: AC1 (no transient protected rendering): confirmed AuthenticatedShell is the sole render path for every real authenticated route via layout.tsx, with session.isPending -> LoadingState and !authenticated -> null before any children ever render - traced as symmetric with the sign-in page. Empirically verified live: cleared the session via a real POST /api/logout (confirmed the session cookie is properly HttpOnly - could not be read/cleared via document.cookie from JS), then navigated directly to a protected deep link (/saved) - landed cleanly on the sign-in form with zero protected content visible at any point (screenshot-verified), then logged back in successfully.

AC3 (password-change/session-revocation): confirmed POST /api/account/password and POST /api/account/sessions/revoke-others both carry real rate limiting (5/hour), strict Zod body validation and correct CSRF/origin checks via the global onRequest hook; a wrong current-password attempt returns 400 without touching the session cookie, so retry-after-typo does not unfairly burn the rate-limit budget. AccountSecurity (rendered at the real /settings route) has working confirm-before-destructive-action dialogs for both actions and correctly clears cache + redirects with a clear notice after a password change (since the server revokes every session including the current one).

AC2 (shared reset policy, explicit unsaved-edit handling): confirmed the prior session's SESSION_EXPIRED_EVENT centralization (single listener in AuthenticatedShell) and the SSE connection's self-closing session-expired handler already give search/leads/profile/resumes one shared reset path, not several. Found a real, previously-unaddressed gap via a dispatched Independent Reviewer: saved-leads.tsx and profile-editor.tsx already track a local 'dirty' flag with their own discard-confirmation dialogs for in-app navigation, but every page wrapping them discarded the setter (`const [, setDirty] = useState(false)`, or resume/page.tsx's outright `onDirty={() => {}}` no-op), making that signal invisible to the global session-expiry handler, which unconditionally cleared the cache and redirected.

Fixed with the reviewer's own recommended remediation: added v2/apps/web/src/lib/unsaved-changes.ts (a plain module-level flag, not React state - it only needs to be read once, synchronously, at the moment of expiry) wired into saved/page.tsx, applications/page.tsx and resume/page.tsx's real onDirty callbacks; AuthenticatedShell's onExpired handler now checks it and shows one confirm() before clearing/redirecting if there is unsaved work, matching the existing discard() pattern's wording rather than inventing a new UX language. Added an unmount-cleanup effect in both SavedLeads and ProfileEditor so navigating away by any means (not just the in-component discard() path) always clears the flag, preventing it from staying stuck true on an unrelated later page.

Live-verified both branches with real keyboard-simulated typing (not raw DOM manipulation, which does not reliably trigger React's controlled-input onChange - caught and corrected this in my own test methodology before trusting the result): typed real text into a lead's notes field (confirmed dirty via the Save Notes button becoming enabled), dispatched the real session-expired event, and confirmed (a) dismissing the resulting confirm() keeps the user on /saved with the typed text still present, and (b) accepting it proceeds to the sign-in page with the honest 'Any unsaved changes were not saved' message.

A real Independent Reviewer found a second issue while verifying: v2/scripts/check-ui.ts asserted a stale keyboard-tab-order list for the /dashboard sidebar (missing Applications/Resume from the expected reachable set, which are now real CS-6/CS-50 routes) - fixed the assertion and its comment to match the current, real navItems order. Actually running check-ui.ts afterward (required temporarily freeing port 5390 from the local dev API, then restarting it afterward) surfaced that the file has additional, separate, pre-existing breakage at an earlier assertion (line ~327, stale pre-CS-6 label names in a different navigation test) unrelated to the one fixed here - disclosed honestly as confirming, not contradicting, the already-recorded "check-ui.ts needs its own rewrite" status in .ai/progress.json, rather than claimed as resolved.

Restarting the local dev API server to run check-ui.ts surfaced a real, pre-existing local-fixture data defect (the same match.dimensions: {} bug from earlier this session recurring against a rebuilt/reseeded local Postgres) which the CS-33 read-contract fix now correctly rejects on read - repaired the one affected local row directly, confirmed /saved renders correctly again. Not a regression in the application; a direct, expected consequence of CS-33 now validating on read where it previously did not.

Verified: v2 typecheck/lint clean; Prettier clean on every touched file; next build clean (13/13 routes); Lighthouse accessibility/best-practices/SEO/agentic-browsing all 100/100 on /dashboard after all changes.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2026-09-25 (real CareerScope Independent Reviewer dispatch, read-only by capability - no edit tool, and it disclosed up front that it had no shell and therefore no git, marking everything requiring execution as UNCONFIRMED rather than implying agreement). Verdict transcribed verbatim by the Orchestrator. VERDICT: REVISE - NOT ready for UAT. Reviewer summary: "No protected-content flash on any route, RSC path included; session policy and account-security journeys are genuinely well built; but AC2 test clause has zero executable coverage and the evidence cites a CI-required script it describes as broken." BLOCKING: AC2 requires the shared reset policy to be DEFINED AND TESTED across search SSE, preparation, leads, profile and resumes. The policy is defined and the implementation was independently confirmed sound - the reviewer verified there is no protected-content flash on any route including the RSC path - but the "test" half has ZERO executable coverage. The evidence also cites check-ui.ts while describing it as broken, which is now doubly stale: the suite has since been repaired and runs green. Add real executable coverage for the reset policy, refresh the stale citation, then re-review.

AC2 BLOCKING FINDING ADDRESSED 2026-09-25. The Independent Reviewer found the policy defined and the implementation sound but the TEST half entirely absent. AC2 says "Define and test a shared reset policy across search SSE, preparation, leads, profile and resumes so old requests or caches cannot restore prior-session data". The reset is cache.clear() in authenticated-shell.tsx on both logout (:71) and SESSION_EXPIRED_EVENT (:57). Asserting that the function is CALLED would prove nothing about whether data becomes unreachable, so the new test signs out and then signs in as a GENUINELY DIFFERENT REAL OWNER (the foreign-owner fixture, which has its own run, job and lead), then requires the first owner data to be absent from all five surfaces AC2 names: /jobs, /saved, /applications, /resume, /preparation. A surviving React Query cache would repopulate those screens from memory before any network response, which is exactly the failure the criterion describes. It also re-proves owner isolation ACROSS a session boundary rather than only within one.

TWO DESIGN CORRECTIONS MADE DURING THE WORK, both recorded because each was a real defect in my own first attempt. (1) My first version called quiet() per route and FAILED with "cs-36 reset /jobs never stopped issuing requests" - because /jobs polls /api/searches every 5 seconds unconditionally, which is the very behaviour documented on CS-55. The helper can never settle there. Removed. (2) More importantly, the absence assertions were count() === 0, which would have passed VACUOUSLY on a page that had not rendered yet - the exact check-that-cannot-fail shape this suite keeps finding. Each route now asserts a POSITIVE ANCHOR belonging to the NEW owner first (Foreign Owner Secret Query on /jobs, Foreign Owner Secret Role on /saved, and the real empty-state text on the others), so the absence checks cannot be reached until the page has genuinely loaded as that owner.

FALSIFICATION CAVEAT - STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT DOES NOT MEET MY OWN STANDARD. I removed cache.clear() from the logout path (mutation verified present) and the suite DID fail, exit 1 - but it failed at check-ui.ts:1265, a PRE-EXISTING sign-out assertion, before execution ever reached my new block. So: the reset property IS guarded, and removing it is caught. But the MARGINAL coverage of my new cross-owner test is NOT independently proven - an earlier assertion intercepts the same mutation first. A falsification must be specific to the new coverage to count as evidence for it, and this one is not. I could not find a cheap mutation that only the new block catches within this cycle. A reviewer is entitled to require one before accepting AC2 as tested, and I am not claiming otherwise. What IS established: the test runs green across chromium, firefox and webkit, exercises five real surfaces as a second real owner, and cannot pass vacuously thanks to the positive anchors.

NEGATIVE FALSIFICATION RESULT - MY NEW TEST DOES NOT GUARD THE PROPERTY IT WAS WRITTEN FOR. This supersedes the earlier "unproven" caveat with something stronger: it is now DISPROVEN, not merely unverified. The coordinating session correctly diagnosed my first mutation as too coarse - removing cache.clear() entirely breaks sign-out, so a pre-existing assertion at check-ui.ts:1265 intercepted it. It proposed a narrower one: clear ONLY the session key and leave the data keys cached, so sign-out still completes and redirects (1265 passes) while the next owner screens can repopulate from the previous owner data. That is the honest analogue of a real regression - someone optimising logout to clear less than everything. I ran it: cache.clear() replaced with cache.removeQueries({ queryKey: [session] }), mutation verified present, typecheck clean. THE FULL SUITE PASSED, exit 0. My CS-36 block did not notice. WHY, and it is a genuine limitation rather than a bug in the mutation: React Query serves stale cached data instantly on mount and then refetches. My assertions run after waitFor() on the new owner positive anchor, by which time the refetch has completed and replaced the stale data. So the test proves FINAL-STATE owner isolation across a session boundary - which is real and worth having - but NOT the transient cache flash, and AC2 "old requests or caches cannot restore prior-session data" is arguably about exactly that flash. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE TICKET: AC2 test clause is still NOT satisfied. Catching the flash needs an assertion that observes the first paint after navigation rather than the settled state - a different technique from anything else in this suite. I am not claiming AC2 as tested, and a reviewer should not accept it as such on the strength of a green run. RECORDED AS A WIN ANYWAY: the narrow mutation turned an ambiguous caveat into a definite answer in one ten-minute run. A falsification that PASSES is the most useful kind of negative result - it tells you the check is decorative before anyone relies on it.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND, AND IT INVALIDATES BOTH MY FIX AND THE PROPOSED ONE. The review diagnosed three causes for the CS-36 block being decorative (timing; getByText cannot read form controls; secrets belonging to the wrong session) and proposed a four-line fix asserting Full Name via .inputValue() on /resume, since profile-editor uses queryKey [profile] with staleTime Infinity and therefore never refetches. All three of its causes are CONFIRMED and its reasoning about staleTime is correct. I implemented the fix. IT STILL DOES NOT WORK, and I ran the experiments rather than assuming. (1) Selective clear on the logout path only: suite PASSED. (2) Suspecting my own new P3 fix was masking it - the unauthenticated resolve clears the cache right after logout - I disabled BOTH reset paths: suite STILL PASSED. (3) Inspecting the block itself gave the answer. THE BLOCK NAVIGATES WITH page.goto() FOR EVERY ROUTE. That is a FULL DOCUMENT LOAD. React Query cache is in-memory with no persister, so it is destroyed by any document navigation regardless of whether cache.clear() ran. NO assertion placed after a page.goto() can ever observe cache bleed - not mine, and not the proposed .inputValue() one, which also uses page.goto. The test was measuring server state the whole time, which is why it could never distinguish a working reset from a broken one.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY TEST AC2, recorded so the next attempt does not repeat this: the navigation must be CLIENT-SIDE - sidebar links or router pushes - so the document and its cache survive the sign-out/sign-in boundary. Only then is there a cache to bleed. Combined with the review other correct points (use .inputValue() for form controls, assert the value held by the IMMEDIATELY preceding session), that is a testable design. THE STRUCTURAL ALTERNATIVE IS BETTER AND THE REVIEW WAS RIGHT TO RATE IT ABOVE ANY TEST: [profile], [leads, status] and [resumes] are all OWNER-AGNOSTIC keys, which is precisely WHY one owner cache can serve another. Keyed as [profile, ownerId] a different owner simply misses the cache and the entire bug class becomes UNREPRESENTABLE rather than tested. That is the same move as CS-57 keying on routeOptions.url and CS-56 constraining at extraction. It would also make this whole falsification problem moot. HONEST STATUS: AC2 test clause UNMET. I am not claiming otherwise after four attempts. What IS delivered and does work: the block proves FINAL-STATE owner isolation across a session boundary on five surfaces as a second real owner, with positive anchors preventing vacuous passes. That is worth keeping; it is just not what AC2 asks for.

P3 FIXED (review finding, 2026-09-25): authenticated-shell.tsx had a THIRD teardown path that did not clear the cache - "if (session.isSuccess && !authenticated) router.replace(/)". A session resolving unauthenticated WITHOUT a 401, so api() never dispatches SESSION_EXPIRED_EVENT, redirected while leaving every data key intact. Now calls cache.clear() first. All three teardown paths verified present at authenticated-shell.tsx:43, :69 and :83. This fix is also what masked experiment (1) above, which is itself evidence it closed a real gap: with it in place, a broken logout reset is compensated by the unauthenticated-resolve reset. Defence in depth for the product, and a complication for testing - both worth knowing.
