CS38-1 GUARD ATTEMPTED 2026-09-25 AND NOT DELIVERED - reverted after a timebox. Recording the attempt because a failed approach with a known stopping point is worth more to the next person than silence. THE RULE IS PRECISE AND SHOULD BE TESTABLE: countLabel() in dashboard/page.tsx returns String(items.length) when nextCursor is null and `${items.length}+` when it is not, so the displayed count never presents a capped page as a total. The stat card renders immediately before Saved jobs, which is a stable user-visible anchor. WHAT I BUILT: a two-case loop intercepting GET /api/leads?status=saved&limit=50 to return two items with and without a nextCursor, asserting the rendered value by EQUALITY (2+ then 2). Equality is bidirectional by construction - a countLabel collapsed to always-N fails the paginated case and always-N+ fails the complete case - which is the property the reviewer praised in CS-13 AC3 and is stronger than the presence/absence pair I first wrote. WHY IT WAS REVERTED: the interception never took effect. The rendered value never became 2+, and page.waitForFunction timed out across three successive attempts with two different locator strategies (a filter() over nested divs, then an xpath preceding-sibling on the label). I verified the URL predicate matches the real request path and query, and confirmed every earlier lead-list route in the file is properly unrouted, so a leftover handler is ruled out. The cause was NOT identified. STATUS UNCHANGED AND HONEST: CS38-1 (the no-invented-total rule is guarded by nothing) and CS38-2 (AC3 stale/paginated/failing matrix does not exist) both REMAIN OPEN. What the CS-13 work already contributes to AC3 is real - empty and failing dashboard states are exercised at 320, 768 and 1440 across three engines - so the matrix is partially covered for empty and failing, and uncovered for populated, stale and paginated. NEXT ATTEMPT SHOULD START BY DIAGNOSING THE INTERCEPT, not by rewriting the assertion: one run that logs the actual rendered statValue and whether the route handler fired would settle in a single cycle what three assertion rewrites could not. I stopped rather than spend a fourth cycle guessing, which is the same call I made on CS-36 after four failed test designs.

evidence: STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-24 from DISCOVERY to READY - this ticket was BEHIND reality, not ahead of it. Its premise, that Preparation and Career Links are not reachable through dedicated navigation, is obsolete. Verified against current bytes: /preparation and /career-resources are real routes in v2/apps/web/src/app/(app)/, both render through the shared AuthenticatedShell auth boundary, and both appear as real sidebar and mobile-nav entries in dashboard-shell.tsx navItems with working hrefs. The repaired browser suite already asserts both destinations by label AND href, and exercises the Career Links filter/empty states and the Preparation absent-profile, unavailable and retry states. So AC1 is substantially DONE. Deliberately NOT promoted further than READY: AC2 (preparation grounded in the saved profile and the rules-v1 contract, distinguishing absent profile from unavailable result without implying AI or job-specific assessment) and AC3 (resource provenance, static/curated scope, safe external-link behaviour) were not systematically verified in this run, and this ticket had ZERO evidence entries before today.

AC2 EVIDENCE 2026-09-25, gathered from source rather than asserted. "Keep preparation grounded in the saved profile and rules-v1 contract; distinguish absent profile, unavailable result and retry without implying AI or job-specific assessment." GROUNDED IN THE SAVED PROFILE: the caption renders report.data.profileRevision, the actual saved revision, so the screen names the exact profile version it reviewed. THREE STATES ARE GENUINELY DISTINGUISHED, each with correct semantics: absent profile is a role="status" reading "Save a profile to prepare your review and practice questions."; unavailable is a role="alert" carrying the real error; retry is an explicit Refresh button, disabled while fetching. Loading is a fourth, role="status" with a spinner. THE "WITHOUT IMPLYING AI" CLAUSE WAS ACTIVELY VIOLATED UNTIL TODAY, and this is why the ticket could not be evidenced before: the screen rendered the fixed string "AI inference off" while simultaneously showing live "Get AI coaching" buttons - a direct self-contradiction whenever AI was enabled. That is CS-48 F-1, now fixed at the source of truth (a real capability flag on GET /api/session) rather than by editing the wording. With AI off the screen says "AI inference off" and shows no AI control at all; with AI on it says "optional AI coaching available" and the control appears. Either way the screen and the system agree. The check-ui suite already exercises this screen end to end across chromium, firefox and webkit - the absent-profile status, the Interview Practice heading, the rules-based caption bound to the real saved revision, a forced 503 producing the alert, and Refresh recovering - and passes. NOT YET EVIDENCED, stated plainly: AC3 (Career Links resource provenance, static/curated scope explicit, safe external-link behaviour, filter/empty/error states) has NOT had the same systematic pass. The suite covers the filter and the empty state, but provenance and external-link safety were not verified. This ticket stays READY, not QA, on that basis.

AC3 WORKED CRITERION-CLAUSE BY CLAUSE, and it split: three clauses were already satisfied and one was genuinely NOT. ALREADY SATISFIED, verified at source: "without introducing external fetching or inference" - careerResources in career-links-view.tsx is a module-level constant of eight entries, with no fetch, no API call and no inference anywhere in the component. "Preserve safe external-link behavior" - every link already carried target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" and every URL is an https literal. "Verify filter/empty states" - the filter matches on name and category, and the empty case renders role="status" "No resources found.", both already exercised by the cross-engine suite. ON THE ERROR STATE: there is none, and that is CORRECT rather than a gap. The list is static with nothing that can fail - no request, no parse, no external dependency at render time. Inventing an error state for a code path that cannot occur would be fabricating UI. Recorded so a later reader does not read its absence as an oversight.

AC3 CLAUSE GENUINELY NOT MET, now fixed: "keep resource provenance and static/curated scope EXPLICIT". Nothing on screen said what the list was. Eight links under a heading reading "Resources" can reasonably be read as personalised, ranked, or kept current - it is none of those. Added a line stating it is a fixed, hand-picked list that ships with CareerScope, not personalised, not ranked, not checked for freshness, opening on the provider own site in a new tab. This is the same honesty rule that made the preparation screen report its real AI capability instead of a hardcoded caption (CS-48 F-1): a screen must not imply more than the system does. It is functional labelling, not styling - no spacing, typography, colour or layout was touched, so the UI freeze holds.

BOTH PROPERTIES ARE NOW ASSERTED IN check-ui.ts ACROSS THREE ENGINES, because both are silently losable - the provenance line is one deletion away, and rel="noopener noreferrer" is exactly the attribute an unrelated refactor drops with nobody noticing. A tab opened with target="_blank" and no rel can reach back through window.opener. The assertion iterates EVERY rendered resource link and requires https, target="_blank", and both noopener and noreferrer, with an explicit length > 0 guard so an empty list fails loudly instead of vacuously passing. PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL: removing rel="noopener noreferrer" produces "chromium career resource lacks noopener/noreferrer: https://remoteok.com/ rel=\"\"" and exit 1. Restored, suite green on chromium, firefox and webkit, exit 0. PROCESS NOTE, and the rule earned its keep again: my FIRST attempt at this falsification failed to apply - a Python quoting error inside PowerShell - and the verification step caught it before I ran anything, because the printed line still showed rel present. Under the old habit that would have been a green run reported as a falsification. Redone with a script file that asserts its own precondition.

F-1 CLOSED 2026-09-25 - the sixth unguarded-property finding tonight, and the second caught before it could rot. The suite pinned the preparation CAPTION exactly but nothing pinned the BUTTON, so deleting "if (session.data?.aiEnabled !== true) return null;" from AiElaborate would have left the suite green while silently restoring CS-48 F-1: the control reappears with AI off and 503s on click. Fixed by asserting ABSENCE, which is the honest assertion in this environment since AI_ENABLED is false: the "Get AI coaching" trigger must not exist at all when the server reports no provider. PROVEN with the reviewer exact scenario, mutation verified present first: removing the gate produces "chromium the AI coaching trigger renders while the server reports no AI provider", exit 1. Restored, green on chromium, firefox and webkit, exit 0.

AC3 ERROR-STATE CLAIM STRENGTHENED from an absence into a positive architectural statement, per the reviewer recommendation - and it is a better answer than mine was. My evidence said "there is no error state and that is correct because the list is static". True, and confirmed: module-level constant, no fetch, no async, no parse, nothing that can fail. But as written it invites the objection "what about the session?". THE COMPLETE ANSWER: the only failable dependency IS handled, one level up. AuthenticatedShell renders session.isError into an ErrorState with onRetry, and every (app) route including /career-resources renders through it. So the screen DOES have an error state - it is OWNED BY THE SHARED SHELL rather than duplicated per screen, which is precisely what CS-13 exists to achieve. Recording it this way makes it much harder to misread later as a gap.

STANDARD WORDING ADOPTED 2026-09-25 from CS-39, which stated the claim, its ceiling and its unlock in one line: "All three criteria met and asserted. Promotable on a green CI run; not promoted here." Every ticket in this cohort now carries the same sentence, plus the second bar discovered later - local execution on Node v22.23.2 against a declared floor of 24. NO QA TICKET IS PROMOTABLE TONIGHT ON EXECUTION EVIDENCE, and that is ONE GATE rather than nineteen separate problems.

WORDING CORRECTED 2026-09-25 FROM "All applicable criteria met" TO THE COUNTED FORM. The distinction is not cosmetic: "ALL THREE CRITERIA MET" IS FALSIFIABLE BY COUNTING; "ALL APPLICABLE CRITERIA MET" CANNOT FAIL, because an unmet criterion can be reclassified as not-applicable without anyone editing a number. It is the same shape as \bsurfaced\b, DEFERRED and eol=crlf - a word anyone can write that silently changes how a claim is graded - except that this one sat in the STATUS FIELD OF TEN TICKETS, which is the field a promotion decision reads. That makes it the most consequential of the four, not the least.

THIS TICKET IS WHERE THE PHRASE PROPAGATED FROM, and the correction is recorded here rather than only on the tickets that inherited it. Its currentStep was quoted as the cohort standard at least six times, AS "All three criteria" - while the field actually read "All applicable criteria". THE STRONGER FORM WAS BEING QUOTED WHILE THE WEAKER FORM WAS SPREADING, under cover of the quotation. Ten tickets carried the weakened form and NOT ONE carried a counted form.

SCOPE OF THE CORRECTION, stated so it is not over-read: replacing the phrase makes each tickets EXISTING claim falsifiable. It does NOT re-verify the criteria - each ticket asserted its criteria were met when the wording was applied, and that assertion is unchanged. What changes is that a wrong one can now be caught by counting. If any of the ten is wrong, the counted form is what will expose it.

WHERE A CRITERION GENUINELY DOES NOT APPLY, IT MUST BE NAMED AND REASONED - "AC2 does not apply because no nonce strategy was adopted", in the manner of CS-34 AC3 - rather than letting the word "applicable" carry the exemption silently. THE REMEDY IS THE SAME AS THE OTHER THREE: MAKE THE EXEMPTION VISIBLE RATHER THAN FORBIDDEN. A named, reasoned exclusion is fine; an unnamed one is a check that cannot fail.

SWEEP BOUNDS THE CLASS: eleven hedging forms were searched across every tickets currentStep, summary and completedSteps - applicable, where relevant, as appropriate, substantially, effectively met, largely, essentially, for practical purposes, in spirit, materially met, to the extent. RESULT: "applicable" 10, EVERYTHING ELSE 0. One word, ten tickets, nothing else.

THAT IS A MATERIALLY BETTER STATEMENT THAN "we found a hedge", and it is the instance-versus-class question applied to the finding itself. It means the record does NOT hedge habitually, the problem has a single shape, and correcting those ten CLOSES THE CLASS IN THE BACKLOG rather than one instance of it. It also predicts the corrected form will hold: if the record hedged habitually, replacing one word would invite the next one. It does not.

RE-SWEPT AFTER THE EDITS, because a corrected sentence that quietly reintroduced a hedge would be the most ironic possible outcome: ALL ELEVEN PATTERNS NOW RETURN 0 IN EVERY STATUS-BEARING FIELD. The word survives only inside evidence entries that QUOTE the old wording in order to explain the correction, which is where it belongs.

AND THE COUNTED FORM WAS THEN EXERCISED RATHER THAN TRUSTED - the whole point of a falsifiable claim is that somebody falsifies it. Each of the ten counted claims was checked against its tickets REAL acceptanceCriteria length: CS-35 3/3, CS-39 3/3, CS-52 4/4, CS-56 3/3, CS-57 3/3, CS-63 3/3, CS-65 2/2, CS-66 3/3, CS-71 3/3, CS-74 3/3. TEN OF TEN AGREE. Under the old wording that check was not possible at all.

COUNT NOT YET RE-TAKEN 2026-09-25, recorded as owed work rather than left as an unverified claim. When "All applicable criteria met" was replaced with the counted form across ten tickets, THE WORDING WAS CORRECTED AND THE COUNT WAS NOT. Two of the ten were then found wrong within minutes - CS-74 (AC3 half-met) and CS-52 (AC4 unmet) - so the remaining eight cannot be assumed right. A COUNTED CLAIM OVER AN UNCOUNTED CRITERION IS NO BETTER THAN THE HEDGE IT REPLACED; it is only more falsifiable, and falsifying it is the outstanding work.

THE WORDING CORRECTION PROVED ITSELF WITHIN MINUTES, ON THE FIRST TICKET TO ADOPT IT. CS-74 took the counted form and a wrong count was found almost immediately - AC3 half-met - and CS-52 followed with AC4 unmet. THAT IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE CHANGE, DEMONSTRATED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: "applicable" had been concealing exactly this, and removing it surfaced two wrong counts in one pass.

AND IT IS THE LESSON AGAINST THIS SESSION: THE FORM WAS CORRECTED AND THE COUNT WAS NOT RE-TAKEN. Ten tickets were re-worded in one edit, with an explicit note that the criteria had not been re-verified - which was honest but insufficient, because the counted sentence reads as a verified claim regardless of a caveat recorded elsewhere. The remaining eight now say so IN THE STATUS FIELD ITSELF rather than in an evidence entry nobody promoting a ticket would reach.

TOKEN SCAN 2026-09-25 RETURNED CLEAN FOR THIS TICKET - every criterion is named by identifier somewhere in the evidence. RECORDED AT ITS REAL STRENGTH AND NO HIGHER: THAT MEANS "NO CRITERION IS UNMENTIONED", NOT "ALL CRITERIA ARE MET". The COUNT NOT YET RE-TAKEN label STAYS, because a proxy that asks whether the token AC2 appears is not asking whether AC2 is satisfied. Nothing suggests a problem here; nothing has verified one either.

COUNT NOT RE-TAKEN AND THE LABEL DELIBERATELY KEPT 2026-09-25 - THIS IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME, NOT A GAP. Its three criteria concern REACHABLE NAVIGATION, PREPARATION STAYING GROUNDED IN THE SAVED PROFILE, AND PROVENANCE REMAINING EXPLICIT. NONE OF THOSE IS SETTLED BY READING A FILE - they need the browser suite or a human, and both are gated. A source read would produce a confident number about something it cannot observe.

SO CS-39 IS THE ONE TICKET OF THE EIGHT WHERE THE HONEST PLACEHOLDER SURVIVES THE RE-TAKE, AND IT SURVIVES FOR A REASON THAT IS ITSELF EVIDENCE: the criteria are UI-level. Converting it would have been the counted-claim-over-an-uncounted-criterion defect in its purest form - a number produced by a method structurally incapable of reaching the property.

items.title: Saved search domain and UI discovery
items.userProblem: Reusable search criteria need a durable owner-scoped definition distinct from an executed run or a scheduled search.
items.source: ChatGPT TICKET-PLAN-20260920 proposal; owner approved discovery recording only; source validation pending
acceptanceCriteria: Define versioned owner-scoped saved criteria, edit/disable semantics, validation and revision-conflict behavior separately from immutable run snapshots
Specify and test create/read/edit/disable contracts with valid, malformed, foreign-owner and stale-revision fixtures before page implementation
Keep scheduling off; any later execution integration must satisfy CS-26 and receive explicit activation approval, while manual reuse must retain normal run limits and idempotency
evidence: AC1 DELIVERED 2026-09-25: docs/SAVED-SEARCH-DOMAIN.md. It defines the versioned owner-scoped saved criteria and, centrally, WHY they must be separate from the immutable run snapshot - search_runs.request is a historical record that match evidence, idempotency and the audit trail all depend on never changing, so if editing criteria rewrote it, every stored match score would become evidence for a query that no longer exists. One mutable versioned definition, many immutable snapshots taken from it. That is the same shape as the existing profileRevision column, so it follows precedent rather than inventing a second pattern.

ENTITY GROUNDED IN THE REAL SCHEMA, not invented: criteria is the existing CreateSearch (commands.ts - query 2..160, useProfileTitles, sources 1..5) validated with THE SAME schema the pipeline uses rather than a copy, because a second definition would drift and the first drift would make a saved search un-runnable while still passing its own validation. ONE DELIBERATE EXCLUSION WITH A SECURITY REASON: origin is EXCLUDED from stored criteria. It describes how a run was triggered, not what the owner is looking for, and storing it would let a saved search assert its future runs are "scheduled" - precisely the execution authority AC3 forbids. origin stays a property of the run, supplied at execution time. Revision conflicts follow ProfileRevisionConflict exactly, with a DISTINCT code SAVED_SEARCH_REVISION_CONFLICT rather than a reused one, because CS-35 established that route-reachable conflicts carry distinct client-actionable codes and the client allowlist decides per code whether to offer discard-and-reload. A saved-search conflict and a profile conflict need different offers. Optimistic rather than locked: the conflicting case is one owner with two tabs, and a lock would add a held-resource failure mode to an application that has none. Disable is a TIMESTAMP and is not delete - hard-deleting would leave historical runs pointing at criteria that no longer exist, and a timestamp answers WHEN, which a boolean cannot. Delete is explicitly out of scope. Names are deliberately NOT unique per owner, with the reasoning recorded.

AC2 HALF SATISFIED - SPECIFIED, NOT TESTED, and stated plainly rather than implied. The four contracts (create/read/edit/disable) are specified with their inputs, successes and failure modes, including that a foreign-owner id returns 404 and never 403 because a 403 confirms the id exists and is an enumeration oracle. The four fixture classes AC2 names are specified with the traps recorded: valid must assert the revision ACTUALLY ADVANCED because asserting no-error passes against a no-op write; malformed covers empty/oversize query, zero and six sources, unknown source id, whitespace-only name and extra keys, and must FAIL rather than be silently coerced; foreign-owner must use a SECOND REAL OWNER row by its real id, not a random uuid, because a random id only proves unknown ids 404 which is a weaker claim - the CS-51 lesson; stale revision must test BOTH revision-1 and revision+1, since testing only the low side passes against an implementation comparing < rather than !==. And the specific check-that-cannot-fail trap for this domain is recorded: an assertion that a foreign-owner read returns no data passes trivially against a broken query returning nothing to anybody, so every negative must be paired with a positive on the same surface in the same test.

NOT DONE AND NOT DISGUISED: no schema, no migration, no repository, no route, no tests. The executable half of AC2 is missing, so this ticket STAYS IN DISCOVERY and is deliberately not promoted. The choice is recorded in the document itself: under time pressure a design that specifies testable contracts is genuinely useful to whoever implements it, whereas a half-written schema plus a few passing tests would LOOK like more progress and be worth less. The remaining work is listed in order - schema and forward-only migration on a disposable database, then the repository and conflict class, then the contract tests each proven able to fail, then routes, and only then any UI. AC3 SATISFIED: the document states that saving grants no execution authority, that CS-26 remains the gate for anything unattended, that a manual re-run is an ordinary run under the same rate limits and idempotency rules, that a disabled search may not execute, and that excluding origin makes "this search runs itself" unrepresentable rather than merely disallowed.

CONVERGENCE NOTE, recorded because this one differs in kind from the other five: the origin exclusion is the FIRST PREVENTIVE application of the principle rather than a remedial one. CS-57 (routeOptions.url), CS-56 (extraction-time constraint), CS-13 F-2 (what+detail), CS-52 (script registration) and CS-61 (owner-scoped keys) each made an EXISTING defect class unrepresentable - the bug was found, then the shape that permits it was removed. This one removes the shape before anyone could write the defect. Rather than stating "saved searches must not schedule themselves" as a rule in a document someone has to remember, the data model has no field in which a saved search could say "I run myself". The claim is not disallowed; it is inexpressible. ALSO WORTH PRESERVING from the design, each a lesson applied forward rather than merely remembered: validating with the SAME schema rather than a copy, because two validators that agree today diverge silently tomorrow and the first drift would make a saved search un-runnable while still passing its own validation - a check-that-cannot-fail in schema form; and a DISTINCT conflict code rather than reusing ProfileRevisionConflict, because reusing it would have compiled, passed, and offered the wrong recovery action to the owner - CS-35 lesson applied to a ticket written before CS-35 was fixed.
REVIEWER VERDICT 2026-09-25: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS. All findings FIXED IN THE DOCUMENT by this session (docs/** is owned here). Ticket correctly remains DISCOVERY.

F-1 FIXED (P1, the serious one) - THE SECURITY PROPERTY WAS DEFEATED BY A ZOD DEFAULT, and the document named no mechanism for the exclusion. It said criteria is CreateSearch MINUS origin, and separately that validation REUSES the pipeline schema rather than copying it. Those cannot both be executed: commands.ts:44 is origin: z.enum([...]).optional().default("manual"), and a .default() FIRES ON undefined, so parsing criteria that omit origin ADDS it. An implementer following the document literally would have stored origin on every saved search - the exact execution authority the document forbids two paragraphs earlier.

F-1 REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY by the orchestrator before writing the fix, not accepted on report: input keys query,sources -> parsed keys origin,query,sources, origin injected -> "manual". The fix written into the document is createSearchSchema.omit({ origin: true }) - a DERIVATION, not a copy, so the no-drift argument survives intact. ALSO VERIFIED WITH A PAIRED POSITIVE the finding did not include, because "it omits origin" is equally true of a schema that validates nothing: the derived schema STILL rejects extra keys (.strict) and STILL rejects duplicate sources.

F-1 LESSON, recorded in AGENT-SETUP.md because it INVERTS THIS PROJECTS FAVOURITE PRINCIPLE: origin exclusion was logged as the sixth convergence and the only PREVENTIVE one, and it is the single instance where the mechanism did not deliver the intent. Stating that a state is unrepresentable is A CLAIM ABOUT A TYPE SYSTEM, and claims about type systems are testable - parse a fixture and look at the keys. Until then "cannot be expressed" is prose, and prose does not constrain an implementer who reuses the schema you told them to reuse.

F-2 FIXED (the second implementable defect) - FOLLOWING THE DOCUMENT EXACTLY RECREATED CS-35s BUG. It required a distinct SAVED_SEARCH_REVISION_CONFLICT code and correctly pointed at the CLIENT allowlist, but never mentioned the SERVER table: app.ts:168 conflictMessages, with the fallback at ~:200 rendering an unmapped code as "Idempotency conflict" - exactly the mislabelling CS-35 was opened to fix. Both source facts verified. The document now requires BOTH registrations and states the real test: a stale-revision edit must reach the owner carrying the saved-search message rather than the generic fallback.

F-3 FIXED: the quoted schema excerpt elided .strict() - the ONLY reason the "extra keys" malformed fixture rejects - and the duplicate-sources .refine(), a real rejection path. Both are now in the excerpt with a note saying why each is there, so the fixtures do not look like they test something the schema does not do.

F-4 FIXED: sources is sorted on parse, so a reorder-only edit parses byte-identical - which put "increments on every accepted mutation" and "assert the revision actually advanced" in direct conflict. Settled in one rule: an identical-result mutation is a NO-OP that does not advance revision and is not an error, so the valid fixture must change the stored value rather than reorder. Also states the failure mode - a reorder fixture asserting an advance would fail against a CORRECT implementation and get "fixed" by bumping revision on every request.

F-5 FIXED: "the same idempotency rules" read as "derive the key the same way", and CS-26s deterministic scheduled-<UTC day> key would have collapsed two legitimate manual re-runs into a 409. The document now states that a manual run supplies a FRESH key and that "same rules" means the same guarantees, not the same key.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 15:45 IST on 2026-09-25 this verdict should be re-taken rather than trusted.

F-2 INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED AT SOURCE 2026-09-25 AND IT IS A REAL FINDING, NOT A THEORETICAL ONE. SAVED_SEARCH_REVISION_CONFLICT IS ABSENT FROM app.ts conflictMessages - verified, and verified further to be absent from ALL tracked v2 source, so nothing else registers it either. The table maps eight codes; this is not one of them.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS EXACT, because the fallback at app.ts:202 is conflictMessages[error.code] ?? "Idempotency conflict": A STALE-REVISION EDIT ON A SAVED SEARCH WOULD BE RENDERED TO THE OWNER AS AN IDEMPOTENCY CONFLICT. AN UNMAPPED CODE DOES NOT FAIL LOUDLY - IT MISLABELS QUIETLY, which is the worse of the two.

AND THE IRONY IS THE POINT, WORTH KEEPING AS THE REASON THE DESIGN REVIEW MATTERED: THAT MISLABELLING IS PRECISELY WHAT CS-35 WAS OPENED TO FIX, AND THE conflictMessages TABLE EXISTS TO PREVENT IT. A DESIGN THAT CITES CS-35 AS ITS PRECEDENT WOULD HAVE REINTRODUCED CS-35 BUG - because it registered the new code in the class and not in the table, and only one of those two places is where the user-visible string is chosen.

THE GENERAL RULE: A NEW CODE HAS TO BE REGISTERED IN TWO PLACES, AND THE ONE THAT IS EASY TO FORGET IS THE ONE THE USER SEES. The design doc already records this at its own ~:192; the confirmation here is that the omission is live in current source, so the doc guidance is load-bearing rather than cautionary.

THIRD DEFECT FROM THE SAME origin: z.enum([...]).optional().default("manual"), CONFIRMED 2026-09-25. The tally is now: (1) the design silently storing the field it forbade, found by a security design review; (2) a signature rejecting every valid call in the test suite, found by a build-configuration fix; (3) A FALSE IDEMPOTENCY COLLISION ON UNSORTED sources, found only because a half-right prescription was attempted and ITS FAILURE WAS INVESTIGATED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND.

THREE DEFECTS, ONE ZOD DEFAULT, THREE UNRELATED ROUTES, AND NO ROUTE WOULD HAVE FOUND THE OTHERS. That is the strongest evidence this run produced that a single modelling choice propagates further than the ticket introducing it - and the argument for reviewing schema defaults as interface decisions rather than conveniences.

AND THE THIRD IS THE ONE WORTH GENERALISING: A FIX THAT FAILS FOR AN UNEXPECTED REASON IS AN OBSERVATION. The instinct to reach for a cast at that moment discards it. Here the unexpected TS2769 in production code was the only thing that revealed the storage and idempotency coupling.

items.title: Alerts domain and notification semantics discovery
items.userProblem: Repeated or stale job sightings must not become duplicate or misleading notifications.
items.source: ChatGPT TICKET-PLAN-20260920 proposal; owner approved discovery recording only; source validation pending
acceptanceCriteria: Define owner-scoped alert identity, repeat-sighting deduplication, freshness, read/dismiss and retention semantics with no inference that an uncertain or old job is closed
Specify replay, duplicate, malformed and foreign-owner negative cases and bounded delivery/retry budgets before choosing an implementation
Keep email providers, background delivery and scheduling disabled pending separate approval; any later scheduled integration must satisfy CS-26 and existing outbox/idempotency contracts
evidence: AC1 DELIVERED 2026-09-25: docs/ALERTS-DOMAIN.md. Central decision - an alert is a SIGHTING RECORD, not a notification. Modelled as a notification its identity would be tied to a delivery, so re-delivery would mean re-alerting; modelled as a sighting record, delivery becomes an optional projection and "did we already tell them" is answered by state on the record rather than by remembering what was sent. That is what lets AC3 hold without a placeholder delivery mechanism.

IDENTITY GROUNDED IN THE REAL SCHEMA, not invented: job_sightings is already keyed (ownerId, fingerprint) with firstSeenAt, lastSeenAt and a distinct-searches count, and already demonstrates the required pattern - a posting seen again updates lastSeenAt, it does not become a new row. The alert key extends it by savedSearchId (CS-42) DELIBERATELY: the same posting matching two different saved searches is two different pieces of information, and keyed only by (ownerId, fingerprint) the second match would be silently swallowed.

AC1 FRESHNESS FOLLOWS CS-27 IMPLEMENTATION, NOT ITS DOCS: check-lead-liveness.ts defines CheckResult = live | stale | unknown and returns unknown for a blocked dispatcher, an unresolvable host and too many redirects, reserving stale for an unambiguous 404/410. Alerts must carry that three-state vocabulary through to the owner and MUST NOT collapse unknown into stale. Two inferences are forbidden by name: an uncertain posting is not a closed posting, and an OLD posting is not a closed posting - age is not evidence. Retention may REMOVE an old alert; nothing may REINTERPRET it as closed.

AC1 RE-MATCH RULE IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO REGRESS: re-matching must not clear readAt or dismissedAt. Dismissal is about the posting, not about the sighting - resurrecting a dismissed alert because the job was seen again would make dismissal useless exactly for the postings an owner sees most often. Stated with its consequence: a discovery run returning the same 40 postings daily must produce ZERO new alerts; if it produces 40 the symptom is an owner who stops reading alerts entirely.

AC2 SPECIFIED, NOT TESTED (half met): replay, duplicate, malformed, foreign-owner and deleted-saved-search behaviours are defined, plus four testing traps. Alert-specific trap: the dedup test must run the same match TWICE and assert count is still 1 - asserting "an alert exists" after ONE match passes against an implementation with no deduplication at all. Also carried forward: pair every negative with a positive on the same surface (a foreign-owner "no alert" assertion passes trivially against a pipeline producing no alerts for anybody), and unknown must be asserted DISTINCTLY from stale or the test passes against the exact defect AC1 forbids.

AC2 DELIVERY BUDGETS SPECIFIED BEFORE ANY DELIVERY EXISTS, so they are bounded from the start rather than after the first incident: per-owner cap with overflow SUMMARISED rather than dropped ("and 12 more" is information, silence is not); retries reuse the existing outbox/idempotency contracts rather than a second delivery mechanism; an exhausted retry budget must never mark an alert read or dismissed as a side effect of a delivery problem; no unbounded fan-out (500 matches is one summarised notification, never 500).

AC3 MET: no email provider, no background delivery, no scheduling, no placeholder channel. Alerts are READ, not pushed - until a channel is approved an alert is something the owner sees when they open the application, which is a complete and useful feature on its own and needs no external approval. Any later scheduled integration must satisfy CS-26 and the existing outbox/idempotency contracts rather than introducing a parallel queue.

CROSS-REFERENCES VERIFIED AT SOURCE before recording, not assumed: CS-26 = "Nothing runs discovery on a schedule" (BLOCKED, the scheduling gate), CS-27 = "Postings never expire or get re-checked" (BLOCKED, the freshness dependency), CS-28 = "Two different openings can be merged into one" (UAT, so the fingerprint identity rules alerts defer to genuinely exist rather than being assumed). CS-42 disabledAt precedent confirmed present 3x in SAVED-SEARCH-DOMAIN.md.

STATUS HELD AT DISCOVERY DELIBERATELY: AC2 executable tests are not written and no schema, repository or route exists. Same reasoning as CS-42 - a design specifying testable contracts and naming their traps is useful to whoever implements it, whereas a partial implementation would look like more progress and be worth less. AC1 and AC3 met, AC2 half met. Blocked behind CS-42 by construction: alerts are keyed by savedSearchId and cannot be built before saved searches exist.
REVIEWER VERDICT 2026-09-25: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS. All findings FIXED IN THE DOCUMENT by this session. Ticket correctly remains DISCOVERY.

F-1 FIXED (the one semantic incompatibility in the whole Tier C set) - THE DRIFT WAS PREDICTED AND IT EXISTS IN THE PREDICTED DIRECTION. The negative-case table had a row for a DELETED saved search, which CS-42 explicitly puts OUT OF SCOPE with a reason, and NO ROW AT ALL for disabledAt, which is the state CS-42 actually defines. It was written against an operation its dependency declined to provide. Load-bearing rather than cosmetic, because disabling raises three real questions and one of them collides with this documents own rules.

F-1 FIX, and the collision resolved explicitly: disabling STOPS PRODUCTION immediately (no new alerts, no lastMatchedAt updates); existing alerts REMAIN AND STAY LISTED, because they record postings the owner really was shown and hiding them destroys history rather than pausing a subscription; and re-enabling resumes production but MUST NOT alter readAt or dismissedAt and MUST NOT resurface a dismissed alert. That last is stated separately from the re-match rule precisely because re-enabling is the case an implementer is most likely to treat as "start fresh".

F-2 FIXED with the verification the reviewer could not perform: the schema column is NAMED sightings but its comment says "Distinct searches this posting has turned up in". Those are different quantities and the NAME SUGGESTS THE WRONG ONE - in a document whose entire subject is not conflating one occurrence with many. The document now relies on the documented meaning, flags the mismatch, and requires an implementer to confirm at the increment site, because a comment is an authors claim rather than proof of behaviour.

F-4 FIXED: the unknown-versus-stale trap named no fixture, and check-lead-liveness.ts reaches unknown from SIX distinct places (counted at source), several slow or awkward to stage. The document now names two fast deterministic producers - a 5xx, or a 302 with no Location header - and explicitly forbids using a timeout, which is slow and is the exact flakiness class CS-58 already records.

F-5 FIXED: "recorded as a failure" named no surface and was therefore unfalsifiable - any implementation can claim it records the failure somewhere. It now points at CS-23s existing empty/failed/completed run outcome vocabulary rather than at a log line.

items.title: Account recovery and verification lifecycle discovery
items.userProblem: Self-service recovery and verification do not have an approved sender or a complete privacy-preserving lifecycle.
items.source: ChatGPT TICKET-PLAN-20260920 proposal; owner approved discovery recording only; source validation pending
acceptanceCriteria: Document recovery/verification requirements and threat model separately from existing authenticated password change and operator recovery
Specify non-enumerating responses, bounded attempts, expiring single-use tokens, replay rejection, safe origin/link handling and session invalidation with positive, malformed and abuse fixtures
Require explicit approval of sender, domain, secret handling and security design before implementing or enabling email or recovery pages; keep registration disabled and existing recovery available
evidence: AC1 + AC3 DELIVERED 2026-09-25: docs/ACCOUNT-RECOVERY-THREAT-MODEL.md. Requirements and threat model only - no route, no token, no page, no email. Recovery is documented separately from the two surfaces that already exist and were verified at source: POST /api/account/password (authenticated, rate-limited password:${ownerId} 5/hour) and manual operator recovery. POST /api/register is confirmed disabled, returning 404 "Registration unavailable" - it already refuses to confirm it exists.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT DEFINES THE THREAT MODEL: authenticated password change is guarded by a secret only the owner knows; recovery is guarded by ACCESS TO A MAILBOX, so it is a second, weaker authentication path onto the same account whose security ceiling is an email account CareerScope does not control. Enabling it permanently changes what an attacker needs from "the password" to "the password OR the mailbox". That is why AC3s approval gate is substantive rather than procedural.

BLOCKER DISCOVERED WHILE WRITING, NOT VISIBLE FROM THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA - AC2 requires BOUNDED ATTEMPTS and recovery is unauthenticated, so there is no ownerId to key on. Both available keys are currently unusable. (1) IP keying is inert: /api/login and /api/register hash request.ip, and per CS-59 verified at source Caddy proxies over loopback in a shared network namespace with header_up -X-Forwarded-For DELETING the header, so request.ip is 127.0.0.1 for every production request. Those limiters are not per-client at all - they are ONE GLOBAL BUCKET shared by the entire internet, which any single client can exhaust for everyone. A recovery endpoint keyed the same way would satisfy "bounded attempts" on paper with a control that bounds nothing per attacker.

BLOCKER PART 2 - EMAIL KEYING TURNS THE LIMITER INTO AN ENUMERATION ORACLE, and the collision is easy to miss because each control is correct in isolation. If the limiter rejects with 429 while normal submission returns 202, the response distinguishes a repeatedly-submitted address from an unknown one - an enumeration oracle BUILT OUT OF THE CONTROL MEANT TO PREVENT ABUSE - and it lets an attacker deny a known victim recovery by exhausting their bucket deliberately. RESOLUTION, the load-bearing rule of the document: the limiter must gate the SIDE EFFECT, never the RESPONSE. A rate-limited recovery request returns the same 202 and the same body and simply sends nothing. A recovery endpoint that CAN return 429 has already failed AC2 regardless of how well its limits are tuned.

DEPENDENCY CS-59 ADDED TO THIS TICKET (was empty). CS-44 cannot honestly satisfy AC2 while every client shares one rate-limit key. Recording that dependency is the most useful output of this ticket - it would otherwise have been discovered mid-implementation, or not at all.

AC2 SPECIFIED, NOT TESTED: non-enumerating responses closed at four leakage sources rather than the obvious one (status/body, TIMING - an existing account does hash work a missing one does not, and an unmeasured constant-time claim is a check that cannot fail - error paths, and logs). Token requirements: hashed at rest like a password so a database disclosure yields no usable tokens; absolute non-sliding expiry; atomic single-use because a read-then-write check has a race; and expired must be INDISTINGUISHABLE from invalid or expiry becomes a probe for whether a token was ever real.

AC2 ORIGIN HANDLING - the reset link origin comes from server configuration, NEVER from the request. A Host or X-Forwarded-Host header echoed into an email body is a token-exfiltration primitive: the attacker submits the victims address, the victim receives a genuine email from the real sender, and the link points at the attacker. Plus no open redirect after reset, no token in a query string that survives into a referrer, and no third-party resources on the reset page.

AC2 SESSION INVALIDATION stated with its real verification: a completed reset must kill EVERY session for the account, not just the one performing it, because recoverys main legitimate use is suspected compromise and leaving the attackers session alive defeats the purpose. Verification is NOT "the user can log in with the new password" - it is that a session established BEFORE the reset no longer works.

AC2 FIXTURE TRAPS, carried forward and sharpened: every negative needs a positive on the same surface in the same test ("no email sent to the foreign address" passes against a build that sends nothing to anybody); the non-enumeration test must compare two responses BYTE FOR BYTE rather than assert each is 202 separately, because two 202s with different bodies both pass a per-response assertion and still leak; the single-use test must run CONCURRENTLY since a sequential double-redemption passes against the read-then-write race that is the defect worth catching; and the origin test must supply a hostile Host header and assert whose host the emitted link contains, not that it is well-formed.

STATUS HELD AT DISCOVERY: AC1 and AC3 met by the document, AC2 specified but no fixtures written, and implementation is gated on owner approval of sender, domain, secret handling and this security design PLUS closure of CS-59. Registration stays disabled and existing recovery stays available, per AC3. Until all four approval conditions hold the correct state is exactly the current one.

REVIEWER VERDICT 2026-09-25: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS, and assessed the STRONGEST OF THE THREE - "this one does not read as written under time pressure". Every code claim it makes verified FACT, including header_up -X-Forwarded-For in BOTH Caddyfile blocks plus trustProxy: false. All findings fixed in the document. Ticket correctly remains DISCOVERY.

F-3 FIXED - A GENUINE GAP THE DOCUMENT DID NOT NAME. It required a completed reset to invalidate every session, but said nothing about OUTSTANDING RESET TOKENS WHEN A PASSWORD CHANGES THROUGH THE AUTHENTICATED ROUTE. The sequence is the realistic one: an attacker submits the victims address so a live token exists, the victim suspects compromise and changes their password through the authenticated route, and the attackers token remains valid. The document now states that a password change through ANY route invalidates all outstanding reset tokens - a recovery token is an alternative proof of ownership, so changing the credential must retire every outstanding proof, not only the sessions. It matters because IT IS PRECISELY WHAT A COMPROMISED OWNER WILL ACTUALLY DO; they will not think to cancel a reset email they never requested.

F-1 FIXED: the CS-59 dependency WAS added to backlog.json, but the document still read as though it were outstanding and the paragraph appeared twice. Now recorded once, as a dependency already captured.

F-2 FIXED: "blocked on CS-59" read as a sequencing note. The document now says plainly that CS-59 is a PROXY-LAYER CHANGE ON A SINGLE-HOST DEPLOYMENT - the same class as the host-blocked tickets needing an operator session - and that nothing in the web or API tier can fix it, because the header is deleted before the application ever sees the request.

F-4 FIXED: the 429 fixture is now marked BLOCKED alongside the control it tests, because there is no usable rate-limit key until CS-59 is fixed and the fixture cannot be written before the limiter it asserts on exists. Marked as blocked rather than listed as merely outstanding.

F-5 FIXED: the verification-lifecycle half made the sharpest claim in the document - that an unverified account behaving differently at login IS an enumeration oracle reachable without touching recovery - and supplied no fixtures for it. A claim that sharp with nothing to falsify it is the weakest kind of assertion. Five fixtures added, with the three login responses required to be compared TO EACH OTHER byte for byte in the same test, because asserting each is a 401 separately passes while all three carry different bodies.

RECORDED AS THE POSITIVE VERDICT NOT TO BE LOST UNDER SIX FINDINGS: on the criterion that matters most - does each document name its own check-that-cannot-fail before any code exists - ALL THREE TIER C DOCUMENTS PASS. CS-44s is the sharpest, and its limiter-as-enumeration-oracle discovery converts a tuning question into a structural one: a recovery endpoint that CAN return 429 has already failed AC2, no matter how well its limits are tuned. No duplication across the three; the non-confirmation rule is consistent while correctly using DIFFERENT mechanisms for different trust contexts - 404-never-403 on authenticated surfaces, escalating to byte-identical responses and no-429 on the unauthenticated one. The escalation is principled, not accidental.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 15:45 IST on 2026-09-25 this verdict should be re-taken rather than trusted.

BLOCKER PREMISE UPGRADED TO FACT 2026-09-25: this documents CS-59 dependency rested on "request.ip is 127.0.0.1 for every production request", which compose.production.yml now settles directly (CAREERSCOPE_UPSTREAM: 127.0.0.1:5280, network_mode: service:proxy on every app service). The bounded-attempts blocker is established fact rather than inference.

MOVED DISCOVERY -> BLOCKED 2026-09-25, seventh owner gate. A ticket that ENUMERATES FOUR SPECIFIC APPROVAL CONDITIONS IS NOT EXPLORING A DESIGN SPACE - IT IS WAITING. Its own evidence already said so: gated on owner approval of sender, domain, secret handling and this security design, plus closure of CS-59, and "until all four approval conditions hold the correct state is exactly the current one". Same reasoning that moved CS-30 out of DISCOVERY earlier today; same class of misfiling.

PRESENT IT TO THE OWNER AS A PARTIAL COMPLETION, because that is what it is: AC1 AND AC3 ARE ALREADY DELIVERED in docs/ACCOUNT-RECOVERY-THREAT-MODEL.md, and only AC2 is open and specification-only. MOST OF THE WORK IS DONE AND FOUR SIGNATURES ARE MISSING - the same shape as CS-46.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; re-check if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 17:00 IST on 2026-09-25.

items.title: Remote-viewable engineering control center via Pages, and a separately-gated ticket-write path
items.userProblem: The engineering control center (scripts/engineering-ui.mjs) is deliberately loopback-only, so the owner can only see current tickets/agent state on the machine it runs on, not from a phone or a second office system.
items.source: owner request, 2026-09-21
acceptanceCriteria: Read-only remote viewing reuses the existing encrypted-admin export pattern (mobile-site/admin.enc.json, docs/ENCRYPTED-ADMIN.md): a manual, on-demand export encrypts a snapshot of .ai/backlog.json (and optionally LOOP-STATE.json/findings.json) with an owner passphrase never sent to GitHub, publishes it as a static asset alongside the existing public Pages artifact, and is decrypted client-side on request — not a live server, not real-time, and not a new always-on backend

The published snapshot excludes anything not already safe for the existing public/admin split: no secrets, credentials, resume content, private profile data, or details that would materially help an attacker (e.g. no verbatim security-finding exploit specifics beyond what already ships in this repository's own public history)
Snapshot staleness is visible in the UI (last-exported timestamp), so the owner never mistakes a stale remote view for the live loopback dashboard

Remote ticket CREATION/editing is treated as an explicitly separate, higher-risk sub-scope and is NOT authorized by this ticket: it needs its own owner-authenticated write path, integrity/audit trail, and a defined sync back into the git-tracked .ai/backlog.json (or a replacement store) — recorded here as a design question, not implemented

No new always-on public server, database, or credential store is introduced without a separate architecture/security review; the loopback control center's read-only, local-only contract is unchanged for its existing use
items.securityImpact: Publishing any engineering/ticket detail beyond localhost is a real exposure change and needs the same discipline as the existing encrypted admin snapshot; remote write access is a materially larger risk (integrity, replay, unauthorized ticket tampering) and stays unapproved until separately designed
items.architectureImpact: Read path: reuse of the existing static-Pages + encrypted-snapshot pipeline, no new service. Write path: undesigned; likely needs a real authenticated backend distinct from GitHub Pages, out of scope here
items.currentStep: Deferred discovery; read-only export approach identified, write path unresolved
items.summary: The owner wants to check tickets from a phone or another computer. The safe, buildable half is a manually-published encrypted read-only snapshot using the pattern already built for the public admin view. Being able to add tickets remotely is a much bigger, separately-gated problem and is recorded here rather than assumed.

items.title: Resume-derived matching facts have no owner approval or per-skill exclusion gate
items.userProblem: A user who reviews their parsed resume and explicitly declines a bad skill/title finds it silently reappearing in every future match, with no way to exclude it short of deleting the entire resume.
items.source: Product Architect, during CS-22 review, 2026-09-22
acceptanceCriteria: A documented, owner-confirmed product decision on whether resume-derived skills/titles are always-on supplementary evidence (current CS-22 behavior, now accurately documented rather than silently shipped) or must be gated behind an explicit per-fact approval/exclusion step before reaching matching

If exclusion is required: a per-skill/title exclude mechanism that survives across searches until the resume is re-parsed, distinct from the existing profile-editor proposal-review flow (which edits preferences.techStack directly and already works), and that composes without conflict with the always-on union in packages/matching/src/context.ts

v2/ARCHITECTURE.md's resume-integration row and packages/matching/src/context.ts's docstring stay accurate to whatever is decided - this ticket exists specifically so that reconciliation is deliberate, not accidental
evidence: v2/ARCHITECTURE.md (pre-CS-22): 'Resume metadata and resume-derived matching facts | ... owner approval and matching integration pending' - this repository's own architecture doc anticipated an approval gate before matching integration; CS-22 shipped matching integration without one

v2/apps/web/src/components/profile-editor.tsx's existing review flow lets a user edit/decline resume-derived proposals before saving to preferences.techStack - but packages/matching/src/context.ts's buildCandidateContext() separately re-reads the raw, unreviewed resume_results.parsed.derived on every search and unions it in regardless of that review step, so a declined skill is not actually excludable short of deleting the whole resume

Real Product Architect review of CS-22 (native runSubagent): 'APPROVED WITH FINDINGS' verdict, F2 - flagged this as a genuine, foreseeable design tension requiring an actual product decision, not a silent ship

VERIFIED 2026-09-24 by direct source read of packages/matching/src/context.ts: the always-on union is real and exactly as the ticket describes - skills: normalizeSkillList([...preferences.techStack, ...resumeSkills]) and titles: dedupe([...preferences.titles, ...(derived?.titles ?? [])]). No per-skill exclusion exists anywhere in the function. resolveYears() correctly treats years differently (a typed non-zero value wins over the resume guess), which confirms the union for skills/titles is a deliberate asymmetry, not an oversight.

AC3 VERIFIED ALREADY SATISFIED, no change needed: buildCandidateContext()s docstring already states verbatim "There is no per-skill exclusion - the only way to remove a resume-derived skill or title from every future match is to delete the resume itself", and v2/ARCHITECTURE.md:704 already reads "matching integration implemented (CS-22) - derived skills/titles/years now reach scoring, always-on and additive, visible in match evidence; owner approval/exclusion of specific resume-derived facts before they reach matching remains pending (see CS-46)". Both were checked against current bytes, not assumed.

DONE 2026-09-24: added a "Resume-derived matching facts cannot be excluded individually" section to docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md recording the verified current behaviour, the quoted code, the profile-editor vs buildCandidateContext divergence, the product-trust (not data-exposure) framing, and BOTH options stated neutrally for the owner to choose between. The limitation was previously absent from that file entirely.

NOT DONE, and deliberately so: option 1 has NOT been recorded as accepted and no exclusion mechanism was invented. AC1 says "owner-confirmed product decision"; the owner was unavailable for this run. Recording current behaviour as the decision would be exactly the silent reinterpretation the ticket exists to prevent. OWNER ACTION REQUIRED: choose option 1 (zero code change, ticket closes) or option 2 (per-fact exclusion gate, needs a MatchingProfile change in v2/packages/core/src/profile.ts).

COST TO CLEAR MEASURED 2026-09-25, and it is the cheapest ticket on the board: AC3 IS ALREADY SATISFIED AGAINST CURRENT BYTES (the docstring at packages/matching/src/context.ts:19-24), and AC2 applies ONLY IF OPTION 2 IS CHOSEN. So the whole ticket reduces to one binary owner choice, and OPTION 1 MEANS ZERO CODE CHANGE AND IMMEDIATE CLOSURE. What is outstanding is about sixty seconds of owner attention, not engineering.

Doing so activated a pre-existing, previously-dormant design characteristic: resume-derived skills and titles are unioned into every match permanently, with no way to exclude a specific one short of deleting the whole resume - which conflicts with the product's own documented 'explicit editable proposal' review step for the rest of the profile. This ticket is where that gets an actual decision instead of staying an accident of activation order.

items.title: Nothing watches the six unattended host timers themselves
items.userProblem: Six systemd timers now run unattended (monitor, backup, discovery, liveness, retention, proxy-recovery). If any one of them silently stops firing - a corrupted unit, an accidental disable, a full disk preventing systemd from spawning it - nothing alerts on that absence. The backup timer failing silently is the worst case: the owner would believe recoverability exists when it does not.
items.source: Owner + ChatGPT second opinion, 2026-09-23, following CS-24/25/26/27/3 all reaching UAT in the same session
acceptanceCriteria: One host-native scheduler-health checker verifies the expected last-run time/status of all six existing timers (monitor, backup, discovery, liveness, retention, proxy-recovery) and emits a single sanitized alert when any one becomes overdue, reusing the existing webhook-alerting pattern rather than inventing six separate ad-hoc checks

Documented and explicitly accepted: a local checker alone is not a true dead-man-switch, because it dies with the VPS itself - the eventual architecture (host timers -> local scheduler-health checker -> external/off-host dead-man-switch -> alert) is recorded even if the off-host leg is not built in this ticket
Priority within the fix, if attempted incrementally, follows the second-opinion ranking: HIGH - backup, monitor, proxy-recovery; MEDIUM - scheduled discovery, liveness re-check; LOWER - retention

Explicitly sequenced after the held frontend tickets (CS-6, CS-13, CS-14, CS-16, CS-17, CS-18, CS-19) - not to be folded into that work, and not to be started before the owner has had a chance to prioritize it against those
evidence: docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md - "Nothing watches the watcher" section, disclosed incrementally across CS-24/25/26/27/3

ChatGPT second opinion (owner-shared thread, 2026-09-23): acceptable as a short-term disclosed gap, but the six-timer count changes the priority; recommended one shared scheduler-health checker over six separate watchdogs, and explicit visibility to the owner in the meantime, especially for the backup timer

SIX TIMERS VERIFIED AGAINST THE REPO, not assumed: careerscope-{monitor,backup,discovery,liveness,retention,proxy-recovery} each have a .service + .timer in infra/v3. No discrepancy with the six named in the ticket. Two schedule shapes found and both handled: monitor and proxy-recovery are monotonic (OnUnitActiveSec 5min/2min); backup, discovery, liveness and retention are OnCalendar with RandomizedDelaySec 300-600s.

AC1 SATISFIED: infra/v3/scheduler-health.sh is ONE checker for all six, not six ad-hoc checks. It reads real systemd state (systemctl show: LoadState, UnitFileState, ActiveState, LastTriggerUSec, NextElapseUSec*, TimersMonotonic/Calendar, plus the triggered service Result/ActiveState/ExecMainStatus) and cross-checks systemctl list-timers. The expected interval is DERIVED FROM THE UNIT ITSELF - monotonic timers from their own OnUnitActiveUSec/OnBootUSec, calendar timers by expanding the unit own OnCalendar via systemd-analyze calendar --iterations=2 and differencing - so a schedule change in a unit file cannot silently drift from what the checker expects. It emits ONE aggregated alert reusing the existing json_escape + send_alert webhook pattern from monitor.sh/backup.sh/recover-proxy.sh (SCHEDULER_WEBHOOK_URL falling back to MONITOR_WEBHOOK_URL), https-only, edge-triggered with 6h re-notify and a one-shot recovery message.

AC3 SATISFIED AND PROVEN BEHAVIOURALLY, not just documented: grace is tiered per the ticket own HIGH/MEDIUM/LOWER ranking - backup 10% of interval (min 10m, the strictest of all six, per the ticket own reasoning that a silently dead backup is the worst case); monitor and proxy-recovery 50% (min 10m); discovery and liveness 100% (min 30m); retention 200% (min 1h). Every floor exceeds the corresponding unit RandomizedDelaySec so a randomized start is never misread as a missed run. A test asserts the ranking behaviourally: at the SAME 1.5x relative overrun, backup alerts and retention does not.

FAILURE MODES MADE STRUCTURALLY LOUD - the core of this ticket. Exit codes are deliberately NOT monitor.sh always-0 pattern: 0 = all six evaluated and healthy, 1 = a watched timer is unhealthy, 2 = STRUCTURALLY UNABLE TO VERIFY. There is no path where an unreadable state yields a healthy report. Handled as loud failures: unit not installed (LoadState != loaded); disabled or inactive; systemctl missing entirely (alert STILL sent, exit 2); systemctl erroring, empty or unparseable; LastTriggerUSec n/a, 0, epoch, absent, garbage or in the future; interval underivable (never a fallback guess); active timer with no next elapse; service Result != success; and TWO independent short-result-set assertions so fewer than six timers can never pass.

PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL: infra/v3/check-scheduler-health.sh runs 63 assertions, all PASS, exit 0. Valid input passes (exit 0, no alert). Invalid input fails: an overdue backup exits non-zero, the alert names exactly that timer and marks it HIGH, no other timer is named, exactly one aggregated alert is sent; a service with Result=failed exits non-zero. MALFORMED input fails loudly: LastTriggerUSec=n/a is reported as never having run rather than healthy; a missing unit exits 2 and REFUSES to call 5 of 6 a pass; systemctl returning garbage reports the parse failure once per timer; an empty read is reported, not swallowed; systemctl absent entirely still alerts rather than dying quietly. Real emitted messages were captured for the healthy, degraded, blind-missing-unit and blind-garbage cases.

THE TEST SUITE CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT IN THE CHECKER ITSELF during development: the recovery transition was logged to stdout as a plain "ok" while the word "recovered" reached only the webhook. Fixed by moving the notify decision above the log line. An earlier run also produced two failures caused by the TEST freezing "now" at suite start while the suite takes ~15 min under Git-bash - the checker was right and the fixtures were wrong; fixtures now stamp at write time. Recorded because a test that never caught anything is not evidence.

AC2 SATISFIED (documentation): docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md "Nothing watches the watcher" rewritten to PARTIALLY ADDRESSED (CS-47) with the off-host leg explicitly OPEN and NOT built - it records that a local checker dies with its VPS, detects a timer that stopped but not a host that stopped, and cannot watch its own timer. The four-stage architecture (host timers -> local scheduler-health checker -> external/off-host dead-man-switch -> alert) is recorded with stage three marked NOT BUILT. docs/OPERATIONS/MONITORING.md gained a "Scheduler health (CS-47)" runbook with the threshold table, exit codes, sanitization, the on-host stop-a-timer proof to run after installation, and install marked operator-only, not yet performed.

OPERATOR-ONLY AND THEREFORE UNVERIFIED - stated plainly, not implied away. setup-scheduler-health.sh has NEVER been run, on production or anywhere; no unit is installed on any host; no live systemd behaviour has been observed (everything is proven against stub systemctl/systemd-analyze/curl); no webhook has ever been posted to. HIGHEST-VALUE THING TO CHECK FIRST ON THE HOST: systemctl show timestamp/timespan property rendering varies by systemd version (raw microseconds vs human string), as does systemd-analyze "Iteration #2:" vs "Iter. #2:". The parsers accept both forms and fail loudly on anything else, so the worst case is a permanent loud false alarm rather than a silent pass - the safe direction, but noisy until confirmed on Ubuntu 24.04.

KNOWN RESIDUAL: a freshly installed watched timer reports "has never recorded a run" until it first fires (up to 24h for backup) - intentional and documented, but installation order matters. The scheduler-health timer cannot watch itself. The gap is NARROWED, not closed: this is not a dead-man-switch and must not be described as one.

ORCHESTRATOR INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION 2026-09-25, closing the gap disclosed earlier in this ticket. I re-ran infra/v3/check-scheduler-health.sh myself to completion: 69 PASS, 0 FAIL, exit 0, ending "all scheduler-health checks passed". DISCREPANCY WORTH RECORDING: the builder reported 63/63; the actual count is 69 assertions. More coverage than claimed rather than less, so this is not an inflated claim - but it does mean the builder figure was not precise, and I am recording the number I measured rather than the number I was told. The final assertions confirm the sanitization contract specifically: no double quote from a value reaches the message, no shell or HTML metacharacters reach the message, the value is capped at 64 characters, and it is still shown truncated rather than dropped silently. VERIFICATION LEVEL: LOCALLY VERIFIED and CI-WIRED (the check already runs in CI, stub-driven by design). NOT LIVE-HOST VERIFIED - setup-scheduler-health.sh has never been run, no unit is installed anywhere, and no webhook has ever been posted to. INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2026-09-25 (read-only, no shell - it did NOT run the suite and said so). VERDICT: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS - not UAT. It read check-scheduler-health.sh end to end, ACTIVELY TRIED TO MAKE IT VACUOUS AND FAILED, and calls it the best-constructed check of the four it reviewed. It credits the behavioural ranking test (backup alerts at 1.5x overrun, retention does not, at the same relative overrun), the 0/1/2 exit contract, the tr -cd allowlist and the https-only webhook that never prints a full URL. F-1 (P3 but REAL, and it defeats a whole class of assertion): the curl stub is "echo post >> $FAKE_CALLS_FILE; exit 0" - it records THAT a POST happened and DISCARDS THE BODY. Every sanitization assertion therefore runs against stdout, never against the JSON actually sent, which means json_escape() IS NEVER EXERCISED BY ANY TEST. The 69 assertions I independently verified include sanitization checks that are, on this reading, checking the wrong stream. FIX: have the stub write its -d argument to a file and assert the payload parses as JSON and that the escaping held. NOT YET FIXED. Also noted: names() and occurrences() are byte-identical duplicate functions in the same file. ITS STATUS VERDICT, which I accept verbatim: "a watchdog that has never watched anything on the host it protects cannot be accepted."

items.title: Initial optional AI provider: OpenRouter free-model only
items.userProblem: CareerScope has no AI-assisted capability at all today (v2/ARCHITECTURE.md: "Inference is off... AI is DEFERRED - INTENTIONAL"). The owner wants an initial, strictly-scoped AI capability - lead-note summarization, follow-up suggestions and plain-English explanations of already-computed deterministic evidence - using only OpenRouter free (:free) models, off by default, with no paid fallback and no risk to the deterministic matching/exclusion/ranking/application engine.
items.source: Owner, 2026-09-23 - full written specification supplied directly
acceptanceCriteria: A new, separate AI-provider abstraction exists (does not touch or repurpose the existing local-Ollama-only inference.ts, which is deliberately hosted-provider-hostile by design and stays that way) with a swappable provider interface so a future provider/model change does not require rewriting call sites

Config: AI_ENABLED (default false), OPENROUTER_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_MODEL (must end :free, explicit id required - openrouter/free wildcard rejected). Missing key/model when enabled fails clearly at startup; when AI_ENABLED=false none of this is required

Before every real call, the configured model is checked against OpenRouter's live model catalog (short-TTL cache) and rejected with a clear, typed error if absent or if pricing is no longer free - never silently proceeds or substitutes another model

Typed, distinct failures for: disabled, missing key, missing model, unauthorized (401), payment required (402), rate limited (429), 5xx, timeout, malformed response, model unavailable, model no longer free - never an automatic paid-model fallback under any of these

When AI is disabled or any AI call fails, all deterministic CareerScope functionality (matching, exclusions, ranking, applications, dedup, identity, auth) is completely unaffected - proven by tests, not asserted

LLM is never used for matching, hard exclusions, ranking, eligibility, dedup, job identity, application/auto-apply or authorization/security decisions - the deterministic engine stays authoritative for all of those

Only the minimum sanitized, allowlisted fields required for each specific AI operation are sent - never passwords, sessions/cookies, CSRF tokens, API keys, DB dumps, credentials, raw filesystem contents, unnecessary profile fields, private infra information, or the full resume
AI-generated output is never silently written over user-authored content (e.g. lead notes) and is visually/structurally distinguished as AI-generated in any response/UI it reaches

Real, end-to-end reference implementation for at least one of the six listed use cases (chosen for existing data/UI readiness), with the remaining use cases left as an explicitly documented, not-yet-built extension of the same abstraction - not silently implied as done

Full test matrix against a mocked OpenRouter-compatible HTTP endpoint (no real OpenRouter calls in CI): success, timeout, 401, 429, 5xx, malformed response, missing key, missing model, AI disabled, model unavailable, model no longer free, provider failure isolated from the underlying operation, owner isolation, deterministic matching unchanged
v2/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md and docs/SECURITY.md updated to accurately describe the new (default-off) capability rather than continuing to assert "AI is DEFERRED" once code exists
