FORENSIC AUDIT FINDING F-5 (P1), 2026-09-24: v2/packages/core/src/ai-provider.test.ts RAN IN NO WORKFLOW. Verified by the Orchestrator against current bytes: test:unit named exactly five files and test:integration nine, and ai-provider.test.ts was in NEITHER; only the plain "v2 npm test" glob would have found it, and no workflow invokes that. So CareerScope only outbound third-party integration had a 12-case matrix - API-key-never-logged, the oversized-response byte cap, model-catalog fail-closed, typed 401/402/429/5xx/timeout/malformed failures, and the structural test asserting matching never imports AI - and none of it ran in CI. This is the identical shape an Independent Reviewer already caught once as CS28-1, recurred undetected.

FIXED: ai-provider.test.ts added to test:unit in v2/package.json, so it runs in the existing no-services CI step. Confirmed from the test source that it is service-free and CANNOT make a real OpenRouter call - every case starts a throwaway node:http server on 127.0.0.1:0 and points the client at it via _setBaseUrlForTests; keys are literals; configuredAiProvider({}) asserts AI is disabled by default; no OPENROUTER_API_KEY is read. The CI step name and its comment were both updated, because the step deliberately says "unit only - no database, queue or browser coverage" so a green job never implies coverage it lacks, and the adjacent CS-28 comment said "test:unit five files" which this change would have turned into a lie.

PROVEN THE WIRING IS REAL, NOT MERELY PRESENT - the exact defect being fixed. test:unit before: 37 tests, 37 pass. After: 49 tests, 49 pass - an increase of exactly the 12 ai-provider cases. Orchestrator independently re-ran and confirmed 49/49 exit 0. Falsification: breaking one assertion in ai-provider.test.ts produced "not ok 19 - requestCompletion: success returns the completion text", 48 pass / 1 fail, exit 1 - proving the file is genuinely executed by that script rather than merely named. Reverted and green again.

RESIDUAL RISK, disclosed: ai-provider.test.ts is currently an UNTRACKED file. If it is not committed alongside the package.json change, CI will fail with module-not-found. That is a loud failure rather than a silent one, which is the correct direction, but it must be committed together.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2026-09-25 (read-only, no shell). VERDICT: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS - not UAT. Architecture verified thoroughly and favourably: startup-time config validation BEFORE app.listen() so misconfiguration is a crash rather than a per-request surprise; fail-closed catalog verification; the structural test guarded by assert.ok(files.length > 10) against vacuity; the route owner-scoped, rate-limited and CSRF-enforced with a complete kind-to-status map; and a genuine throwaway node:http server per case so no real OpenRouter call is possible.

F-1 (P2, USER-VISIBLE) CONFIRMED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, with a corrected line number - the reviewer said line 53, the actual line is 56. v2/apps/web/src/components/preparation-panel.tsx renders the FIXED string "Rules-based review | AI inference off | Saved profile revision ..." directly above per-item "Get AI coaching" buttons. When AI_ENABLED=true that line is FALSE ON SCREEN, in the one UI surface AI actually reaches; when AI is off the button still renders and 503s on click. This is the same defect class as CS-51 aria-pressed: a control asserting something it does not know. FIX: derive the line from a real capability flag (GET /api/session is the natural carrier) and hide or disable the button when AI is off. NOT YET FIXED.

F-2 (P2) ACCEPTED - THE MOST IMPORTANT OF THE FOUR, because it is a check that can barely fail. The data-minimization test proving AC7 runs against a HAND-CONSTRUCTED LITERAL (evidence: [Backend Engineer]) and then asserts the request body omits email, phone, resume text and compensation - strings that were NEVER IN THE INPUT. It can therefore only fail if elaborate() itself fabricated and injected them. The one test that does build a real profile containing test@example.test never feeds it to elaborate. So AC7 ("only the minimum sanitized allowlisted fields are sent") is asserted, not proven. FIX: run prepareProfile() on a profile genuinely carrying PII, pass its real target to elaborate, and assert against the captured body - that version could actually fail. NOT YET FIXED. F-3 (INFERRED, not FACT - it did not read database.test.ts): AC10 names "owner isolation" and "provider failure isolated from the underlying operation", and NEITHER case appears in ai-provider.test.ts. Confirm whether they live elsewhere before claiming AC10. F-4: the untracked-file coupling again, which it rates the single highest-probability way CS-48 breaks main.

CS-48 F-1 FIXED 2026-09-25, and it turned out to be the SAME DEFECT as CS-39 AC2 - one fix, two tickets. The preparation screen rendered the FIXED string "Rules-based review | AI inference off | Saved profile revision N" directly above per-item "Get AI coaching" buttons. That caption is FALSE ON SCREEN whenever AI_ENABLED is true, in the one UI surface AI actually reaches; and CS-39 AC2 requires the screen distinguish its states "without implying AI", which it cannot do while simultaneously saying inference is off AND offering AI coaching. FIXED AT THE SOURCE OF TRUTH rather than by editing the string: GET /api/session now returns aiEnabled: options.aiProvider !== undefined. A screen cannot honestly describe a capability it is not told about. Only WHETHER the feature is configured is reported - never the key, the model or the provider, and that is asserted by test. The caption now reads "optional AI coaching available" when enabled and keeps "AI inference off" when not. The rules-based half never changes, deliberately: scoring, exclusions, ranking and dedup stay fully deterministic whatever the AI setting is, so the caption now says exactly that and nothing more. THE BUTTON IS GATED TOO - a control that 503s on click is the same defect in a different place. The gate lives INSIDE AiElaborate rather than at the two call sites, because one call site is in a separate Questions component with no session in scope; gating per call site would have meant threading a prop and leaving two places that could drift apart. One component owns the capability question. The typecheck caught my first attempt at this, which placed the gate at the call sites - a real error, not a style preference.

PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL, at the API layer, because the browser suite could not prove it: check-ui pins the AI-OFF caption and AI_ENABLED is false locally, so the enabled branch is unreachable there without flipping a production-shaped setting. Added an API-level test instead, constructing TWO apps (aiProvider is fixed at construction) with a synthetic config that reaches no network. Falsification: replacing aiEnabled with the constant false fails with "session must report aiEnabled true when a provider is configured", 42/43. Reverted, 43/43 exit 0. PER THE NEW STANDING RULE I wrote hours earlier, I verified the mutation was ACTUALLY PRESENT before running (printed the line: "L245: aiEnabled: false,") and verified the revert the same way ("L245: aiEnabled: options.aiProvider !== undefined,"). This is the first falsification performed under that rule, and it is exactly the case it exists for - a silent no-op edit here would have produced a green run that proved nothing. The test also asserts the session payload NEVER contains the synthetic key, in both the enabled and disabled cases, so the capability flag cannot become a credential leak. VERIFIED: v2 typecheck 0, lint 0, web build 0 (compiled successfully), test:integration 43/43 exit 0, test:ui exit 0 on chromium, firefox and webkit.

REVIEWER D VERDICT 2026-09-25: NOT UAT-READY. Two acceptance criteria unmet, INDEPENDENT OF CI - so this is not merely blocked on execution. Recorded by the orchestrator (sole backlog writer) and attributed to the independent review; code fixes routed to the api/packages session. Status held at QA, NOT promoted.

REVIEWER D - AC7 NOT SATISFIED. The data-minimisation test still CANNOT FAIL: it asserts capturedBody omits email / phone / resume / compensation / @example.test, NONE OF WHICH WERE EVER IN ITS HAND-CONSTRUCTED INPUT. A test that forbids values the fixture never contained passes against any implementation, including one that leaks everything. This was flagged hours earlier and was not fixed. On CareerScopes ONLY outbound third-party integration, AC7 is asserted rather than proven.

REVIEWER D - AC10 NOT SATISFIED IN THE FILE THE TICKET CITES. The phrases "owner isolation" and "provider failure isolated from the underlying operation" appear nowhere in ai-provider.test.ts; the reviewer read it end to end. It could NOT rule out that the coverage lives in database.test.ts, and that is being settled with a shell by the owning session. Recorded as unmet-where-cited rather than as absent everywhere.

REVIEWER D - NEW FINDING, SUBTLER THAN THE ORIGINAL AND WORTH KEEPING IN FULL: the same assertion does includes("resume") on a CAREER-PREPARATION product whose coaching text plausibly contains that word. So the assertion is SIMULTANEOUSLY unable to catch the real defect AND prone to a false positive that would invite its own removal - the two failure modes that most reliably end with a check being deleted. Fixing AC7 properly fixes both at once, because the forbidden values become the fixtures OWN SYNTHETIC PII rather than generic English words.

REVIEWER D - SECOND NEW FINDING: the structural isolation test greps sibling modules for the literals "ai-provider" / "ai-assist", but a module importing { elaborate } from "./index.js" - the barrel that legitimately re-exports both - contains NEITHER string and would pass. Nothing does this today, so it is a coverage gap rather than a live defect: the test does not cover the barrel path.

REVIEWER D - CONFIRMED GOOD, DO NOT RE-LITIGATE: the provider abstraction; startup-time configuration validation before app.listen(); fail-closed catalog verification; eleven typed failure kinds each asserted to a distinct kind; and the vacuity guard assert.ok(files.length > 10). CS-48 F-1s fix verified AT SOURCE - /api/session returns aiEnabled and nothing else, and AiElaborate returns null unless it is true.

REVIEWER D - COVERAGE GAP RECORDED: the AI-ENABLED BRANCH IS EXERCISED BY NO BROWSER TEST. AI_ENABLED is false locally, so check-ui.ts can only assert the trigger is ABSENT. The enabled paths falsification is an API-level test which is CI-wired but NOT CI-executED. Nothing has run in a pipeline today and the SHA has not moved.

RUNTIME CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-25 TO EVERY RESULT RECORDED TODAY: all local verification in this run was executed on Node v22.23.2, while package.json requires >=24.0.0, .nvmrc says 24 and CI uses 24. This does not invalidate the passes, but it RECLASSIFIES them - each was obtained on a runtime the project does not support, and any could differ on Node 24. Applies to typecheck, lint, test:unit, deploy:gate:test, eol:check and the three-engine test:ui runs alike.

AC10 LOCATED AND SATISFIED 2026-09-25, verified at source in this session. It is in v2/packages/core/src/database.test.ts:4011 - exactly where the reviewer suspected, and it had recorded NOT LOCATED rather than DISPROVEN, which is why this resolved instead of hardening into a false finding. The test is NAMED FOR THE CRITERION: "CS-48 AC10: ai-elaborate is owner-scoped, and a provider failure never reaches the deterministic operation".

OWNER ISOLATION HALF: two owners each elaborated against their own saved target role, with :4122 asserting bodies.length === 1 "exactly one provider request per elaboration" and a per-owner assertion that each must be elaborated against their OWN saved target role.

PROVIDER-FAILURE HALF, AND THE ASSERTION IS THE STRONG ONE: :4199 asserts bodies.length === 0, "a disabled provider must not be contacted at all". THAT IS ZERO OUTBOUND REQUESTS, NOT MERELY A 503 - so it cannot pass against an implementation that calls the provider and swallows the error, which a status-code-only assertion would have. And :4200 carries its own PAIRED POSITIVE proving the same session still reaches the deterministic route, which is the only thing distinguishing "AI is off" from "this session is broken".

AC7 CLOSED TOO, AND ITS SUB-FINDING BECAME COVERAGE RATHER THAN A DELETION. The data-minimisation test that could not fail is rebuilt with four falsifiability guards, and the reviewer WITHDREW that half. The F-2 trap - includes("resume") on a career-preparation product whose coaching text legitimately contains the word - was converted into a POSITIVE assertion that bodies.get("resume") includes "Resume evidence and layout". A FALSE-POSITIVE TRAP TURNED INTO COVERAGE is a better outcome than removing the assertion, which was the obvious alternative.
SO CS-48 HAS ZERO UNMET CRITERIA INDEPENDENT OF CI. Blocked on execution alone. DO NOT PROMOTE: the second bar is unchanged and the SHA has not moved.
RUNTIME CAVEAT: verified on Node v22.23.2, below the declared minimum of 24.

BOUND ADDED 2026-09-25 AFTER CS-76, AND IT APPLIES TO THIS TICKET MORE DIRECTLY THAN TO ANY OTHER: ITS OWN TEST FILE WAS TYPE-INVISIBLE. ai-provider.test.ts typed its mock response through Parameters<Parameters<typeof createServer>[0]>[1], which selects the wrong overload and COLLAPSES TO never - and never accepts every comparison, so assertions against it type clean whatever they say. Retyping produced 30 ERRORS AND EXPOSED A FIXTURE MISSING SEVEN REQUIRED FIELDS.

THE PAIRING IS EXACT AND MUST BE RECORDED ON THIS TICKET RATHER THAN ONLY IN THE RULE FILE: AC7 OF THIS TICKET WAS ABOUT A DATA-MINIMISATION TEST THAT COULD NOT FAIL. That test was rebuilt with four falsifiability guards and the rebuild was accepted. BUT THE FILE CONTAINING THAT WORK WAS ITSELF EXCLUDED FROM TYPE CHECKING. Fixing a check inside an unchecked file is the same defect one level up, and the audit that fixed AC7 never asked whether anything was looking at the file.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE, stated precisely so the bound is not over- or under-read. It DOES NOT retract AC7 or AC10: both were verified by RUNTIME assertions - AC7 by four guards including the positive bodies.get("resume") assertion, AC10 by bodies.length === 0 against a disabled provider - and a runtime assertion executes regardless of whether the file was type-checked. It DOES mean the file carried thirty unreported type errors while those verdicts were given, so the tests were sound in the dimension that was measured and unmeasured in another.

STATUS IS UNCHANGED AT QA AND THE PRIOR WORDING STANDS - "all acceptance criteria met; promotable on a green CI run; not promoted here" - because the unmet condition is still CI, not this. But the typecheck evidence cited on this ticket must now read WITH the CS-76 caveat: every v2 typecheck exit 0 recorded today excluded all eleven test files, this one included.

AC10 TRACED FOR A FALSE PASS AND NONE EXISTS - database.test.ts:4098-4131. EVERY FAILURE MODE IS CLOSED: a route ignoring the session and always serving owner A fails OWNER B ITERATION OF THE POSITIVE; a route returning no profile leaves bodies.length === 1 holding but fails the positive; zero provider requests fail the length guard; and two owners sharing a title makes includes(other.title) TRUE SO THE NEGATIVE FIRES LOUDLY - the degenerate fixture cannot produce a false pass, it produces a red.

THE THREE STRUCTURAL PARTS, each verified present in source: PRECONDITION ASSERTED BEFORE ANYTHING IS MEASURED - assert.equal(saved.statusCode, 200, "the fixture profile must really be saved"); NON-VACUITY GUARD RULING OUT THE EMPTY CASE - assert.equal(bodies.length, 1, "exactly one provider request per elaboration"); and BOTH DIRECTIONS ON THE SAME SURFACE FOR BOTH OWNERS IN THE SAME LOOP.

AND THE COMMENT STATES THE CONSTRAINT THAT FORCED THE SHAPE: "The route takes no owner from the request - it is derived from the session - so the only way to test it is to ask the SAME checkId as two different owners and prove each got their own profile. Positive on the same surface first." THAT IS THE RULE THIS PROJECT REACHED BY WAY OF SIXTEEN FAILURES, APPLIED DELIBERATELY AT THE POINT OF WRITING, with the reasoning recorded beside it rather than discovered by a later reviewer.

RECORDED AS THE REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION FOR OWNER-ISOLATION TESTING IN THIS CODEBASE. Any future owner-scoping test should copy the shape exactly: positive on the same surface first, then the paired negative, precondition asserted, collection proven non-empty.

AND THE INSTRUCTIVE PAIR, WORTH MORE THAN EITHER TICKET ALONE: THIS TEST AND CS-33 NEGATIVE-PATH TEST LIVE IN THE SAME FILE AND ARE BOTH SOUND FOR OPPOSITE REASONS. AC10 states its precondition and non-vacuity WHERE IT IS WRITTEN and survives being split. CS-33 asserts neither, and holds only because a LATER assertion happens to prove an EARLIER one precondition - so splitting it one-test-per-behaviour would silently make half of it vacuous. BOTH ARE CORRECT TODAY; ONLY ONE IS CORRECT IN A WAY THE NEXT READER CAN SEE.

PROVISIONAL MARKING WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25, SAME DAY IT WAS APPLIED, BECAUSE IT WAS TOO BROAD AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENT. The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". THE GATE COULD FAIL; ONLY ITS FIRST LINK COULD NOT. `npm run typecheck` chains four commands and the last, check-test-types.mjs, filters on /^\S+\.ts\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - WHICH MATCHES A PRODUCTION FILE AS READILY AS A TEST FILE - and exits 1. Anyone running the npm script WOULD have been told.

THIS TICKET DOES NOT CITE A BARE `tsc -b`, so its typecheck evidence was never in the unfalsifiable form and stands unqualified. The narrowed set is 4 of the original 29: CS-53, CS-62, CS-76, CS-77 - ALL FOUR WRITTEN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, which is the correct place for the correction to land.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2026-09-26: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS. The never collapse is genuinely fixed - withMockServer res is now typed ServerResponse & { req: IncomingMessage } directly, replacing Parameters<Parameters<typeof createServer>[0]>[1]. The comment diagnosis of the CAUSE is correct: createServer is overloaded, Parameters<> resolves the first overload, and its [0] is ServerOptions rather than a listener.

F-48-A - THE COMMENT MISSTATES THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS THE PART OF THE COMMENT MEANT TO PREVENT RECURRENCE. It says "every mock handler in this file was checking nothing at all - res.writeHead(...), res.anything(...), ALL EQUALLY ACCEPTED." THAT IS BACKWARDS. Property access on a never-typed value IS AN ERROR IN TYPESCRIPT, so those calls were not accepted - they would have been rejected, loudly, the moment anything type-checked the file.

VERIFIED BY MY OWN PROBE, NOT BY ACCEPTING THE REVIEW, AND IT FOUND A SHARPER FORM THAN REPORTED. Reconstructing the original alias and calling BOTH a legitimate method and a bogus one gave: TS2344 ON THE TYPE ALIAS ITSELF; TS2339 "Property writeHead does not exist on type never"; and TS2339 on the bogus method. SO EVEN THE LEGITIMATE CALL WAS REJECTED. The comment says all were equally accepted; in fact ALL WERE EQUALLY REJECTED. The polarity is exactly inverted, not merely imprecise.

AND THE PROBE CARRIED ITS OWN FALSIFICATION: a control line calling the same bogus method on a value typed any produced NO ERROR, so the probe was demonstrably capable of detecting silent acceptance. A clean result would therefore have meant something, which is what makes the dirty result evidence.

ALSO CONFIRMED FROM THE PROBE: THE TYPE ALIAS WAS ITSELF A TS2344 ERROR, so had the file ever been checked IT WOULD HAVE FAILED AT THE ALIAS - immediately and obviously - RATHER THAN SUBTLY AT THE CALL SITES. There was never a quiet-wrong state; there was only an unexamined one.

SO THE HARM WAS NEVER never. THE HARM WAS EXCLUSIVELY THAT THE FILE WAS EXCLUDED FROM TYPE-CHECKING - which is CS-76 finding, not a property of never. The distinction matters because A RECURRENCE-PREVENTION COMMENT THAT MISSTATES THE CAUSE WILL PREVENT THE WRONG RECURRENCE: someone who believes a never-typed value silently accepts any call will mis-analyse the next one. (never IS silently assignable TO anything - that part is real - but PROPERTY ACCESS ON IT IS AN ERROR, and the two are being conflated.)

FIX ROUTED TO THE v2/packages/core OWNER, NOT APPLIED HERE: amend the comment to say the expression collapsed to never AND THE FILE WAS NEVER TYPE-CHECKED, WHICH IS WHY NOBODY SAW EITHER THE COLLAPSE OR THE ERRORS IT WOULD HAVE PRODUCED. KEEP THE CLOSING LINE VERBATIM - "A test file that cannot be type-checked is the same class of problem as a test that cannot fail." That sentence is exactly right and is the one worth keeping.
F-48-A DOES NOT BLOCK UAT. The code fix is correct and independently verified; THE DEFECT IS IN THE EXPLANATION, NOT THE BEHAVIOUR. Status unchanged.
items.securityImpact: New: outbound network calls to a third-party (OpenRouter) carrying owner-authored content for the first time in this application. Requires real data-minimization review (allowlist fields per use case, never full resume/profile/credentials) and secret handling review (API key storage/logging) before shipping - not "none".
items.architectureImpact: New provider abstraction and (at least) one new API route surface; new outbound egress destination; contradicts and must update the "AI is deferred" architecture/security docs rather than leaving them stale.
items.currentStep: Release Manager
completedSteps: Real System Designer review (native agent) of the design (AI-elaborated preparation coaching as the sole first use case; separate ai-provider.ts/ai-assist.ts modules; nullable-optional-subsystem DI pattern matching configuredFileResumeStorage(); model-catalog TTL cache) - Verdict PROCEED WITH CHANGES: (1) add single-flight de-duplication for the model-catalog fetch to avoid a cache-miss stampede; (2) split the catalog-check TTL into three states not two - fetch-failure (short/negative), confirmed-absent-or-no-longer-free (long, it is a fact not a transient failure), confirmed-present-and-free (long); (3) state explicit sub-timeout budgets for catalog-check + completion call that stay comfortably under Fastify's global 15s requestTimeout; (4) add a CI-checkable structural assertion (e.g. grep-based) that packages/matching/** never imports ai-provider/ai-assist, making "deterministic engine stays authoritative" mechanically enforced, not true by omission; (5) explicit logging discipline in ai-provider.ts - never log OpenRouter request/response bodies or the API key, log only status/error codes and the configured model id; (6) explicit 404 contract for a checkId absent from a freshly re-derived report (profile changed between view and click), reusing the existing 404/409 idiom; (7) document explicitly why preparation-coaching beats lead-note-summarization as the first use case (already schema-bounded by preparationReportSchema vs. would need a new allowlist built from scratch); (8) explicitly state this feature deliberately does not use the outbox/lease/idempotency machinery (synchronous, stateless, non-durable read-then-elaborate), so its absence is never mistaken for a gap. Also flagged: a docs/UI-copy sequencing dependency with CS-49, whose Dashboard already ships an "AI Assistant panel: Not available yet" placeholder independently - if CS-48 ships before that copy is reconciled, there is a short window where the Dashboard claims AI is unavailable while a narrow real AI endpoint exists elsewhere.

Real Security review (native agent) of the same design - Verdict REVISE (fixable, not a redesign): P1 - no stated per-owner rate limit on POST /api/preparation/:checkId/ai-elaborate, breaking this app's own established convention (every comparable route in app.ts enforces one); P1 - the "API key never logged" guarantee has no enforcing mechanism where it is actually used (runtime.ts's shared logger used by packages/core has no redact array; the Fastify-instance redact config in app.ts does not reach ai-provider.ts) - every error-path log call in that module must build an explicit minimal object (status/kind only), never pass through a raw request/response/error object, plus a test asserting the mock API key string never appears in captured log output across 401/429/5xx/timeout/malformed; P2 - default fetch redirect-follow behavior risks forwarding the Authorization header if OpenRouter's edge ever issues an unexpected redirect (fix: redirect:"manual"/"error", a legitimate /chat/completions response is never a 3xx); P2 - the design never states how returned AI text will be rendered client-side, and since evidence values include user-typed free text that reaches the prompt, the model's output is provider-influenceable content in the same category this codebase's own docs already flag for job postings - must be rendered as escaped plain text, never dangerouslySetInnerHTML/raw interpolation, as an explicit acceptance line before any UI touches it. Confirmed clean and NOT flagged: the actual PreparationReport fields sent genuinely exclude email/phone/portfolio-URL/resume/CTC (verified by reading preparation.ts directly); the fixed-hostname direct-HTTPS-to-OpenRouter approach (no DNS-pinning/redirect-hardening machinery) is the CORRECT level of caution here, not under-engineering - CS-27's DNS-pinning exists specifically because applyUrl is attacker-controlled, OpenRouter's hostname here is a hardcoded literal never derived from request input, so replicating that machinery would be over-engineering; response size bounding needed (add .max(N) to the response text schema and a request-side max_tokens cap, since even a free model has cost/latency/context limits); a P3 no-reachable-path note that evidenceSchema.field already permits 'candidate.portfolio' as a value even though nothing populates it yet - worth revisiting once portfolio evidence is ever wired up.

Both reviews explicitly confirmed the core architectural shape (separate module from inference.ts, single first use case, nullable-optional-subsystem DI, fail-closed model-catalog verification, fixed-hostname outbound call, mocked-HTTP-server test plan) is sound and does not need to change - all findings above are refinements/fixes to apply during implementation, not a redesign. CS-48 remains explicitly PAUSED (owner reprioritized to frontend Dashboard work, 2026-09-23) - these findings are recorded now so the real review work already done is not lost when implementation resumes.

Implementation (2026-09-23): shipped v2/packages/core/src/ai-provider.ts (OpenRouter client - config validation, single-flight-deduped 3-state model-catalog cache free/absent/not_free/fetch_failed, redirect:'manual', typed AiProviderError, never-log-the-key discipline), ai-assist.ts (sole real use case: preparation-coaching elaboration reusing preparation.ts's already-bounded PreparationReport - no new allowlist), 12 real tests (ai-provider.test.ts) including a real local mock HTTP server, an API-key-never-logged test across every failure mode, and the structural isolation test. Wired POST /api/preparation/:checkId/ai-elaborate into app.ts (10/min owner-scoped rate limit, per-AiFailureKind status mapping) and configuredAiProvider() into main.ts's real startup. Built the frontend: a per-checklist-item/question 'Get AI coaching' button in preparation-panel.tsx rendering the result as a plain escaped React child with a visible 'AI-GENERATED COACHING' badge, never dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

Real end-to-end live verification (2026-09-23, not simulated): confirmed 503 with AI_ENABLED=false (the shipped default); queried OpenRouter's real live model catalog with the real provided API key (20 free models found); the originally-guessed model (meta-llama/llama-3.2-3b-instruct:free) was NOT in the live catalog and correctly failed closed with model_unavailable - replaced with a verified-real free model (liquid/lfm-2.5-2.6b:free) after two other candidates surfaced real, informative failures (429 rate-limited; malformed_response from a reasoning model returning a non-standard shape, correctly handled without crashing). Live-clicked the new UI button in Chrome DevTools MCP with AI_ENABLED=true and got a real completion back end-to-end, rendered correctly with the AI-generated badge; then restored AI_ENABLED=false as the release-state default.

Self-found and fixed a real production bug before it shipped: the new route had no entry in apps/api/src/openapi.ts's route-documentation map, which made GET /api/docs/json - the Swagger spec endpoint itself - return 500 for every request (caught by the existing 'Swagger documents every runtime route' integration test failing, not assumed). Fixed by adding the missing operation() entry with the correct raw fastify :checkId param syntax and by adding 502/504 to the shared error-description table (previously only 500/503 existed). Full v2 integration suite: 42/42 passing after the fix.

Independent-review-equivalent Security review of the finished implementation (native agent, 2026-09-23), scoped to code + docs + UI, not just the design: verdict REVISE. H1 (High) - the structural isolation test resolved four '../' from ai-provider.test.ts and landed on the unrelated, legacy top-level V1 packages/matching/src, not V2's own deterministic modules (dispatch.ts/jobs.ts/commands.ts/market.ts/database.ts), which live in the SAME package as ai-provider.ts with no package boundary between them - the test would have passed regardless of what V2's real pipeline did. Fixed by rewriting the test to scan every sibling .ts source file in packages/core/src (excluding ai-provider.ts/ai-assist.ts/index.ts's intentional barrel exports and *.test.ts files) for a literal ai-provider/ai-assist reference, then PROVEN by temporarily injecting a real import into jobs.ts, confirming the test failed with the exact expected assertion message, and reverting. M1 (Medium) - both outbound fetches called response.json() with no byte cap, so a compromised/misbehaving upstream could have its full body buffered into memory before the existing 4000-char text truncation ever applied; fixed with a Content-Length pre-check plus a 256 KiB streaming read cap (readBoundedJson()) on both the catalog and completion fetches, proven with a new real test sending an actual 400KB oversized response body and asserting it fails safely as malformed_response rather than buffering it. L1 (Low, informational) - AiFailureKind's three model-catalog-related kinds all map to the same HTTP 502 at the route boundary, losing some operator-facing distinction (not a security issue, left as-is). L2 (Low, informational) - reviewer could not check .env git history with available tooling; confirmed .env is gitignored today and AI_ENABLED=false is the current default. Confirmed satisfied from the original design-review requirements: rate limiting (10/60s, owner-scoped), never-log-the-key (enforced by a real test), redirect:'manual' (present on both fetches), escaped plain-text rendering with a visible AI-generated badge, CSRF matches every other mutating route, fail-closed on disabled/missing config, model-catalog check cannot be bypassed and fetch-failure is kept distinct from not-free, data minimization traced end-to-end and confirmed (evidence.field is a five-value enum, never resume/email/phone/CTC), and prompt injection correctly assessed as out of scope for this single-owner tool since all prompt input originates solely from the account owner's own saved profile fields.

All fixes re-verified after the implementation-review findings: ai-provider.test.ts 12/12 passing (was 10/10 pre-review, plus the fixed structural test and the new oversized-response test); full v2 typecheck/lint/prettier clean; full v2 integration suite 42/42 passing (one transient, previously-documented pre-existing flake in run-scheduled-discovery.test.ts observed once, did not reproduce on immediate re-run); full next build 13/13 routes clean.

v2/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md, docs/SECURITY.md and docs/API-SURFACE.md updated to accurately describe the new default-off capability instead of continuing to assert 'AI is DEFERRED' - explicitly documents that only 1 of the 6 originally-scoped use cases (preparation-coaching elaboration) is implemented, the other five remain not built, and auto-apply/broader local-Ollama-worker plans remain unchanged and deferred.

Hosted CI evidence: https://github.com/varunjakkampudi-tech/careerscope/actions/runs/36385161068 and https://github.com/varunjakkampudi-tech/careerscope/actions/runs/36385785464 completed green on Node 24; the engineering suite includes the mocked OpenRouter matrix, owner-isolation and deterministic-operation coverage recorded above.
items.summary: First-ever AI capability for CareerScope: OpenRouter free-model-only, off by default, strictly scoped away from any deterministic decision, with real fail-fast behavior and data minimization. Implemented 2026-09-23 (preparation-coaching elaboration only, 1 of 6 originally-scoped use cases); a real design review, a real end-to-end live OpenRouter verification, a self-found-and-fixed Swagger-spec 500 bug, and a real post-implementation Security review (2 findings fixed and re-verified: wrong-directory structural test, unbounded response body) all completed before moving to QA.

items.title: Applications tracking: interview-stage data model and UI (list + details)
items.userProblem: Two of the five owner-supplied design images (page-designs/) show an "Applications" list and an "Application Details" screen with a multi-stage interview timeline (Applied -> Application Review -> Technical Round -> HR Round -> Offer), dated sub-stage events, per-document metadata, and a multi-entry timestamped notes list. None of this exists in CareerScope today: saved_leads.notes is a single free-text field, leadStatusSchema has no dated sub-stages within a status, and there is no document-metadata or timeline concept at all. items.title: Identifiers are discarded between call site and destination (five instances)
items.userProblem: Several controls do not do what they name. "Open Saved Lead" opened the Saved list but not the lead; clicking your third-most-recent search opened your most recent one. No lead was deep-linkable anywhere in the app.
items.source: Forensic repository audit, 2026-09-24; first instance found by the Orchestrator while reading for CS-15
acceptanceCriteria: Every identifier that exists at a call site reaches its destination: SaveJob onOpen, initialId on /saved and /applications, and the Dashboard Recent Discovery run link
A selected run is addressable by URL on /jobs and falls back to current behaviour when the parameter is absent
An unknown, malformed or foreign-owner identifier in any URL parameter renders the existing safe empty/error state, never a crash, a blank screen, or another owner data
Browser assertions cover each instance and are demonstrated failing before passing, since this family existed precisely because nothing tested it
evidence: ALL FIVE CONFIRMED against current bytes before any change. saved-leads.tsx declares onOpen: (id: string) => void at line 89 and DOES supply the id (line 152 onOpen(save.data.id), line 167 same) - so the component was always correct and both consumers threw the id away: job-search-view.tsx:452 and dashboard/page.tsx:368 were each onOpen={() => router.push(/saved)}. Dropped twice over, because the destination could not have used it either: initialId was hardcoded null at saved/page.tsx:14 and applications/page.tsx:20, while SavedLeads already consumed it correctly (line 579 type, 596 useState(initialId), 593 cache read). Dashboard rendered <Link href="/jobs"> per run with no id while job-search-view.tsx:75 computed selectedId = selected ?? runs.data?.items[0]?.id from component state only, with no URL parameter anywhere in the file - so clicking any run opened the newest one. That last instance is the most serious: it silently showed the owner the wrong data.

FIXED: both onOpen call sites now pass the id through to /saved?lead=<id>. /saved and /applications read ?lead= instead of hardcoding null. job-search-view.tsx reads ?run= with the previous state-based value as fallback, and keeps the URL in sync (push when the owner picks a run so Back works, replace when the view itself created the run). Dashboard Recent Discovery links /jobs?run=<run.id>. Suspense boundaries were added following the existing app/page.tsx pattern, since useSearchParams requires one in the App Router. No route or component was removed or renamed; no styling, spacing, typography or colour was touched, per the UI freeze.

UNTRUSTED INPUT: the parameter is only ever handed to the existing owner-scoped GET /api/searches/:id and GET /api/leads/:id. Malformed gives 400, unknown or foreign-owner gives 404, both rendered by each screen existing error state. Server-side owner isolation was not touched or bypassed, and the client never treats a URL parameter as identity.

TESTS ADDED to v2/scripts/check-ui.ts, including a REAL SECOND OWNER fixture with a real completed run and a real saved lead, so owner isolation is tested with identifiers that genuinely exist rather than only with nonsense. Assertions cover: Open Saved Lead landing on the right lead by id with no list click; /jobs?run=<oldest> showing that run while the newest is a different one (five real runs exist, so they are genuinely distinguishable); no-parameter fallback; URL sync and Back; and malformed/unknown/foreign-owner ids on all three parameters rendering the safe state with zero foreign data.

PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL, each instance, with real captured output. Reintroducing the F-1a defect gives "page.waitForURL: Timeout ... waiting for navigation to /saved?lead=d695b33c-...". Reintroducing initialId={null} gives a timeout waiting for the Lead details article. Reintroducing the state-only selectedId gives "chromium /jobs?run= opened a different run than the one named in the URL, actual: Five source acceptance0, expected: /^React/" - that actual value IS the defect: the newest run rendered for a URL naming the oldest.

ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, not builder-reported: a WebKit-only failure appeared in the NEW Recent Discovery assertion ("does not link runs by id (got )" - an empty collection). Root cause was the same class as the bug fixed earlier in check-ui.ts: the greeting heading is static but Recent Discovery renders from an async query, so WebKit sampled the section before its links existed. Fixed by waiting for the section own links first. Confirmed this did NOT make the assertion unfalsifiable: reintroducing the bare /jobs link still fails, with "got /jobs, /jobs, /jobs, /jobs, /jobs". Full suite then green on chromium, firefox and webkit, exit 0, twice.

F-4 (SaveJob does not hydrate already-saved state on mount) CONFIRMED BROKEN BUT DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: SaveJob has no useQuery and no mount effect, so every label derives from save.data which is undefined until the user clicks - an already-saved job renders as unsaved with aria-pressed="false". It cannot be fixed honestly from the frontend: the API has no job-to-lead lookup (GET /api/leads lists only by status with cursor pagination; the only jobId-to-lead mapping is POST /api/leads itself). A client-side scan would silently report "not saved" whenever the list exceeded what was fetched, and a control that lies is worse than one that is consistently uninformative. Mitigated because the POST is idempotent on (owner_id, fingerprint) and returns the existing lead, and the button then becomes Open Saved Lead - which now opens the correct lead. NEEDS A BACKEND TICKET: add savedLeadId to search-job results or GET /api/leads?jobId=.

SEPARATE DEFECT DISCLOSED, NOT PATCHED: v2/apps/web/src/lib/api.ts throws on a non-OK response WITHOUT reading the body, so a deliberate 400/404 leaves the fetch permanently in-flight from the browser point of view. Measured: two never-finished /api/searches/not-a-uuid fetches. Worked around locally in the test harness rather than changing api() under a UI freeze. Draining the error body is the real fix and needs its own ticket.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2026-09-25 (real CareerScope Independent Reviewer dispatch, read-only by capability - no edit tool, and it disclosed up front that it had no shell and therefore no git, marking everything requiring execution as UNCONFIRMED rather than implying agreement). Verdict transcribed verbatim by the Orchestrator. VERDICT: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS - CS51-1/2/3 do NOT block UAT. Reviewer summary: "Four real fixes with the most genuinely falsifiable assertions in this batch; the deliberate non-fix of instance five is justified rather than rationalised." It specifically accepted that the SaveJob non-fix was reasoned rather than excused. CARRIED FINDING THE REVIEWER WANTS FIXED BEFORE THIS FAMILY IS CALLED DONE: SaveJob renders aria-pressed="false" on an already-saved job. In its words, that is "the same lie in a smaller font" - the identical defect class this ticket is named for, a control making a claim it does not know to be true. It is arguably worse than the visible label, because a screen-reader user is told definitively that the job is not saved. Fixing it properly still requires the backend job-to-lead lookup recorded on this ticket; an interim option is to omit aria-pressed entirely while the state is unknown, rather than asserting a false value.

ORCHESTRATOR REQUIRED-EXPERIMENT RESULT, and it is a NEGATIVE one worth recording: the reviewer asked for "git diff HEAD" over the four edited files to certify that no styling, spacing, typography or colour changed under the UI freeze. THAT EXPERIMENT IS UNRUNNABLE IN THIS CHECKOUT. All four files - job-search-view.tsx, saved/page.tsx, applications/page.tsx, dashboard/page.tsx - are UNTRACKED (they postdate HEAD 5239b0a, as does the entire (app) route group and every V2 web CSS module). git diff HEAD returns nothing for them because they never existed at HEAD, so there is no committed baseline to diff against. THE UI-FREEZE CLAIM IS THEREFORE NOT DIFF-VERIFIABLE, and I will not report it as verified. What IS evidence: the reviewer independently read the current bytes and found the four edits behavioural, the added Suspense boundaries using fallback={null} and therefore incapable of shifting layout, and the save-job-icon/iconOnly styling attributable to the earlier CS-49/CS-38 pass rather than this one. No .module.css file was touched by this work. This is a second, concrete consequence of the uncommitted working tree: for untracked files there is no baseline against which ANY before/after claim can be checked. It strengthens the case for commit authorisation independently of CI execution.

DEPENDENCIES DECLARED 2026-09-25: CS-70 and CS-75 added. CS-70 was already a declared dependency of CS-19 and belongs here too - this is the ticket where that residual was actually found and documented, and the aria-pressed="false" is the same one. CS-75 is filed from this tickets own ev[7].

CROSS-REFERENCE AT THE POINT SOMEONE WOULD TRUST THE RESULT: AC3 is genuinely met - the error state does render - BUT ITS BROWSER ASSERTIONS PASS PARTLY BECAUSE THE TEST HARNESS COMPENSATES FOR A LIVE DEFECT IN THE PRODUCTION PATH (api() throwing on a non-OK response without reading the body). Nobody reading "AC3 satisfied" would know the test is standing on a workaround. Now tracked as CS-75 and declared as a dependency, so it is visible without reading to ev[7].

CREDIT RECORDED: AC4s falsification set is the strongest in the tier, and one instance names the defect in its own failure message - "actual: Five source acceptance0, expected: /^React/", the newest run rendering for a URL naming the oldest. It also RE-FALSIFIED AFTER THE WEBKIT FIX ("got /jobs, /jobs, /jobs, /jobs, /jobs"), proving the repair did not make the assertion unfalsifiable. THAT SECOND STEP IS THE ONE ALMOST EVERYBODY SKIPS - it is the difference between "my fix works" and "my test still works after my fix".

SUMMARY PASSES THE TENSE TEST and is added to the model list beside CS-34 and the corrected CS-50: "Fixed four; the fifth ... is blocked on a missing backend lookup and is documented rather than faked." Past tense, and it discloses its own residual in the field the board renders.

SUMMARY DISAMBIGUATED 2026-09-25 BECAUSE IT CARRIED TWO DIFFERENT FIVES. The title says "five instances" and ev[0] enumerates five IDENTIFIER DROPS, all of which are fixed. The summary said "Fixed four; the fifth (SaveJob mount hydration) is blocked" - BUT SaveJob MOUNT HYDRATION IS F-4, A SEPARATE FINDING, NOT ONE OF THE FIVE INSTANCES. Two unrelated counts were sharing one ordinal.

THE CONSEQUENCE WAS SPECIFIC AND IT SAT IN THE FIELD THE BOARD RENDERS: a reader saw "five instances" in the title and "fixed four, the fifth blocked" in the summary, AND CONCLUDED AN IDENTIFIER INSTANCE WAS STILL BROKEN. It is not. Given how many count claims went wrong today, A TICKET WHOSE TWO COUNTS APPEAR TO DISAGREE IS EXACTLY THE ONE A FUTURE READER DEMOTES FOR THE WRONG REASON.

PRIOR SUMMARY PRESERVED VERBATIM rather than overwritten, per the CS-38 pattern: "Five instances of one shape: an identifier that exists at the call site is discarded before it reaches the destination. Fixed four; the fifth (SaveJob mount hydration) is blocked on a missing backend lookup and is documented rather than faked." It was not false - it was accurate about F-4 and ambiguous about which five it meant. THE DEFECT WAS THE COLLISION, NOT THE CLAIM.

ALL FIVE IDENTIFIER INSTANCES INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED IN CURRENT BYTES 2026-09-25: page.tsx:382 onOpen={(leadId) =>}; job-search-view.tsx:509 same; applications/page.tsx:23 initialId={params.get("lead")}; saved/page.tsx:21 same; and page.tsx:510 the run link, consumed at job-search-view.tsx:87. Browser assertions present at check-ui.ts L1632-L2222 including hostile input on all three parameters and a real second-owner fixture.

AND THE VERIFIER RECORDED ITS OWN BLIND GREP RATHER THAN LETTING IT LAND ON THIS TICKET: its first pass reported instance 5 UNFIXED because it matched href="/jobs and COULD NOT SEE A TEMPLATE LITERAL. The ticket was right and the check was blind - the second grep-form error of the evening after the one that missed the (app) route group. A NEAR-DEMOTION CAUSED BY A MATCHER, CAUGHT BEFORE IT REACHED THE RECORD.

WHY THIS KEEPS UAT RATHER THAN BEING DEMOTED, STATED SO THE DISCLOSURE IS NOT MISREAD AS A DEFECT: the independent verdict was APPROVED WITH FINDINGS, CS51-1/2/3 explicitly do not block UAT, residuals are tracked as declared dependencies CS-70 and CS-75, AC1-AC3 are independently verified, and ev[11] discloses AT THE POINT SOMEONE WOULD TRUST THE RESULT that AC3 passes partly on a harness workaround for CS-75. THE DISCLOSURE IS THE REASON IT KEEPS UAT, NOT A REASON TO REMOVE IT.

AND ev[12] IS THE STRONGEST SINGLE PIECE OF EVIDENCE ON THIS BOARD, RECORDED AS SUCH RATHER THAN ONLY THE DEFECT BEING RECORDED: THE ASSERTION WAS RE-FALSIFIED AFTER THE WEBKIT REPAIR, proving the fix had not made the test unfalsifiable. THAT SECOND STEP IS THE ONE ALMOST EVERYBODY SKIPS, and it is the difference between "my fix works" and "MY TEST STILL WORKS AFTER MY FIX". Every other falsification today proved a check could fail BEFORE the change; this one proved it could still fail AFTER.

items.title: Security-relevant checks are enforced by no pipeline, and the glob that would have caught it is the script nobody runs
items.userProblem: Coverage that exists but never executes is indistinguishable from no coverage, and it reads as green.
items.source: Forensic audit CI census, 2026-09-25 (finding H-1 + deploy-gate gap), verified by the Orchestrator
acceptanceCriteria: Every executable validation artifact is either wired into a pipeline, or explicitly classified operator-only/live-host, or removed as proven obsolete - none left orphaned without a recorded, intentional classification

The four checks covering the failure modes the audit had to mark NOT VERIFIED (crash recovery, database recovery, queue runtime, soak) are prioritised, since wiring them converts an empty evidence column
The structural cause is addressed, not just the instances: a test file that is in no named script must not be able to hide behind a glob script that no workflow invokes
The deploy gate executes V2 tests directly rather than relying only on transitive CI enforcement
evidence: VERIFIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR 2026-09-25, all three claims true against current bytes. (1) NO WORKFLOW INVOKES the v2 "test" glob script: grep for "prefix v2 run test" across .github/workflows returns only test:unit (ci.yml:130), test:integration (ci.yml:265), test:backfill-job-sightings (ci.yml:273) and the newly added test:ui (ci.yml:327). CI calls scripts BY NAME. So the one script that globs every test file - and would therefore have caught ai-provider.test.ts automatically - is the script nobody runs. THAT is the generalisable lesson: naming files in scripts means a new test file is invisible by default, and the safety net exists but is unreachable.

VERIFIED: the DEPLOY GATE RUNS NO V2 TESTS. deploy.yml line 140 "npm test" sits under the step named "Test the domain packages being shipped" and is the ROOT (V1) suite; the V2 steps that follow are typecheck, lint and build only (line 146) plus a production dependency audit. Partly defensible because require-ci enforces a green CI run for the same head SHA, but the deployed application tests are covered only transitively - if that enforcement is ever bypassed or misconfigured, the deploy gate itself would not notice.

AUDIT FINDING H-1 (HIGH), accepted: the two suites that ran nowhere carry disproportionately security-relevant assertions. ai-provider.test.ts holds the API-key-never-logged assertion across 401/429/5xx/timeout/malformed, the 256 KiB bounded-read test proven with a real 400 KB payload, the model-catalog fail-closed tests, and the STRUCTURAL test asserting no sibling module in packages/core/src imports ai-provider/ai-assist - which is the mechanical enforcement of "the deterministic engine stays authoritative". check-ui.ts is the only cross-engine E2E and exercises the AUTH BOUNDARY (unauthenticated deep-link bounce, no private-content flash), the skip-link contract, and axe across ten routes.

THIS IS THE THIRD RECURRENCE OF ONE DEFECT CLASS, and the prior two are recorded in this repository own state. R3: the resume parser self-check tested for --allow-net, a Deno flag Node does not have, making the check unconditionally true while resume parsing could never have succeeded in a real deployment. CS28-1: a reviewer found backfill-job-sightings.test.ts invisible to CI. Now ai-provider.test.ts, on the one feature that sends owner content off-box. A class that recurs three times is a structural problem, not three mistakes.

CENSUS CORRECTED from the earlier "ten unwired checks" to ELEVEN - the eleventh is v2/scripts/visual-regression.ts (test:visual). Full list: check-ui.ts (NOW WIRED), visual-regression.ts, check-performance.ts, check-soak.ts, check-crash-recovery.ts, check-database-recovery.ts, check-queue-runtime.ts, benchmark-llm.ts, scripts/check-pages-ui.mjs, scripts/check-skills.mjs, infra/v3/check-full-disk.mjs.

DO NOT RE-WIRE, credit where due: check-monitoring.sh, check-backup.sh, check-proxy-recovery.sh and check-scheduler-health.sh ALREADY run in CI and were deliberately written stub-driven so that they could; check-backup.sh starts a real disposable Postgres container. NINE scripts legitimately require a live host and must be classified OPERATOR-ONLY rather than wired: check-provenance.sh, check-live-origin.sh, check-tls.ts, check-host-firewall.sh, check-owner-login.sh, check-live-flow.mjs, check-query-plans.sh, check-queue-contract.sh, check-maintenance.sh. Their existence is NOT evidence and the classification must say so.

COUPLING NOTE, prominent and unresolved: v2/packages/core/src/ai-provider.test.ts is an UNTRACKED file. It MUST be committed together with the v2/package.json change that names it, or CI fails module-not-found. Loud rather than silent, which is the right direction, but they cannot land separately.

STRUCTURAL HALF DONE 2026-09-25, and it was done FIRST deliberately, because fixing instances fixes files while fixing the structure fixes the class. Added v2/scripts/check-test-registration.ts plus the npm script test:registration and a CI step in the verify job. WHAT IT DOES: globs every *.test.ts under v2 (excluding node_modules, dist and .next), reads every npm script body, and treats any script naming a .test.ts path as CLAIMING that file. A file claimed by no script fails the check. It matches on the PATH rather than on script names, so a new test:whatever runner is picked up automatically - the check must not itself become the next stale enumeration, which would be the same defect one level up. WHY NOT JUST POINT CI AT THE GLOB, which is the obvious alternative and is wrong: six of these files need PostgreSQL, Redis and LocalStack. Running the glob in the no-services job would fail, and running it only in the services job would make the fast feedback loop slow. The scripts enumerate paths for real reasons. This makes the enumeration HONEST rather than removing it.

PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, each specific to a different failure mode, with the mutation verified present before each run per the standing rule. (1) ORPHANED FILE - the exact ai-provider scenario: created packages/core/src/orphan-probe.test.ts named by no script. Output: "1 test file(s) are named by NO npm script, so they run nowhere: - packages/core/src/orphan-probe.test.ts", exit 1. Deleted, verified gone, back to PASS. (2) MISSING FILE - the inverse: appended a nonexistent path to test:unit. Output: "package.json names 1 test file(s) that do not exist", exit 1. A script naming a missing file otherwise fails at run time with a confusing error rather than a clear one. Reverted, verified, back to PASS. IT ALSO REFUSES TO PASS WHILE UNABLE TO LOOK: an explicit assertion requires more than 10 test files to be found, so a broken glob or a wrong root fails loudly instead of reporting "all 0 files registered" - which is precisely the absence-versus-unreadable defect this repository has been bitten by repeatedly. Current run: PASS, all 17 v2 test files registered.

VERIFICATION LEVEL, and the CS-54 lesson applies directly here: this is WIRED and LOCALLY VERIFIED, NOT CI-EXECUTED. I ran the check itself and both falsifications locally; I validated ci.yml with a real YAML parser and confirmed the step is present in the verify job (23 steps). But no pipeline has executed it, and CS-54 just demonstrated that a local green can be actively misleading when the execution environment differs. A CI change verified only by local green is the same class of evidence gap this very ticket is about - things that are not actually executed look identical to things that are. Do not mark CI-EXECUTED without a pipeline run. NOT STARTED, stated plainly so the ticket is not read as done: the other ten unwired executable checks are unclassified; the four covering the NOT-VERIFIED failure modes (crash recovery, database recovery, queue runtime, soak) are not wired; the nine live-host scripts are not yet formally recorded as operator-only; and the deploy gate still runs no V2 tests.

REVIEWER VERDICT 2026-09-25: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS. RECORD DISCREPANCY FLAGGED, AND IT IS WRONG IN OUR OWN FAVOUR: this tickets currentStep says the systemic half is NOT STARTED, but checks-registry.json materialised during the review and check-full-disk.mjs is now classified ci. WRONG IN OUR FAVOUR IS STILL WRONG. Not corrected in this entry because the work belongs to the infrastructure session and the orchestrator has not verified the registry contents; to be re-synced once that session confirms, rather than adjusted on report.

CI VISIBILITY MEASURED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR AT SOURCE, as a standing fact for this ticket: the COMMITTED gates:test runs SIX checks (release:gate:test, agile:gate:test, deploy:gate:test, eol:check, progress:check, agents:check). The WORKING TREE defines EIGHT - state-readers:test and engineering:test were both added today and exist nowhere GitHub can see. test:registration (both) and checks:registry appear only in the UNCOMMITTED ci.yml. So of the guards built today, FIVE ARE INVISIBLE TO CI AND HAVE ZERO PIPELINE EXECUTIONS.

THE ONE EXCEPTION, and it raises CS-65s value: eol:check IS in the committed gates:test, so CI genuinely executes it today. Adding txt to LF_ONLY therefore lands in a check GitHub runs the moment anything is committed - that fix is real coverage, not local-only.

THE ci.yml COMMENT AT :121-127 IS THE BEST STATEMENT OF THE TWO-HOP RULE ANYWHERE IN THIS REPOSITORY, quoted verbatim: "Being named by an npm script is not enough here: the script must be one a workflow actually reaches, because the safety net exists and is unreachable is the original defect." That is the evidence rule encoded INTO CI rather than written down - the eighth convergence, and the first that enforces a PROCESS rule rather than a code invariant.

NOT A DUPLICATE UTILITY, recorded because it was nearly filed as one: scripts/check-test-registration.mjs (root) and v2/scripts/check-test-registration.ts are COMPLEMENTARY, and the reason is documented at ci.yml:121-127 - the root guard covers the root workspace, which the V2 guard does not glob. BOTH HALVES COMPLETE 2026-09-25, and THIS TICKETS OWN RECORD HAD BEEN UNDERSTATING IT ALL EVENING - currentStep still said the systemic half was NOT STARTED while checks-registry.json had already materialised. F-52-1 CLOSED PROPERLY RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER, and this is the eighth convergence DELIVERED rather than proposed: v2/scripts/check-test-registration.ts now imports workflowsExecuting from ci-reachability.mjs and applies it, so THE V2 BAR MOVED FROM "named by an npm script" TO "reached by a workflow". REGISTRY COUNT CONFIRMED AS 44, NOT 45, VERIFIED THREE WAYS IN THIS SESSION: array length 44, distinct check paths 44, and the classification sum 44 (ci 26, operator-only 10, manual 5, on-demand 2, deploy 1). THE SELF-ASSESSMENT BEHIND THE CORRECTION IS WORTH MORE THAN THE NUMBER, and is recorded verbatim: "I wrote I counted the registry array: 45 entries. I did not count it. I eyeballed a long array and reported a number as though it were measured." THE RULE THAT FOLLOWS: A COUNT IS A MEASUREMENT, AND REPORTING ONE YOU DID NOT TAKE IS THE SAME ACT AS REPORTING A CHECK YOU DID NOT RUN.

A HAND-MAINTAINED LIST FOUND BY READING A TICKET, NOT BY A CHECK: check-test-registration.mjs:37 enumerates ["scripts", "infra", "mobile-site"] and omits `data`. THE SAME DIVERGENCE PROBLEM AS THE TWO LF_ONLY LISTS that F-65-1 removed by deriving matchers from .gitattributes. THE PATTERN ACROSS THE WHOLE RUN, stated here because this is the ticket that owns it: EVERY CONVERGENCE TONIGHT WAS THE SAME THING - A HAND-MAINTAINED LIST THAT DRIFTED FROM WHAT IT WAS SUPPOSED TO DESCRIBE. Two lists of what a text file is; one list of columns versus the schema; one list of severities versus the renderer; one list of directories versus the repository.

WORDING CORRECTED 2026-09-25 FROM "All applicable criteria met" TO THE COUNTED FORM. The distinction is not cosmetic: "ALL THREE CRITERIA MET" IS FALSIFIABLE BY COUNTING; "ALL APPLICABLE CRITERIA MET" CANNOT FAIL, because an unmet criterion can be reclassified as not-applicable without anyone editing a number. It is the same shape as \bsurfaced\b, DEFERRED and eol=crlf - a word anyone can write that silently changes how a claim is graded - except that this one sat in the STATUS FIELD OF TEN TICKETS, which is the field a promotion decision reads. That makes it the most consequential of the four, not the least.

COUNT RE-TAKEN AND THE COUNTED CLAIM WAS WRONG: AC4 IS UNMET. It requires "the deploy gate executes V2 tests directly rather than relying only on transitive CI enforcement". Verified at source in this session: NO run: STEP IN deploy.yml INVOKES A V2 TEST. This tickets own ev[1] recorded it plainly - "VERIFIED: the DEPLOY GATE RUNS NO V2 TESTS. deploy.yml line 140 npm test ... is the ROOT (V1) suite".

HOW THE WRONG COUNT AROSE, because the mechanism matters more than the correction: this ticket was described as "BOTH HALVES COMPLETE" - the structural half (F-52-1) and the systemic half (checks-registry). AC4 IS A THIRD THING, and a phrase covering two halves was read as covering the whole. The counted form then inherited that reading without anyone re-checking the fourth criterion.

AC4 INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED UNMET 2026-09-25 AND VERIFIED AT SOURCE HERE. deploy.yml:139-140 runs `npm test`, which is the ROOT `vitest run` over the V1 domain packages. The v2 block at :158-164 runs typecheck, lint, format:check and build, then :168 `npm audit --omit=dev`. THERE IS NO TEST COMMAND FOR V2 ANYWHERE IN THE FILE - checked across the whole workflow, not only the deploy job.

THE DISTINCTION THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN MADE FIRST: AC4 IS OPEN BY DECISION, NOT UNFINISHED. deploy.yml:145-156 is an explicit comment recording the choice - "this gate runs NO V2 tests... That is defensible, because require-ci refuses to deploy a commit whose CI run did not succeed". A criterion left open deliberately and a criterion forgotten need completely different handling, and a record that says only "unmet" loses that.

AND THE COMMENT CONTAINS THE ARGUMENT AGAINST ITSELF, which is what settles it: it ends "the evidence lives in the CI run for the same SHA, and the OVERRIDE_CI INPUT CAN WAIVE EXACTLY THAT EVIDENCE." So the defence offered for relying on the transitive route NAMES THE REASON AC4 EXISTS. The strongest argument that the criterion is unmet rather than satisfied-by-another-route was already written in the file by the person who chose not to meet it.

THE UNLOCK IS AN OWNER CHOICE ABOUT DEPLOYMENT SAFETY, NOT AN ENGINEERING TASK, and must not be quietly resolved by an agent. Either (a) run the V2 suites in the deploy gate, meeting AC4 as written at the cost of a slower deploy and duplicated CI work, or (b) AMEND AC4 to accept require-ci as sufficient AND RECORD IN THE CRITERION ITSELF THAT override_ci CAN WAIVE IT. Option (b) is legitimate only if the waiver is written into the criterion; amending it silently would be the reclassification move that the applicable hedge made possible.

THE SHARPEST OBSERVATION FROM THE REVIEW, recorded because it generalises past this ticket: "AC4 IS THE ONE THAT applicable WOULD MOST EASILY HAVE ABSORBED, SINCE THE TRANSITIVE ROUTE IS GENUINELY DEFENSIBLE." THE HEDGE IS MOST TEMPTING PRECISELY WHERE THE CASE FOR IT IS STRONGEST - which is why removing the word matters more than any individual count it concealed. A hedge that only ever covered indefensible gaps would have been caught long ago.

MECHANISM, recorded because it matters more than the correction: this ticket was summarised as "BOTH HALVES COMPLETE" - the structural half (F-52-1) and the systemic half (checks-registry). AC4 IS A THIRD THING. A phrase counting two halves was read as covering the whole, so the count was right about the set it named and wrong about the set that mattered. A COUNT IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE SET IT IS TAKEN OVER, and "both halves" is a count over a set somebody chose rather than one the ticket defines.

PROVISIONAL MARKING WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25, SAME DAY IT WAS APPLIED, BECAUSE IT WAS TOO BROAD AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENT. The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". THE GATE COULD FAIL; ONLY ITS FIRST LINK COULD NOT. `npm run typecheck` chains four commands and the last, check-test-types.mjs, filters on /^\S+\.ts\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - WHICH MATCHES A PRODUCTION FILE AS READILY AS A TEST FILE - and exits 1. items.title: search_jobs and run_events use separate foreign keys where a composite would make a cross-owner row unrepresentable
items.userProblem: Owner isolation is enforced correctly in the application but is not structurally guaranteed by the schema on two tables.
items.source: Forensic security audit finding M-1, 2026-09-25
acceptanceCriteria: search_jobs and run_events either gain composite (owner_id, run_id) foreign keys matching the pattern already used by lead_history and resume_results, or the divergence is documented with an explicit reason
Any migration is forward-only, tested on a disposable database, and proven not to break existing rows
Owner isolation tests prove a cross-owner row is rejected at the database layer, not only at the application layer
evidence: AUDIT FINDING M-1: search_jobs and run_events reference searches.id and users.id SEPARATELY rather than as a composite (owner_id, run_id). lead_history and resume_results already use genuine composite foreign keys, where a cross-owner row is structurally unrepresentable - so the better pattern exists in this same schema and these two tables diverge from it.

NOT A REACHABLE EXPLOIT TODAY, and this is important context: the auditor read every query in v2/apps/api/src/app.ts and confirmed the application layer always scopes correctly. This is defence-in-depth, not an open door. It is also already recorded as an open P2 in .ai/progress.json and remains true.
NOT INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED by the Orchestrator against the schema in this cycle - carried forward as an audit finding. Confirm against v2/packages/core/src before implementing.

MOVED DISCOVERY -> READY 2026-09-25. The only thing holding it in DISCOVERY was its own note that the defect was "NOT INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED against the schema". That was one file read, and it has now been done twice - by the audit and independently in this session. THE DEFECT IS REAL: run_events and search_jobs declare runId and ownerId as SEPARATE SINGLE-COLUMN FKs, while the same file twice uses the composite pattern foreignKey({ columns: [ownerId, leadId] }) and foreignKey({ columns: [ownerId, uploadId] }). The divergence is real, the precedent is established, and nothing about the design is undecided.

UNRECORDED PREREQUISITE FOUND BY THE AUDIT, WHICH WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE SURFACED MID-MIGRATION: a composite FK (owner_id, run_id) -> search_runs(owner_id, id) REQUIRES A UNIQUE CONSTRAINT ON THE REFERENCED COLUMNS. Verified in this session: search_runs does NOT have one. It carries uniqueIndex("search_owner_key").on(ownerId, idempotencyKey) at schema.ts:84 and index("search_owner_created") at :85, and id alone is the primary key.

MEANWHILE BOTH PRECEDENT TABLES CARRY EXACTLY THE HELPER THAT MAKES IT WORK, and they were plainly added for this purpose: uniqueIndex("lead_owner_id").on(ownerId, id) at schema.ts:202 and uniqueIndex("resume_upload_owner_id").on(ownerId, id) at :271. WITHOUT ADDING uniqueIndex("search_owner_id").on(ownerId, id) FIRST, THE MIGRATION FAILS WITH POSTGRES 42830 - no unique constraint matching given keys for the referenced table. That index is the EXPLICIT FIRST MIGRATION STEP.

RECORDED BECAUSE IT GENERALISES: the pattern to copy already existed twice and nobody had noticed the third table lacked its enabler. A migration that follows an established precedent can still fail on the precondition the precedent quietly satisfies.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; re-check if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 17:00 IST on 2026-09-25.

DELIVERED 2026-09-25, and THE ORDERING CONSTRAINT THE AUDIT IDENTIFIED WAS RESPECTED: the search_owner_id unique index landed in 0015_outgoing_pride.sql:1 and schema.ts:90 before any composite FK was added, so Postgres 42830 was never risked. Both target tables converted - composite foreignKey blocks at schema.ts:157 and :178 alongside the two pre-existing ones - and NO single-column references(() => searches.id) form remains anywhere.

TWO MIGRATIONS DELIBERATELY, NOT ONE, and the reasoning is the keeper: 0015 creates the unique index alone; 0016 drops the four single-column constraints and adds the composite FKs. A SEPARATE MIGRATION IS A GUARANTEE; STATEMENT ORDER INSIDE ONE GENERATED FILE IS AN ASSUMPTION.

BOTH WERE GENERATED BY drizzle-kit AND THEN READ - NEVER HAND-WRITTEN. Recorded explicitly because a hand-written migration that happens to work is a different artefact from a generated one that was reviewed.
MIGRATIONS RECONCILE: 17 .sql files, 17 journal entries, verified independently in this session. No orphaned entry, no unjournalled migration.

TYPECHECK IS THE LOAD-BEARING RESULT FOR THIS TICKET SPECIFICALLY, and is cited here rather than only on CS-61: the composite foreign keys changed the SHAPE of run_events and search_jobs, and `tsc -b` exit 0 across the v2 project is what proves NO CONSUMER WAS LEFT REFERENCING THE OLD SINGLE-COLUMN FORM. A migration that applies cleanly but leaves a stale consumer is the failure mode this rules out.

CEILING, WHICH TRAVELS WITH THE NUMBERS: produced on Node v22.23.2 against a declared floor of 24 (.nvmrc, both engines.node fields, ci.yml NODE_VERSION). NONE OF IT IS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE SUPPORTED RUNTIME AND NONE OF IT IS CI EVIDENCE - the SHA has not moved.

CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-25 AFTER CS-76, AND IT NARROWS RATHER THAN RETRACTS THE CLAIM. The load-bearing result cited here is that tsc -b proves no consumer was left referencing the pre-composite single-column form of run_events and search_jobs. THAT REMAINS TRUE FOR SOURCE CONSUMERS. It was never true for TEST consumers: all ten packages/core test files are excluded from the build, so A TEST STILL REFERENCING THE OLD SHAPE WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN CAUGHT BY THE TYPECHECK. The runtime suites passing is the evidence covering that gap, not tsc.

BOUNDED TYPECHECK EVIDENCE - RE-WORDED FROM "PROVISIONAL" 2026-09-25, AND THE VERB CHANGE IS THE POINT. This ticket cites a BARE `tsc -b`, which is incremental and was observed exiting 0 while a genuine production error existed (collect.ts TS2353) because a stale .tsbuildinfo declared the project up to date. THAT DOES NOT RETRACT THE RESULT AND DOES NOT MAKE IT SUSPECT: the command ran, it reported truthfully on what it examined, and the source it examined did compile. IT BOUNDS THE RESULT. The run was NARROWER THAN THE CLAIM IT WAS QUOTED FOR - it is evidence that the projects tsc considered up to date had no new errors, not evidence that the tree is clean. "PROVISIONAL" WAS THE WRONG WORD BECAUSE IT IMPLIES THE RESULT MIGHT BE FALSE. It was not false; it was narrow. Re-verify the wider claim with `tsc -b --force` or a cleared .tsbuildinfo - and note that v2 typecheck now begins with --force, so the npm script no longer has this bound. The original lines are deliberately kept: they record what was actually run. NOTHING IS DEMOTED FOR THIS.

The existing database tests include the cross-owner rejection at the database layer.
