items.title: Two IP-keyed rate limiters collapse to a single global bucket behind the proxy
items.userProblem: The only unauthenticated write path in the API has no rate limit, and the obvious fix does not work because every request reaches the API from the same address.
items.source: Security review of CS-57, finding P2, 2026-09-25; the design constraint found by the Orchestrator while attempting the fix
acceptanceCriteria: The login limiter cannot be exhausted by a third party in a way that locks the legitimate owner out of signing in
The register limiter is either keyed usefully or explicitly documented as global-and-acceptable while registration stays disabled

Any future limiter on POST /api/logout is keyed on something other than the client IP, and exhausting any other limiter must never prevent signing out - the property test at database.test.ts:3300 must keep passing unchanged
No limit is implemented by skipping auth.logout for malformed tokens, which would reintroduce the timing asymmetry CS-57 AC2 exists to remove
docs/SECURITY.md and docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md accurately describe which limits are per-owner, which are per-account and which are global
evidence: ORIGIN: CS-57 exempted POST /api/logout from the session requirement so a no-cookie logout answers identically to a real one. A Security review correctly observed that this made it the ONLY unauthenticated WRITE path in the API - each call costs a SELECT plus a DELETE FROM sessions, reachable by anything able to set an Origin header. Cheap sustained write/WAL amplification.

ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED, with the evidence recorded on CS-57: a logout:<sha256(request.ip)> limiter at 30/60, following the pattern already used at app.ts:237 and :246, broke database.test.ts:3300 - a test that deliberately exhausts the LOGIN limiter and then asserts logout still returns 200. That property is correct and more important than the finding: being locked out of signing in must not lock you out of signing out. Failure was reproducible with failureType testCodeFailure, explicitly distinguished from the CS-58 cross-talk signature.

THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT, which is the real content of this ticket: trustProxy is false (correctly - a forwarded header is spoofable), so request.ip is the real peer. But the deployed topology puts Caddy in front of the API, so every request arrives from ONE address and a per-IP limit is effectively a GLOBAL limit. Raising the number until the test passed would have produced a control that looks like per-client throttling and is not.

SCOPE NOTE: the same weakness applies to the EXISTING login (10/60 plus 20/60 per account) and register (5/3600) limiters, which use the identical key. Those are pre-existing and out of scope for CS-57, but they are the reason this needs a design decision rather than a number.

CONSTRAINT FROM THE REVIEWER, carried forward verbatim because it is the trap: do NOT satisfy a test by narrowing when auth.logout is called, and do NOT relax the CSRF check on logout "since it is exempt anyway". Both weaken a control to make a test pass.

MECHANISM VERIFIED END TO END 2026-09-25, from source rather than by inference, on three independent pieces of evidence that agree: (1) infra/v3/compose.production.yml:72 sets CAREERSCOPE_UPSTREAM to 127.0.0.1:5280, so Caddy proxies over loopback; (2) the api service uses network_mode: service:proxy, so it SHARES the proxy network namespace and there is no separate address to observe; (3) infra/v3/Caddyfile.production:57 and :78 carry "header_up -X-Forwarded-For", which DELETES the header rather than setting it - a deliberate and correct hardening choice given trustProxy: false, but it means no client address reaches the API by any route. CONCLUSION: request.ip is 127.0.0.1 for EVERY production request. The mechanism is confirmed, and it is stronger than "near-global" - it is exactly global.

SCOPE IS MUCH NARROWER THAN FIRST SUSPECTED, and this correction matters more than the confirmation. I enumerated all NINETEEN rateLimit call sites in v2/apps/api/src/app.ts. Only TWO are IP-keyed: register at L238 and login at L247, both via createHash(sha256).update(request.ip) at L237/L246. The other SEVENTEEN are keyed on request.ownerId or on accountKey and are entirely unaffected. THE SPECIFIC CONCERN RAISED IS REFUTED: docs/SECURITY.md:25 says password change "is rate limited to 5/hour". That limiter is app.ts:300, keyed password:${request.ownerId!} - PER OWNER, exactly as documented. The security document is ACCURATE and must NOT be changed. The same is true of session revocation, uploads, resume operations, preparation, AI elaboration, profile, leads, search, cancel, export and events. No documented control is overstated. Also: login carries a SECOND limiter at L249, login-account:${accountKey} at 20/60, which is per-account and works correctly. That is the real control against credential stuffing against a specific account, and it is intact.

REAL IMPACT, stated without inflation: (a) REGISTER - global 5/3600, but compose.production.yml:30 sets REGISTRATION_ENABLED to false by default, so the route is disabled in the deployed configuration and the practical impact is negligible; (b) LOGIN - global 10/60 means any third party able to reach the origin can exhaust the bucket and LOCK THE LEGITIMATE OWNER OUT OF SIGNING IN for up to a minute, repeatedly. That is a genuine availability defect and a trivially cheap one to trigger. It is NOT a confidentiality defect: the per-account limiter and Argon2id are untouched. PRIORITY HELD AT P2, deliberately, rather than raised to P1. P1 was proposed on the theory that a documented control does not do what it says; verification shows no documented control is overstated. What remains is an availability issue on one route in a single-owner application. Inflating it would make the backlog less useful, which is the opposite of the point.

WHY THE FIX IS NOT "SET trustProxy: true": that would let any client forge X-Forwarded-For and choose its own limiter bucket, defeating the limiter completely - strictly worse than global. And Caddy currently STRIPS the header, so it would also have to be changed to set a trustworthy one. That is a deployment change affecting the security boundary and needs its own review. Design options worth weighing: have Caddy set a trusted client identifier and trust it ONLY from the proxy; apply the limit at the Caddy layer where the real peer is visible; or accept a global login limit and pair it with an owner-facing lockout notification. Do not pick one without a Security and System Designer pass.

REVIEWER VERDICT 2026-09-25: APPROVED AS DESIGN, with one scope finding. Also recorded as THE BEST-EVIDENCED TICKET OF THE BATCH: all four sub-claims of "request.ip is 127.0.0.1 for every production request" confirmed at source - CAREERSCOPE_UPSTREAM: 127.0.0.1:5280, network_mode: service:proxy, header_up -X-Forwarded-For in BOTH Caddyfile blocks, and REGISTRATION_ENABLED:-false. Not near-global. Exactly global.

F-59-1 (P2) - AC5 RE-OPENED. REFUTING AN INFLATED CLAIM IS NOT MEETING THE CRITERION. AC5 requires the documentation to state which limits are per-owner, which are per-account and WHICH ARE GLOBAL. Our evidence concluded that docs/SECURITY.md is accurate and must NOT be changed. The reviewer read it: both its statements are true, but NOWHERE DOES IT SAY THE LOGIN LIMITER IS A SINGLE GLOBAL BUCKET, and its trustProxy: false line states the safety property while omitting the availability consequence - which is this tickets entire subject. The refutation is correct and closes a DIFFERENT question; AC5 requires an ADDITION to SECURITY.md, not a defence of it.

F-59-1 PATTERN - this is the TICKETS-OWN-RESTATEMENT-NARROWS-ITS-CRITERION shape, the third instance recorded today. A ticket answers a question adjacent to its acceptance criterion, answers it correctly, and the criterion quietly stops being the thing measured.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 15:40 IST on 2026-09-25 this verdict should be re-taken rather than trusted.

UPGRADED FROM INFERENCE TO FACT 2026-09-25: compose.production.yml settles what was previously argued - CAREERSCOPE_UPSTREAM: 127.0.0.1:5280 and network_mode: service:proxy on every app service. "request.ip is 127.0.0.1 for every production request" is now FACT, not inference. REGISTRATION_ENABLED:-false likewise.

AC5 CLOSED 2026-09-25 - the addition was made, not argued for. docs/SECURITY.md now carries a "Which rate limits are per-owner, per-account and global" table stating explicitly that login:<sha256(request.ip)> and register:<sha256(request.ip)> are A SINGLE SHARED GLOBAL BUCKET in production, alongside the per-owner and per-account limiters that are unaffected.

IT ALSO RECORDS THE AVAILABILITY CONSEQUENCE THE trustProxy: false LINE OMITTED, which was this tickets entire subject: no request is attributed to the wrong owner and nothing leaks, but the login limiter bounds EVERYONE TOGETHER, so one client can exhaust the shared budget and deny logins to all users while doing nothing to bound a distributed attacker per-source. And it names the wrong fix explicitly - setting trustProxy: true would believe a header the proxy currently DELETES, converting an availability problem into a spoofable one.
NO GATE WAS NEEDED FOR THIS: docs/ is owned by this session, the change required no host, no commit and no owner decision. It was the free win in the READY tier and is now done.

PRIORITY NOTE: CS-44 has newly added CS-59 as a dependency, so CS-59 now blocks downstream discovery work as well as its own acceptance. The remaining half is the proxy-layer change, which is infrastructure and host-bound.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; re-check if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 16:45 IST on 2026-09-25.

RE-PRIORITISED P2 -> P1 2026-09-25: CS-44 now declares CS-59 as a dependency, because AC2 bounded attempts cannot be honest while every client shares one rate-limit key. CS-59 therefore BLOCKS DOWNSTREAM DISCOVERY WORK as well as its own acceptance, which is more than its recorded P2 reflected.

NOTE FOR THE COORDINATOR: AC5 IS NO LONGER OUTSTANDING. It was closed earlier in this session - docs/SECURITY.md now carries the per-owner / per-account / GLOBAL table naming the two IP-keyed limiters as a single shared bucket, with the availability consequence and the trustProxy: true anti-fix recorded. The remaining half is the proxy-layer change, which is infrastructure and host-bound.

AC5 COMPLETED 2026-09-25 with three further amendments to docs/SECURITY.md, the third of which is the one that closes it properly. (a) typo fixed - "a availability" -> "an availability". (b) the per-owner table row no longer hand-waves at "the other authenticated limiters": it now names the read budgets searches-read/leads-read (240/min) and profile-read/market-read (120/min), and states WHY they are safe - ownerId comes from the session, so THE BUCKET CANNOT BE CHOSEN BY A CALLER.

(c) THE OWNER-ISOLATION PARAGRAPH NOW LISTS FOUR TABLES, NOT TWO: lead_history, resume_results, run_events and search_jobs all key on (ownerId, id) of the owning row, following CS-53 landing this cycle. AC5 asked the documentation to state which limits are global; the section now ALSO states what makes per-owner isolation STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN CONVENTIONAL - a cross-owner reference is not representable.
AC1 STILL NEEDS THE SECURITY AND SYSTEM DESIGNER PASS and has NOT been pre-empted. CS-44 now depends on this ticket.
items.securityImpact: Availability and resource-exhaustion on an unauthenticated write path. No confidentiality or integrity impact: the DELETE keys on sha256 of a caller-supplied token, so it can only destroy a session whose token the caller already holds.
items.architectureImpact: Rate-limit keying strategy across the API; possibly requires the proxy to pass a trustworthy client identifier, which is a deployment change and needs its own review.
items.currentStep: READY. Mechanism VERIFIED end to end from source. Scope is narrower than first suspected: 2 of 19 limiters affected, no documented control is overstated. The real impact is a trivial owner-lockout DoS on login.
items.summary: Logout became the only unauthenticated write when CS-57 exempted it. The obvious per-IP limiter both breaks a correct property test and is near-global behind the proxy, so this needs a key that is not the client IP.

items.title: There is no test file under v2/apps/api, so API HTTP tests are undiscoverable
items.userProblem: Someone looking for the API tests finds an empty directory, concludes there are none, and writes duplicates - or worse, concludes the API is untested and stops looking.
items.source: Security review of CS-57, 2026-09-25 - the reviewer could not locate an assertion that does exist, precisely because of this
acceptanceCriteria: API HTTP-level tests are discoverable from v2/apps/api, whether by living there or by an explicit pointer that a reader cannot miss
Any move preserves the existing assertions exactly - no test is weakened, skipped or dropped in the relocation, and the same npm script still executes them
The test count before and after is identical, proving nothing was lost in the move
evidence: v2/apps/api/src contains only app.ts, main.ts and openapi.ts. There is NO .test.ts file anywhere under v2/apps/api - confirmed by directory listing, not inference.

The API HTTP-level tests actually live in v2/packages/core/src/database.test.ts and run via test:integration. They are real and substantial - the CS-57 suite alone drives app.inject() for no-cookie, stale-cookie, live-session, forged-CSRF, wrong-method and neighbouring-path cases.

THIS DEFECT HAS ALREADY CAUSED A FALSE FINDING, which is the strongest possible evidence for it: the 2026-09-25 Security review raised a P2 that CS-57 AC2 had "no automated coverage" and that the claimed CSRF-403 assertion was "NOT LOCATED". It was looking in v2/scripts/check-ui.ts and had no grep. The assertion exists at database.test.ts:3771-3777 inside the CS-57 test at :3714. A careful reviewer, reading exactly where a reasonable person would read, reached the wrong conclusion about security coverage.
The reviewer own framing is worth keeping: API tests living in packages/core/src/database.test.ts is "the last place anyone would look".
REVIEWER VERDICT 2026-09-25: APPROVED.

F-60-2 RECORDED AS A POSITIVE, which is unusual enough to be worth stating plainly: if the tests genuinely move to v2/apps/api/src/*.test.ts, CS-52s guard PROTECTS THE MOVE FOR FREE. The new path must be claimed by a script or it is an orphan, and test:integration stale reference becomes a missing. BOTH HALVES OF A BOTCHED MOVE FAIL LOUDLY, which materially lowers the risk this tickets architectureImpact warns about.

F-60-1: if AC1 is satisfied by a POINTER FILE, nothing keeps the pointer true - and a pointer naming a moved file is WORSE than no pointer, because it is confidently wrong. AC1 must require the pointer to be machine-checked rather than merely present.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 15:40 IST on 2026-09-25 this verdict should be re-taken rather than trusted.

CONFIRMED GENUINELY READY 2026-09-25 by independent audit, and it is the clean pick-up of this tier: every identifier its acceptance criteria name was verified to exist, there is no undeclared dependency and no scope contradiction, and the criteria are satisfiable as written. P3, small, one sitting.

AND THE MOVE IS MECHANICALLY PROTECTED: CS-52s guard turns a stale path into a `missing` and a new unclaimed path into an `orphan`, both failing at check-test-registration.ts:98. Both halves of a botched move fail loudly, which is why this one can be handed to anyone.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; re-check if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 16:45 IST on 2026-09-25.

ONE REAL RESIDUAL FROM THE 2026-09-25 TEST SWEEP, RECORDED HERE FOR THE WORKERS SESSION - v2/apps/workers/search/src/collect.test.ts:699 iterates result.outcomes with .every(o => o.errorCode === "source_timeout") AND result.outcomes HAS NO LENGTH GUARD. Verified by reading from the construction site forward rather than from the assertion backward.

IT IS A SHARPER SHAPE THAN "NO GUARD", WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED REVIEW: a count assertion IS present seven lines above - assert.equal(elapsed.length, 5) - and elapsed is pushed once per provider inside a finally block, so it genuinely proves all five sources ran and timed out. BUT elapsed AND result.outcomes ARE TWO DIFFERENT COLLECTIONS. If the collector dropped outcomes, result.outcomes would be empty, every() would return true, and a five-source-timeout test would pass having verified no outcome at all.

THE GUARD IS ON A DIFFERENT COLLECTION THAN THE ONE BEING ITERATED. That is distinct from a missing guard and harder to see, because the nearby count assertion satisfies the eye. FIX: assert.equal(result.outcomes.length, 5) before the every(). One line; not blocking; changes no ticket status.

LINE NUMBER CORRECTED IN THIS RECORD FROM :698 TO :699 BEFORE IT WAS RELIED ON. The first write cited :698, which is assert.equal(result.jobs.length, 0) - a DIFFERENT and correctly-guarded assertion. An off-by-one in a citation is not cosmetic: it points the next reader at a line that looks fine, and the finding then reads as already fixed. It was caught because the recording script asserted the cited line actually contained result.outcomes.every before writing anything.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-28: v2/apps/api/TESTING.md now provides an explicit pointer beside the API source to packages/core/src/database.test.ts and its unchanged test:integration command. No assertions moved or weakened; the test surface is identical by construction.
items.securityImpact: None directly. It caused a security reviewer to report a coverage gap that does not exist, which is a meaningful second-order risk - a false negative in the other direction would be worse.
items.architectureImpact: Test file placement only. No production code change. Note database.test.ts is large and shared, so a move must be careful and must not split a suite that shares fixtures.
items.currentStep: Release Manager - hosted CI run 36424073277 passed the integration suite with the discoverability pointer in place and the unchanged test:integration command.
items.summary: API HTTP tests exist and are good, but they live where nobody looks. A Security reviewer already concluded coverage was missing when it was not.

items.title: React Query keys are owner-agnostic, so one owner cache can serve another
items.userProblem: Cached data is keyed without the owner, so the only thing preventing one owner seeing another data after a session change is that something remembered to clear the cache.
items.source: Independent review of CS-36, 2026-09-25, after four attempts to TEST the property each failed for a different reason
acceptanceCriteria: Owner-scoped query keys - [profile, ownerId], [leads, ownerId, status], [resumes, ownerId] and any sibling - so a different owner structurally misses the cache instead of relying on a reset having run. EXEMPTION, stated so nobody rewrites it circularly: [session] stays owner-agnostic, because it is the query through which the owner is DISCOVERED and cannot be keyed by its own result.
cache.clear() on the three teardown paths is retained as defence in depth, not removed because the keys now make it redundant

Prove the change does what it claims. With every cache.clear() deliberately disabled, drive owner A -> sign out -> owner B ENTIRELY THROUGH THE APPS OWN UI WITHIN A SINGLE DOCUMENT - no page.goto(), no page.reload(), no context recreation at any point - and assert owner B receives none of owner A cached data. PAIRED POSITIVE CONTROL, SAME TEST, SAME SURFACE: with the resets still disabled and the keys reverted to owner-agnostic, owner B MUST receive owner A data. Without that control the experiment cannot show it was capable of observing the defect. ANCHOR THE EXPERIMENT ON THE [profile] QUERY: profile-editor.tsx:400 sets staleTime: Infinity, so it NEVER REFETCHES. The bleed is therefore PERSISTENT rather than a flash, which makes the assertion far harder to pass by accident and removes any argument that a race, not the cache, produced the result.
evidence: ORIGIN: CS-36 AC2 requires that old requests or caches cannot restore prior-session data. FOUR attempts to test that property each failed for a different reason - timing, getByText not reading form controls, secrets belonging to the wrong session, and finally the root cause that the test navigates with page.goto(), a full document load that destroys the in-memory cache unconditionally. Four failures with four distinct causes is the signal to change approach rather than attempt a fifth test.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT: profile-editor.tsx:397 uses queryKey [profile]; saved-leads and resume-panel use [leads, status] and [resumes]. NONE carries an owner. That is precisely WHY one owner cache can serve another - the second owner asks for the same key and gets the first owner data. cache.clear() works, but it is the only thing standing between the two, on three separate teardown paths, one of which (the unauthenticated resolve) was found missing the call entirely during this work.

WHY STRUCTURAL BEATS TESTED HERE, and this is the general lesson rather than a preference: keyed as [profile, ownerId] a different owner simply MISSES the cache. The bug class becomes unrepresentable rather than tested, and the entire question of how to observe a transient cache flash in a browser test disappears. It also lets cache.clear() be a belt rather than the only thing holding the trousers up.

FIFTH CONVERGENCE ON ONE PRINCIPLE IN A SINGLE RUN, which is why this is filed rather than noted: CS-57 keying on routeOptions.url made a path-normalisation bypass unrepresentable; CS-56 constraining at extraction time made unconstrained titles unrepresentable; CS-13 F-2 splitting message into what+detail made a bare error message a COMPILE ERROR; CS-52 checking script registration made an invisible test file impossible; and this. When five independent investigations reach the same shape of answer, that is the codebase indicating where its defects come from.

SCOPE NOTE: filed separately rather than expanded into CS-36 deliberately. CS-36 AC2 test clause stays UNMET and recorded; this gets its own acceptance criteria, because it is a design change to caching rather than a test for an existing behaviour.

REVIEWER VERDICT 2026-09-25: REJECTED AS SPECIFIED. Two P1s, both caught BEFORE anyone implemented it. Status moved READY -> DISCOVERY on the reviewers recommendation, which the coordinator adopted: implementing against the previous wording produces either a forbidden server change or an email-keyed near-miss.

F-61-1 (P1) - architectureImpact WAS FALSE, and the WRONG FIX IS THE EASY ONE. Verified at source by the orchestrator: v2/apps/web/src/lib/session.ts:4-16 is the entire client session contract - { authenticated, csrf?, email?, registrationEnabled?, aiEnabled? }. THERE IS NO ownerId ON THE CLIENT. So AC1 keys are unimplementable without either adding ownerId to GET /api/session (a server change the ticket forbade) or keying on email, which is OPTIONAL and MUTABLE. An implementer under time pressure takes the email route PRECISELY BECAUSE THE TICKET TOLD THEM NOT TO CHANGE THE SERVER, and gets [profile, undefined] whenever email is absent - owner-agnostic again, indistinguishable from the bug being fixed. An identity PROXY is not an identity. architectureImpact amended to require the server change.
F-61-1 PATTERN, worth the list: "no server change" was ASSERTED WITHOUT READING THE CLIENT CONTRACT, and falsified by a fifteen-line type. One file read at filing time would have caught it.

F-61-2 (P1) - AC3 WOULD HAVE BEEN THE FIFTH VACUOUS FALSIFICATION, BY DEFAULT. Verified good news first, and it corrects our own record: all three teardown paths in authenticated-shell.tsx use router.replace() - CLIENT-SIDE navigation, not a document load (L44 unauthenticated resolve, L70 SESSION_EXPIRED_EVENT, L84 logout.onSuccess). The in-memory cache therefore genuinely SURVIVES an owner change through the apps own UI, which is what makes AC3 possible at all.

RECORD CORRECTION, wrong in our own favour previously: ALL THREE cache.clear() CALLS ARE PRESENT (L43, L69, L83), including the unauthenticated-resolve one an earlier evidence entry recorded as missing. AC2 is currently satisfiable.

F-61-2 THE TRAP, and why AC3 was amended: our own CS-36 evidence records that attempt four failed because the test navigated with page.goto(), a full document load that destroys the in-memory cache unconditionally. THAT HAZARD IS UNCHANGED AND THE OLD AC3 DID NOT EXCLUDE IT. The obvious fifth attempt - log in as A, page.goto("/"), log in as B, assert B sees nothing - PASSES with owner-scoped keys, PASSES with ["profile"], and PASSES with every cache.clear() disabled. The navigation does the work and the assertion cannot tell.

F-61-2 LESSON, sharper than the one we recorded when praising AC3 for encoding its own falsification: A CRITERION CAN ENCODE ITS OWN FALSIFICATION AND STILL BE VOID IF IT OMITS THE CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES THE EXPERIMENT VALID. AC3 now states the constraint (single document, no goto/reload/context recreation) AND a paired positive control - with resets disabled and keys reverted, owner B MUST receive owner A data - because that control is the only thing that can prove the experiment could observe the defect at all.

F-61-3 (P3) FIXED IN AC1: the criterion said "and any sibling", but ["session"] at session.ts:24 is itself owner-agnostic and must be, since it is how the owner is discovered. The exemption is now named, so an implementer does not circularly rewrite it.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 15:40 IST on 2026-09-25 this verdict should be re-taken rather than trusted.

AC3 SHARPENED 2026-09-25 with a detail verified at source: profile-editor.tsx:400 is staleTime: Infinity, so the [profile] query never refetches. Anchoring the experiment there makes the cached bleed PERSISTENT rather than a momentary flash - a far harder thing to pass by accident, and it forecloses the "it was a race, not the cache" explanation before anyone offers it.

AC1 MET AND THE MECHANISM VERIFIED, not asserted. THE API SIDE CHOSE A THIRD OPTION BETTER THAN EITHER THIS SESSION PROPOSED: app.ts:254 returns `owner: createHash("sha256").update(`owner:${session.ownerId}`).digest("hex")` - AN OPAQUE DIGEST, not the raw ownerId and not email. Three properties, each killing one identified failure mode: ALWAYS PRESENT on authenticated responses (unlike email?, so the key cannot silently become owner-agnostic); IMMUTABLE per owner (unlike email, an identity PROXY); and OPAQUE, so the raw owner id never reaches the browser. THAT LAST IS A SECURITY PROPERTY THE "add ownerId" SUGGESTION FROM THIS SESSION WOULD HAVE QUIETLY GIVEN AWAY.

AND THE DIGEST IS DELIBERATELY NOT DERIVED FROM THE SESSION TOKEN - the subtle half. A per-session value would satisfy isolation AND destroy the cache on every sign-in: a performance regression disguised as a fix.

WEB SIDE IMPLEMENTED IN v2/apps/web: Session gained `owner?: string` with the reasoning recorded; ownerKey(owner, name, ...rest) places the owner segment immediately after the name SO PREFIX INVALIDATION KEEPS WORKING (invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["leads"] }) still matches ["leads", owner, status]); a NO_OWNER sentinel exists so an absent owner can never collapse to an owner-agnostic key; and 16 query definitions across 6 files are scoped.

["session"] IS DELIBERATELY NOT SCOPED and must never be - it is the query through which the owner is DISCOVERED, so keying it by its own result would be circular. The exemption is named in AC1 and in the source comment.

THE TRAP WAS REAL AND IS CLOSED: `enabled: !!owner` is now on ALL SIXTEEN owner-scoped queries - 10 existing enabled clauses extended, 6 created where none existed. Without it a query can run BEFORE the session resolves, building ["leads", undefined, status] and MERGING EVERY OWNER BACK INTO ONE BUCKET while looking owner-scoped in the source. It is also the hazard AC3 would have missed, since the first owner data would sit in the undefined bucket rather than the keyed one.

VERIFIED PER FILE, NOT BY TOTALS: dashboard/page.tsx 6/6, job-search-view 2/2, preparation-panel 1/1, profile-editor 1/1, resume-panel 2/2, saved-leads 4/4. Composition is correct where two conditions are needed - `enabled: !!owner && session.data?.authenticated === true` rather than one or the other. v2 typecheck exit 0, lint clean.

AC3 REMAINS OPEN AND IS THE REAL WORK: the single-document experiment with every cache.clear() disabled, no page.goto/reload/context recreation, anchored on the [profile] query (staleTime: Infinity, so the bleed is persistent rather than a flash), WITH the paired positive control proving the test can observe the defect at all.
RUNTIME CAVEAT: verified on Node v22.23.2, below the declared minimum of 24.

CS-36 NOW DEPENDS ON THIS TICKET: its AC2 test clause has been UNMET through four attempts, and its own evidence identifies this tickets structural approach as the way out. CS-61 AC3 is therefore the unlock for BOTH - one experiment, two tickets. That raises the value of AC3 above what this ticket alone reflects.

DELIBERATELY NOT CAVEATED BY CS-76, AND THE REASON IS WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE BLANKET-APPLYING THE CAVEAT WOULD HAVE BEEN ITS OWN ERROR. CS-76 excludes test files in packages/core, apps/api and apps/workers/search. apps/web does the OPPOSITE - its include is ["next-env.d.ts","**/*.ts","**/*.tsx",...] with only node_modules excluded, so web test files WOULD be type-checked; there simply are none today. THE SIXTEEN OWNER-SCOPED QUERY KEYS AND THEIR enabled GUARDS LIVE IN apps/web AND WERE GENUINELY TYPE-CHECKED.

THE GENERAL POINT: a caveat applied uniformly to all 26 tickets citing a typecheck pass would have been faster and WRONG - it would have downgraded evidence that is actually sound, which corrodes the record in the opposite direction from an overclaim but corrodes it just the same. THE SCOPE OF A CAVEAT IS ITSELF A MEASUREMENT.

AC3 EXPERIMENT DESIGN SUPPLIED 2026-09-25 - COPY CS-48 AC10 AT database.test.ts:4098-4131, which is now recorded as the reference implementation for owner-isolation testing here. ITS SHAPE: assert the precondition before measuring anything, prove the collection non-empty so the empty case cannot pass, run the POSITIVE ON THE SAME SURFACE FIRST, then the paired negative, and drive both owners through the SAME identifier so the route cannot distinguish them by input. CS-61 AC3 HAS ALREADY DEFEATED FOUR ATTEMPTS; a fifth should look like this rather than be invented again.

PROVISIONAL MARKING WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25, SAME DAY IT WAS APPLIED, BECAUSE IT WAS TOO BROAD AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENT. The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". THE GATE COULD FAIL; ONLY ITS FIRST LINK COULD NOT. `npm run typecheck` chains four commands and the last, check-test-types.mjs, filters on /^\S+\.ts\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - WHICH MATCHES A PRODUCTION FILE AS READILY AS A TEST FILE - and exits 1. Anyone running the npm script WOULD have been told.

THIS TICKET DOES NOT CITE A BARE `tsc -b`, so its typecheck evidence was never in the unfalsifiable form and stands unqualified. The narrowed set is 4 of the original 29: CS-53, CS-62, CS-76, CS-77 - ALL FOUR WRITTEN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, which is the correct place for the correction to land.

API HALF VERIFIED AT SOURCE 2026-09-26: app.ts:254 returns a sha256 digest of "owner:<ownerId>" - 64 hex characters on every authenticated response. A DIGEST RATHER THAN ownerId, deliberately: the client only needs to tell owners apart, and publishing the raw id would put THE ONE VALUE THAT MUST NEVER BE CLIENT-SUPPLIED into client hands. Not token-derived either, since a per-session value would churn the cache on every sign-in for no extra isolation.

WEB HALF AUDITED AND COMPLETE: 32 source files scanned, 16 OWNER-SCOPED QUERY KEYS AND 16 enabled: !!owner GATES, plus one deliberately unscoped ["session"] key. Every file carrying a scoped key also carries a gate.

THE AUDIT WALKED THE FILESYSTEM RATHER THAN USING git grep, AND THAT WAS NOT INCIDENTAL: git grep FOUND GATES IN ONLY FOUR FILES BECAUSE IT CANNOT SEE UNTRACKED FILES, AND 68% OF v2/apps/web/src IS UNTRACKED. Using it would have reported a shortfall that does not exist - the same blind spot that produced a wrong CS-76 AC1 total earlier in this run, avoided this time only because the lesson was already written down.

THE isSuccess TRAP IS CONFIRMED REAL AND CONFIRMED AVOIDED. app.ts:223-226 returns a SUCCESSFUL 200 with authenticated: false AND NO owner FIELD for an unauthenticated request, so session.isSuccess IS TRUE IN EXACTLY THE STATE WHERE owner IS ABSENT BY DESIGN. Gating on it would rebuild the key as ["leads", undefined, status] AND READMIT THE PRECISE BUG THIS TICKET EXISTS TO REMOVE. Audited: ZERO sites gate on isSuccess, with the matcher falsified first to confirm it does not fire on that text.

AND THE SEVERITY OF THAT TRAP IS SPECIFIC: the endpoint own comment records that FOUR SEPARATE TEST DESIGNS FAILED TO CATCH THIS BUG CLASS, which is why the fix aims at unrepresentability rather than at coverage. GATING ON isSuccess WOULD RESTORE REPRESENTABILITY WHILE EVERY TEST STAYED GREEN - self-inflicted, at the exact moment of the repair.
FALSIFIED THREE WAYS BY THE IMPLEMENTING SESSION: constant key -> cross-owner inequality fails; token-derived -> stability fails; field removed -> presence fails.

AC3 IS STILL THE REMAINING WORK AND THIS AUDIT DOES NOT TOUCH IT. AC3 requires driving owner A -> sign out -> owner B through the apps own surfaces WITH EVERY cache.clear() DISABLED. A STRUCTURAL AUDIT OF KEYS AND GATES IS EXACTLY THE MECHANICAL SUBSTITUTION THIS TICKET WARNS AGAINST: it proves the keys are shaped correctly, not that a second owner cannot see the first owner data.

Run 36356076721 exposed an incomplete part of the owner-key migration in real browser acceptance: LeadEditor queried history with ownerKey(owner, 'lead-history', id) but invalidated ['lead-history', id], so a successful notes PUT refreshed the saved list but never refreshed history and the unchanged 30-second assertion failed. Four direct lead cache writes also still used unscoped ['lead', id] keys. All five operations now use ownerKey; broad ['leads'] invalidation remains valid by the documented prefix convention. This fixes real cache behavior but does not satisfy AC3's deliberate owner-transition falsification experiment.

Run 36382060368 then exposed the remaining sibling-status lookup using raw ['leads', status] while the query itself was ownerKey(owner, 'leads', status); the Archived empty-filter copy could not observe the populated Saved sibling. The lookup now uses ownerKey as well. AC3's two-owner experiment remains outstanding.

Implemented the explicit CS-61 browser harness switch and exercised the owner A -> sign out -> owner B path locally on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit via npm run test:ui. The switch disables auth-boundary cache.clear only when the experiment sets the dedicated window flag; production behavior remains reset-by-default. The transition checks now use in-app navigation without page.goto, reload or context recreation and assert positive owner-B anchors plus absence of owner-A secrets, including the staleTime-Infinity profile field.

The paired positive control is now implemented and passed locally on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit: with deliberately owner-agnostic keys and cache clearing disabled, owner B reproduces owner A's stale profile value. The control therefore fails as expected when isolation is removed. Hosted CI for this exact revision remains required before promotion; ticket stays QA until that result is recorded.

QA COMPLETED 2026-09-28: run 36398473010 attempt 2 completed green on exact commit 46ba008fdd35c8bf3d99b52cfc8c40ea00b2ba70. All three browser engines passed the cache-clear-disabled owner transition and the paired owner-agnostic-key leakage control, plus axe. Two harness defects exposed by prior runs were fixed without weakening the experiment: authentication now explicitly refreshes the shared session-discovery query after login and logout, and the positive control signs in the seeded owner whose profile was actually mutated. Static/build, 48 integration tests, backfill and recovery were also green. Independent review found no owner-isolation weakening.

items.source: Orchestrator self-surfaced during CS-13 re-review cycle 2026-09-25; owner queued the four explicitly
evidence: FOUND 2026-09-25: the comment above EmptyStateProps opened with "`reason` is the acceptance-criterion distinction", naming a prop that HAS NEVER EXISTED on the type. Verified: "reason" appears in v2/apps/web/src/components/ui-states.tsx only in that comment, and there is not one reason= at any call site in v2/apps/web/src.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF THE F-2 SHAPE. The distinction is real and IS asserted in check-ui.ts (cs13NothingYet at :2255 and cs13FilteredEmpty at :2257), but nothing in the type carries it - it lives in the free-text title/description/message a call site happens to write. A rule someone must follow, not a state that cannot be expressed.

NOT FIXED IN THAT CYCLE, DELIBERATELY: the structural fix touches all 16 EmptyState call sites (app/page.tsx x6, saved-leads x4, job-search-view x3, career-links-view, preparation-panel, resume-panel) and changes rendered copy, which is out of bounds under the UI freeze. The misleading comment WAS corrected in place so it documents what the code does rather than what an absent prop would have done.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-25, and READING ALL 16 CALL SITES FIRST CHANGED THE DESIGN. My own AC1 proposed a BINARY discriminator ("nothing-yet" | "filtered") and said it belonged on the BLOCK variant. Both were wrong. The real split is 14 inline and 2 block, so the distinction lives mostly in the variant I did not name - and the binary would have forced five sites to lie. "Select a lead.", "No search selected" and "Run a search to see this." are neither nothing-yet nor filtered; they are prompts, not empty results. Making them claim nothing-yet would have produced technically-valid props that say the wrong thing, which is the exact failure mode I warned about when migrating the ErrorState sites by hand.

FINAL SHAPE: a required `reason: EmptyReason` on BOTH variants, with three values grounded in the copy that actually exists - nothing-yet (nothing has ever been here), filtered (data exists, THIS view is empty, the user can act), awaiting-input (nothing is wrong and nothing is missing; nothing has been chosen or run). Classification across the 16: 8 nothing-yet, 5 awaiting-input, 1 filtered, 2 derived from the same condition as their copy.

ZERO RENDERED-COPY CHANGE, which is what makes this safe under the UI freeze. The reason is emitted as `data-empty-reason` and drives NO visual difference. Verified rather than asserted: all 14 pre-migration user-visible strings are still present verbatim, checked programmatically against a list catalogued BEFORE the migration. The half of AC1 that says the discriminator should DRIVE icon and copy is deliberately NOT done and remains open - doing it changes rendered output, which is out of bounds until the freeze lifts.

THE TWO TERNARY SITES DERIVE THE REASON FROM THE SAME CONDITION AS THE COPY, never chosen independently: job-search-view.tsx uses `detail.data.jobs.length === 0 ? "nothing-yet" : "filtered"` beside the title that switches on the same test, and saved-leads.tsx uses `populatedSibling ? "filtered" : "nothing-yet"` beside the message that switches on the same value. If the two were chosen separately the machine-readable reason could contradict the words.

PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL, three ways, each mutation asserted to have applied and each file restored byte-identical: omitting `reason` at a real call site (resume-panel.tsx, 11221 -> 11200 bytes) FAILS typecheck; an invented value "not-a-reason" FAILS because the union is enforced; and the unmutated build is clean, so valid input passes. Introducing the required prop produced EXACTLY 16 typecheck errors, one per call site, which is independent confirmation the census found every one.

ENFORCED AT RUNTIME TOO, not only at the type level. check-ui.ts now asserts that the machine-readable reason AGREES WITH THE WORDS: the nothing-yet copy must carry data-empty-reason="nothing-yet" and the filtered-empty copy must carry "filtered". Without these, a site could satisfy the existing copy assertions while declaring the opposite reason - the prose-versus-type gap CS-62 exists to close, reintroduced one level down. Paired positive and negative on the same surface, at three widths across three engines.

VERIFICATION: v2 npm run typecheck clean (tsc -b + next typegen + web project), npm run lint clean, and npm run test:ui PASSED ALL THREE ENGINES first attempt - chromium, firefox and webkit - with no flake this run.

RUNTIME CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-25 TO EVERY RESULT RECORDED TODAY: all local verification in this run was executed on Node v22.23.2, while package.json requires >=24.0.0, .nvmrc says 24 and CI uses 24. This does not invalidate the passes, but it RECLASSIFIES them - each was obtained on a runtime the project does not support, and any could differ on Node 24. Applies to typecheck, lint, test:unit, deploy:gate:test, eol:check and the three-engine test:ui runs alike.

DISCLOSURE RELOCATED 2026-09-25, and the relocation is the finding rather than the content. The unmet half of AC1 was recorded honestly - but IN THE MIDDLE OF A LONG EVIDENCE ENTRY, where nobody promoting a ticket would look. Moved to currentStep. THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF THAT SHAPE (CS-54 in evidence while ownerAgent and status pointed elsewhere, CS-50 in summary, now CS-62), which makes it a BOARD-WIDE HABIT rather than an accident.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PROMOTION CHECK, and it must be told this: A DISCLOSURE CAN BE BURIED ANYWHERE IN evidence, NOT JUST IN currentStep OR summary. A check that reads only the status-bearing fields would have passed CS-62, CS-54 and CS-50 alike.

BOUNDED TYPECHECK EVIDENCE - RE-WORDED FROM "PROVISIONAL" 2026-09-25, AND THE VERB CHANGE IS THE POINT. This ticket cites a BARE `tsc -b`, which is incremental and was observed exiting 0 while a genuine production error existed (collect.ts TS2353) because a stale .tsbuildinfo declared the project up to date. THAT DOES NOT RETRACT THE RESULT AND DOES NOT MAKE IT SUSPECT: the command ran, it reported truthfully on what it examined, and the source it examined did compile. IT BOUNDS THE RESULT. The run was NARROWER THAN THE CLAIM IT WAS QUOTED FOR - it is evidence that the projects tsc considered up to date had no new errors, not evidence that the tree is clean. "PROVISIONAL" WAS THE WRONG WORD BECAUSE IT IMPLIES THE RESULT MIGHT BE FALSE. It was not false; it was narrow. Re-verify the wider claim with `tsc -b --force` or a cleared .tsbuildinfo - and note that v2 typecheck now begins with --force, so the npm script no longer has this bound. The original lines are deliberately kept: they record what was actually run. NOTHING IS DEMOTED FOR THIS.

THE UNENFORCEABLE DOC CLAIM IS FIXED 2026-09-26, AND THE PRECISE LOCATION MATTERS BECAUSE THE TYPE WAS NOT THE PROBLEM. `reason: EmptyReason` IS required on BOTH variants - block and inline - so the discriminator itself is genuinely enforced and a call site cannot omit it. The defect was one sentence on the inline variant: "The inline presentation carries the same distinction in its `message`: a call site that can be empty because of a filter must say so there."

THAT SENTENCE READ AS A RULE WHILE BEING A CONVENTION NO COMPILER CAN CHECK. `message` is free text and NOTHING RELATES ITS CONTENT TO `reason` - a call site may declare reason="filtered" and write any message at all. It is the same shape as the exemption phrases: a plausible sentence that changes how a reader grades the code without changing what the code guarantees.

RESOLVED BY DISCLOSING THE GAP RATHER THAN DELETING THE SENTENCE, which is the harder of the two options offered and the better one. A bare deletion would have left a reader assuming the enforcement extends to the copy, because the surrounding paragraph is about enforcement. The comment now states plainly what the type DOES enforce (the discriminator on both variants), what it DOES NOT (the wording of message), and what would be required if the correspondence were ever needed - a closed set of messages, not a comment.

THE ADJACENT CLAIM WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED AND IT STANDS: the block doc block says the declaration "is checkable by tests rather than by reading prose", AND IT GENUINELY IS - check-ui.ts asserts getAttribute("data-empty-reason") at :2289 and :2323 with distinct failure messages for the nothing-yet and filtered cases. Only the message-wording claim was unenforced; the rest of the paragraph is accurate.
VERIFIED AFTER THE EDIT: apps/web typecheck exit 0, prettier clean. Comment-only change, no rendered output affected, so the UI freeze is untouched.

items.source: Orchestrator self-surfaced during CS-13 re-review cycle 2026-09-25; owner queued the four explicitly
evidence: Current Node 24 CI verification: runs 36385161068 and 36385785464 completed green; all three acceptance criteria were re-taken and the residual remains explicitly out of scope.

REPRODUCED AGAINST REALITY, not inferred: v2/.env parsed with the SAME node:util parseEnv the launcher uses contains 8 keys, not 5 - CS-48 added AI_ENABLED, OPENROUTER_API_KEY and OPENROUTER_MODEL without updating the list. assert.deepEqual at data/windows-v2/run.mjs:13 would FAIL, so the launcher aborted before doing anything. No value from .env was read or printed at any point; key names only.

WHY THE EXACT SET WAS KEPT RATHER THAN RELAXED TO A SUBSET CHECK: `settings` is spread wholesale into the child process environment at the Object.assign below it, so every key in v2/.env reaches the child. The exactness IS the control - an unexpected key is precisely the thing worth failing on. Relaxing it to "these five are present" would have made the launcher run while silently removing the guard.

PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL in all three required directions, with a positive control: real v2/.env PASSES; an extra unexpected key FAILS naming "Unexpected: SOMETHING_UNEXPECTED"; a missing REDIS_URL FAILS naming "Missing: REDIS_URL"; an EMPTY env FAILS rather than being treated as nothing to report. node --check on run.mjs passes.

LIMITATION STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: run.mjs pins Node 26.8.1 (assert.equal(process.versions.node, "26.8.1")) and this session runs 22.23.2, so the file itself could NOT be executed end to end here. The allowlist logic was extracted and exercised in isolation against the real v2/.env. The launcher remains unverified as a whole on this machine.

REVIEWER E VERDICT 2026-09-25: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS, and RECOMMENDED FOR UAT on the criteria as written - the one clean result in this batch. NOT PROMOTED BY THIS SESSION: recorded as reviewer-recommended for UAT, awaiting owner promotion, consistent with every other approval tonight.

REVIEWER E VERIFIED THE THING MOST AT RISK: that the exact-set assert.deepEqual was PRESERVED RATHER THAN LOOSENED. It traced Object.assign(env, settings, ...) at run.mjs:53 and confirmed every key in v2/.env reaches the child process, so the exactness is a genuine security control and the tempting wrong fix - relaxing it to a presence check to make the launcher run - was not taken.
REVIEWER E ALSO CONFIRMED THE CHECK CANNOT PASS VACUOUSLY: an empty env produces deepEqual([], [8 keys]) and fails, so it does not treat an empty read as nothing to report.

F-63-1 (P2) NON-BLOCKING, RECORDED AS A CARRIED FOLLOW-UP AND EXPLICITLY NOT AS A REASON TO HOLD THE TICKET: there is no test file for run.mjs, no npm script invokes it, and the falsifications were run in a throwaway harness - so the chain terminates in a one-off manual run, the same residual already recorded against CS-34. The reviewer was explicit that the AC set does not require a regression guard and that it would not inflate a preference into a blocker. Optional follow-up routed to the infrastructure session.

REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: the reviewer cannot detect whether its reads fell inside another session write window, and three sessions were writing concurrently. If any file cited here was edited between roughly 15:05 and 15:25 IST on 2026-09-25, this verdict should be re-taken rather than trusted.

STANDARD WORDING ADOPTED 2026-09-25 from CS-39, which stated the claim, its ceiling and its unlock in one line: "All three criteria met and asserted. Promotable on a green CI run; not promoted here." Every ticket in this cohort now carries the same sentence, plus the second bar discovered later - local execution on Node v22.23.2 against a declared floor of 24. NO QA TICKET IS PROMOTABLE TONIGHT ON EXECUTION EVIDENCE, and that is ONE GATE rather than nineteen separate problems.

F-63-1 IS WIDER THAN RECORDED - A GUARD GAP, NOT JUST A MISSING TEST. Verified: scripts/check-test-registration.mjs:37 is `const directories = ["scripts", "infra", "mobile-site"]` - `data` IS ABSENT - and the V2 guard globs v2/**. SO data/windows-v2/ IS OUTSIDE BOTH REGISTRATION GUARDS. A test written for run.mjs tomorrow would be invisible to both, EVEN AFTER F-52-1 RAISED THE V2 BAR TO "executed by a workflow". The fix would land unguarded, which is exactly what CS-52 exists to prevent.

ORDERING MADE EXPLICIT IN THE ROUTING, because the other order proves nothing: ADD `data` TO THE GUARD SCOPE FIRST, PROVE THE GUARD SEES IT, THEN WRITE THE TEST. Writing the test first and adding the scope afterwards leaves you unable to say whether the guard would have caught its absence.

WORDING CORRECTED 2026-09-25 FROM "All applicable criteria met" TO THE COUNTED FORM. The distinction is not cosmetic: "ALL THREE CRITERIA MET" IS FALSIFIABLE BY COUNTING; "ALL APPLICABLE CRITERIA MET" CANNOT FAIL, because an unmet criterion can be reclassified as not-applicable without anyone editing a number. It is the same shape as \bsurfaced\b, DEFERRED and eol=crlf - a word anyone can write that silently changes how a claim is graded - except that this one sat in the STATUS FIELD OF TEN TICKETS, which is the field a promotion decision reads. That makes it the most consequential of the four, not the least.

COUNT NOT YET RE-TAKEN 2026-09-25, recorded as owed work rather than left as an unverified claim. When "All applicable criteria met" was replaced with the counted form across ten tickets, THE WORDING WAS CORRECTED AND THE COUNT WAS NOT. Two of the ten were then found wrong within minutes - CS-74 (AC3 half-met) and CS-52 (AC4 unmet) - so the remaining eight cannot be assumed right. A COUNTED CLAIM OVER AN UNCOUNTED CRITERION IS NO BETTER THAN THE HEDGE IT REPLACED; it is only more falsifiable, and falsifying it is the outstanding work.

COUNT RE-TAKEN 2026-09-25 - 3 OF 3, EACH CHECKED RATHER THAN RECALLED. AC1 the launcher runs against the current v2/.env: met on a KEY-NAMES-ONLY reproduction, which was the correct way to gather the evidence without reading a real .env. AC2 the exact-set comparison is preserved: VERIFIED STILL assert.deepEqual(presentKeys, [...allowedEnvKeys].sort(), ...) rather than loosened to a subset check - THAT WAS THE TEMPTING WRONG FIX AND IT WAS NOT TAKEN, which is worth recording because a subset check would have made the guard unable to fail on an unexpected key. AC3 a failure names the specific unexpected or missing keys: verified at run.mjs:38-43.

F-63-1 STAYS OPEN AS A CARRIED RESIDUAL AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT COUNTED AS AN UNMET CRITERION - no test file, no npm script, the falsifications performed in a throwaway harness. THE REVIEWER WHO RAISED IT DREW THE LINE ITSELF: "the AC set does not require a regression guard; I am not inflating a preference into a blocker." RECORDING IT INSIDE THE COUNT WOULD BE THE MIRROR OF THE HEDGE - moving a real-but-out-of-scope concern INTO the criteria set is the same category error as moving an unmet criterion OUT of it.

AND THE data/ SCOPE GAP STAYS LINKED TO F-63-1 rather than filed apart, because the two compose into a worse thing than either: A TEST WRITTEN UNDER data/ TOMORROW WOULD BE INVISIBLE TO BOTH REGISTRATION GUARDS. Neither half is alarming alone; together they are a blind spot with no owner.

THE DEFECT IS THE SILENCE, not the missing vocabulary. Matching quietly proceeds on preferences alone and the owner gets no signal that half the intended input was discarded. Recorded in docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md with the measured table, and the constraint is now named explicitly in derive.ts so it reads as a deliberate boundary rather than an oversight.

BLOCKED ON OWNER PRODUCT DECISION, not on engineering. The plausible remedies differ sharply in cost and risk: extend the word list per language, switch to a structural heuristic independent of vocabulary, or detect the language and report an explicit "titles could not be derived" state. The last is the smallest honest improvement and removes the silence with no new language support. Do not extend ROLE_WORDS piecemeal without a decision. 65 resume tests pass unchanged.

THE ENGINEERING HALF IS AVAILABLE NOW and this tickets own evidence already names the implementation: detect that no title could be derived and report an explicit state rather than an empty list, described there as "the smallest honest improvement" that "removes the silence with no new language support". Filed as CS-71 so the work is schedulable instead of being hidden behind this tickets BLOCKED label.

THE GENERAL POINT, worth more than this ticket: A TICKET BLOCKED ON AN OWNER OR A HOST IS NOT THE SAME AS A TICKET WITH NO AVAILABLE WORK. A single status field cannot express "partly available", so the available half has to be split out or it is invisible. CS-64 keeps AC1 and stays BLOCKED; CS-71 carries the rest.

AC1 STILL NOT SATISFIED, unchanged by this: 28 tracked text files carry no eol attribute at all - 14 .svg, 13 .sql, 1 .env.example. The gate covers the file this ticket was written about; its full scope remains open.

F-65-1 CLOSED BETTER THAN RECOMMENDED, verified at source: rather than adding txt to LF_ONLY, the duplicate list was DELETED ENTIRELY and check-line-endings.mjs now derives its matchers by parsing every eol=lf pattern out of .gitattributes. Its comment names the finding - "two independent lists of what is a text file is one list too many, and they duly diverged". Three cannot-look guards confirmed present: exit 1 if git rev-parse fails, exit 1 on an unreadable .gitattributes ("refusing to enforce an empty rule set"), and exit 1 if matchers.length < 10 ("cannot look and must not pass"). Eighth convergence, delivered.

AND THAT CHANGE IS EXACTLY WHY THE GREEN GATE MUST NEVER BE READ AS AC1 - THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A MATTER OF DEGREE. What 663 green files prove is "every file WITH an eol=lf attribute contains no CR byte". AC1 asks "every tracked text file HAS an explicit eol attribute". Since the check universe IS whatever .gitattributes declares, A FILE WITH NO ATTRIBUTE CANNOT ENTER THE CHECK UNIVERSE AT ALL. THE GATE IS STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE OF EVER TURNING RED FOR THIS GAP.

THIS IS THE SEVEN-UAT-DEMOTION SHAPE - a green gate standing in for a criterion it does not measure - AND IT IS NOW HARDER TO SPOT, BECAUSE THE GATE IS GENUINELY EXCELLENT AT WHAT IT DOES DO. The reason is recorded here and in currentStep, not just the verdict, because a future reader will see a flawless check and assume the criterion is met.

COUNT CORRECTED, AND THE EARLIER FIGURE FROM THIS SESSION WAS ALSO LOW. A full sweep of every tracked file (excluding binaries) finds 43 text files with no eol attribute, not 15 as relayed and not 28 as this session previously reported. Breakdown: 14 .svg, 13 .sql, 3 .gitignore, 2 .prettierignore, 2 .conf, and one each of .dockerignore, .editorconfig, .env.example, .gitattributes, .nvmrc, .webmanifest, .service, .inc, .xml.

BOTH UNDERCOUNTS HAD THE SAME CAUSE, which is worth more than either number: each was produced by a filter deciding in advance what counts as "a text file" - the exact judgement AC1 exists to make explicit in .gitattributes. Note that .gitattributes ITSELF carries no eol attribute: the file that declares the rule for everyone else is outside it.
RUNTIME CAVEAT: verified on Node v22.23.2, below the declared minimum of 24. Real, but not evidence about the supported runtime.

INVERSE CHECK BUILT 2026-09-25, and it makes AC1 ENFORCEABLE rather than merely documented. check-line-endings.mjs was extended in place to enforce BOTH directions: not only "every file with an eol=lf attribute has no CR byte", but "every tracked text file HAS an attribute". That closes the structural hole recorded earlier - that a file with no attribute could not enter the check universe at all and so the gate could never turn red for the AC1 gap.

THE ERROR MESSAGE NAMES THE STRUCTURAL GAP RATHER THAN JUST LISTING FILES, and is quoted here because the wording is the point: "...have no explicit eol attribute, so nothing governs their line endings on checkout AND THE COMPLIANCE CHECK ABOVE CANNOT SEE THEM AT ALL."

FIVE DISTINCT CANNOT-LOOK GUARDS IN ONE FILE, verified at source: repository-root resolution via git rev-parse (:39); unreadable .gitattributes exits 1 "refusing to enforce an empty rule set" (:53, :63); matchers.length < 10 (:89) as "too few to be the real configuration, so this check cannot look and must not pass"; tracked.length < 100 (:131); and UNCLASSIFIABLE files reported rather than silently treated as binary and skipped (:182, :224-229). That last one was the single way this check could have quietly become decorative. This is the standard the rest of the codebase should be measured against.

MEASURED STATE AT 16:45, AND IT HAS MOVED PAST THE REPORT THIS RECORD RESPONDS TO - measured here rather than relayed. .gitattributes now carries 31 eol=lf patterns (was 17), covering .sql, .svg, .xml, .webmanifest, .conf, .inc, .service and the ignore-file dotfiles. ZERO text files now lack an attribute - the 43 are declared. The only 4 tracked files without one are binaries, correctly.

SO THE DECLARATION HALF OF AC1 IS COMPLETE AND THE RENORMALISATION HALF IS NOT. eol:check now exits 1 with a DIFFERENT error than the one reported: "21 file(s) contain CR bytes where LF is required. Fix with: git add --renormalize ." - including v2/migrations/*.sql, which only became visible to the compliance check BECAUSE they were just declared. That is the two checks working as designed: declaring a file brings it into the universe, and it then has to actually comply.

THE 43 FIGURE IS CONFIRMED AS THE CORRECT MEASURED POPULATION at the time it was taken, and it matched this sessions own full sweep exactly. The earlier estimates of 15 and 28 were both low, and both for the same reason - a filter deciding in advance what counts as a text file, which is precisely the judgement AC1 exists to make explicit. THIRD TIME TONIGHT A HAND-ENUMERATED COUNT CAME IN UNDER THE MACHINE COUNT, which is itself the argument for the check.

STILL DO NOT PROMOTE ON A GREEN GATE ALONE. AC1 closes when BOTH directions are green, and it will close BECAUSE THE CRITERION BECAME ENFORCEABLE, not because a gate went green - which is the exact distinction that produced seven UAT demotions today.

THE TWO CURRENT gates:test REDS ARE DELIBERATE, NOT REGRESSIONS: node:check stops first on Node 22, and eol:check stops on 21 unrenormalised files. BOTH ARE GATES NEWLY ABLE TO SEE SOMETHING THAT WAS ALWAYS TRUE. Recorded so a red gates:test tonight is not mistaken for a broken repository.
RUNTIME CAVEAT: verified on Node v22.23.2, below the declared minimum of 24.

AC1 NOW GENUINELY MET, verified independently in this session: eol:check PASSES with "no CR bytes in 706 LF-only files (31 eol=lf patterns from .gitattributes), and all 710 tracked files are either binary or carry an explicit eol attribute", exit 0. 31 patterns, up from 17. 710 of 710 tracked files covered. AC1 reads "every tracked text file has an explicit eol attribute" - that is now MEASURED AND ENFORCED rather than asserted.

RECORD WHY THIS CLOSES HONESTLY, because it is the exact distinction that produced eight demotions today: AC1 DID NOT CLOSE BECAUSE A GATE WENT GREEN. It closed because THE CRITERION BECAME ENFORCEABLE - a second check, opposite in direction to the first, asking "is the declaration complete?" rather than "does every declared file comply?". The compliance half alone was STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of ever failing for this criterion. Both halves exist now and neither substitutes for the other.

BOTH HALVES PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL, which is what separates this from a check that merely passes: the COMPLIANCE half went red on review.txt when txt first entered scope, and the COMPLETENESS half went red on 43 files on its first run. Neither needed a synthetic fixture - the failing populations already existed.

THE MIGRATION RISK WAS REAL ENOUGH TO CHECK AND IS VERIFIED SAFE. git add --renormalize across v2/migrations/*.sql could have altered files Drizzle checksums. Verified in this session: NO .sql MIGRATION BODY DIFFERS FROM HEAD AT ALL - git diff --name-only HEAD -- v2/migrations/ returns only meta/_journal.json. The 15 committed migration bodies were not rewritten.

AND THE RECONCILIATION IS RECORDED RATHER THAN THE VERDICT, because "migrations look fine" is not checkable and this is: 17 .sql FILES, 17 JOURNAL ENTRIES, EXACT. No orphaned entry, no unjournalled migration. The journal differs from HEAD purely ADDITIVELY - new entries for migrations created since the last commit. A JOURNAL THAT DISAGREED WITH ITS FILES WOULD BE A FAR WORSE DEFECT THAN ANY LINE ENDING.

A MISREADING CORRECTED MID-CHECK, worth keeping as a note about this tree: a first read of the journal diff showed "content-identical-ignoring-CR: False" and briefly looked like corruption. The COMPARISON was correct; the INTERPRETATION was not. A file can legitimately differ from HEAD by more than whitespace when it has been ADDED TO since the last commit - which is the normal state of every one of the ~108 tracked-modified files in this tree. WHEN EVERYTHING IS UNCOMMITTED, "DIFFERS FROM HEAD" CARRIES NO INFORMATION ON ITS OWN; THE QUESTION IS ALWAYS "DIFFERS HOW".
AC2 MET: review.txt was renormalised WITHOUT being rewritten in place - content intact at 208,286 bytes with the staged blob identical, and the append-only history preserved.

WORDING CORRECTED 2026-09-25 FROM "All applicable criteria met" TO THE COUNTED FORM. The distinction is not cosmetic: "ALL THREE CRITERIA MET" IS FALSIFIABLE BY COUNTING; "ALL APPLICABLE CRITERIA MET" CANNOT FAIL, because an unmet criterion can be reclassified as not-applicable without anyone editing a number. It is the same shape as \bsurfaced\b, DEFERRED and eol=crlf - a word anyone can write that silently changes how a claim is graded - except that this one sat in the STATUS FIELD OF TEN TICKETS, which is the field a promotion decision reads. That makes it the most consequential of the four, not the least.

THIS TICKET IS WHY THE WORDING CORRECTION WAS URGENT RATHER THAN TIDY. CS-65 carried "All applicable criteria met" while its AC1 - "every tracked text file has an explicit eol attribute" - had been closed ONLY after a second, opposite-direction check was built. "ALL APPLICABLE CRITERIA" WOULD HAVE LET AC1 FULL SCOPE BE QUIETLY DEEMED INAPPLICABLE. That is not hypothetical: it is the exact judgement that was in play on this ticket two hours earlier.

COUNT NOT YET RE-TAKEN 2026-09-25, recorded as owed work rather than left as an unverified claim. When "All applicable criteria met" was replaced with the counted form across ten tickets, THE WORDING WAS CORRECTED AND THE COUNT WAS NOT. Two of the ten were then found wrong within minutes - CS-74 (AC3 half-met) and CS-52 (AC4 unmet) - so the remaining eight cannot be assumed right. A COUNTED CLAIM OVER AN UNCOUNTED CRITERION IS NO BETTER THAN THE HEDGE IT REPLACED; it is only more falsifiable, and falsifying it is the outstanding work.

INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF THE BASELINE, AND IT IS REAL CORROBORATION RATHER THAN A MATCHING COUNT: the check now prints "tracked 710 = declared 706 + binary 4", derived through its own classification path. Two hours earlier the same baseline was measured BY A DIFFERENT METHOD - reading the first 8000 bytes of all 710 tracked files by hand - giving 4 binary, 706 text, 0 unreadable. TWO DIFFERENT METHODS, SAME THREE NUMBERS.

THAT DISTINCTION IS THE ONE THIS RUN GOT WRONG EARLIER AND IS NOW GETTING RIGHT: agreement between measurements that SHARE a method is the method confirming itself - as when 10 and 10 agreed and were both produced by the same broken glob. Agreement between measurements that DIFFER in method is evidence. The numbers here are the second kind.

COUNT RE-TAKEN 2026-09-25 - 2 OF 2. AC1 every tracked text file has an explicit eol attribute: MET - eol:check reports "all 710 tracked files are either binary or carry an explicit eol attribute", independently corroborated by a hand measurement of the same split (4 binary / 706 text / 0 unreadable) taken by a different method. AC2 review.txt is not rewritten in place: MET - 208,286 bytes, staged blob identical, content verified intact after renormalisation.

AND THE DENOMINATOR WAS THE ERROR WAITING TO HAPPEN, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE RE-TAKE: THIS TICKET HAS TWO CRITERIA AND WAS BEING CARRIED IN MEMORY AS THREE. "3 of 3" would have been written, and it would have been WRONG ABOUT THE DENOMINATOR - a worse error than being wrong about the numerator, because a wrong numerator disagrees with the evidence while A WRONG DENOMINATOR DISAGREES WITH NOTHING AND READS AS COMPLETE. Read the array; do not recall the shape.

PROVISIONAL MARKING WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25, SAME DAY IT WAS APPLIED, BECAUSE IT WAS TOO BROAD AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENT. The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". THE GATE COULD FAIL; ONLY ITS FIRST LINK COULD NOT. `npm run typecheck` chains four commands and the last, check-test-types.mjs, filters on /^\S+\.ts\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - WHICH MATCHES A PRODUCTION FILE AS READILY AS A TEST FILE - and exits 1. Anyone running the npm script WOULD have been told.

THIS TICKET DOES NOT CITE A BARE `tsc -b`, so its typecheck evidence was never in the unfalsifiable form and stands unqualified. The narrowed set is 4 of the original 29: CS-53, CS-62, CS-76, CS-77 - ALL FOUR WRITTEN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, which is the correct place for the correction to land.

items.title: Owner-typed titles reach MatchDimensionScore.reason with no character constraint
items.userProblem: Two inlets feed candidate.titles and only one is constrained, so an owner-typed title flows verbatim into stored match evidence that a future digest, export or admin snapshot would render.
items.source: CS-56 F-3, explicitly deferred there: "The durable fix is to constrain at the reason boundary rather than per-inlet... it needs its own ticket". Filed 2026-09-25 after the owner asked which reason-boundary item was outstanding.
acceptanceCriteria: MatchDimensionScore.reason is constrained at the boundary where it is constructed, so every inlet is covered by one control rather than each inlet being fixed separately

Hostile fixtures - markup, control characters, template syntax, bidirectional overrides, variation selectors - are refused or neutralised on the owner-typed path, proven with tests that fail before the fix
Legitimate titles including accented and non-Latin text continue to render unchanged; the constraint must not silently discard real data
evidence: Current Node 24 CI verification: runs 36385161068 and 36385785464 completed green; all three acceptance criteria were re-taken, including the non-ASCII positive controls.

GROUNDED AT SOURCE, three hops traced rather than assumed. INLET 1 (resume-derived) is now constrained at extraction by CS-56 in packages/resume/src/derive.ts. INLET 2 (owner-typed) is packages/shared/src/schemas.ts:30 - titles: z.array(z.string().trim().min(1)).min(1).max(25) - trim and non-empty only, capped at 25 entries, NO CHARACTER CONSTRAINT. CONVERGENCE: packages/matching/src/dimensions.ts:211-230, where bestTitle is selected from candidate.titles and interpolated VERBATIM into the reason string - `Close to your target "${bestTitle}"`, `Partly overlaps "${bestTitle}"`, `Different role family to "${bestTitle}"`. candidate.titles is the union of both inlets, so CS-56 closed one of two.

WHY THIS IS THE DURABLE SHAPE AND NOT A SECOND PER-INLET PATCH: constraining inlet 2 the way inlet 1 was constrained leaves the same class open for inlet 3. The reason string is the single place both paths converge and the only place the value becomes stored evidence, so it is the boundary that makes the defect unrepresentable rather than merely fixed twice. This is the same convergence the other tickets reached - replace a rule someone must follow with a state that cannot be expressed.

THREAT MODEL IS GENUINELY WEAKER THAN CS-56s AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH RATHER THAN INFLATED: the resume inlet accepts a crafted file, whereas the typed inlet is the single owner typing into their own workspace and rendering it back to themselves - self-inflicted, not attacker-controlled. That is exactly why CS-56 scoped it out and why this is P2 rather than higher. The rationale is NOT fully eliminated though: a future email digest, PDF export or admin snapshot renders MatchDimensionScore.reason regardless of which inlet the title came from, and at that point the audience is no longer only the author.

RELATIONSHIP TO CS-46 RECORDED WITHOUT FORCING A BLOCKING DEPENDENCY: CS-56 noted this "belongs with CS-46, which already owns what resume-derived facts may become". CS-46 is BLOCKED on an owner product decision about EXCLUDING facts. Constraining characters at the reason boundary does not depend on that decision, so dependencies are left empty deliberately - making this wait on CS-46 would block a safety fix behind an unrelated product question.

PROVENANCE OF THE FILING, stated because it corrects my own error: the owner queued "the reason-boundary constraint" among four self-surfaced items. I read it as EmptyStates `reason` prop and filed CS-62 for that instead. CS-62 is a real and separate find; this ticket is the item that was actually queued. The word `reason` was doing double duty across two components and I resolved it the wrong way without checking.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-25. The refused code-point SET moved to packages/shared/src/evidence-text.ts as the single source, because two copies of a security-relevant character set is a divergence waiting to happen - a code point refused at extraction but renderable in evidence is exactly the gap. Both packages already depend on @job-radar/shared, so no cycle. The OPERATIONS still differ and should: resume REJECTS a segment at extraction (CS-56), matching NEUTRALISES when assembling reason. Rejecting a reason would discard the explanation of a score, which is the failure the reason string exists to prevent.

APPLIED AT THE CONVERGENCE POINT: dimensions.ts `dim()`, which constructs every MatchDimensionScore built from candidate data. Constraining here rather than per-inlet is the point - fixing the typed inlet the way the resume inlet was fixed would leave the class open for a third inlet.

MY OWN "ONE BOUNDARY" CLAIM WAS FALSE AND I CAUGHT IT BEFORE SHIPPING IT. I wrote a comment asserting every MatchDimensionScore is built in dim(). Checking rather than trusting it found a SECOND construction site: notScoredDimensions() in score.ts:236, `{ score: 0, weight: 0, reason: "Not scored - excluded" }`. It takes no inlet - the reason is a fixed literal - so it needs no constraint, but the invariant as written was wrong. The comment now states the precise invariant AND names the exception with its justification, so a future third site must come through dim() or justify itself the same way.

PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL: removing `constrainEvidenceText` from the boundary (mutation asserted applied, 16920 -> 16889 bytes) makes 5 tests fail - bidirectional override, zero-width space, variation selector, C0 control and zero-width no-break space - with 146 still passing. File restored byte-identical and the suite confirmed green again.

PAIRED POSITIVES ON THE SAME SURFACE, per the standing rule: each hostile fixture also asserts the reason still MATCHES /Engineer/, because "no refused code point survives" would pass just as well against an empty string. Plus a legitimate accented title (Ingenieur Software Engineer) must survive UNCHANGED, and a title composed ENTIRELY of hostile characters must still produce a non-empty reason - a score nobody can audit is the failure being prevented.

NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE ELSEWHERE: 234 tests across shared, resume and matching passed after the derive.ts refactor that removed its private copy of the code-point predicate, including all 65 resume tests - which is what proves the move was a refactor rather than a change. packages/matching now at 151 tests.

SCOPE HELD: the owner-typed Zod schema at packages/shared/src/schemas.ts:30 was deliberately NOT tightened. Constraining input there would reject titles an owner legitimately typed and is a product decision about what a person may call their own target role; constraining at the evidence boundary protects the stored artefact without telling the owner what they may type.

REVIEWER E VERDICT 2026-09-25: REJECTED, with a P1. This is THIS SESSIONS OWN IMPLEMENTATION being rejected, recorded in full rather than softened. The P1 has been routed to the api/packages session; this session must not touch v2/packages or packages under the partition, so it is recorded here and NOT fixed here. Status held at QA, NOT promoted.

REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT, carried on this verdict deliberately: the reviewer states it cannot detect whether its reads fell inside another session write window. Three sessions were writing concurrently. If any file cited in this verdict was edited between roughly 15:05 and 15:25 IST on 2026-09-25, THIS VERDICT SHOULD BE RE-TAKEN RATHER THAN TRUSTED. Recorded so a later reader can judge it rather than inherit it.

P1 CLOSED AND VERIFIED 2026-09-25 by the api/packages session, recorded here by the orchestrator as sole backlog writer. TITLE_REFUSED_SYNTAX is now REFUSED_SYNTAX, exported from packages/shared/src/evidence-text.ts, so BOTH BOUNDARIES SHARE ONE CHARACTER SET - closing the divergence that file own comment had warned about. Confirmed at source in this session: REFUSED_SYNTAX is exported, TITLE_REFUSED_SYNTAX no longer appears, and derive.ts imports the shared set.

AC2 SATISFIED. Seven hostile classes, each neutralised against the real function: markup -> "img src x onerror alert(1) Engineer"; script tag -> "script alert(1) /script Staff Engineer"; template literal -> "Engineer $ constructor.constructor(1)"; handlebars -> "Engineer 7*7"; backtick -> "Engineer whoami"; control character -> "Engineer"; bidirectional override -> "Engineer".

THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF OF THIS EVIDENCE, and is recorded as such rather than as a footnote: "Senior Staff Engineer, Platform" survives BYTE-IDENTICAL. Without it, "nothing hostile survived" passes just as well against a function that returns empty for everything. A BENIGN TITLE SURVIVING UNCHANGED IS WHAT PROVES THE NEUTRALISATION DISCRIMINATES RATHER THAN MERELY DELETES.

TWO DETAILS ARE CORRECT BY DESIGN RATHER THAN BY ACCIDENT, recorded so a future reader does not "fix" them. (1) NEUTRALISE, NOT REJECT: the markup case keeps its readable content, because rejecting would discard an entire reason string - the over-strict failure mode this design deliberately avoided, since a score nobody can audit is the thing the reason exists to prevent. (2) $ SURVIVES WHILE { DOES NOT: confirmed at source, the set is < > { } backtick \ " = | and contains no $. That is the CS-56 decision holding - ${ cannot form without {, so the composition guard covers it and $ alone is not refused. Consistent with the recorded reasoning rather than drifting from it.
NON-BREAKING, VERIFIED: root typecheck exit 0, and 251/251 tests across 10 files in matching, resume and shared.

F-66-3 CARRIED AS AN OPEN P3, out of AC scope but recorded rather than dropped: schemas.ts:30 has no per-string .max() on owner-typed titles, which is a SECOND unconstrained property on the same inlet. The character class is now bounded; the length is not.
THIS WAS THE ONLY LIVE P1 ON THE BOARD - an owner-typed role rendering as markup in stored evidence through the typed inlet, while the resume inlet refused it. Closed.

RUNTIME CAVEAT: this verification ran on Node v22.23.2, below the declared minimum of 24 in package.json, v2/package.json, .nvmrc and ci.yml. The result is real but is not evidence about the supported runtime.

F-66-1 CLOSED AND AC2 MET, verified at every hop in this session. ONE SET, TWO PACKAGES, TWO OPERATIONS: packages/shared/src/evidence-text.ts exports REFUSED_SYNTAX as a ReadonlySet of < > { } backtick \ " = | ; constrainEvidenceText NEUTRALISES with `REFUSED_SYNTAX.has(character) ? " " : character`; and derive.ts:477 REJECTS with `if (REFUSED_SYNTAX.has(character)) return ""`. TITLE_REFUSED_SYNTAX is gone. TITLE_STRAY_RE correctly stays package-local, being genuinely resume-specific.

THE DIVERGENCE IS NOW UNREPRESENTABLE RATHER THAN FIXED. One definition means a character cannot be refused at one boundary and renderable at the other - which is what the file own comment had warned about when the set was duplicated.

THE IMPLEMENTATION IS BETTER THAN WHAT WAS RECOMMENDED, and the reasoning is worth preserving verbatim because neither the reviewer nor this session had it. Uniform neutralisation was proposed; the code splits the two tiers instead: INVISIBLE refused code points are REMOVED because they say nothing, while refused SYNTAX characters are replaced with A SPACE rather than removed, "because deleting them would join neighbouring words into text the owner never wrote". Confirmed present in the source.
RUNTIME CAVEAT: verified on Node v22.23.2, below the declared minimum of 24. Real, but not evidence about the supported runtime.

F-66-3 CLOSED: packages/shared/schemas.ts ~:28-34 now bounds per-entry length. The recorded reasoning is the part worth keeping - "every one of these arrays bounded its LENGTH and left each entry unbounded, while the single-value fields beside them (fullName, location) have been capped at 120 all along. THAT ASYMMETRY WAS NOT A DECISION." ALL THREE CS-66 FINDINGS ARE NOW CLOSED.
