items.title: Control Center hid BLOCKED work in an unnamed bucket and left open findings uncounted
items.userProblem: The owner uses this board to decide what needs their attention, and the seven tickets waiting on them were rendered in a bucket the board could not name, next to a header reporting nothing in flight.
items.source: Owner direct request 2026-09-25 after trying to check progress on the board
acceptanceCriteria: BLOCKED renders in its own named column and is counted there
An unrecognised status or severity produces a visible error rather than a silent bucket, proven by feeding the renderer a bogus value
Findings counters are labelled so they cannot be read as ticket priorities, and no open finding is invisible
evidence: DEFECT 1 CONFIRMED AT SOURCE: scripts/engineering-ui.mjs COLS had six columns and no BLOCKED entry, so all seven BLOCKED tickets fell into the loose bucket rendered as "Not mapped". The tile renderer already had a `blocked` CSS class, so the board knew the status existed visually while having no column for it. FIXED: a Blocked column with its own count. Verified against real data - Not mapped went 7 -> 0, and CS-3, CS-24, CS-25, CS-26, CS-27, CS-46, CS-64 now render under Blocked. Column totals now sum to 66, equal to the item count, so nothing is dropped.

DEFECT 1 STRUCTURAL PART: the column list was defined CLIENT-SIDE inside the page template while nothing validated statuses server-side. It is now a single server-side BOARD_COLUMNS constant injected into the page, so the list the server validates against and the list the client renders from CANNOT DIVERGE. Two copies would allow a status to be renderable but unvalidated, or validated but unrenderable, which is how BLOCKED reached an unnamed bucket in the first place.

DEFECT 1 VISIBILITY: an unrecognised status now pushes an entry into stateErrors, the channel the client already renders as a persistent unmissable banner, naming the status AND the affected ticket ids and stating that they are not counted in any column. The "Not mapped" column is relabelled "Not mapped - UNRECOGNISED STATUS" and describes itself as a defect in the data or the board rather than as a category of work.

DEFECT 2 DIAGNOSED BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING, and THE NUMBER WAS CORRECT. The counters read .ai/findings.json, not backlog priorities: 10 findings, 5 open, P2:3 and P3:2, so "0 P0 / 0 P1 / 3 P2" matched the data exactly. The defect was the LABEL - the board tiles carry P0/P1/P2 tags from the BACKLOG, so "0 P1 findings" beside four P1 tickets read as a contradiction. Relabelled to "P0/P1/P2/P3 open findings". Making the correct count wrong to satisfy an ambiguous label would have been the real defect, and was explicitly not done.

DEFECT 2 REVEALED A THIRD, UNREPORTED PROBLEM: P3 was counted by no cell and rendered nowhere, so 2 of the 5 open findings were invisible on a board whose purpose is to show what is open. A P3 cell was added and an open finding with an unrecognised severity now reports through stateErrors. Verified against real data: all 5 open findings are now accounted for by the four cells.

PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL - four separate mutations, each asserted to have actually applied, each restored byte-identical, with the suite confirmed green again afterwards. Removing unknown-status reporting: FAILS. Removing unknown-severity reporting: FAILS. Removing BLOCKED from its column: FAILS. Removing P3 from the counted severities: FAILS. A clean synthetic state produces no errors (positive control) and a CLOSED finding with an odd severity is correctly not reported, so the checks are not merely always-on.

THE NEW TEST WOULD HAVE BEEN A TEST THAT NEVER RAN, which is the CS-52/CS-60 class and would have been self-defeating here. vitest.config.ts includes only packages/*/src/**/*.test.ts and apps/api/src/**/*.test.ts, so scripts/*.test.mjs is invisible to npm test, and NO npm script referenced scripts/engineering-hook.test.mjs either - 22 passing tests that had never been executed by any gate. Added engineering:test and wired it into gates:test. 28 tests now run there (22 pre-existing + 6 new), all passing.

NOT CHANGED DELIBERATELY: "Target release: —" is left empty. The sprint file carries no targetReleaseDate and inventing one would be precisely the kind of unevidenced claim this run has been removing.

SHIPPED-BUT-NOT-LIVE CAUGHT BY THE COORDINATOR, and it is the deliverable-versus-consumer gap in its most literal form. The fix was correct on disk and the board still rendered "Not mapped | 7", because the ui process had been running since 2026-09-23 00:08 - over two days before the 13:50 edit - and Node does not hot-reload. Source on disk was NOT evidence the board was fixed.

RESTARTED AND VERIFIED AT THE CONSUMER, three levels rather than one: (1) new process pid 34376 started 14:10, after the edit; (2) the SERVED page contains the Blocked column, "Nothing blocked", "UNRECOGNISED STATUS" and "P3 open findings", and no longer contains the old "P1 findings" label; (3) THE LIVE RENDERED DOM, read with a real browser, shows columns Backlog 12, To Do 7, In Progress 0, BLOCKED 7, QA 17, UAT 24, Production 0 - summing to 67 - with NO "Not mapped" column, strip labels "P0/P1/P2/P3 open findings", blocked tiles rendering, and zero page errors.

INCIDENTAL DOC DRIFT FOUND WHILE RESTARTING: the engineering contract and AGENTS.md instruct `npm run ui:engineering`, which DOES NOT EXIST - npm reports "Missing script". The real scripts are `engineering:center` and `agile:ui`. Anyone following the documented command gets an error rather than a board.
REVIEWER E VERDICT 2026-09-25: APPROVED WITH FINDINGS. Recorded by the orchestrator and attributed to the independent review. Status held at QA, NOT promoted.

REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT, carried on this verdict deliberately: the reviewer states it cannot detect whether its reads fell inside another session write window. Three sessions were writing concurrently. If any file cited in this verdict was edited between roughly 15:05 and 15:25 IST on 2026-09-25, THIS VERDICT SHOULD BE RE-TAKEN RATHER THAN TRUSTED. Recorded so a later reader can judge it rather than inherit it.

HISTORICAL SCOPE LIMIT RECORDED 2026-09-25: CS-30 carried status DISCOVERY while its own evidence at that checkpoint recorded a blocker. CS-67 makes UNRECOGNISED statuses fail visibly; cross-field consistency between a recognised status and separate ticket prose is deliberately a different check and is not part of this rendering ticket.

QA CLOSED 2026-09-28: hosted run 36398473010 attempt 2 completed green on Node 24, including the engineering UI suite and browser/accessibility coverage. The KNOWN_SEVERITIES-driven rendering and mutation proof are closed; this ticket is ready for UAT.

RUNTIME CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-25 TO EVERY RESULT RECORDED TODAY: all local verification in this run was executed on Node v22.23.2, while package.json requires >=24.0.0, .nvmrc says 24 and CI uses 24. This does not invalidate the passes, but it RECLASSIFIES them - each was obtained on a runtime the project does not support, and any could differ on Node 24. Applies to typecheck, lint, test:unit, deploy:gate:test, eol:check and the three-engine test:ui runs alike.

STANDARD WORDING ADOPTED 2026-09-25 from CS-39, which stated the claim, its ceiling and its unlock in one line: "All three criteria met and asserted. Promotable on a green CI run; not promoted here." Every ticket in this cohort now carries the same sentence, plus the second bar discovered later - local execution on Node v22.23.2 against a declared floor of 24. NO QA TICKET IS PROMOTABLE TONIGHT ON EXECUTION EVIDENCE, and that is ONE GATE rather than nineteen separate problems.

F-67-1 STILL OPEN, VERIFIED AT SOURCE, AND THE CODE IS THIS SESSIONS OWN. engineering-ui.mjs:539-544 renders four literal cells - cell(n("P0")...), cell(n("P1")...), cell(n("P2")...), cell(n("P3")...). KNOWN_SEVERITIES exists at :96, is used for VALIDATION at :185 and is exported at :657, but strip() NEVER ITERATES IT. Deleting the P3 line leaves all six tests green and restores the original CS-67 defect with a one-line edit.

THE COMMENT ABOVE IT IS THE PROOF THE CLASS WAS NOT CLOSED, and this session wrote it: it explains precisely why a missing P3 mattered - "open findings could exist that no cell on this board accounted for" - AND THEN ADDS A FOURTH LITERAL RATHER THAN REMOVING THE REASON A FIFTH COULD GO MISSING. THE INSTANCE WAS FIXED; THE CLASS WAS NOT. That is the same distinction that has run through this entire run, applied to the very fix that was meant to demonstrate it.

FALSIFICATION REQUIREMENT FOR THE FIX, routed with it: IF DELETING A SEVERITYS RENDERING LEAVES THE SUITE GREEN, THE DEFECT HAS BEEN REBUILT IN A LOOP INSTEAD OF IN FOUR LINES. Iterating is not the goal; the goal is that an unrendered severity fails a test.

F-67-1 CLOSED AND VERIFIED AT SOURCE 2026-09-25 - AND IT CLOSES THE CLASS, NOT ONLY THE INSTANCE. scripts/engineering-ui.mjs:96 defines KNOWN_SEVERITIES = [P0, P1, P2, P3]; :543 serialises it into the client as SEVS; :579 records "the severity cells are generated from KNOWN_SEVERITIES, not written out". THE FOUR HAND-WRITTEN cell(n(Pn)) CALLS ARE GONE - measured as zero, with the matcher first proven able to find an injected literal so that zero means zero rather than meaning the matcher missed.

THE ORIGINAL DEFECT IS NOW STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE: adding a severity to the constant ADDS ITS CELL BY CONSTRUCTION, so no severity can be counted-but-unrendered. That was the exact failure - P3 was counted by nothing and rendered nowhere, so open findings could exist that no cell on the board accounted for. AND THE EARLIER FIX HAD ADDED A FOURTH LITERAL, WHICH CLOSED THE INSTANCE AND LEFT THE CLASS OPEN. This is the difference between the two, in the same file, an hour apart.

TWELFTH CONVERGENCE, AND THE THIRD AIMED AT OUR OWN INSTRUMENTATION RATHER THAN THE PRODUCT - after the promotion check and the eol completeness check. ALL THREE REPLACE "SOMEONE MUST NOTICE" WITH "THE REPOSITORY REFUSES." That is the only kind of fix that survives a tired reader at the end of a long session, which is precisely when this board gets used.

AND THE SEVERITY OF THE ORIGINAL IS WORTH RESTATING NOW THAT IT IS CLOSED: THIS IS THE BOARD THE OWNER READS TO DECIDE WHAT NEEDS ATTENTION. A severity silently uncounted THERE is a different order of defect from one in a test - a wrong test misleads an engineer who can read the code beside it, whereas a wrong dashboard misleads the person choosing what to look at, who by definition is not looking at the code.

PROVISIONAL MARKING WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25, SAME DAY IT WAS APPLIED, BECAUSE IT WAS TOO BROAD AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENT. The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". THE GATE COULD FAIL; ONLY ITS FIRST LINK COULD NOT. `npm run typecheck` chains four commands and the last, check-test-types.mjs, filters on /^\S+\.ts\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - WHICH MATCHES A PRODUCTION FILE AS READILY AS A TEST FILE - and exits 1. Anyone running the npm script WOULD have been told.

THIS TICKET DOES NOT CITE A BARE `tsc -b`, so its typecheck evidence was never in the unfalsifiable form and stands unqualified. The narrowed set is 4 of the original 29: CS-53, CS-62, CS-76, CS-77 - ALL FOUR WRITTEN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, which is the correct place for the correction to land.

items.title: Root scripts/ test files are unguarded, and two of them are silently red
items.userProblem: check-test-registration only guards v2 *.test.ts, so root scripts/ test files can be invoked by nothing - and two of them have been failing with nobody able to know.
items.source: Found 2026-09-25 while answering the coordinator question of whether engineering-ui.test.mjs was actually wired
acceptanceCriteria: Every *.test.mjs under root scripts/ is either invoked by an npm script or explicitly recorded as excluded with a reason
A registration guard covers root scripts/, not only v2, and covers .mjs as well as .test.ts
The two currently-red suites are fixed or quarantined with their diagnosis recorded; neither is weakened to go green
evidence: GUARD GAP CONFIRMED AT SOURCE: v2/scripts/check-test-registration.ts sets `const root = fileURLToPath(new URL("..", import.meta.url))`, which is v2/, and its own docstring scopes it to "every *.test.ts under v2". Root scripts/*.test.mjs is outside it TWICE - wrong directory and wrong extension. vitest.config.ts includes only packages/*/src/**/*.test.ts, apps/api/src/**/*.test.ts and apps/web/src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}, so no glob covers scripts/ either. A root scripts test is invisible to npm test AND unguarded.
MEASURED: 15 test files under root scripts/. Before this cycle SIX were invoked by no npm script, including scripts/engineering-hook.test.mjs - 22 passing tests that no gate had ever executed.

THE SHARPER FINDING: unwired does not merely mean unproven, it can mean SILENTLY RED. Of the four still-unwired files, TWO FAIL. engineering-runner.test.mjs: 15 pass, 5 fail, all in "runner enforces test totals", with "Cannot read properties of null (reading tests)" - a reader expecting a node:test reporter shape it is not getting. setup-admin-secret.test.mjs: 0 pass, 1 fail, "expected: 384, actual: 438".

setup-admin-secret DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN JUST REPORTED: 384 is 0o600 and 438 is 0o666, so the assertion is on restrictive file permissions. Windows does not enforce POSIX modes and fs.chmod is effectively a no-op there, so this almost certainly passes on Linux/CI and fails only on this host. That distinction matters: wiring it into gates:test on Windows would break the gate for a non-defect, and someone would then be tempted to weaken the assertion - which is the exact move the contract forbids.

ACTION TAKEN, deliberately partial: the two GREEN suites were wired in (engineering-contract.test.mjs, engineering.test.mjs), taking engineering:test from 28 to 195 tests, all passing. The two RED suites were NOT wired, because wiring a red suite into a gate either breaks the gate or invites someone to weaken the test. They are recorded here with their diagnosis instead of being hidden or quietly made green.

NO CANONICAL STATE MUTATED by running them: .ai/ had zero files modified in the window, the dirty count was unchanged at 206 and the backlog stayed at 67 items - checked because the contract warns that legacy mutation tests write canonical state.

CROSS-SESSION OBSERVATION 2026-09-25 15:0x, reported not fixed because package.json belongs to the infrastructure session under the three-session partition. `engineering:test` has been extended to include scripts/engineering-runner.test.mjs - the suite this ticket recorded as RED and deliberately excluded. Measured just now: npm run engineering:test is 215 tests, 210 pass, 5 FAIL, exit 1. The five failures are the SAME pre-existing "runner enforces test totals" cases diagnosed earlier (Cannot read properties of null reading tests), so nothing new was broken - but gates:test chains engineering:test, so THE GATE CHAIN IS NOW RED.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A NITPICK: a red suite inside a gate has exactly two outcomes, and both are bad. Either the gate stays red and stops being a signal anyone reads, or somebody weakens the five assertions to get it green - and the contract forbids exactly that. The correct resolutions are to fix the reader those five cases exercise, or to quarantine the file with a recorded reason, NOT to relax the assertions. Routed to the owning session rather than edited here.

ALSO OBSERVED, correctly inside the infrastructure session scope and noted only so the record is complete: scripts/ci-reachability.mjs and scripts/check-test-registration.mjs are new untracked files, and package.json now carries test:registration => node scripts/check-test-registration.mjs. That is a root-scripts registration guard, which is the AC2 of this ticket - so AC2 may now be satisfied by that session. This session did not verify it and does not claim it; the owning session should supply the evidence.

METHOD NOTE, recorded because it nearly produced a false report: the compliance check I wrote to prove I had not written outside my partition flagged these three files as MY violations. It could not tell my writes from another sessions - mtime says WHEN a file changed, never WHO changed it. The files are untracked additions and a scripts-block edit in the other sessions own paths, and my own last package.json write predates them. With three writers, "the working tree changed" is no longer evidence that I changed it.

ORDERING CONSTRAINT RECORDED 2026-09-25, and it is a release-sequencing fact rather than a preference: this ticket owns the diagnosis of setup-admin-secret.test.mjs (384 vs 438 - 0o600 against 0o666, NTFS not enforcing POSIX modes), and its AC3 is half-gated on a Linux run. IT MUST LAND BEFORE OR WITH THE COMMIT THAT EXPOSES THAT SUITE, because the commit is what makes the suite visible to CI, and a diagnosis that arrives afterwards arrives after the confusion it exists to prevent.
REVIEW WINDOW CAVEAT: three sessions were writing concurrently; re-check if a cited file moved between roughly 15:05 and 16:45 IST on 2026-09-25.

RELEASE BLOCKER, CONFIRMED BY RUNNING IT IN THIS SESSION 2026-09-25: npm run engineering:test exits 1 with 215 tests, 210 pass, 5 FAIL (not ok 38, 39, 40, 42, 43 - "runner enforces test totals", scripts/engineering-runner.test.mjs).

IT IS ARMED BY COMMITTING, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. engineering:test is chained into gates:test and gates:test runs in CI - but the COMMITTED gates:test does not include it. CI IS GREEN TODAY ONLY BECAUSE IT CANNOT SEE THIS SUITE, AND THE FIRST COMMIT IS WHAT ARMS IT. So this must be run GREEN BEFORE the commit, not after: if it goes in red, the first pipeline run of this entire body of work fails on the meta-suite, and it will look as though the commit broke something when the commit merely REVEALED it.

THE IRONY IS ALSO THE DIAGNOSIS: ci.yml describes that very file as "the test runners own TAP parser, INCLUDING ITS REFUSAL TO REPORT TOTALS IT CANNOT SUBSTANTIATE". The guard against reporting unsubstantiated totals is itself red, in a suite CI cannot see. Routed to the infrastructure session WITH AN EXPLICIT INSTRUCTION NOT TO FIX IT BY RELAXING WHAT THE RUNNER ENFORCES - the failing assertions are the feature.

RETRACTED 2026-09-25, AND THE RETRACTED ENTRY IS THE ONE THIS SESSION WROTE FIFTEEN MINUTES EARLIER. The two entries above describing engineering-runner.test.mjs as a RELEASE BLOCKER "ARMED BY COMMITTING" are WRONG and are left in place rather than deleted so the correction is visible. engineering-runner.test.mjs IS NOT BROKEN.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE, verified in this session by running the child command the runner spawns - the command nobody ran before escalating: `node --test --test-isolation=none --test-reporter=tap scripts/engineering.test.mjs` returns "bad option: --test-isolation=none" and exit 9 on this machine. The child dies before emitting a byte of TAP, which is why the artefact shows zero stdout bytes and null totals, and why success is false. THE TEST IS CORRECT: it asserts success === true and fails, which is exactly what ci.yml describes it as doing - "refusing to report totals it cannot substantiate".

SO THE SUITE IS THE ONLY THING IN THIS REPOSITORY CURRENTLY DETECTING A REAL ENVIRONMENT DEFECT, and an instruction to fix it had already gone out. Had it been followed we would have weakened the one guard that refuses to report unsubstantiated totals, ON THE NIGHT FIFTEEN CHECKS THAT COULD NOT FAIL WERE CATALOGUED. The only part of that instruction worth keeping - "do not fix it by relaxing what the runner enforces" - was load-bearing by accident rather than by judgement.

THE ENVIRONMENT DEFECT IT FOUND, verified at source: package.json engines.node ">=24.0.0", v2/package.json ">=24", .nvmrc "24", ci.yml NODE_VERSION "24" - AND THIS MACHINE IS RUNNING v22.23.2. EVERY LOCAL VERIFICATION RECORDED TODAY WAS EXECUTED TWO MAJOR VERSIONS BELOW THE PROJECTS DECLARED MINIMUM AND BELOW WHAT CI USES.

MARKED AS INFERENCE, NOT FACT: --test-isolation=none is PRESUMABLY supported on Node 24, which is why the suite was written against it. That cannot be verified without a Node 24 on this machine. The honest statement is: the flag fails on v22.23.2, the project requires >=24, and behaviour on 24 is UNTESTED.

REVISED COMMIT RISK, in the safer direction: the earlier claim that the first commit would arm a red suite and fail the first pipeline run is PROBABLY NOT TRUE ON NODE 24, which is what CI uses. "Probably" is the honest word, because nobody has run this suite on 24. THE COMMIT IS LESS DANGEROUS THAN THIS TICKET SAID AN HOUR AGO, NOT MORE. The commit-gate analysis itself is unchanged and still verified: committed gates:test runs six checks, the working tree defines eight, and test:registration x2 and checks:registry are absent from the committed ci.yml.

RUNTIME CAVEAT ADDED 2026-09-25 TO EVERY RESULT RECORDED TODAY: all local verification in this run was executed on Node v22.23.2, while package.json requires >=24.0.0, .nvmrc says 24 and CI uses 24. This does not invalidate the passes, but it RECLASSIFIES them - each was obtained on a runtime the project does not support, and any could differ on Node 24. Applies to typecheck, lint, test:unit, deploy:gate:test, eol:check and the three-engine test:ui runs alike.

SETTLED AS FACT 2026-09-25, UPGRADING THE ENTRY ABOVE THAT WAS MARKED INFERENCE. Reproduced independently in this session with a PAIRED POSITIVE CONTROL ON THE SAME SURFACE, in the same run. NEGATIVE, stable flag name: `node --test --test-isolation=none --test-reporter=tap scripts/engineering.test.mjs` -> "bad option: --test-isolation=none". POSITIVE, experimental flag name, SAME FILE: `--experimental-test-isolation=none` -> 159 tests, 159 pass, 0 fail. THE TEST FILE IS 159/159 GREEN. THE ONLY DEFECT IS THE FLAG NAME.

THE MECHANISM, which explains the exact version window: Node added the flag in v22.8.0 as --experimental-test-isolation and RENAMED it to the stable --test-isolation in v23.6.0. This machine is v22.23.2 - AFTER the flag existed, BEFORE the rename - so it accepts the experimental spelling and rejects the stable one. ci.yml sets NODE_VERSION 24, which is past the rename, so --test-isolation=none is valid there, the child emits TAP, totals parse and the five assertions pass.

THEREFORE, AS FACT AND NOT INFERENCE: THE FIVE FAILURES CANNOT OCCUR ON CI. THIS IS NOT A RELEASE BLOCKER AND THE COMMIT DOES NOT ARM ONE. The earlier escalation is fully retracted WITH A REASON rather than merely withdrawn.

scripts/engineering-runner.test.mjs IS NOT BROKEN AND MUST NOT BE TOUCHED. It behaved perfectly throughout: it detected a child that produced no substantiable totals and refused to report any. IT IS THE ONLY THING IN THIS REPOSITORY THAT NOTICED THE MACHINE WAS ON AN UNSUPPORTED RUNTIME. Any instruction to "fix" it should be read as an instruction to delete the one guard that worked.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND IS THE REAL FINDING: local Node v22.23.2 against a declared minimum of 24 in package.json, v2/package.json, .nvmrc and ci.yml. Every local result today was produced below the supported floor. The passes are not invalidated, but NO LOCAL exit 0 TONIGHT IS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE SUPPORTED RUNTIME, and that caveat is recorded on every ticket carrying a local verification.

PROVISIONAL MARKING WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25, SAME DAY IT WAS APPLIED, BECAUSE IT WAS TOO BROAD AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENT. The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". THE GATE COULD FAIL; ONLY ITS FIRST LINK COULD NOT. `npm run typecheck` chains four commands and the last, check-test-types.mjs, filters on /^\S+\.ts\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - WHICH MATCHES A PRODUCTION FILE AS READILY AS A TEST FILE - and exits 1. Anyone running the npm script WOULD have been told.

THIS TICKET DOES NOT CITE A BARE `tsc -b`, so its typecheck evidence was never in the unfalsifiable form and stands unqualified. The narrowed set is 4 of the original 29: CS-53, CS-62, CS-76, CS-77 - ALL FOUR WRITTEN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, which is the correct place for the correction to land.

items.title: Test evidence is gitignored, so a large fraction of it is unreproducible by anyone
items.userProblem: Visual baselines, diff images and every screenshot the browser suites write live under a gitignored directory, so the proof behind a batch of tickets exists only on one machine and cannot be re-derived by a reviewer, by CI, or by a later run on that same machine.
items.source: Independent review 2026-09-25, D's third cross-cutting pattern; verified independently at source by the orchestrator before filing
acceptanceCriteria: Visual baselines are versioned, or the visual check is explicitly recorded as advisory-only with the reason, so nobody cites it as proof
A fresh clone cannot silently generate its own baseline and report success; the first run without a baseline must fail or refuse, never self-approve
Evidence cited in a ticket can be re-derived by someone who did not run the original command
evidence: VERIFIED AT SOURCE by the orchestrator, not taken on report. .gitignore:21 is "test-results/". check-pages-ui.mjs:16 sets the baseline directory to test-results/pages-baseline - INSIDE the ignored tree. ZERO visual baselines are tracked: the 20 repository files matching baseline/snapshot/png patterns are drizzle migration snapshots, design concept images and unrelated crypto helpers. test-results/ currently holds 1864 files including 534 PNGs, none of them in the repository.

THE STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE, which is worse than "the evidence is missing": on a fresh clone there is no baseline, so the first run must create one from whatever the code renders at that moment. A visual check whose baseline is produced by its own first run CANNOT FAIL on a fresh clone. This is a check-that-cannot-fail at the REPOSITORY level rather than inside a single assertion - the same class the whole batch has been hunting, one layer up.

A PIPELINE WILL NOT FIX THIS, which is why it is filed separately from every CI-execution item. CI would regenerate the baseline on every run and pass. The defect is that the artefact is not versioned, not that nothing runs.

SCOPE: CS-32s rejection is ONE INSTANCE of this, not the whole of it. The same pattern makes the UI-freeze claim unverifiable on the tickets with untracked-only evidence, and it affects the PROOF rather than just the diff, so it is broader than the untracked-baseline problem already recorded elsewhere.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-28: scripts/pages-baseline contains the reviewed 192-case matrix; a missing file now fails loudly, and npm run pages:visual matched every case locally. The chromium-search-light-320 case produced no diff and the threshold comment now states pixelmatch's actual 0.1 setting.

items.title: The API exposes no job-to-lead lookup, so the UI cannot know a job is already saved
items.userProblem: An already-saved job renders "Save Job" with aria-pressed="false" because SaveJob has no mount query and derives every label from a mutation result that is undefined until clicked. That is not an uninformative control - it is a control asserting a state it does not know, telling a screen-reader user definitively NOT SAVED. The same lie in a smaller font. A duplicate posting can also be saved twice, because the frontend cannot ask whether a job is already on the shortlist.
items.source: Filed 2026-09-25 from the UAT audit. CS-19 and CS-51 both requested this backend ticket in their evidence and neither could create it; the request sat in prose and never became work.
acceptanceCriteria: The API lets an owner-scoped caller determine whether a given job is already saved as a lead, without leaking any other owner data
SaveJob hydrates already-saved state on mount so the control reports the state it is confirming, with aria-pressed reflecting reality before any click

Saving a posting that deduplicates to an existing saved lead is recognised rather than creating a second lead, and the test proves it by attempting the duplicate and asserting the lead count is unchanged - not merely that no error was thrown
evidence: CONFIRMED AT SOURCE 2026-09-25: no fingerprint, alreadySaved or isSaved handling exists anywhere in the save path under v2/apps/web/src. Fingerprint deduplication exists in discovery but the UI does not use it when saving.

THIS IS THE BLOCKER UNDER TWO OTHER TICKETS. CS-19 AC4 cannot be met without it, and CS-51 recorded the same residual. Both said in their evidence that a backend ticket was needed; neither could file one, so the need was documented repeatedly and never scheduled. Filing it is the entire unlock.

TEST TRAP RECORDED IN AC3 BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION: asserting that a duplicate save "does not error" passes against an implementation that silently creates a second lead. The assertion must be on the LEAD COUNT being unchanged, paired with a positive that a genuinely new job DOES create one - otherwise the negative passes against a save path that saves nothing at all.
items.currentStep: READY. Blocks CS-19 AC4 and carries CS-51 disclosed residual. The API exposes no job-to-lead lookup, so an already-saved job renders "Save Job" with aria-pressed="false" - a control asserting a state it does not know. Both tickets asked for this in prose and neither could file it.

items.title: Resume title derivation fails silently; report an undeterminable title set instead of an empty list
items.userProblem: A resume whose titles cannot be derived returns an empty list, which is indistinguishable from a resume that genuinely had no recognisable role, so matching quietly proceeds on preferences alone with no signal.
items.source: Split from CS-64 on 2026-09-25. CS-64's AC2 and AC3 are decision-independent by their own wording; only AC1 needs an owner decision, and the BLOCKED label was hiding available engineering work.
acceptanceCriteria: An undeterminable title set is reported as such rather than returned as an empty list, so a caller can distinguish "could not determine" from "genuinely none"
Proven with a non-English positive case AND an English regression case in the same test, so the change cannot pass by breaking English extraction
No new language support is added and ROLE_WORDS is not extended - that is CS-64 AC1 and needs an owner decision
evidence: Current Node 24 CI verification: runs 36385161068 and 36385785464 completed green; all three acceptance criteria were re-taken and the owner decision remains correctly isolated to CS-64.

MEASURED BASIS, carried from CS-64 and verified there at source: deriveTitles returns 0 titles for "Ingenieur logiciel senior", "Softwareentwickler", "Desarrollador de software" and "Sviluppatore software", while returning 1 for "Senior Software Engineer" and "Data Analyst". The CS-56 character allowlist is NOT the cause - it permits \p{M} so accents survive, and an accented title containing an English role word derives intact.
THE DEFECT IS THE SILENCE, NOT THE VOCABULARY. Which languages to recognise is a product decision and stays in CS-64. Ending the silence is not, and it is the smallest honest improvement available.

TEST TRAP RECORDED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION: a test asserting only that a non-English resume now reports "undeterminable" would pass against an implementation that reports undeterminable for EVERYTHING, including English. The English regression case in the same test is what makes the non-English assertion mean anything - AC2 requires both, on the same surface.

OWNERSHIP NOTE: packages/resume is the api/packages sessions active write area under the three-session partition. This ticket is filed by the orchestrator and routed there; it must not be implemented from the web session.

DELIVERED BY THE api/packages SESSION AND VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY HERE 2026-09-25. deriveTitles no longer returns a bare array: it returns TitleDerivation { status, titles } with TitleDerivationStatus = "derived" | "no-content" | "undeterminable". THE SILENT FAILURE IS ENDED - an undeterminable title set now says so instead of being indistinguishable from a resume that genuinely had no recognisable role.

THE IMPLEMENTATION IS SHARPER THAN THE CRITERION I WROTE, and the extra state is the valuable part. AC1 asked for a two-way distinction; the build delivers THREE, separating "no-content" (there was nothing to read) from "undeterminable" (there WAS text and none of it was recognisable as a role). Those are different facts about the resume and they warrant different handling - collapsing them would have reintroduced a smaller version of the same ambiguity this ticket exists to remove. The docstring covers the case that makes it necessary: a language the extractor does not read AND an English resume whose roles it failed to match are both "could not determine".

AC2 SATISFIED, AND THE TEST IS BUILT THE WAY THE CRITERION DEMANDED - all three cases in ONE test (derive.test.ts:299-327), with the reason written into the file: "a deriveTitles broken for everybody would satisfy the non-English resume yields no titles perfectly". Non-English Spanish input -> status "undeterminable", titles []. CONTROL 1, same test: "Senior Software Engineer | Acme Corp, Pune" -> status "derived", titles ["Senior Software Engineer"], proving the function still reads English. CONTROL 2, same test: empty input -> status "no-content", asserted NOT EQUAL to the undeterminable status, proving the two empty results are genuinely different values rather than one value wearing two names.

AC3 HELD: ROLE_WORDS was NOT extended and no new language support was added. The English-only gate is unchanged - which is correct, because which languages to recognise is CS-64 AC1 and remains the owner decision.
NON-BREAKING: 251 tests across 10 files pass in resume, matching and shared.
RUNTIME CAVEAT: verified on Node v22.23.2, below the declared minimum of 24. Real, but not evidence about the supported runtime.

WORDING CORRECTED 2026-09-25 FROM "All applicable criteria met" TO THE COUNTED FORM. The distinction is not cosmetic: "ALL THREE CRITERIA MET" IS FALSIFIABLE BY COUNTING; "ALL APPLICABLE CRITERIA MET" CANNOT FAIL, because an unmet criterion can be reclassified as not-applicable without anyone editing a number. It is the same shape as \bsurfaced\b, DEFERRED and eol=crlf - a word anyone can write that silently changes how a claim is graded - except that this one sat in the STATUS FIELD OF TEN TICKETS, which is the field a promotion decision reads. That makes it the most consequential of the four, not the least.

COUNT NOT YET RE-TAKEN 2026-09-25, recorded as owed work rather than left as an unverified claim. When "All applicable criteria met" was replaced with the counted form across ten tickets, THE WORDING WAS CORRECTED AND THE COUNT WAS NOT. Two of the ten were then found wrong within minutes - CS-74 (AC3 half-met) and CS-52 (AC4 unmet) - so the remaining eight cannot be assumed right. A COUNTED CLAIM OVER AN UNCOUNTED CRITERION IS NO BETTER THAN THE HEDGE IT REPLACED; it is only more falsifiable, and falsifying it is the outstanding work.

THIS TICKET currentStep BECAME THE TEMPLATE FOR THE COHORT 2026-09-25 - "N criteria; COUNT NOT YET RE-TAKEN since the wording correction - treat the per-criterion status as unverified, not as met." IT NEITHER HEDGES NOR OVER-COUNTS: it states the number, states that the number has not been verified per criterion, and names the outstanding work. A TICKET THAT SAYS "I HAVE NOT CHECKED THIS YET" IS MORE USEFUL THAN ONE SAYING "all applicable criteria met" AND MORE USEFUL THAN A WRONG COUNT.

AND THE LABEL IS CURRENTLY UNDERSTATING THIS TICKET, which is the safe direction and is recorded as such: an independent reviewer verified all three criteria ARE evidenced - AC1 three-state TitleDerivation where the criterion asked only for two, AC2 a single test carrying Spanish -> undeterminable, English -> derived and empty -> no-content ASSERTED NOT-EQUAL to undeterminable, AC3 ROLE_WORDS confirmed unextended. An honest under-claim awaiting confirmation is the correct resting state; an honest over-claim is not.

TOKEN SCAN 2026-09-25 RETURNED CLEAN FOR THIS TICKET - every criterion is named by identifier somewhere in the evidence. RECORDED AT ITS REAL STRENGTH AND NO HIGHER: THAT MEANS "NO CRITERION IS UNMENTIONED", NOT "ALL CRITERIA ARE MET". The COUNT NOT YET RE-TAKEN label STAYS, because a proxy that asks whether the token AC2 appears is not asking whether AC2 is satisfied. Nothing suggests a problem here; nothing has verified one either.

COUNT DISCHARGED 2026-09-25 - 3 OF 3, on the independent verification already recorded here: AC1 a three-state TitleDerivation WHERE THE CRITERION ASKED FOR TWO, AC2 a single test carrying Spanish -> undeterminable, English -> derived and empty -> no-content ASSERTED NOT-EQUAL to undeterminable, AC3 ROLE_WORDS confirmed unextended. The earlier label was UNDERSTATING a ticket in good shape, which was the safe direction; it is now stated at its real strength.

items.title: Automate the promotion question that caught five UAT demotions in two batches
items.userProblem: Every UAT demotion found tonight was caught by one question asked against text the repository already had, yet nothing in the promotion path asks it, so the same class recurs every time a ticket is promoted.
items.source: Filed 2026-09-25 after the question caught 5 of 5 across two independent audit batches - CS-14, CS-17, CS-50, CS-2 and CS-19 original ground - before any source was read.
acceptanceCriteria: A check fails promotion when any acceptance criterion has a recorded unmet status, in the ticket own evidence or in a file it depends on

It distinguishes RECORDED-UNMET (blocks promotion) from NO-EVIDENCE-RECORDED (demands a write-up but does not by itself prove the code is undelivered), because CS-18 proved those are different failures with opposite correct responses
Proven able to fail: a synthetic ticket carrying a disclosed-residual phrase must be rejected, and a clean ticket must pass, in the same run

SIBLING CONSISTENCY: if a criterion of the form "proven by doing X on a real system" has siblings that were demoted for that exact shape, the ticket must be demoted too. Consistency across tickets is itself checkable, and this is the rule that would have caught the highest-cost instance - five tickets were treated one way and a sixth, the only P0, was not.

NEGATIVE FIXTURE PAIR, mandatory: CS-19 and CS-51 carry an IDENTICAL disclosed residual in near-identical language, and the correct outcomes are OPPOSITE - CS-19 demoted, CS-51 held. The check must produce both. A check with only positive fixtures can prove it fires but not that it DISCRIMINATES.
evidence: FIVE FOR FIVE ACROSS TWO BATCHES, every one caught by a single question - "does any acceptance criterion have a recorded unmet status, in the ticket own evidence or in a file it depends on?" - asked BEFORE any source was read. CS-14 (KNOWN-LIMITATIONS records screen readers as OPEN - HUMAN VALIDATION while AC4 requires verified-not-assumed), CS-17 (its own evidence says no dismiss action and no schema), CS-50 (AC1 requires owner-confirmed; recorded as confirmed by a non-owner), CS-2 (its own evidence says the named defect did not reproduce), CS-19 original ground (a prescribed backend ticket that did not exist).

IT NEEDS NO REVIEWER, NO JUDGEMENT AND NO SHELL. Every disqualifying fact was already written down by the ticket itself. THE FAILURE WAS NEVER A SHORTAGE OF EVIDENCE - IT WAS THAT NOTHING IN THE PROMOTION PATH READ WHAT THE TICKET ALREADY SAID.

THE SECOND CRITERION EXISTS BECAUSE OF CS-18, and it is the part most likely to be dropped: CS-18 had NO recorded evidence for any of its four criteria and looked exactly like a failure. Verifying at source showed all four DELIVERED by match-evidence.tsx, which cites CS-18 in its own comment. A no-evidence check would have flagged it correctly about the bookkeeping and WRONGLY about the code. The two outcomes must be reported differently or the check will produce confident false demotions - which is worse than the gap it closes.
OWNERSHIP: this is a root scripts/ guard, which belongs to the infrastructure session under the three-session partition. Filed and routed, not implemented here.

SPEC EXTENDED 2026-09-25 after CS-7. The question as originally specified - does any criterion have a recorded unmet status - would NOT have caught CS-7, because CS-7 records its criterion as pending rather than unmet. What catches it is CROSS-TICKET CONSISTENCY: CS-3, CS-24, CS-25, CS-26 and CS-27 were all demoted for the "proven on a real system" shape, and CS-7 carries the same shape with "pipeline" in place of "host". THAT COMPARISON IS MECHANICAL and it is the rule that would have caught the only P0 in the backlog.

GUARD ADDED 2026-09-25 BECAUSE THE CONSISTENCY RULE WOULD OTHERWISE OVER-FIRE, and the case that breaks it is already on the board. CS-19 and CS-51 disclose the SAME residual - SaveJob mount hydration, aria-pressed="false" - in near-identical wording including the same "needs a backend ticket" phrase. CS-19 is demoted; CS-51 holds. Naively that looks exactly like the inconsistency used to demote CS-7.

IT IS NOT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE RULE: CS-19s AC4 says a duplicate posting already saved is RECOGNISED - the residual is INSIDE that criterion, since a control that cannot recognise an already-saved job is failing it. CS-51s AC1 enumerates four identifiers and asks that every identifier EXISTING AT A CALL SITE reaches its destination - and in the mount-hydration case NO IDENTIFIER EXISTS AT THE CALL SITE TO DISCARD. Nothing is dropped; something is unavailable. Different defect, different criterion.

THE GENERAL FORM: THE SAME RESIDUAL CAN BE IN SCOPE FOR ONE CRITERION AND OUT OF SCOPE FOR ANOTHER. COMPARE CRITERIA BY WHAT THEY ASSERT, NOT BY THE RESIDUALS TEXT. This is the third near-miss tonight where reading the criterion cold changed the answer, which is the strongest argument that this check must REPORT FOR REVIEW rather than fail the build wherever scope is arguable.

DELIVERED AND PROVEN 2026-09-25, verified independently in this session. promotion:test passes 12/12, and THE FIXTURE NAMES SHOW IT DISCRIMINATES RATHER THAN MERELY FIRES - which was the whole risk with this check. Included: "the same residual blocks one criterion and not another (CS-19 vs CS-51)" - the mandatory negative fixture pair; "a DEFERRED limitation is advisory, never blocking (CS-33 false positive)"; "validated as an adjective does not trigger the register cross-reference"; "nothing outside the claim fields is scanned"; plus blocking cases for the CS-2, CS-50 and CS-7 shapes.

LIVE RUN AGAINST THE REAL BOARD: 17 UAT tickets, 0 BLOCKING, 3 advisory (CS-22, CS-33, CS-51). All three correctly advisory - CS-51s residual is out of its AC1 scope exactly as argued when the guard was specified, and CS-33s is a disclosed unrelated flake. AFTER SEVEN DEMOTIONS THE UAT TIER IS CLEAN BY A MECHANICAL CHECK THAT NEEDS NO REVIEWER.
AND IT INDEPENDENTLY SURFACED CS-22, which a reviewer had listed as unexamined. That is the difference between a check and a habit: the habit audits what someone thought to look at.

THE DISCRIMINATION REQUIREMENT WAS NOT DECORATIVE. Specified because CS-19 and CS-51 carry an identical disclosed residual with opposite correct outcomes; a check with only positive fixtures proves it fires but not that it tells them apart. It now demonstrably does.
RUNTIME CAVEAT: verified on Node v22.23.2, below the declared minimum of 24. Real, but not evidence about the supported runtime.

W-1 CONFIRMED 2026-09-25, AND IT CORRECTS A CLAIM RECORDED ABOVE BY THIS SESSION. The entry stating "17 UAT tickets, 0 BLOCKING" is left in place rather than deleted, but IT MUST NOT BE CITED AS RELEASE-READINESS EVIDENCE. Verified at source: check-promotion-evidence.mjs:207 is `const namesCriterion = /\bAC\s*\d\b/i.test(flat)` and :211 is `severity: namesCriterion ? "blocking" : "advisory"`. THE BLOCKING BRANCH REQUIRES THE RESIDUAL TO SPELL "AC<n>".

THE ACCURATE STATEMENT, replacing the one recorded earlier: THE TIER WAS CLEANED BY REVIEWERS. The check then reported 0 blocking for a reason PARTLY INDEPENDENT OF THAT - a residual contradicting a criterion in plain English grades advisory, not blocking. Run against the real CS-19 and CS-17 with their evidence as it read BEFORE the demotion notes (which spell "AC4") were appended, both come back ADVISORY. TWO OF THE FOUR DEMOTIONS THIS CHECK WAS BUILT FROM WOULD HAVE PASSED IT.

THE HEURISTIC IS BACKWARDS, AND THAT IS THE FIX RATHER THAN A TUNING CHANGE: naming an AC is evidence that a disclosure is PRECISE, not evidence that it is SERIOUS. The historical CS-17 fixture represented missing dismiss-action and schema support, named no AC, and was the gravest residual of the four.

THE CLOSING IRONY, recorded because it is genuinely the point rather than a flourish: THE GATE BUILT TO CATCH CHECKS THAT CANNOT FAIL HAS A BRANCH THAT CANNOT FAIL, FOR EXACTLY THE CASES THAT MOTIVATED IT. And it was reintroduced by the same session reporting on the class.

FIXTURE REQUIREMENT FOR THE FIX, and it is the only set that matters: THE FOUR ORIGINALS, with their evidence AS IT READ BEFORE THE DEMOTION NOTES WERE APPENDED. A check that flags them only after a later demotion annotation is checking the annotation, not the original ticket.

DO NOT LET THE FIX TOUCH `no-acceptance-criteria` (:193, severity blocking). It is a genuine cannot-look guard - it refused to assess tickets it could not evaluate rather than returning a clean result, and it caught a malformed synthetic fixture on the first try. THE DEFECT IS `namesCriterion` ALONE.

A METHOD FAILURE WORTH KEEPING, from the experiment that settled this: the first attempt used synthetic tickets with NO acceptanceCriteria, all three cases returned blocking, and "W-1 disproven" had already been written. The rule that actually fired was no-acceptance-criteria - entirely unrelated to the claim - INCLUDING FOR THE POSITIVE CONTROL, whose failure to discriminate is exactly what should have raised the alarm and did not. Only the precondition assertions on the second attempt ("CS-19 has 4 acceptance criteria", printed BEFORE any conclusion) made the result trustworthy. THIRD TIME TODAY THE PRECONDITION RULE HAS RESCUED A CONCLUSION.

GATE FIXED AND RE-PROVEN 2026-09-25 BY THE EXPERIMENT THAT DISPROVED THE OLD ONE, which is the only form of proof worth having here. Same script, same fixtures - the real CS-19 and CS-17 with their PRE-DEMOTION evidence text that does not spell AC<n> - and the opposite result: BLOCKING for both. The CS-17 message now quotes its historical missing-dismiss/schema residual rather than a generic label.

AND IT STILL DISCRIMINATES, WHICH MATTERED MORE THAN THE FIX. The risk in making residuals blocking by default was turning the gate into noise - noise gets a gate disabled, and a disabled gate protects nothing. All three negative controls held: CS-22 advisory (its residual is attributed to a separate ticket), CS-33 advisory ("did not reproduce"), and CS-51 ADVISORY - the case whose residual is IDENTICAL to CS-19s but out of scope for ITS criteria. THE CS-19/CS-51 DISCRIMINATION SURVIVED THE FIX, which is the property that makes this gate worth having at all.

THE CLAIM IS REINSTATED ONLY IN THIS FORM, and must not be restated as "0 blocking": THE GATE IS PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL FOR THE FOUR CASES THAT MOTIVATED IT, PROVEN TO STILL DISCRIMINATE AGAINST THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS, AND REPORTS 1 BLOCKING ACROSS 17 UAT TICKETS. It runs in advisory mode and does not yet fail the build. The 1 blocking is CS-9, a P1, now demoted.

ADVISORY-MODE STAGING IS CORRECT AND DELIBERATE: it reports and exits 0, with "re-run with --strict once the shapes have proven themselves". A new gate that fails the build on its first day gets switched off; one that reports for a while earns the right to block.

A NEW CHECK THIS MAKES POSSIBLE, worth folding into this tickets scope: "All N criteria met and asserted" IS NOW MACHINE-CHECKABLE AGAINST acceptanceCriteria.length, and "All applicable criteria met" never was. A promotion check can now assert that a tickets own claimed count matches its real one - a one-line comparison that would catch a criterion being silently dropped or reclassified. THAT IS THE CONVERGENCE THE WORDING CHANGE BOUGHT: a sentence that was prose became a sentence a script can refute.

SHAPE 5 NOW CATCHES 6 OF 6, WAS 1 OF 6 - verified by re-running the experiment that exposed the gap, with the same six tickets presented as UAT promotion candidates carrying their real criteria: CS-7, CS-3, CS-24, CS-25, CS-26 and CS-30 all CAUGHT. That includes CS-3 "proven by killing Caddy" and CS-24 "proven by stopping a container", BOTH OF WHICH PREVIOUSLY MISSED. The rule now matches the criterion DEMAND rather than an enumerated verb list, so a seventh phrased differently will also be caught - which was the entire point of fixing the class rather than adding two verbs.

AND IT STILL DISCRIMINATES, which mattered more than the broadening: 16 UAT tickets, 0 BLOCKING, 4 advisory. SHAPE 5 FIRES ON NONE OF THE 16. Broadening from a verb list to a class did NOT turn it into noise - the real risk, because a gate that flags everything gets disabled and then protects nothing. The three negative controls (CS-22, CS-33, CS-51) still grade advisory.

THE DEFERRED LEVER IS NOW COUNTED RATHER THAN LOCKED, and the count is printed every run: "limitations register: 25 sections, 15 OPEN (blocking), 8 DEFERRED/PARTIAL (downgraded to advisory)". RECORD 8 AS TODAY BASELINE, the same way 4 is the binary baseline. The lever is not removed - it cannot be, since a genuine deferral is legitimate - but a register-wide OPEN->DEFERRED edit now MOVES A NUMBER SOMEBODY WILL SEE.

P-1 CLOSED WITH ITS REASONING KEPT IN PLACE: \bsurfaced\b is gone from ATTRIBUTED_ELSEWHERE, and the only surviving occurrences are comments documenting WHY - "it is a bare English verb... CS-23 AC2 is literally is surfaced to the owner". THE FIX AND ITS REASON TRAVEL TOGETHER, which is what makes a fix survive the next reader; an undocumented one has to be re-derived to be trusted.

STILL OUTSTANDING ON THE GUARDS, recorded so the green result is not read as completion: L-1 (eol=crlf satisfies direction 2 and is checked by neither half - the third exemption-value), L-3 (unrepresentable .gitattributes patterns dropped silently), N-3 (a blank .nvmrc treated more leniently than a corrupt one), P-4 ("did not reproduce" carrying two opposite meanings), P-5 (Shape 5 suppressor accepts topic words where Shape 3 demands a locator).

AND THE CEILING ON "0 BLOCKING ACROSS 16 UAT TICKETS": IT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT THE TIER RECORDS, NOT ABOUT CI. The commit gate is untouched. A tier whose records are internally consistent is not a tier that has been executed.

CHECK #19 THAT COULD NOT FAIL, AND IT IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL OF THE RUN BECAUSE IT IS NOT AN ASSERTION - IT IS A GATE, AND IT SITS UPSTREAM OF THE OTHERS. `npx tsc -b` exited 0 while apps/workers/search/src/collect.ts carried a genuine TS2353 in PRODUCTION CODE; `tsc -b --force` exited 2 on the same tree, and deleting that project .tsbuildinfo made plain `tsc -b` go red and stay red. The project is in the build graph - this was incremental state reporting success over a real error, NOT an excluded file.

THE DIFFERENCE IN BLAST RADIUS IS THE POINT: A TEST THAT CANNOT FAIL MISGRADES ONE TICKET. A TYPECHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL MISGRADES EVERY TICKET THAT CITED IT - and it is the single most-cited piece of evidence on this board. 29 tickets carry a typecheck claim and all 29 are now marked provisional.

AND IT HAS THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES THIS WHOLE FAMILY DANGEROUS: THE GREEN WAS NOT A BUG IN ANYONE LOGIC. tsc -b did exactly what incremental build means; nobody wrote a bad check. THE EVIDENCE WAS STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE OF FAILING AND IT STILL LOOKED EXACTLY LIKE EVIDENCE - the one sentence that fits all nineteen.

FIRST OF THE NINETEEN WHERE THE TOOLING, RATHER THAN AN ASSERTION, WAS THE THING THAT COULD NOT FAIL. Every prior instance was something somebody wrote; this one is a documented feature of a standard build tool, used correctly, producing an unfalsifiable result.

ATTRIBUTION, AS THE REPORTING SESSION ASKED AND AS IT IS CORRECT TO RECORD: the fault is NOT the tooling - tsc -b behaved as documented. It relayed "tsc -b exit 0" as evidence several times tonight, including in consolidated status, having run the command and reported its exit code accurately. THE INSUFFICIENCY WAS NEVER ASKING WHETHER THE COMMAND WAS CAPABLE OF RETURNING ANYTHING ELSE - the identical error it had been auditing in other people tests all evening, committed against the most load-bearing gate on the board.

I COULD NOT REPRODUCE THE DIVERGENCE MYSELF AND I AM RECORDING THAT PLAINLY RATHER THAN CLAIMING A VERIFICATION I DO NOT HAVE. My run gave tsc -b exit 0 AND tsc -b --force exit 0 - no divergence - because collect.ts had been fixed at 18:41:29, ONE MINUTE BEFORE THE RUN. The finding was true when reported; the evidence for it is the reporting session three observations, not mine. THE GATE-HARDENING ITEM REMAINS OPEN AND UNVERIFIED BY ME.

A COMMENT THAT EXPLAINS A FIXED DEFECT CAN ITSELF BE WRONG, AND IT IS A DISTINCT HAZARD FROM THE DEFECT - recorded from F-48-A. The ai-provider.test.ts comment correctly diagnoses WHY the type collapsed to never and then misstates WHAT never does, asserting that bogus calls were "equally accepted" when property access on never is an error. The code is right and the lesson attached to it is wrong.

THIS IS THE INVERSE OF THE BEST ARTEFACT OF THE PREVIOUS RUN - "Widening the parameter alone is NOT sufficient, and I checked rather than assumed" - which put a correct rule into the code at the moment it was learned. A COMMENT IS READ BY THE PERSON ABOUT TO MAKE THE MISTAKE, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY A WRONG ONE IS EXPENSIVE: it will be trusted at the moment it matters most, by someone with no reason to doubt it.

A NEW AND RARER ACT RECORDED FROM CS-31 F-4: PROTECTING A CHECK FROM A FUTURE WELL-INTENTIONED REPAIR. The 1x1 hidden assertion is knowingly over-strict and was left over-strict, with the reason written down, BECAUSE LOOSENING IT WOULD REOPEN THE DEFECT IT CLOSES. Everything else this run has been about making checks able to fail; THIS IS ABOUT KEEPING A CHECK ABLE TO FAIL AFTER THE NEXT PERSON READS IT AND THINKS IT TOO STRICT.

IT IS THE SAME INSIGHT AS THE RUNBOOK REMOVAL NOTE - "do not reintroduce a second criterion here" - arrived at independently in a different medium. BOTH ANTICIPATE A PLAUSIBLE, WELL-MEANT FUTURE EDIT AND LEAVE THE ARGUMENT AGAINST IT IN PLACE. A rule with its reason attached survives a reader who disagrees with it; a bare rule does not.

2026-09-28: hosted workflow run https://github.com/varunjakkampudi-tech/careerscope/actions/runs/36424073277 passed the registered promotion-evidence and ticket-consistency checks. The synthetic fail/pass controls and the CS-19/CS-51 opposite-outcome pair remain covered by promotion:test.

items.title: ownerAgent and architectureImpact can contradict where the evidence says the work lives
items.userProblem: A ticket can be scoped to one tier while its acceptance criteria can only be met by a change in another, and the disclosure sits in evidence - which someone picking up a READY ticket never reads that far to find.
items.source: Filed 2026-09-25 from the READY-tier audit, after the same shape appeared three times: CS-59, CS-61 and CS-54.
acceptanceCriteria: A validator asserts that ownerAgent and architectureImpact are consistent with the tier the evidence says the remaining work lives in, and fails when they disagree

It fails on CS-54 as it stood before correction - ownerAgent Frontend, architectureImpact naming a Next.js strategy, evidence saying the work belongs to the infrastructure session - and passes on CS-59, which declares the cross-tier dependency in architectureImpact
Proven able to fail: a synthetic ticket with a contradicting ownerAgent is rejected and a consistent one passes, in the same run
evidence: THREE INSTANCES OF ONE SHAPE, which is what makes it structural rather than three mistakes: a ticket scoped to tier A whose acceptance criteria can only be met by a change in tier B. CS-59 DECLARES it in architectureImpact and is therefore safe. CS-61 CONTRADICTED it - architectureImpact said "No server change" while AC1 required a server change. CS-54 IS THE MOST DANGEROUS VARIANT: the disclosure exists, but in EVIDENCE, while ownerAgent, architectureImpact and status all still pointed at the tier that cannot do the work.

WHY A VALIDATOR RATHER THAN A REVIEW HABIT: all three were caught by reading evidence to the end, and SOMEONE PICKING UP A READY TICKET NEVER READS THAT FAR. A reviewer catching it each time is the instance; a validator makes the class unrepresentable. Ninth convergence, and the second aimed at this projects own process rather than at the product.
OWNERSHIP: a root scripts/ validator, which belongs to the infrastructure session under the three-session partition. Filed and routed, not implemented here.

SCOPE EXTENDED 2026-09-25 BY A SWEEP OF THIS SESSIONS OWN WORK. After finding a stale currentStep on CS-54 - a ticket this session had itself demoted - a board-wide audit found FIVE MORE STATUS/currentStep DISAGREEMENTS, AND ALL FIVE WERE ON TICKETS MOVED TODAY BY THIS SESSION: CS-10 (BLOCKED, said QA/UAT), CS-30 (BLOCKED, said DISCOVERY), CS-44 (BLOCKED, said DISCOVERY), CS-53 (READY, said DISCOVERY), CS-61 (DISCOVERY, said READY). Plus seven tickets with no currentStep at all, five of them filed by this session.

THE GENERAL FORM, AND IT IS WHY THIS BELONGS IN THE SAME VALIDATOR: CHANGING `status` AND CHANGING THE FIELDS THAT DESCRIBE THE STATUS ARE TWO SEPARATE ACTS, AND NOTHING ENFORCES THAT THE SECOND FOLLOWS THE FIRST. The board renders currentStep, so every one of those six was showing a reader a status the ticket did not hold. This is the same class as ownerAgent/architectureImpact drift and should be one check, not two.

RECORDED AGAINST THIS SESSION RATHER THAN AS AN OBSERVATION ABOUT THE BOARD: the defect was introduced by the same session that spent the day correcting it on other tickets. That is the argument for the validator rather than for more care.

items.title: The Node version floor is declared in four places and enforced by nothing
items.userProblem: Every local verification today ran two major versions below the declared minimum and almost everything passed, so the floor that four files declare is not a floor.
items.source: Filed 2026-09-25 after engineering-runner.test.mjs turned out to be the ONLY thing detecting that the running Node was below engines.node.
acceptanceCriteria: A preflight in gates:test fails loudly when the running Node is below engines.node, BEFORE any suite runs, naming both the required and the running version
The required version is read from package.json engines.node rather than hardcoded, so it cannot drift from the declaration it enforces
Proven able to fail: simulate a below-floor version and confirm the preflight rejects it, and confirm a compliant version passes, in the same run
evidence: VERIFIED AT SOURCE: package.json engines.node ">=24.0.0", v2/package.json ">=24", .nvmrc "24", ci.yml NODE_VERSION "24" - and the machine running every verification today is v22.23.2.

THE QUESTION WORTH MORE THAN THE BUG: WHY DID EXACTLY ONE SUITE NOTICE? Everything else ran green on an unsupported runtime, INCLUDING CHECKS WHOSE ENTIRE PURPOSE IS VERIFYING OTHER CHECKS. A version floor that only one test enforces - and only incidentally, by happening to use a newer flag - IS A FLOOR THAT IS NOT ENFORCED.

THIS IS THE CHEAPEST OF THE CONVERGENCES. It converts "we happened to have one test that used a newer flag" into an enforced invariant, and it is a few lines. Every other convergence this run required a refactor or a contract change.
OWNERSHIP: a root scripts/ preflight wired into gates:test, which belongs to the infrastructure session under the three-session partition. Filed and routed, not implemented here.

CAUSE NOW PROVEN RATHER THAN SUSPECTED 2026-09-25, which strengthens this tickets case rather than weakening it: the flag was added in Node v22.8.0 as --experimental-test-isolation and renamed to --test-isolation in v23.6.0. This machine at v22.23.2 sits inside that window, which is why exactly one suite noticed the runtime was wrong - it happened to use a VERSION-SENSITIVE FLAG.

THE COST OF NOT HAVING THIS PREFLIGHT IS NOW MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: the absence produced an INCORRECT ESCALATION TO THE OWNER claiming a release blocker, and an instruction to "fix" the one guard that had correctly refused to report unsubstantiated totals. A preflight failing loudly when the running Node is below engines.node would have surfaced this IN ONE LINE, before any suite ran, instead of via a five-assertion failure in the only suite that happened to be version-sensitive.

A THIRD NODE VERSION IS IN PLAY, unflagged until now: data/windows-v2/run.mjs:10 asserts process.versions.node === "26.8.1". So the Windows launcher demands 26.8.1, .nvmrc pins 24, and the machine runs 22.23.2. 26.8.1 satisfies >=24 so it is NOT a contract violation - but THE LAUNCHER REQUIRES A RUNTIME THE REPOSITORYS OWN VERSION FILE DOES NOT NAME, and CS-63 cannot be executed end-to-end on either of the other two.

FOLDED INTO THIS TICKETS SCOPE: a preflight that reads engines.node would also have caught the launchers stricter, undocumented pin - it is the same class of unenforced declaration, one layer further in.

DELIVERED AND PROVEN 2026-09-25, verified independently in this session. node:check is scripts/check-node-version.mjs and runs FIRST in gates:test, before anything else. Live output: "::error::Node v22.23.2 is below the required major 24. Install Node 24 (see .nvmrc) and re-run." with exit 1.

EVERY LOCAL RESULT REPORTED TONIGHT WOULD HAVE BEEN REFUSED BY THIS GATE. That is precisely the point, and it closes the finding that produced this ticket: a version floor that only one test enforces - and only incidentally, by using a version-sensitive flag - is not a floor.

gates:test NOW FAILS FOR EXACTLY ONE REASON: this machine is on Node 22. That is the CORRECT failure. It is an environment fact rather than a code defect, and on CI Node 24 the chain runs clean. Recorded that way so a red gates:test tonight is not mistaken for a broken repository.
RUNTIME CAVEAT: verified on Node v22.23.2, below the declared minimum of 24. Real, but not evidence about the supported runtime.

WORDING CORRECTED 2026-09-25 FROM "All applicable criteria met" TO THE COUNTED FORM. The distinction is not cosmetic: "ALL THREE CRITERIA MET" IS FALSIFIABLE BY COUNTING; "ALL APPLICABLE CRITERIA MET" CANNOT FAIL, because an unmet criterion can be reclassified as not-applicable without anyone editing a number. It is the same shape as \bsurfaced\b, DEFERRED and eol=crlf - a word anyone can write that silently changes how a claim is graded - except that this one sat in the STATUS FIELD OF TEN TICKETS, which is the field a promotion decision reads. That makes it the most consequential of the four, not the least.

AC2 EVIDENCED 2026-09-25, having been MET IN CODE BUT UNEVIDENCED - eleven entries described the preflight output, cause, cost and wording, and NOT ONE recorded the property AC2 is actually about. Verified at source: scripts/check-node-version.mjs:93-107 reads package.json and v2/package.json, FAILS if either omits engines.node ("the floor has to be written down somewhere"), and derives the major with majorFromRange(...) from the declared range. THE FLOOR IS PARSED, NOT HARDCODED, from three declaration sources including .nvmrc.

AND THE SUSPICION THAT POINTED AT A HARDCODED FLOOR WAS MISLEADING, checked rather than relayed: every literal 24 in that file is IN A COMMENT (lines 7, 70, 71, 185, 187), including the one documenting the N-2 fix. The comparison itself uses the parsed value. The reviewer hedged conditionally, and the check settled it the other way.

AC3 CLOSED 2026-09-28 with the required paired controls in one PowerShell invocation on Node v24.19.0: the simulated child process with Node v22.23.2 exited 1 and printed `Node v22.23.2 is below required major 24`; the normal node scripts/check-node-version.mjs then exited 0 and printed `PASS Node v24.19.0 satisfies floor 24, declared consistently in 7 places`. This proves both rejection and compliant acceptance against the declared floor.
