items.title: api() throws on a non-OK response without reading the body, leaving the fetch in-flight
items.userProblem: A deliberate 400/404 leaves the request permanently in-flight from the browser point of view, so error paths cannot be exercised honestly and a test harness has to compensate for it.
items.source: Filed 2026-09-25 from CS-51 ev[7], which disclosed it and said it needs its own ticket. CS-52 through CS-74 were checked and no such ticket existed - the same orphan pattern as CS-70.
acceptanceCriteria: api() consumes or cancels the response body before throwing, so a non-OK response does not leave the fetch in-flight
CS-51's test harness workaround is removed, and its AC3 browser assertions still pass without it - which is what proves the production path was fixed rather than the test re-tuned

Proven able to fail: a deliberate 400 and a deliberate 404 each complete rather than hanging, asserted on the request actually settling, with a successful request in the same test as the positive control
evidence: DISCLOSED BY CS-51, NOT PATCHED THERE, AND CORRECTLY SO: its evidence records that api.ts throws on a non-OK response WITHOUT READING THE BODY, measured as two never-finished /api/searches requests, and that it was "worked around locally in the test harness rather than changing api()". Confirmed at source in this session: v2/apps/web/src/lib/api.ts:106 tests response.ok and :119 throws, with the body read only on the 409 conflict path at :74.

WHY IT IS MORE THAN AN ORDINARY ORPHAN: CS-51s AC3 IS ACCEPTED, and its browser assertions pass PARTLY BECAUSE THE HARNESS COMPENSATES FOR THIS DEFECT. The error state does render, so AC3 is genuinely met - but the evidence for an accepted criterion is standing on a workaround for a live production-path defect, and that was invisible to anyone reading the verdict.

THE SECOND CRITERION IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE: removing the harness workaround and having CS-51s assertions still pass is what distinguishes "the production path was fixed" from "the test was re-tuned around it". Without that step this ticket could be closed by changing the test.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-28: v2/apps/web/src/lib/api.ts now cancels every unread non-409 response body before throwing. The 409 path still consumes its structured body through readConflict(). The CS-51 check-ui workaround that waited for response arrival is removed; its deep-link and foreign-owner error paths now use the normal request-settlement gate.

LOCAL FALSIFICATION 2026-09-28: api.test.ts drives real Response objects backed by ReadableStreams for deliberate 400 and 404 failures, asserts both promises reject with the matching ApiError, and asserts the stream cancel callback fires. The positive control remains the existing successful API path. v2 typecheck passes with all 16 test files. Hosted browser CI is still required before UAT.
items.currentStep: Release Manager - hosted CI run 36424073277 passed the browser/integration suites after non-OK response-body cancellation and removal of the CS-51 workaround.

items.title: Every v2 test file is excluded from type checking, so a test can silently assert against never
items.userProblem: v2 typecheck runs tsc -b over the project references, and all three referenced projects exclude src/**/*.test.ts. Eleven of eleven tracked v2 test files are therefore invisible to the type checker, so a type error inside a test is silent - including the error that makes a mock collapse to never and the assertions around it check nothing. Every "v2 typecheck exit 0" reported to date excluded the tests.
items.source: independent review, 2026-09-25, verified at source by the orchestrator
acceptanceCriteria: v2 typecheck covers every tracked v2 test file, proven by enumerating git ls-files against the resolved file list of the configs - not by sampling and not by the command merely exiting zero

The existing exclude stays in the emitting configs. Tests must not be emitted into dist, so the fix is an additional noEmit test project, not the deletion of the exclusion that keeps build output clean
The new project is proven able to fail: a deliberate type error introduced into a test file must make v2 typecheck exit non-zero, and removing it must make it pass again

The ai-provider.test.ts never collapse is fixed at the root - the mock response type must resolve to the real ServerResponse shape, and the fixture must supply every required field rather than being accepted because the type is never
A green v2 typecheck after this change is recorded with its real scope, and the earlier passes are marked in the record as having excluded tests
evidence: VERIFIED AT SOURCE BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, NOT RELAYED. v2/tsconfig.json has files:[] and references packages/core, apps/workers/search and apps/api. ALL THREE CARRY THE IDENTICAL exclude ["src/**/*.test.ts"]. v2 typecheck is `tsc -b && next typegen && tsc --noEmit --project apps/web/tsconfig.json`, so the only config that would include a test file is apps/web - AND APPS/WEB CONTAINS NO TEST FILES. The coverage gap is therefore total, not partial.

ELEVEN OF ELEVEN, ENUMERATED RATHER THAN SAMPLED: git ls-files reports 11 tracked v2 test files - 10 in packages/core (bull-queue, commands, database, file-storage, inference, market, profile, queue, resumes, runtime) and 1 in apps/workers/search (collect.test.ts). EVERY ONE SITS UNDER AN EXCLUDED src/** PATTERN. The count is a measurement, taken from the tracked file list.
AND apps/api CARRIES THE SAME EXCLUDE WITH ZERO TEST FILES TODAY, which means THE NEXT API TEST ANYONE WRITES IS BORN INVISIBLE. The gap is not only historical; it is waiting.

THE CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE IS THE WORST AVAILABLE INSTANCE. ai-provider.test.ts typed its mock response as Parameters<Parameters<typeof createServer>[0]>[1], WHICH SELECTS THE WRONG createServer OVERLOAD AND COLLAPSES TO never. Retyping it turned 30 ERRORS -> 0, and those errors exposed a fixture MISSING SEVEN REQUIRED FIELDS. The file was checking nothing.

RECORD THE PAIRING, BECAUSE IT IS THE SHARPEST ILLUSTRATION OF THIS ENTIRE RUN: that is A CHECK THAT COULD NOT FAIL, INSIDE THE TEST FILE FOR CS-48 - the ticket whose AC7 was itself about a data-minimisation test that could not fail. The test was painstakingly rebuilt to be falsifiable WHILE THE FILE CONTAINING IT WAS TYPE-INVISIBLE. Fixing a check inside an unchecked file is the same class of defect one level up, and nobody looked at the level up.

THE FIX IS NOT DELETING THE EXCLUDE, and the ticket must not be read that way. The exclusion is correct for the emitting projects: outDir is dist and tests must not ship. THE ROOT WORKSPACE ALREADY SOLVES THIS EXACTLY - root typecheck is `tsc --build --force && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json && tsc -p tsconfig.test.web.json`. V2 IS MISSING THE EQUIVALENT. The pattern to copy exists in this repository.

THIS CAVEAT NOW TRAVELS WITH EVERY TYPECHECK RESULT REPORTED TODAY, alongside the Node-22-against-a-floor-of-24 caveat: the full integration pass, and each per-slice pass, TYPE-CHECKED NO TEST FILE. That does not retract those results - the source did compile - but it bounds them, and an unbounded "typecheck exit 0" is the shape of claim that produced eight demotions.

DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED IN THE SAME BREATH: adding tsconfig.test.json needs an edit to v2/package.json, another session path. The probe config was DELETED RATHER THAN LEFT BEHIND, because a half-wired gate that nothing runs is worse than an absent one - it reads as coverage.

AND THE MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE HELD ON THE WAY IN, which is worth recording as much as the finding: a first probe reported "157 type errors", the probe was recognised as resolving overloads differently from the real build, AND THE NUMBER WAS REBUILT AND RE-MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS SPOKEN. A wrong count caught before it was uttered, by the session that produced it. Three counts today were not.

SWEEP OF ALL FIFTEEN NEVER-TYPE-CHECKED TEST FILES COMPLETED 2026-09-25, AND THE RESULT CUTS AGAINST THE REASONABLE PRIOR. The expectation was that files never seen by a type checker would be full of vacuous assertions. THEY ARE NOT. The paired-positive and non-empty-guard discipline is applied consistently - routes.size >= 30, jobs.length === 25, bodies.length === 1, ids.length >= 6, elapsed.length === 5, the [200, 200, 429] multiset. ONE FLAW WAS FOUND AND IT IS A TAUTOLOGY, NOT A MISSING GUARD: somebody wrote a guard and it could not fail.

SO THE ABSENCE OF TYPE CHECKING DID NOT PRODUCE SLOPPY TESTS, AND THAT MUST BE STATED PLAINLY ON THIS TICKET RATHER THAN LEFT AS AN IMPLIED WORRY. Filing a P1 about missing type coverage invites the reader to assume the uncovered code is bad; here it is not, and saying so is part of reporting the finding honestly.

BUT THIS SHARPENS THE CASE FOR CLOSING THE GAP RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT, AND IS THE REASON THE PRIORITY STAYS P1: the type checker caught a never collapse THAT MADE AN ENTIRE FILE VACUOUS, AND NO AMOUNT OF ASSERTION DISCIPLINE WOULD HAVE SURFACED IT. The two defences cover DIFFERENT failures. GOOD ASSERTIONS CANNOT DETECT THAT THE TYPE THEY ASSERT AGAINST HAS COLLAPSED; A TYPE CHECKER CANNOT DETECT A TAUTOLOGY. Neither substitutes for the other - the same non-substitution argument CS-65 made about its two halves.

THE FIVE TS7022 SITES ARE NOT VACUOUS ASSERTIONS AND MUST NOT BE COUNTED AS SUCH - verified at database.test.ts:1108-1142. first, second and firstResult collapse to any through circular inference: each is assigned from a ternary returning either auth.revokeOtherSessions(...) or auth.login(...), then pushed into an operations array whose own type is inferred from them. THAT IS A TYPE-HYGIENE DEFECT, NOT A CORRECTNESS ONE.

THE TEST IS A GENUINE CONCURRENCY PROOF AND THE any DOES NOT WEAKEN IT: it installs a BEFORE DELETE/INSERT trigger, takes advisory lock 7654322, starts a revoke and a login IN BOTH ORDERS, then WAITS ON pg_locks AND pg_blocking_pids TO CONFIRM REAL CONTENTION rather than assuming it, releases the lock, and asserts the outcome. The contention is observed, not hoped for.

EVERY ASSERTION THERE IS A RUNTIME ASSERTION: assert.equal(... , true) at :1134, assert.equal(typeof loginToken, "string") at :1135, assert.equal(Boolean(await auth.session(loginToken)), firstOperation === "revoke") at :1136-1139, assert.ok(await auth.session(activeToken)) at :1140, plus TWO MORE PAST THE REPORTED RANGE - assert.ok(await auth.session(other)) at :1141 AND THE NEGATIVE assert.equal(await auth.session(older), null) AT :1142. assert.* COMPARES ACTUAL VALUES AND DOES NOT CONSULT THE STATIC TYPE.

AND :1135 IS THE TELL: assert.equal(typeof loginToken, "string") IS EXACTLY THE ASSERTION SOMEBODY WRITES WHEN THEY CANNOT LEAN ON THE TYPE. The test was already compensating at runtime for what the compiler was not giving it, which is evidence the author knew and covered it rather than evidence of neglect.

THE DISTINCTION IS THE THING WORTH KEEPING, AND IT DECIDES HOW THE WHOLE 96 IS READ. A never COLLAPSE IN A MOCK TYPE MAKES ASSERTIONS VACUOUS, because the mock shape is never validated against anything - the test asserts about an object that satisfies every constraint by construction. AN any COLLAPSE IN A VALUE UNDER TEST DOES NOT, because the assertions still execute against the real value at runtime. IT REMOVES PROTECTION; IT DOES NOT REMOVE THE CHECK. Same diagnostic family, opposite consequence.

SO ai-provider.test.ts WAS THE FIRST KIND - genuinely asserting nothing, and retyping it surfaced a fixture missing seven required fields. THESE FIVE ARE THE SECOND KIND. FIX FOR HYGIENE, NOT FOR CORRECTNESS: one annotation on operations so the inference terminates. Recording them as "three vacuous assertions in the file holding CS-48 AC10" WOULD PUT A FALSE FINDING NEXT TO A REAL ONE, which is the failure mode that makes a real finding easy to dismiss.

THE 96 BROKEN DOWN, so the raw number does not acquire authority it has not earned: ~76 TS2345 from ONE dist-vs-src resolution misconfiguration - fix the config and RE-COUNT rather than reporting 76 as 76 findings; 9 TS2550 which is the Promise.withResolvers lib-target DECISION, to be recorded either way rather than silently retargeted; 5 TS7022 hygiene with sound assertions; 6 unexamined.

THE HONEST HEADLINE: THE V2 TEST SUITE HAD NEVER BEEN TYPE-CHECKED, AND WHEN IT WAS, IT PRODUCED ONE REAL VACUITY (ai-provider.test.ts never), ONE CONFIG PROBLEM, ONE LIBRARY DECISION AND SOME HYGIENE. That is a far better outcome than the raw number suggested, and it agrees with the independent loop-assertion sweep. THE TESTS ARE IN GOOD SHAPE; THE TOOLING AROUND THEM WAS NOT - and those are different problems with different owners.

IMPLEMENTATION LANDED 2026-09-25. v2/tsconfig.test.json exists with noEmit true, composite false and a paths mapping for @careerscope/core, and v2 typecheck now chains `npm run typecheck:tests` (node scripts/check-test-types.mjs). AC2 IS MET AS WRITTEN: the emitting configs keep their exclude, so tests still never reach dist - the fix ADDS a project rather than deleting the exclusion, which was the explicit requirement.

AC1 CHECKPOINT MEASUREMENT FROM 2026-09-25, NOW SUPERSEDED BY THE CLOSURE EVIDENCE BELOW: the include was ["packages/*/src/**/*.test.ts", "apps/api/src/**/*.test.ts", "scripts/**/*.test.ts"], and enumerating git ls-files against those patterns gave 10 COVERED, 1 MISSED - v2/apps/workers/search/src/collect.test.ts. AC1 required every tracked V2 test file, so the checkpoint count was 10 of 11. The measurement carried its own falsification: a deliberately bogus include pattern was checked to match zero files, so a silently-empty pattern set could not have produced this result.

THE EXCLUSION IS DELIBERATE AND ITS REASON IS RECORDED IN THE CONFIG ITSELF - "apps/workers is deliberately absent: its test files have known issues and ownership of that path is unconfirmed, so widening scope there would be reaching into someone else is work. That is a recorded gap, not an oversight." THAT IS THE RIGHT CALL AND THE RIGHT PLACE TO RECORD IT. It does not make the criterion met.

SO THIS IS THE OPEN-BY-DECISION SHAPE AGAIN, THE SECOND TODAY AFTER CS-52 AC4, AND IT GETS THE SAME TREATMENT: the unlock is either to extend the include once workers ownership is confirmed, or TO AMEND AC1 SO THE EXCLUSION IS WRITTEN INTO THE CRITERION RATHER THAN LIVING ONLY IN a config comment. Amending it silently would be the reclassification move. Until one of those happens the count is 4 of 5, not 5 of 5.

AND THE CONFIG CARRIES BOTH CAVEATS AT THE POINT OF CAUSE, which is why this will survive its next reader: the never-collapse that motivated the project is described in full, and the paths mapping records that the src/dist split is NOT purely a type artifact - at runtime tsx honours the exports map so the two Database classes are genuinely different, VERIFIED BY PROBE, and the compiler therefore no longer flags database.test.ts:1617/1620, which compares ResumeConflict (src) against Conflict (dist) deliberately. THAT BOUNDARY NOW RESTS ON ITS RUNTIME ASSERTION ALONE, with its one dependant named.

GATE STATUS, AND IT MUST BE STATED IN THESE WORDS BECAUSE THE NAIVE READING IS THE OPPOSITE: `v2 typecheck` IS NOW EXIT 1, AND NOTHING BROKE. `tsc -b` over the production project references is STILL EXIT 0 - the application compiles exactly as it did all evening. The gate went red because it BECAME ABLE TO SEE FILES IT WAS PREVIOUSLY BLIND TO. A reader comparing this run to the last one would otherwise conclude a regression landed.

THIRD GATE TONIGHT TO GO DELIBERATELY RED, and the pattern is worth naming: node:check on Node 22, eol:check on the unrenormalised files, and now the test typecheck. EVERY ONE WENT RED BY BECOMING ABLE TO FAIL. A red that appears the moment a check starts looking is the opposite of a regression, and a project that cannot tell those apart will revert its own improvements.

DO NOT RECORD "v2 typecheck: exit 0" ANYWHERE FROM THIS POINT. THE HONEST LINE IS: production code compiles and lints clean, unit suites 55/55 with 0 skipped, AND THE TEST-TYPECHECK GATE IS NEWLY WIRED AND REPORTING 56 DIAGNOSTICS ACROSS THREE KNOWN CAUSES. It will stay exit 1 until CS-77 and the library-target decision land.

NOTHING IN THE 56 IS A DEFECT IN SHIPPED CODE - they are one type-modelling error at a call boundary (36), one library-version decision (9), test hygiene (5) and 6 unexamined, ALL IN FILES THAT DO NOT REACH dist. That bounds the release impact precisely, and it is a different statement from "the gate is green".

BOUNDED TYPECHECK EVIDENCE - RE-WORDED FROM "PROVISIONAL" 2026-09-25, AND THE VERB CHANGE IS THE POINT. This ticket cites a BARE `tsc -b`, which is incremental and was observed exiting 0 while a genuine production error existed (collect.ts TS2353) because a stale .tsbuildinfo declared the project up to date. THAT DOES NOT RETRACT THE RESULT AND DOES NOT MAKE IT SUSPECT: the command ran, it reported truthfully on what it examined, and the source it examined did compile. IT BOUNDS THE RESULT. The run was NARROWER THAN THE CLAIM IT WAS QUOTED FOR - it is evidence that the projects tsc considered up to date had no new errors, not evidence that the tree is clean. "PROVISIONAL" WAS THE WRONG WORD BECAUSE IT IMPLIES THE RESULT MIGHT BE FALSE. It was not false; it was narrow. Re-verify the wider claim with `tsc -b --force` or a cleared .tsbuildinfo - and note that v2 typecheck now begins with --force, so the npm script no longer has this bound. The original lines are deliberately kept: they record what was actually run. NOTHING IS DEMOTED FOR THIS.

CHAIN VERIFIED GREEN INDEPENDENTLY 2026-09-26: npm run typecheck in v2 exits 0 and prints "PASS 15 v2 test files type-check clean (no emit)". The chain now begins with tsc -b --force, so the stale-incremental bound recorded earlier no longer applies to the npm script.

AND MY OWN EARLIER AC1 MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG - 10 OF 11 WAS A CONFIDENT WRONG TOTAL. IT USED `git ls-files` ALONE, WHICH CANNOT SEE UNTRACKED FILES, ON A TREE WHERE 260 FILES ARE UNTRACKED (CS-80). The real universe is 17 v2 test files: 11 tracked and 6 UNTRACKED - api.test.ts, ai-provider.test.ts and four under v2/scripts. I filed CS-80 about untracked files having no baseline AND THEN TOOK A MEASUREMENT THAT COULD NOT SEE THEM.

CORRECTED COUNT: 15 of 17 are matched by tsconfig.test.json include patterns. THE TWO MISSES ARE NOT BOTH GAPS. v2/apps/web/src/lib/api.test.ts IS type-checked - by a DIFFERENT LINK in the same chain, since apps/web/tsconfig.json includes **/*.ts with only node_modules excluded and the chain runs tsc --noEmit --project apps/web/tsconfig.json. CHECKING ONE CONFIG IN ISOLATION IS THE SAME FRAGMENT ERROR AS READING ONE LINE WITHOUT ITS NEIGHBOURS, and it is the sixth sibling-shape instance applied to my own check.

SO THE GENUINE COVERAGE IS 16 OF 17 AND THE ONLY REAL GAP IS v2/apps/workers/search/src/collect.test.ts, which is tracked, deliberately excluded, and documented in the config as "a recorded gap, not an oversight". AC1 SAYS EVERY TRACKED V2 TEST FILE, SO IT REMAINS UNMET - but by one file for a stated reason, not by two for unknown ones.

THE MEASUREMENT ITSELF ALSO NEEDED TWO REPAIRS BEFORE IT COULD BE TRUSTED, BOTH RECORDED BECAUSE THEY ARE THE SAME CLASS THIS TICKET EXISTS TO CLOSE: a naive comment-stripping regex /\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//  STRIPPED FROM THE "/*" INSIDE THE GLOB "**/*.ts", corrupting the config it was reading - comment removal must be string-aware or it damages the very file it parses. And the include-pattern matcher was falsified with a deliberately bogus pattern first, so 15 means 15 rather than whatever the regex happened to catch.
THE OUTSTANDING NUMBER FROM THIS TICKET IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS BETTER THAN THE QUESTION: 0 OF 13 ASSERTIONS WERE DISABLED. 1 OF 13 WAS A REAL DEFECT OF A DIFFERENT KIND.

AND IT WAS TESTED RATHER THAN INFERRED FROM A GREEN SUITE, which is what makes it evidence: the API was mutated from 401 to 403 and the suite re-run, producing AssertionError: 403 !== 401. THE ASSERTIONS WERE LIVE ALL ALONG WHILE THE TYPES AROUND THEM WERE UNCHECKED. Mechanism: tsx strips types without checking them, so an any DISABLES TYPE CHECKING, NOT EXECUTION - which is the precise reason the never collapse was harmless at runtime and catastrophic to confidence.

SITE 11 IS THE EXCEPTION AND BELONGS IN THE RECORD: the synthetic provider yielded a job MISSING hasFullDescription, so it was never a valid RawJob. NOT A DISABLED ASSERTION - A FIXTURE THAT DID NOT MATCH THE PRODUCTION SHAPE, invisible until v2 tests were type-checked for the first time. The field is load-bearing at collect.ts:121 (whether to fetch detail) and normalize.ts:83 and :463 (description handling and dedup ranking), so the fixture was exercising a path the real shape would never take.

A QUESTION ANSWERED "NONE, BUT HERE IS WHAT I FOUND INSTEAD" IS WORTH MORE THAN ONE ANSWERED WITH A NUMBER. The question asked how many assertions were disabled; the honest answer was none, plus one defect of a class nobody had asked about.

AC1 COVERAGE CLOSED 2026-09-28: v2/tsconfig.test.json now explicitly includes apps/workers/search/src/**/*.test.ts. collect.ts was corrected to accept CreateSearchInput (the caller-facing schema input), and the two synthetic RawJob fixtures now provide required hasFullDescription. npm --prefix v2 run typecheck:tests passes with 16 test files; the emitting project excludes remain unchanged. apps/web remains covered by its own Next tsconfig, so the only separate test project is intentionally outside this config.

AC3 MUTATION PROVEN 2026-09-28: adding `const cs76MutationProof: number = 'deliberate-type-error'` to collect.test.ts made npm --prefix v2 run typecheck:tests fail with TS2322 in that test file; removing the mutation restored PASS 16 v2 test files. The noEmit checker is therefore able to fail on a test-only type defect, not merely report a green empty or dependency-only set.

QA COMPLETED 2026-09-28: exact-revision hosted CI run 36398473010 attempt 2 passed the forced V2 production and test typecheck, reporting 16 V2 test files type-check clean with no emit, and the full static/build, integration, browser, axe, backfill and recovery matrix completed green on commit 46ba008fdd35c8bf3d99b52cfc8c40ea00b2ba70.

items.title: createSearch is typed against parsed output but hashes whatever the caller passes, so its idempotency hash depends on whether the caller parsed first
items.userProblem: CreateSearch is z.infer (the OUTPUT type) while the function neither parses nor requires parsed input, and requestHash is computed over the caller-supplied object. Callers that parse and callers that pass a literal produce different hashes for a logically identical request, and that hash is what decides IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
items.source: type-check sweep after CS-76, verified at source by the orchestrator
acceptanceCriteria: createSearch accepts unparsed input at its type boundary without any caller having to construct the parsed shape by hand, and the 36 existing call sites compile unchanged

The idempotency request hash is computed over the NORMALISED request, so two logically identical calls hash identically regardless of whether the caller parsed first, whether origin was supplied, and in what order sources were given

Proven by a test that passes the same logical request twice under one idempotency key - once as a literal and once pre-parsed - and asserts NO IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED conflict; falsified by reverting the normalisation and observing the conflict appear
No test fixture is edited to add origin or to pre-sort sources in order to satisfy the signature
evidence: VERIFIED AT SOURCE. commands.ts:54 exports CreateSearch = z.infer<typeof createSearchSchema> - THE OUTPUT TYPE. database.ts:35 takes request: CreateSearch AND NEVER PARSES IT. So the declared parameter is the PARSED shape while the function body treats the value as whatever arrived.

THAT IS WHY 36 TYPE ERRORS REMAINED AFTER THE RESOLUTION FIX: the tests pass { query, sources } and the parameter demands origin, which a Zod .default() makes OPTIONAL ON INPUT AND REQUIRED ON OUTPUT. 32 in database.test.ts, 2 in profile.test.ts, 1 each in bull-queue.test.ts and resumes.test.ts. THE TESTS ARE CORRECT AND THE SIGNATURE IS WRONG. Adding origin to 36 fixtures would be EDITING CORRECT TESTS TO SATISFY A WRONG SIGNATURE.

BUT z.input ALONE IS NOT THE FIX, AND THIS IS THE PART THE TYPE ERROR HIDES. database.ts:36 computes requestHash = sha256(JSON.stringify(request)) OVER THE CALLER-SUPPLIED OBJECT, and :80 compares it - if (!existing || existing.requestHash !== requestHash) - TO DECIDE IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. So the hash is a function of CALLER-SIDE FORMATTING, not of the request.

AND THE TWO REAL CALLERS ARE ON OPPOSITE SIDES OF THAT LINE. app.ts:656 passes createSearchSchema.parse(request.body) - origin present, sources SORTED by the schema .transform. run-scheduled-discovery.ts:95 passes an OBJECT LITERAL. Relaxing the type to z.input would make passing unparsed input legitimate everywhere, at which point MISSING origin OR UNSORTED sources SILENTLY CHANGE THE HASH.

CONSEQUENCE IF LEFT AS z.input: a retry under the same idempotency key that parses when the original did not - or supplies sources in a different order - HASHES DIFFERENTLY AND RAISES A SPURIOUS IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED 409. That is CS-35 own named path, so the failure would surface as a confusing but correctly-coded conflict rather than as a type error.

CORRECT FIX: accept z.input<typeof createSearchSchema> at the boundary AND PARSE INSIDE createSearch, hashing the PARSED value. That makes the type honest about what callers may pass, makes the hash independent of caller formatting, and needs no fixture edits. app.ts would then parse twice, which is harmless - .default and the sort .transform are both idempotent - though the route parse could be dropped once the domain owns it.

THE ROOT IS THE SAME ONE Zod .default() THAT PRODUCED CS-42 DESIGN DEFECT HOURS EARLIER: the field the design forbade was silently injected on parse. HERE THE SAME CONSTRUCT PRODUCED A SIGNATURE THAT HAS BEEN REJECTING EVERY VALID TEST CALL SINCE IT WAS WRITTEN - INVISIBLE, BECAUSE NO V2 TEST FILE WAS TYPE-CHECKED. One .default(), two unrelated defects, neither found by the other route.

THIS TICKET NOW BLOCKS A GATE RATHER THAN SITTING BEHIND ONE: its 36 diagnostics are the largest share of the 56 keeping `v2 typecheck` at exit 1 since the test project was wired. That raises its practical urgency without changing its severity - the defect is a type-modelling error in a signature, not a fault in shipped behaviour, and it should not be re-graded upward merely because it is now visible.

AND THE LIFETIME OF THE DEFECT IS THE POINT WORTH KEEPING: createSearch signature HAS BEEN REJECTING EVERY VALID CALL IN THE TEST SUITE SINCE IT WAS WRITTEN, and nobody knew, because no v2 test file was type-checked. A TYPE-MODELLING DEFECT THAT EXISTED FOR THE ENTIRE LIFE OF THE PROJECT AND WAS INVISIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION.

LINKED TO CS-42 DELIBERATELY: the same origin: z.enum([...]).optional().default("manual") produced BOTH this signature defect AND the design defect where the field the design forbade was silently stored. ONE ZOD DEFAULT, TWO DEFECTS, FOUND FOUR HOURS APART BY TWO COMPLETELY DIFFERENT ROUTES - a security design review and a build-configuration fix. NEITHER ROUTE WOULD HAVE FOUND THE OTHER. That is the clearest evidence in this run that a single modelling choice propagates further than the ticket that introduces it.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-25 BY THE OWNING SESSION. commands.ts exports CreateSearchInput = z.input<typeof createSearchSchema> with the input/output distinction stated precisely in a comment. database.ts:35 takes CreateSearchInput; database.ts:62 is const request = createSearchSchema.parse(input); and :63 hashes THAT value. So the stored request always carries origin, sources is sorted by the .transform before hashing, and the idempotency hash no longer depends on caller-side formatting. AC1 and AC2 appear satisfied by inspection; AC3 falsification is not yet recorded.

A NEAR-MISS ON THIS TICKET IS RECORDED IN FULL BECAUSE IT NEARLY BECAME A P1 AGAINST ANOTHER SESSION. AT 18:12 THIS FILE READ: const request = input as CreateSearchInput as ReturnType<typeof createSearchSchema.parse>; - A DOUBLE TYPE ASSERTION - directly beneath a comment saying "PARSED HERE" and a twenty-line justification of why canonicalising matters. A finding was written stating that the comment documented a fix the code did not perform, that the cast deleted the $type<CreateSearch>() compile guard, and that the exact failure the comment described was now unguarded.

IT WAS NEVER FILED, BECAUSE THE RECORDING SCRIPT ASSERTED THE DEFECT WAS STILL PRESENT BEFORE WRITING AND IT WAS NOT. The file had been written again at 18:14:43 with the real parse. I HAD READ A FILE MID-EDIT AND ALMOST REPORTED A TWO-MINUTE INTERMEDIATE STATE AS A DEFECT IN SOMEBODY ELSE WORK.

THE RULE ALREADY EXISTED IN AGENT-SETUP AND I STILL WALKED INTO IT: "with concurrent writers, a bad read is more likelier than a bad file." IT WAS RECORDED ABOUT backlog.json AND NOT GENERALISED TO SOURCE FILES OWNED BY OTHER SESSIONS - which is the same partial application defect as guarding one site and not its sibling. A RULE LEARNED ON ONE FILE TYPE IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY APPLIED TO ANOTHER.

AND THE NEAR-MISS HAD AN AGGRAVATING FEATURE WORTH KEEPING: THE INTERMEDIATE STATE WAS MAXIMALLY CONVINCING. A cast beneath a thorough, technically correct comment that pre-empts the objection is more persuasive than a bare mistake - a reviewer reading top-down is MORE likely to be fooled, not less. The finding would have been articulate, specific, and about a file that had already been fixed.

CONSEQUENCE ADOPTED: DO NOT REPORT A DEFECT IN ANOTHER SESSION PATH FROM A SINGLE READ. Re-read immediately before recording, compare mtime, and prefer asking the owner over filing. The precondition guard is what enforced this - FOURTH TIME TODAY A PRECONDITION HAS RESCUED A CONCLUSION, AND THE SECOND TIME THE THING IT CAUGHT WAS MINE.

MEASUREMENT DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN: a test-typecheck run during this window reported 74 diagnostics including 29 TS2584 and 26 TS2304 - "cannot find name" errors that indicate the types/lib configuration was itself mid-edit. THAT NUMBER IS NOT RECORDED AS A RESULT. Counting a tree while another writer is inside it produces noise, and a noisy number that looks precise is worse than no number.

A REAL BEHAVIOURAL BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED IN PASSING, AND IT IS NOT A TYPING CONCERN: sources carries .transform(sort), so BEFORE THE PARSE MOVED INSIDE, AN UNSORTED AND A SORTED SPELLING OF THE SAME REQUEST HASHED DIFFERENTLY AND COLLIDED AS A FALSE IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. A caller passing ["himalayas","remoteok"] instead of ["remoteok","himalayas"] would have been told their request already completed with different details. Invisible for the same reason as everything else here - the callers that would expose it are tests, and no v2 test file was type-checked.

THE ORCHESTRATOR PRESCRIPTION FOR THIS TICKET WAS HALF-RIGHT AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH. It said "type the parameter as z.input - one type, not 36 call sites." APPLIED IN ISOLATION THAT MOVES THE ERROR INTO PRODUCTION CODE - database.ts(63,10) TS2769 - because searches.request is $type<CreateSearch>(), the OUTPUT type. WIDENING THE PARAMETER ALONE WOULD PERSIST A RUN WITH NO origin, trading a type error in tests for a DATA DEFECT IN STORAGE, with the type checker then silent about it.

SO THE FIX NEEDED BOTH HALVES - widened parameter AND the parse moved inside - for two independent load-bearing reasons, of which the prescription had identified only the first: request IS STORED and must always carry origin; and requestHash DRIVES IDEMPOTENCY over a value carrying .transform(sort).

SHIPPABILITY ARGUMENT RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS WHAT MAKES THIS SAFE RATHER THAN MERELY CORRECT: re-parsing an already-parsed request is a FIXED POINT - trim, sort and the default are each idempotent - so the API path is unchanged and NO EXISTING HASH MOVES. No test fixture was edited, which was the explicit requirement.

SIBLING SURVEY CAME BACK A CLEAN BOUNDED NEGATIVE: 37 z.infer types enumerated and every parameter position using them checked. INPUT DIFFERS FROM OUTPUT IN EXACTLY TWO CORE SCHEMAS - jobs.ts:5, WHICH ALREADY EXPORTS CollectedJobInput = z.input<...> AND ALREADY USES IT for its caller-facing parameter, and commands.ts, the one that was wrong. storage.ts and resumes.ts have no .default/.transform/.coerce so z.infer is correct there; LeadRepository and ProfileRepository.save take input: unknown and parse inside, the strictest form of all. createSearch WAS THE ONLY INSTANCE.

AND THE CORRECT PATTERN WAS ALREADY IN THE CODEBASE ONE FILE AWAY. THIRD TIME TODAY THE FIX ALREADY EXISTED NEARBY - after the root tsconfig.test.json for CS-76, and jobs.ts here. BEFORE DESIGNING A FIX, LOOK FOR THE SIBLING THAT ALREADY SOLVED IT.

ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED, AND NOT BY ME: the drop is 56 -> 24 from this fix (-32) and 24 -> 15 from another session adding lib: ["ES2024","DOM"] at 18:17:14. The implementing session noticed that write had landed BETWEEN ITS OWN TWO MEASUREMENTS AND DECLINED THE CREDIT. The orchestrator had the same two numbers and had already written -41 to review.txt. A DELTA BETWEEN TWO MEASUREMENTS IS NOT EVIDENCE OF A CAUSE WHEN ANOTHER WRITER TOUCHED THE TREE BETWEEN THEM.

INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED 2026-09-25 AND THE ORDERING WAS ASSERTED RATHER THAN EYEBALLED: createSearchSchema.parse(input) is at database.ts:62 and the sha256 of JSON.stringify(request) at :63, with the check written to FAIL if the parse line number were not strictly less than the hash line number. So the hash is computed from the canonicalised form - sorted sources, trimmed query, defaulted origin - and TWO SPELLINGS OF THE SAME REQUEST NOW PRODUCE ONE HASH. The false IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED is closed, not merely described.

PRODUCTION VERIFIED BECAUSE THIS TOUCHED A DEPLOYED-PATH FILE, which the test-typecheck number alone would not have covered: tsc -b exit 0, measured with spawnSync OUTSIDE POWERSHELL after $LASTEXITCODE through the npm.cmd shim produced a false red earlier today. Unit suites 55/55 with 0 skipped and lint clean were reported by the implementing session.

THE BEST ARTEFACT OF THE RUN IS A SENTENCE IN THAT COMMENT BLOCK: "Widening the parameter alone is NOT sufficient, AND I CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED." It is the rule this entire run discovered, WRITTEN INTO THE CODE BY THE SESSION THAT APPLIED IT, AT THE MOMENT IT APPLIED IT - not into a retrospective. Anyone who later tries the simpler fix finds the reason it fails, in the file, BEFORE they try it. A retrospective is read by people who already know; a comment is read by the person about to make the mistake.

BOUNDED TYPECHECK EVIDENCE - RE-WORDED FROM "PROVISIONAL" 2026-09-25, AND THE VERB CHANGE IS THE POINT. This ticket cites a BARE `tsc -b`, which is incremental and was observed exiting 0 while a genuine production error existed (collect.ts TS2353) because a stale .tsbuildinfo declared the project up to date. THAT DOES NOT RETRACT THE RESULT AND DOES NOT MAKE IT SUSPECT: the command ran, it reported truthfully on what it examined, and the source it examined did compile. IT BOUNDS THE RESULT. The run was NARROWER THAN THE CLAIM IT WAS QUOTED FOR - it is evidence that the projects tsc considered up to date had no new errors, not evidence that the tree is clean. "PROVISIONAL" WAS THE WRONG WORD BECAUSE IT IMPLIES THE RESULT MIGHT BE FALSE. It was not false; it was narrow. Re-verify the wider claim with `tsc -b --force` or a cleared .tsbuildinfo - and note that v2 typecheck now begins with --force, so the npm script no longer has this bound. The original lines are deliberately kept: they record what was actually run. NOTHING IS DEMOTED FOR THIS.

AC3 TEST STRENGTHENED 2026-09-28: the canonicalisation integration test now passes the first call as an unparsed literal and the retry as a schema-preparsed value under the same idempotency key, while retaining the paired genuinely-different conflict control. Node 24 typecheck passes. The service-backed integration run could not complete locally because the Redis dependency was unavailable and the queue test remained retrying; no local integration pass is claimed. Hosted CI remains required for promotion.

AC3 FALSIFICATION AND QA COMPLETED 2026-09-28: isolated hosted run 36397888648 changed only requestHash back to JSON.stringify(input). The service-backed canonicalisation test failed on its literal-versus-pre-parsed retry with Conflict code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED at database.test.ts:4555, while recovery, the image build and the main static job passed. The temporary verification branch was deleted after evidence capture and its managed worktree archived. items.title: V2 minimises the matching profile to the three fields V1 matcher reads, and nothing enforces that correspondence - the failure mode is a silently wrong score
items.userProblem: v2/packages/core declares a file: dependency on the V1 shared and resume packages, and V2 passes its MatchingProfile into V1 buildCandidateContext, which takes MatchableProfile. V2 deliberately narrows application to expectedCtc, yearsOfExperience and willingToRelocate - exactly the three the matcher reads. The correspondence is maintained by convention alone. The day context.ts reads a fourth field it will receive undefined inside deterministic scoring, which is a wrong match score rather than an error.
items.source: v2 test typecheck after CS-76, traced to source by the orchestrator
acceptanceCriteria: A fourth application field read by the matcher fails to compile against what V2 supplies, rather than arriving as undefined inside deterministic scoring
V2 narrowing is PRESERVED, not widened to the full ApplicationDetails - the minimisation is deliberate and must not be discarded to satisfy a type checker
The boundary is not silenced with a cast or an any at the call site - the fix must preserve the signal that the two shapes must agree
The V1/V2 dependency direction and the types that cross it are stated in the architecture record, since a file: dependency from V2 into V1 packages is currently a fact only package.json carries
Proven by mutation: making the matcher read a fourth application field must fail v2 typecheck, and reverting it must make it pass again
evidence: NOT A LIVE BUG, AND THE REASON MAKES IT A BETTER FINDING RATHER THAN A LESSER ONE. packages/matching/src/context.ts READS EXACTLY THREE application FIELDS - yearsOfExperience (:37), willingToRelocate (:41), expectedCtc (:42) - VERIFIED BY ENUMERATING EVERY application.<field> ACCESS IN THE FILE AND ASSERTING THE SET EQUALS THOSE THREE. V2 Pick SUPPLIES EXACTLY THOSE THREE. At runtime buildCandidateContext receives every field it consumes.

THE TWO TYPES LIVE IN DIFFERENT WORKSPACES AND THE DEPENDENCY IS DELIBERATE AND DECLARED: MatchableProfile at packages/shared/src/types.ts:160 (V1), MatchingProfile at v2/packages/core/src/profile.ts:60 (V2), and v2/packages/core/package.json declares "@job-radar/shared": "file:../../../packages/shared" in dependencies with "@job-radar/matching" in devDependencies. ARCHITECTED REUSE, NOT AN ACCIDENTAL IMPORT.

THE STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE IS EXACTLY ONE FIELD, MEASURED RATHER THAN DESCRIBED. candidate is Pick<..., "location"> on both; preferences is the full type on both; derived is DerivedResume | null on both. ONLY application DIFFERS, AND V2 NARROWS IT: the full ApplicationDetails in V1, Pick<..., "expectedCtc" | "yearsOfExperience" | "willingToRelocate"> in V2.

V2 NARROWING IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT - IT IS DELIBERATE DATA MINIMISATION, consistent with the same discipline applied to resumes, logging and evidence text throughout this codebase. Its own doc comment says so: the profile is "snapshotted onto the search at creation time... never re-fetched mid-run, so a run scoring stays consistent even if the owner uploads a new resume while it is in flight."

SO THE DEFECT IS NOT THAT THE TYPES DIFFER. IT IS THAT A DELIBERATE MINIMISATION DEPENDS ON AN UNENFORCED AGREEMENT WITH A CONSUMER IN ANOTHER WORKSPACE. THE THREE FIELD NAMES ARE THE WHOLE CONTRACT, which is why they are written into this ticket rather than left to be re-derived.

AND THE FAILURE MODE IS THE PART THAT SETS THE PRIORITY: THE DAY context.ts READS A FOURTH application FIELD, V2 Pick WILL NOT SUPPLY IT, AND THE VALUE ARRIVES AS undefined INSIDE DETERMINISTIC SCORING. NOT A CRASH - A SILENTLY WRONG MATCH SCORE. That is materially worse than a crash, and it is exactly the class this project keeps finding: A CORRECTNESS PROPERTY MAINTAINED BY CONVENTION, INVISIBLE UNTIL IT IS VIOLATED.

DO NOT WIDEN V2 TO THE FULL ApplicationDetails - that would discard a deliberate minimisation to satisfy a type checker and hand the matcher fields it has no business receiving. DO NOT SILENCE IT WITH "as MatchableProfile" either: that removes the only signal the shapes have diverged, permanently, IN THE ONE PLACE THE BOUNDARY IS EXERCISED.

CORRECT DIRECTION: MAKE THE DEPENDENCY EXPLICIT THE WAY IT ACTUALLY RUNS - have the matcher declare its own minimal input type that V2 satisfies structurally, which is the same edit as narrowing MatchableProfile.application to those three fields. It removes both diagnostics, preserves the minimisation, AND IMPROVES V1 BY NO LONGER DEMANDING DATA IT DOES NOT USE. Data minimisation expressed in the type system.

THE ERROR WE ARE LOOKING AT IS THE MECHANISM WORKING, THE FIRST TIME IT HAS EVER BEEN ABLE TO SPEAK. The test crossing this boundary lives in a file that had never been type-checked until CS-76 was wired an hour earlier. A change to either side would not have been flagged against the other at any point in the project history.

SAME SHAPE AS THE Database-from-dist VERSUS Database-from-src CAVEAT recorded earlier today - TWO DECLARATIONS OF ONE CONCEPT KEPT IN AGREEMENT BY NOTHING BUT CONVENTION. That one was found by probe and written down with its dependent named; this one gets the same treatment, and unlike that one it has a fix rather than only a caveat.

INCIDENTAL BUT WORTH KEEPING, from the same test comment: this path was "never exercised before because collect.ts hardcoded derived: null regardless of what searchHandler passed in." THE PATH HAD BEEN DEAD, AND THIS TEST IS WHAT BROUGHT IT UNDER COVERAGE - which is also why the mismatch had never been observed.

PAIR THIS WITH A SECOND, INDEPENDENT INSTANCE OF THE SAME PRINCIPLE WHEN THE ARCHITECTURE RECORD IS WRITTEN (AC3). database.ts:73-74 records that the resume-snapshot SQL "projects only the `derived` sub-key of the parsed JSONB document - the raw resume text in `parsed.text` never leaves Postgres for this query, let alone this process." THAT IS THE SAME TAKE-ONLY-WHAT-THIS-OPERATION-NEEDS DISCIPLINE AS V2 THREE-FIELD MatchingProfile PICK, STATED AT THE STORAGE LAYER INSTEAD OF THE TYPE LAYER.

AND THE PAIRING IS THE ARGUMENT, NOT DECORATION: the principle is CLEARLY HELD ACROSS LAYERS AND ITS ENFORCEMENT IS UNEVEN. The SQL projection enforces itself - the text is not selected, so it cannot leak. The MatchingProfile pick DOES NOT - it depends on an unenforced agreement with a consumer in another workspace. Same intent, one structurally guaranteed and one convention. THE ARCHITECTURE RECORD SHOULD STATE BOTH AND SAY WHICH IS WHICH.

METHOD NOTE FROM LOCATING THAT COMMENT, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME TRAP AGAIN: a single-line search for "never leaves Postgres" RETURNED NOTHING. The phrase wraps across lines 73 and 74. It was found only by normalising whitespace first. A SINGLE-LINE GREP CANNOT SEE A WRAPPED COMMENT - already a standing rule in this repository, and it still cost a read.

FIXED 2026-09-25 18:41:29 AND THE FIX IS BETTER THAN EITHER OPTION THIS TICKET PROPOSED. Neither side of the type boundary was changed. THE OVERRIDE WAS DELETED: the profile is now passed straight through with no application override at all.

AND THE COMMENT LEFT IN ITS PLACE RECORDS A HAZARD NOBODY HAD IDENTIFIED, INCLUDING ME. What stood there was application: { ...profile.application, currentCtc: "", noticePeriodDays: 0 } - AND THAT WAS NOT BLANKING SENSITIVE VALUES THAT WERE PRESENT. MatchingProfile HAS NEVER CARRIED THOSE TWO FIELDS, so THE OVERRIDE FABRICATED THEM, purely to satisfy V1 MatchableProfile demanding the full ApplicationDetails.

SO THE STUB WAS THE ACTUAL HAZARD AND IT WAS WORSE THAN THE TYPE MISMATCH, for exactly the reason this ticket was filed about the opposite direction: IT SATISFIED THE TYPE. Had the matcher ever begun reading currentCtc or noticePeriodDays it would have received a fabricated empty string and a fabricated zero RATHER THAN FAILING TO COMPILE. The type error this ticket reported was the SAFE symptom; the silent fabrication sitting beside it was the dangerous one.

WHICH INVERTS THE FRAMING THIS TICKET WAS FILED WITH, AND THE INVERSION IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED: I argued the risk was that a future fourth field would arrive as undefined. THE REAL RISK WAS THAT TWO FIELDS WERE ALREADY BEING SUPPLIED AS FABRICATED VALUES. The failure mode was not future and hypothetical; it was present and latent, and it was invisible because it typechecked.

REMAINING ON THIS TICKET: AC3 - the V1/V2 dependency direction and the types crossing it still need stating in the architecture record, paired with the resume-projection minimisation at database.ts:73-74 as recorded above - and AC4, the mutation proof that a divergence fails v2 typecheck. NEITHER IS DISCHARGED BY THE FIX.

PROVISIONAL MARKING WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25, SAME DAY IT WAS APPLIED, BECAUSE IT WAS TOO BROAD AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENT. The #19 finding was real - tsc -b exited 0 with a production type error - BUT IT WAS OVERSTATED AS "the gate could not fail". THE GATE COULD FAIL; ONLY ITS FIRST LINK COULD NOT. `npm run typecheck` chains four commands and the last, check-test-types.mjs, filters on /^\S+\.ts\(\d+,\d+\): error TS\d+/ - WHICH MATCHES A PRODUCTION FILE AS READILY AS A TEST FILE - and exits 1. Anyone running the npm script WOULD have been told.

THIS TICKET DOES NOT CITE A BARE `tsc -b`, so its typecheck evidence was never in the unfalsifiable form and stands unqualified. The narrowed set is 4 of the original 29: CS-53, CS-62, CS-76, CS-77 - ALL FOUR WRITTEN BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, which is the correct place for the correction to land.

items.title: .gitattributes has no trailing newline, so any scripted append silently corrupts its last rule instead of adding a new one
items.userProblem: The file ends at byte 3097 with "f", the last character of ".env.example text eol=lf". An append concatenates onto that line, producing ".env.example text eol=lf*.sqlfixture text eol=crlf". Git still parses it, assigns the appended attributes to the ORIGINAL pattern, and takes the last value - so a declaration is silently overridden and no tool reports an error.
items.source: L-1 falsification experiment, 2026-09-25, reproduced and confirmed at source
acceptanceCriteria: The file ends with a newline, so an append starts a new rule rather than extending the last one
Proven by appending a rule programmatically and asserting the resulting final two lines are the original rule unchanged and the new rule alone - not by inspecting the file by eye
The existing rules are unchanged, verified by comparing the parsed pattern/attribute pairs before and after rather than by a byte diff, since the byte diff will necessarily differ
evidence: CONFIRMED AT SOURCE 2026-09-25: .gitattributes is 3097 bytes, THE LAST BYTE IS 102 ("f"), and the last line is ".env.example text eol=lf". There is no trailing newline. Zero CR bytes, so this is not a line-ending problem - it is a missing final terminator.

THE CORRUPTION MECHANISM, SIMULATED RATHER THAN DESCRIBED: appending "*.sqlfixture text eol=crlf" yields the final line ".env.example text eol=lf*.sqlfixture text eol=crlf". Git reads the pattern as .env.example and the attributes as "text eol=lf*.sqlfixture text eol=crlf", AND TAKES THE LAST VALUE - so .env.example silently acquires eol=crlf and the intended new rule never exists.

WHAT MAKES IT DANGEROUS IS THAT NOTHING FAILS. Git does not reject the line, the file remains valid, and the only symptom is that a declaration quietly changed. THE FAILURE IS SILENT AND IT IS IN THE FILE THAT GOVERNS LINE ENDINGS FOR THE WHOLE REPOSITORY.

THIS IS A LIVE HAZARD RATHER THAN A THEORETICAL ONE: it was hit tonight during the L-1 falsification, and three sessions have been making exactly this kind of scripted edit. It also bit in a second way - an Add-Content append with a PowerShell backtick-n writes CRLF on Windows, which introduced CR bytes into an LF-only file and tripped the COMPLIANCE half of the check rather than the completeness half being tested.

P3 BECAUSE THE BLAST RADIUS IS SMALL AND THE FIX IS ONE BYTE, NOT BECAUSE THE FAILURE IS MILD. A silently overridden eol declaration on the file that governs line endings would be found the way CS-65 was found - late, by its consequences.

2026-09-28: operator executed the append demonstration on the repository working tree using a temporary fixture. The program asserted the source ended in LF, appended a new rule, verified the final two parsed rules were the unchanged original rule plus the new rule, and compared all pre-existing parsed pattern/attribute pairs before and after; all assertions passed and the fixture was removed.
items.currentStep: Release Manager - the newline, append, and parsed-rule demonstrations are complete and recorded; hosted run 36424073277 also passed eol:check.

items.title: Untracked files have no baseline, so no before/after claim about most of the deployed web source can be verified by anyone
items.userProblem: Nothing has been committed since 2026-09-19. 260 files are untracked, including 25 of the 37 files under v2/apps/web/src. For an untracked file git diff HEAD has no baseline at all, so a reviewer cannot certify that a change is limited to what was claimed, cannot certify a freeze, and cannot reconstruct what any earlier review actually saw.
items.source: CS-51 independent audit, 2026-09-25 - a reviewer asked for git diff HEAD to certify the UI freeze and found it unrunnable
acceptanceCriteria: Every file a review is expected to certify has a committed baseline, so git diff HEAD returns a checkable answer rather than nothing
The commit is authorised explicitly by the owner for a named scope - this ticket does not grant it and must not be read as granting it
No personal data, resume, database, credential or generated artefact enters history; the existing ignore rules and publication guards are verified BEFORE the commit, not after
evidence: MEASURED 2026-09-25, NOT ESTIMATED. Working tree: 247 porcelain entries - 127 modified tracked files and 120 untracked entries. EXPANDING UNTRACKED DIRECTORIES GIVES 260 UNTRACKED FILES, because a single porcelain line for a directory hides an arbitrary number of files and counting lines would have understated it by more than double.
THE DEPLOYED WEB SURFACE IS THE WORST AFFECTED: v2/apps/web/src is 12 tracked and 25 untracked - 68% WITH NO BASELINE. v2/scripts is 55%, infra/v3 47%, v2/apps/api/src 33%, v2/packages/core/src 9%.

THE CONCRETE FAILURE THAT PRODUCED THIS TICKET: a reviewer auditing CS-51 asked for git diff HEAD to certify the UI freeze AND THE COMMAND IS UNRUNNABLE - all four files it needed are untracked and postdate HEAD, so there is no before state to diff against. The experiment returned nothing, and NOTHING IS NOT A RESULT.

THIS IS A SEPARATE COST FROM CI NEVER HAVING RUN, AND IT IS THE STRONGER ARGUMENT. CI not running means one class of evidence is unavailable. NO BASELINE MEANS NO BEFORE/AFTER CLAIM OF ANY KIND CAN BE CHECKED BY ANYONE - it applies to every review, today and retrospectively, and it silently weakens reviews that have already been recorded as complete.

AND IT INTERACTS WITH EVERY FINDING OF THIS RUN: a session cannot prove it changed only what it claimed; a reviewer cannot distinguish "this was always like that" from "this was introduced today"; and the near-miss where a file was read mid-edit would have been trivially settled by a diff against a baseline that does not exist.

EXPLICITLY NOT A REQUEST TO COMMIT AND NOT AN AUTHORISATION TO DO SO. The tree is deliberately dirty and that decision is the owner. This ticket records the VERIFIABILITY COST so the decision is made with the cost visible, rather than the cost being discovered by a reviewer who cannot complete an audit.

CS-31 IS A CONCRETE INSTANCE OF THE COST AND SHOULD BE COUNTED AS SUCH: all three of its acceptance criteria are independently verified met, its evidence ends "awaiting promotion on the next green CI run", AND NO SUCH RUN CAN OCCUR WHILE NOTHING IS COMMITTED. It is FINISHED WORK PARKED BEHIND AUTHORISATION, and recording it as outstanding would misrepresent both the work and the blocker.

THAT IS A SECOND, DIFFERENT COST FROM THE NO-BASELINE ONE THIS TICKET WAS FILED ABOUT. No baseline means reviews CANNOT BE COMPLETED; no CI run means completed work CANNOT BE PROMOTED. THE FIRST CORRUPTS EVIDENCE, THE SECOND STALLS DELIVERY, and they are independent - fixing one would not fix the other.

items.title: The zero-width refusal range destroys ZWNJ and ZWJ, so legitimate Devanagari, Arabic and Persian text is silently altered
items.userProblem: isRefusedCodePoint refuses 0x200b-0x200f, which contains U+200C ZWNJ and U+200D ZWJ. Those are not decoration - Indic, Arabic and Persian scripts need them for correct orthography. A Hindi job title using ZWNJ to suppress a conjunct ligature has that joiner silently removed, changing the word. On an India-focused product this is plausible real input, not a hypothetical.
items.source: reviewer E, CS-66 review 2026-09-26, reproduced executably by the orchestrator
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture containing ZWNJ between two Devanagari consonants is added and PROVEN RED BEFORE ANY POLICY CHANGE, so the failure is visible while the decision is taken

The joiner policy is context-sensitive rather than a widened range: ZWNJ and ZWJ are permitted where the surrounding characters make them orthographic, and still refused where they are decorative or adjacent to a script boundary

Both affected paths are addressed with their different behaviours stated: resume REJECTS a title segment containing these, and matching NEUTRALISES them - one drops legitimate input, the other mangles stored evidence
The spoofing rationale that put these characters in the refusal set is preserved and cited, so the change reads as a narrowing of an over-broad rule rather than a removal of a control
evidence: FOUND BY REVIEWER E AND CREDITED TO IT BY NAME. It read a numeric range and knew what lived inside it. NO GREP WOULD HAVE SURFACED THIS, and the code own comment - "zero-width and directional marks" - IS ACCURATE YET CONCEALS IT, because ZWNJ and ZWJ are literally zero-width marks. The single best finding of the review batch.

REPRODUCED EXECUTABLY RATHER THAN RELAYED, against packages/shared/src/evidence-text.ts:22. isRefusedCodePoint(0x200c) -> true and isRefusedCodePoint(0x200d) -> true. constrainEvidenceText on U+0915 + ZWNJ + U+0937 RETURNS THE TWO CONSONANTS WITH THE JOINER REMOVED. The ZWNJ is what suppresses the conjunct ligature, so REMOVING IT CHANGES THE ORTHOGRAPHY, SILENTLY - exactly what AC3 second clause forbids.

THE DETAIL THAT MAKES THIS WORTH ITS OWN TICKET: PLAIN DEVANAGARI PASSES UNTOUCHED - verified as a control in the same probe. So a naive "does non-Latin work?" fixture GOES GREEN. ONLY A FIXTURE CONTAINING ZWNJ SPECIFICALLY CATCHES IT. That is the same shape as an ASCII positive control against a criterion about non-Latin text: the control must exercise the property, not merely be positive.

THE PROBE CARRIED ITS OWN FALSIFICATION: U+0915, an ordinary Devanagari letter, is NOT refused - so the predicate is not simply rejecting everything above ASCII, and the ZWNJ result is specific rather than an artefact.

TWO PATHS ARE AFFECTED DIFFERENTLY AND BOTH MATTER, WHICH IS WHY ONE FIX WILL NOT DO: resume REJECTS a title segment containing these (CS-56 behaviour), so A LEGITIMATE HINDI TITLE IS DROPPED ENTIRELY; matching NEUTRALISES them (CS-66 behaviour), so STORED EVIDENCE IS MANGLED. Silent loss and silent corruption, from one range.

DO NOT SIMPLY WIDEN THE RANGE TO ALLOW ZWNJ AND ZWJ. They are genuinely used in homograph and spoofing attacks, which is WHY they sit in refusal sets. Unicode UTS #39 treats them as restricted BUT PERMITS THEM IN SPECIFIC CONTEXTS, such as between Indic consonants around a virama. THE CORRECT FIX IS CONTEXT-SENSITIVE AND IS A REAL DESIGN DECISION, NOT A ONE-LINE RANGE EDIT.

FILED SEPARATELY FROM CS-66 DELIBERATELY: CS-66 IS ABOUT HOSTILE INPUT BEING CONSTRAINED; THIS IS ABOUT LEGITIMATE INPUT BEING DESTROYED. They will want different answers, and folding this into CS-66 would let a hostile-input verdict close a correctness defect.
